nodes.summary: A gerbe over a site C is a category p : S → C over C such that • p : S → C is a stack in groupoids over C (see Definition [Tag 02ZI]), • for U ∈ Ob(C) there exists a covering (U_i → U) in C such that S_U_i is nonempty, and • for U ∈ Ob(C) and x, y ∈ Ob(S_U) there exists a covering (U_i → U) in C such that x|_U_i ≅ y|_U_i in S_U_i.

nodes.title: Gerbes · Lemma 06P0
nodes.summary: Let C be a site. Let S_1, S_2 be categories over C. Suppose that S_1 and S_2 are equivalent as categories over C. Then S_1 is a gerbe over C if and only if S_2 is a gerbe over C.

nodes.title: Gerbes · Lemma 06P1
nodes.summary: Let C be a site. Let p : X → C and q : Y → C be stacks in groupoids. Let F : X → Y be a 1-morphism of categories over C. The following are equivalent • For some (equivalently any) factorization F = F' ∘ a where a : X → X' is an equivalence of categories over C and F' is fibred in groupoids, the map F' : X' → Y is a gerbe (with the topology on Y inherited from C). • The following two conditions are satisfied • for y ∈ Ob(Y) lying over U ∈ Ob(C) there exists a covering (U_i…

nodes.title: Gerbes · Definition 06P2
nodes.summary: Let C be a site. Let X and Y be stacks in groupoids over C. Let F : X → Y be a 1-morphism of categories over C. We say X is a gerbe over Y if the equivalent conditions of Lemma [Tag 06P1] are satisfied.

nodes.title: Gerbes · Lemma 06P3
nodes.summary: Let C be a site. Let xymatrix X' ar[r]_G' ar[d]_F' & X ar[d]^F Y' ar[r]^G & Y be a 2-fibre product of stacks in groupoids over C. If X is a gerbe over Y, then X' is a gerbe over Y'.

nodes.title: Gerbes · Lemma 06R3
nodes.summary: Let C be a site. Let F : X → Y and G : Y → Z be 1-morphisms of stacks in groupoids over C. If X is a gerbe over Y and Y is a gerbe over Z, then X is a gerbe over Z.

nodes.title: Gerbes · Lemma 06P4
nodes.summary: Let C be a site. Let xymatrix X' ar[r]_G' ar[d]_F' & X ar[d]^F Y' ar[r]^G & Y be a 2-cartesian diagram of stacks in groupoids over C. If for every U ∈ Ob(C) and x ∈ Ob(Y_U) there exists a covering (U_i → U) such that x|_U_i is in the essential image of G : Y'_U_i → Y_U_i and X' is a gerbe over Y', then X is a gerbe over Y.

nodes.title: Gerbes · Lemma 0CJY
nodes.summary: Let p : S → C be a gerbe over a site C. Assume that for all U ∈ Ob(C) and x ∈ Ob(S_U) the sheaf of groups mathitAut(x) = mathitIsom(x, x) on C/U is abelian. Then there exist • a sheaf G of abelian groups on C, • for every U ∈ Ob(C) and every x ∈ Ob(S_U) an isomorphism G|_U → mathitAut(x) such that for every U and every morphism φ : x → y in S_U the diagram xymatrix G|_U ar[d] ar@=[rr] & & G|_U ar[d] mathitAut(x) ar[rr]^α ↦ φ ∘ α ∘ φ^-1 & & mathitAut(y) is commutative.

nodes.title: Functoriality for stacks · Lemma 04WB
nodes.summary: In the situation above, if S is a fibred category over D then u^pS is a fibred category over C.

nodes.title: Functoriality for stacks · Lemma 04WC
nodes.summary: Let u : C → D be a continuous functor of sites. Let p : S → D be a stack over D. Then u^pS is a stack over C.

nodes.title: Functoriality for stacks · Lemma 04WD
nodes.summary: Let u : C → D be a continuous functor of sites. Let p : S → D be a stack in groupoids over D. Then u^pS is a stack in groupoids over C.

nodes.title: Functoriality for stacks · Definition 04WE
nodes.summary: Let f : D → C be a morphism of sites given by the continuous functor u : C → D. Let S be a fibred category over D. In this setting we write f_*S for the fibred category u^pS defined above. We say that f_*S is the pushforward of S along f.

nodes.title: Functoriality for stacks · Lemma 04WF
nodes.summary: In the situation above assume • p : S → C is a fibred category, • C has nonempty finite limits, and • u : C → D commutes with nonempty finite limits. Consider the set R ⊂ Arrows(u_ppS) of morphisms of the form (a, id_V, α) : (U', φ' : V → u(U'), x') → (U, φ : V → u(U), x) with α strongly cartesian. Then R is a right multiplicative system.

nodes.title: Functoriality for stacks · Lemma 04WG
nodes.summary: With notation and assumptions as in Lemma [Tag 04WF]. Set u_pS = R^-1u_ppS, see Categories, Section [Tag 04VB]. Then u_pS is a fibred category over D.

nodes.title: Functoriality for stacks · Lemma 04WH
nodes.summary: With notation and assumptions as in Lemma [Tag 04WG]. If S is fibred in groupoids, then u_pS is fibred in groupoids.

nodes.title: Functoriality for stacks · Lemma 04WI
nodes.summary: Let u : C → D be a functor. Let p : S → C and q : T → D be categories over C and D. Assume that • p : S → C is a fibred category, • q : T → D is a fibred category, • C has nonempty finite limits, and • u : C → D commutes with nonempty finite limits. Then we have a canonical equivalence of categories Mor_Fib/C(S, u^pT) = Mor_Fib/D(u_pS, T) of morphism categories.

nodes.title: Functoriality for stacks · Definition 04WJ
nodes.summary: Let f : D → C be a morphism of sites given by a continuous functor u : C → D satisfying the hypotheses and conclusions of Sites, Proposition [Tag 00X6]. Let S be a stack over C. In this setting we write f^-1S for the stackification of the fibred category u_pS over D constructed above. We say that f^-1S is the pullback of S along f.

nodes.title: Functoriality for stacks · Lemma 04WK
nodes.summary: Let f : D → C be a morphism of sites given by a continuous functor u : C → D satisfying the hypotheses and conclusions of Sites, Proposition [Tag 00X6]. Let p : S → C and q : T → D be stacks. Then we have a canonical equivalence of categories Mor_Stacks/C(S, f_*T) = Mor_Stacks/D(f^-1S, T) of morphism categories.

nodes.title: Functoriality for stacks · Lemma 04WR
nodes.summary: Let f : D → C be a morphism of sites given by a continuous functor u : C → D satisfying the hypotheses and conclusions of Sites, Proposition [Tag 00X6]. Let S → C be a fibred category, and let S → S' be the stackification of S. Then f^-1S' is the stackification of u_pS.

nodes.title: Functoriality for stacks · Lemma 04WS
nodes.summary: Let C and D be sites. Let u : C → D be a functor satisfying the assumptions of Sites, Lemma [Tag 00XU]. Let f : D → C be the corresponding morphism of sites. Then • for every stack p : S → C the canonical functor S → f_*f^-1S is an equivalence of stacks, • given stacks S, S' over C the construction f^-1 induces an equivalence Mor_Stacks/C(S, S') → Mor_Stacks/D(f^-1S, f^-1S') of morphism categories.

nodes.title: Stacks and localization · Lemma 04WU
nodes.summary: Let C be a site. Let U ∈ Ob(C). Then j_U : C/U → C is a stack over C if and only if h_U is a sheaf.

nodes.title: Stacks and localization · Lemma 04WV
nodes.summary: Assume that C is a site, and U is an object of C whose associated representable presheaf is a sheaf. Constructions A and B above define mutually inverse (!) functors of 2-categories ( 2-category of stacks over C/U ) ↔ ( 2-category of pairs (T, p) consisting of a stack T over C and a morphism p : T → C/U of stacks over C )

nodes.title: Basic definitions · Definition 09FD
nodes.summary: A field is a nonzero ring where every nonzero element is invertible. Given a field a subfield is a subring that is itself a field.

nodes.title: Basic definitions · Definition 09FE
nodes.summary: A domain or an integral domain is a nonzero ring where 0 is the only zerodivisor.

nodes.title: Vector spaces · Lemma 09FN
nodes.summary: If k is a field, then every k-module is free.

nodes.title: Vector spaces · Lemma 09FP
nodes.summary: Every exact sequence of modules over a field splits.

nodes.title: The characteristic of a field · Definition 09FR
nodes.summary: The characteristic of a field F is 0 if Z ⊂ F, or is a prime p if p = 0 in F. The prime subfield of F is the smallest subfield of F which is either Q ⊂ F if the characteristic is zero, or F_p ⊂ F if the characteristic is p > 0.

nodes.title: Field extensions · Lemma 09FU
nodes.summary: If F is a field and R is a nonzero ring, then any ring homomorphism φ : F → R is injective.

nodes.title: Field extensions · Definition 09FV
nodes.summary: If F is a field contained in a field E, then E is said to be a field extension of F. We shall write E/F to indicate that E is an extension of F.

nodes.title: Field extensions · Definition 09FW
nodes.summary: A tower of fields E_n/E_n - 1/…/E_0 consists of a sequence of extensions of fields E_n/E_n - 1, E_n - 1/E_n - 2, …, E_1/E_0.

nodes.title: Field extensions · Definition 09FZ
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. If F/k is an extension of fields and S ⊂ F, we write k(S) for the smallest subfield of F containing k and S. We will say that S generates the field extension k(S)/k. If S = (α) is a singleton, then we write k(α) instead of k((α)). We say F/k is a finitely generated field extension if there exists a finite subset S ⊂ F with F = k(S).

nodes.title: Classification of simple extensions · Lemma 09G1
nodes.summary: If a field extension F/k is generated by one element, then it is k-isomorphic either to the rational function field k(t)/k or to one of the extensions k[t]/(P) for P ∈ k[t] irreducible.

nodes.title: Field extensions · Lemma 0H7K
nodes.summary: Let k be a field and let E/k and F/k be field extensions. Then there exists a common field extension M/k, i.e., an extension field such that there exist maps E → M and F → M of extensions of k.

nodes.title: Finite extensions · Definition 09G3
nodes.summary: Let F/E be an extension of fields. The dimension of F considered as an E-vector space is called the degree of the extension and is denoted [F : E]. If [F : E] < ∞ then F is said to be a finite extension of E.

nodes.title: Finite extensions · Lemma 09G5
nodes.summary: Let K/E/F be a tower of algebraic field extensions. If K is finite over F, then K is finite over E.

nodes.title: Finite extensions · Lemma 0BU1
nodes.summary: A finite extension of fields is a finitely generated field extension. The converse is not true.

nodes.title: Multiplicativity · Lemma 09G9
nodes.summary: Suppose given a tower of fields F/E/k. Then [F:k] = [F:E][E:k]

nodes.title: Finite extensions · Definition 09GA
nodes.summary: A field K is said to be a number field if it has characteristic 0 and the extension K/Q is finite.

nodes.title: Algebraic extensions · Definition 09GC
nodes.summary: Consider a field extension F/E. An element α ∈ F is said to be algebraic over E if α is the root of some nonzero polynomial with coefficients in E. If all elements of F are algebraic then F is said to be an algebraic extension of E.

nodes.title: Algebraic extensions · Lemma 09GF
nodes.summary: Let K/E/F be a tower of field extensions. • If α ∈ K is algebraic over F, then α is algebraic over E. • If K is algebraic over F, then K is algebraic over E.

nodes.title: Algebraic extensions · Lemma 09GG
nodes.summary: A finite extension is algebraic. In fact, an extension E/k is algebraic if and only if every subextension k(α)/k generated by some α ∈ E is finite.

nodes.title: Algebraic extensions · Lemma 09GH
nodes.summary: A finitely generated algebraic extension is finite. Let k be a field, and let α_1, α_2, …, α_n be elements of some extension field such that each α_i is algebraic over k. Then the extension k(α_1, …, α_n)/k is finite. That is, a finitely generated algebraic extension is finite.

nodes.title: Algebraic extensions · Lemma 09GI
nodes.summary: Let E/k be a field extension. Then the elements of E algebraic over k form a subextension of E/k.

nodes.title: Algebraic extensions · Lemma 09GJ
nodes.summary: Let E/k and F/E be algebraic extensions of fields. Then F/k is an algebraic extension of fields.

nodes.title: Algebraic extensions · Lemma 09GK
nodes.summary: Let E/F be an algebraic extension of fields. Then the cardinality |E| of E is at most max(aleph_0, |F|).

nodes.title: Algebraic extensions · Lemma 0BID
nodes.summary: Let E/F be a finite or more generally an algebraic extension of fields. Any subring F ⊂ R ⊂ E is a field.

nodes.title: Algebraic extensions · Lemma 0BMD
nodes.summary: Let E/F an algebraic extension of fields. Any F-algebra map f : E → E is an automorphism.

nodes.title: Minimal polynomials · Definition 09GM
nodes.summary: The polynomial P above is called the minimal polynomial of α over k.

nodes.title: Minimal polynomials · Lemma 09GN
nodes.summary: The degree of the minimal polynomial is [k(α) : k].

nodes.title: Algebraic closure · Definition 09GQ
nodes.summary: A field F is said to be algebraically closed if every algebraic extension E/F is trivial, i.e., E = F.

nodes.title: Algebraic closure · Lemma 09GR
nodes.summary: Let F be a field. The following are equivalent • F is algebraically closed, • every irreducible polynomial over F is linear, • every nonconstant polynomial over F has a root, • every nonconstant polynomial over F is a product of linear factors.

nodes.title: Algebraic closure · Definition 09GS
nodes.summary: Let F be a field. An algebraic closure of F is a field overlineF containing F such that: • overlineF is algebraic over F. • overlineF is algebraically closed.

nodes.title: Algebraic closure · Theorem 09GT
nodes.summary: Every field has an algebraic closure.

nodes.title: Algebraic closure · Lemma 09GU
nodes.summary: Let F be a field. Let overlineF be an algebraic closure of F. Let M/F be an algebraic extension. Then there is a morphism of F-extensions M → overlineF.

nodes.title: Algebraic closure · Lemma 09GV
nodes.summary: Any two algebraic closures of a field are isomorphic.

nodes.title: Relatively prime polynomials · Definition 09GX
nodes.summary: If k is any field, we say that two polynomials in k[x] are relatively prime if they generate the unit ideal in k[x].

nodes.title: Relatively prime polynomials · Lemma 09GY
nodes.summary: Two polynomials in k[x] are relatively prime precisely when they have no common roots in an algebraic closure overlinek of k.

nodes.title: Separable algebraic extensions · Lemma 09H0
nodes.summary: Let F be a field. Let P ∈ F[x] be an irreducible polynomial over F. Let P' = dP/dx be the derivative of P with respect to x. Then one of the following two cases happens • P and P' are relatively prime, or • P' is the zero polynomial. The second case can only happen if F has characteristic p > 0. In this case P(x) = Q(x^q) where q = p^f is a power of p and Q ∈ F[x] is an irreducible polynomial such that Q and Q' are relatively prime.

nodes.title: Separable algebraic extensions · Definition 09H1
nodes.summary: Let F be a field. Let K/F be an extension of fields. • We say an irreducible polynomial P over F is separable if it is relatively prime to its derivative. • Given α ∈ K algebraic over F we say α is separable over F if its minimal polynomial is separable over F. • If K is an algebraic extension of F, we say K is separable over F if every element of K is separable over F.

nodes.title: Separable algebraic extensions · Lemma 09H2
nodes.summary: Let K/E/F be a tower of algebraic field extensions. • If α ∈ K is separable over F, then α is separable over E. • if K is separable over F, then K is separable over E.

nodes.title: Separable algebraic extensions · Lemma 09H3
nodes.summary: Let F be a field. An irreducible polynomial P over F is separable if and only if P has pairwise distinct roots in an algebraic closure of F.

nodes.title: Separable algebraic extensions · Lemma 09H4
nodes.summary: Let F be a field and let overlineF be an algebraic closure of F. Let p > 0 be the characteristic of F. Let P be a polynomial over F. Then the set of roots of P and P(x^p) in overlineF have the same cardinality (not counting multiplicity).

nodes.title: Separable algebraic extensions · Definition 09H5
nodes.summary: Let F be a field. Let P be an irreducible polynomial over F. The separable degree of P is the cardinality of the set of roots of P in any algebraic closure of F (see discussion above). Notation deg_s(P).

nodes.title: Separable algebraic extensions · Lemma 09H7
nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 09H6] the correspondence Mor_F(K, overlineF) → ((β_1, …, β_n) as below), φ ↦ (φ(α_1), …, φ(α_n)) is a bijection. Here the right hand side is the set of n-tuples (β_1, …, β_n) of elements of overlineF having the following property: • β_1 ∈ overlineF is a root of P_1; let φ_1 : K_1 → overlineF be the homomorphism over F sending α_1 to β_1, • β_2 ∈ overlineF is a root of P_2^φ_1; let φ_2 : K_2 → overlineF be the homomorphism extending φ_1 sending α_2 to…

nodes.title: Separable algebraic extensions · Lemma 09H8
nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 09H6] we have |Mor_F(K, overlineF)| = ∏_i = 1^n deg_s(P_i).

nodes.title: Separable algebraic extensions · Lemma 09H9
nodes.summary: Assumptions and notation as in Situation [Tag 09H6]. If each P_i is separable, i.e., each α_i is separable over K_i - 1, then |Mor_F(K, overlineF)| = [K : F] and the field extension K/F is separable. If one of the α_i is not separable over K_i - 1, then |Mor_F(K, overlineF)| < [K : F].

nodes.title: Separable algebraic extensions · Lemma 09HA
nodes.summary: Let K/F be a finite extension of fields. Let overlineF be an algebraic closure of F. Then we have |Mor_F(K, overlineF)| ≤ [K : F] with equality if and only if K is separable over F.

nodes.title: Separable algebraic extensions · Lemma 09HB
nodes.summary: Let E/k and F/E be separable algebraic extensions of fields. Then F/k is a separable extension of fields.

nodes.title: Separable algebraic extensions · Lemma 09HC
nodes.summary: Let E/k be a field extension. Then the elements of E separable over k form a subextension of E/k.

nodes.title: Linear independence of characters · Lemma 0CKL
nodes.summary: Let L be a field. Let G be a monoid, for example a group. Let chi_1, …, chi_n : G → L be pairwise distinct homomorphisms of monoids where L is regarded as a monoid by multiplication. Then chi_1, …, chi_n are L-linearly independent: if λ_1, …, λ_n ∈ L not all zero, then ∑ λ_ichi_i(g) not = 0 for some g ∈ G.

nodes.title: Linear independence of characters · Lemma 0EM9
nodes.summary: Let L be a field. Let n ≥ 1 and α_1, …, α_n ∈ L pairwise distinct elements of L. Then there exists an e ≥ 0 such that ∑_i = 1, …, n α_i^e not = 0.

nodes.title: Linear independence of characters · Lemma 0CKM
nodes.summary: Let K/F and L/F be field extensions. Let σ_1, …, σ_n : K → L be pairwise distinct morphisms of F-extensions. Then σ_1, …, σ_n are L-linearly independent: if λ_1, …, λ_n ∈ L not all zero, then ∑ λ_iσ_i(α) not = 0 for some α ∈ K.

nodes.title: Linear independence of characters · Lemma 0CKN
nodes.summary: Let K/F and L/F be field extensions with K/F finite separable and L algebraically closed. Then the map K ⊗_F L → ∏_σ ∈ Hom_F(K, L) L, α ⊗ β ↦ (σ(α)β)_σ is an isomorphism of L-algebras.

nodes.title: Purely inseparable extensions · Definition 09HE
nodes.summary: Let F be a field of characteristic p > 0. Let K/F be an extension. • An element α ∈ K is purely inseparable over F if there exists a power q of p such that α^q ∈ F. • The extension K/F is said to be purely inseparable if and only if every element of K is purely inseparable over F. If we have a field extension L/M (with no condition on the characteristic of M), then we will say the extension is purely inseparable if either L = M or the characteristic of M is a prime number…

nodes.title: Purely inseparable extensions · Lemma 09HF
nodes.summary: Let p be a prime number. Let F be a field of characteristic p. Let t ∈ F be an element which does not have a pth root in F. Then the polynomial x^p - t is irreducible over F.

nodes.title: Purely inseparable extensions · Lemma 09HG
nodes.summary: Let E/k and F/E be purely inseparable extensions of fields. Then F/k is a purely inseparable extension of fields.

nodes.title: Purely inseparable extensions · Lemma 09HH
nodes.summary: Let E/k be a field extension. Then the elements of E purely-inseparable over k form a subextension of E/k.

nodes.title: Purely inseparable extensions · Lemma 09HI
nodes.summary: Let E/F be a finite purely inseparable field extension of characteristic p > 0. Then there exists a sequence of elements α_1, …, α_n ∈ E such that we obtain a tower of fields E = F(α_1, …, α_n) ⊃ F(α_1, …, α_n - 1) ⊃ … ⊃ F(α_1) ⊃ F such that each intermediate extension is of degree p and comes from adjoining a pth root. Namely, α_i^p ∈ F(α_1, …, α_i - 1) is an element which does not have a pth root in F(α_1, …, α_i - 1) for i = 1, …, n.

nodes.title: Purely inseparable extensions · Lemma 030K
nodes.summary: Any algebraic field extension is uniquely a separable field extension followed by a purely inseparable one. Let E/F be an algebraic field extension. There exists a unique subextension E/E_sep/F such that E_sep/F is separable and E/E_sep is purely inseparable.

nodes.title: Purely inseparable extensions · Definition 030L
nodes.summary: Let E/F be an algebraic field extension. Let E_sep be the subextension found in Lemma [Tag 030K]. • The integer [E_sep : F] is called the separable degree of the extension. Notation [E : F]_s. • The integer [E : E_sep] is called the inseparable degree, or the degree of inseparability of the extension. Notation [E : F]_i.

nodes.title: Purely inseparable extensions · Lemma 09HJ
nodes.summary: Let K/F be a finite extension. Let overlineF be an algebraic closure of F. Then [K : F]_s = |Mor_F(K, overlineF)|.

nodes.title: Multiplicativity · Lemma 09HK
nodes.summary: Suppose given a tower of algebraic field extensions K/E/F. Then [K : F]_s = [K : E]_s [E : F]_s and [K : F]_i = [K : E]_i [E : F]_i

nodes.title: Normal extensions · Definition 09HM
nodes.summary: Let E/F be an algebraic field extension. We say E is normal over F if for all α ∈ E the minimal polynomial P of α over F splits completely into linear factors over E.

nodes.title: Normal extensions · Lemma 09HN
nodes.summary: Let K/E/F be a tower of algebraic field extensions. If K is normal over F, then K is normal over E.

nodes.title: Normal extensions · Lemma 09HP
nodes.summary: Let F be a field. Let M/F be an algebraic extension. Let M/E_i/F, i ∈ I be subextensions with E_i/F normal. Then ⋂ E_i is normal over F.

nodes.title: Normal extensions · Lemma 0EXK
nodes.summary: Let E/F be a normal algebraic field extension. Then the subextension E/E_sep/F of Lemma [Tag 030K] is normal.

nodes.title: Normal extensions · Lemma 09HQ
nodes.summary: Let E/F be an algebraic extension of fields. Let overlineF be an algebraic closure of F. The following are equivalent • E is normal over F, and • for every pair σ, σ' ∈ Mor_F(E, overlineF) we have σ(E) = σ'(E).

nodes.title: Normal extensions · Lemma 0BR3
nodes.summary: Let E/F be an algebraic extension of fields. If E is generated by α_i ∈ E, i ∈ I over F and if for each i the minimal polynomial of α_i over F splits completely in E, then E/F is normal.

nodes.title: Normal extensions · Lemma 0BME
nodes.summary: Let L/M/K be a tower of algebraic extensions. • If M/K is normal, then any automorphism τ of L/K induces an automorphism τ|_M : M → M. • If L/K is normal, then any K-algebra map σ : M → L extends to an automorphism of L.

nodes.title: Normal extensions · Definition 09HR
nodes.summary: Let E/F be an extension of fields. Then Aut(E/F) or Aut_F(E) denotes the automorphism group of E as an object of the category of F-extensions. Elements of Aut(E/F) are called automorphisms of E over F or automorphisms of E/F.

nodes.title: Normal extensions · Lemma 09HS
nodes.summary: Let E/F be a finite extension. We have |Aut(E/F)| ≤ [E : F]_s with equality if and only if E is normal over F.

nodes.title: Normal extensions · Lemma 0BR4
nodes.summary: Let L/K be an algebraic normal extension of fields. Let E/K be an extension of fields. Then either there is no K-embedding from L to E or there is one τ : L → E and every other one is of the form τ ∘ σ where σ ∈ Aut(L/K).

nodes.title: Splitting fields · Lemma 09HU
nodes.summary: Let F be a field. Let P ∈ F[x] be a nonconstant polynomial. There exists a smallest field extension E/F such that P splits completely over E. Moreover, the field extension E/F is normal and unique up to (nonunique) isomorphism.

nodes.title: Splitting fields · Definition 09HV
nodes.summary: Let F be a field. Let P ∈ F[x] be a nonconstant polynomial. The field extension E/F constructed in Lemma [Tag 09HU] is called the splitting field of P over F.

nodes.title: Splitting fields · Lemma 09DT
nodes.summary: Existence of normal closure of finite extensions of fields. Let E/F be a finite extension of fields. There exists a unique smallest finite extension K/E such that K is normal over F.

nodes.title: Splitting fields · Definition 0BMF
nodes.summary: Let E/F be a finite extension of fields. The field extension K/E constructed in Lemma [Tag 09DT] is called the normal closure E over F.

nodes.title: Splitting fields · Lemma 0BMG
nodes.summary: Let L/K be an algebraic normal extension. • If L/M/K is a subextension with M/K finite, then there exists a tower L/M'/M/K with M'/K finite and normal. • If L/M'/M/K is a tower with M/K normal and M'/M finite, then there exists a tower L/M"/M'/M/K with M"/M finite and M"/K normal.

nodes.title: Splitting fields · Lemma 0EXL
nodes.summary: Let L/K be a finite extension. Let M/L be the normal closure of L over K. Then there is a surjective map L ⊗_K L ⊗_K … ⊗_K L → M of K-algebras where the number of tensors can be taken [L : K]_s ≤ [L : K].

nodes.title: Roots of unity · Lemma 09HX
nodes.summary: Let A be an abelian group of exponent dividing n such that (x ∈ A mid dx = 0) has cardinality at most d for all d | n. Then A is cyclic of order dividing n.

nodes.title: Primitive element · Lemma 030N
nodes.summary: Let E/F be a finite extension of fields. The following are equivalent • there exists a primitive element for E over F, and • there are finitely many subextensions E/K/F. Moreover, (1) and (2) hold if E/F is separable.

nodes.title: Trace and norm · Definition 0BIF
nodes.summary: Let L/K be a finite extension of fields. For α ∈ L we define the trace Trace_L/K(α) = Trace_K(α : L → L) and the norm Norm_L/K(α) = det_K(α : L → L).

nodes.title: Trace and norm · Lemma 0BIG
nodes.summary: Let L/K be a finite extension of fields. Let α ∈ L and let P be the minimal polynomial of α over K. Then the characteristic polynomial of the K-linear map α : L → L is equal to P^e with e deg(P) = [L : K].

nodes.title: Trace and norm · Lemma 0BIH
nodes.summary: Let L/K be a finite extension of fields. Let α ∈ L and let P = x^d + a_1 x^d - 1 + … + a_d be the minimal polynomial of α over K. Then Norm_L/K(α) = (-1)^[L : K] a_d^e and Trace_L/K(α) = - e a_1 where e d = [L : K].

nodes.title: Trace and norm · Lemma 0BII
nodes.summary: Let L/K be a finite extension of fields. Let V be a finite dimensional vector space over L. Let φ : V → V be an L-linear map. Then Trace_K(φ : V → V) = Trace_L/K(Trace_L(φ : V → V)) and det_K(φ : V → V) = Norm_L/K(det_L(φ : V → V))

nodes.title: Trace and norm · Lemma 0BIJ
nodes.summary: Let M/L/K be a tower of finite extensions of fields. Then Trace_M/K = Trace_L/K ∘ Trace_M/L and Norm_M/K = Norm_L/K ∘ Norm_M/L

nodes.title: Trace and norm · Definition 0BIK
nodes.summary: Let L/K be a finite extension of fields. The trace pairing for L/K is the symmetric K-bilinear form Q_L/K : L × L → K, (α, β) ↦ Trace_L/K(αβ)

nodes.title: Trace and norm · Lemma 0BIL
nodes.summary: Let L/K be a finite extension of fields. The following are equivalent: • L/K is separable, • Trace_L/K is not identically zero, and • the trace pairing Q_L/K is nondegenerate.

nodes.title: Trace and norm · Definition 0BIM
nodes.summary: Let L/K be a finite extension of fields. The discriminant of L/K is the discriminant of the trace pairing Q_L/K.

nodes.title: Galois theory · Definition 09I0
nodes.summary: A field extension E/F is called Galois if it is algebraic, separable, and normal.

nodes.title: Galois theory · Lemma 09I1
nodes.summary: Let E/F be a finite extension of fields. Then E is Galois over F if and only if |Aut(E/F)| = [E : F].

nodes.title: Galois theory · Definition 09DV
nodes.summary: If E/F is a Galois extension, then the group Aut(E/F) is called the Galois group and it is denoted Gal(E/F).

nodes.title: Galois theory · Lemma 09I2
nodes.summary: Let K/E/F be a tower of algebraic field extensions. If K is Galois over F, then K is Galois over E.

nodes.title: Galois theory · Lemma 0EXM
nodes.summary: Let L/K be a finite separable extension of fields. Let M be the normal closure of L over K (Definition [Tag 0BMF]). Then M/K is Galois.

nodes.title: Galois theory · Lemma 09I3
nodes.summary: Let K be a field. Let G be a finite group acting faithfully on K. Then the extension K/K^G is Galois, we have [K : K^G] = |G|, and the Galois group of the extension is G.

nodes.title: Fundamental theorem of Galois theory · Theorem 09DW
nodes.summary: Let L/K be a finite Galois extension with Galois group G. Then we have K = L^G and the map (subgroups of G) → (subextensions L/M/K), H ↦ L^H is a bijection whose inverse maps M to Gal(L/M). The normal subgroups H of G correspond exactly to those subextensions M with M/K Galois.

nodes.title: Galois theory · Lemma 0BMH
nodes.summary: Let L/M/K be a tower of fields. Assume L/K and M/K are finite Galois. Then we obtain a short exact sequence 1 → Gal(L/M) → Gal(L/K) → Gal(M/K) → 1 of finite groups.

nodes.title: Infinite Galois theory · Lemma 0BMJ
nodes.summary: Let E/F be a Galois extension. Endow Gal(E/F) with the coarsest topology such that Gal(E/F) × E → E is continuous when E is given the discrete topology. Then • for any topological space X and map X → Gal(E/F) such that the action X × E → E is continuous the induced map X → Gal(E/F) is continuous, • this topology turns Gal(E/F) into a profinite topological group.

nodes.title: Infinite Galois theory · Lemma 0BMK
nodes.summary: Let L/M/K be a tower of fields. Assume both L/K and M/K are Galois. Then there is a canonical surjective continuous homomorphism c : Gal(L/K) → Gal(M/K).

nodes.title: Infinite Galois theory · Lemma 0BU2
nodes.summary: Let L/K be a Galois extension with Galois group G. Let Lambda be the set of finite Galois subextensions, i.e., λ ∈ Lambda corresponds to L/L_λ/K with L_λ/K finite Galois with Galois group G_λ. Define a partial ordering on Lambda by the rule λ ≥ λ' if and only if L_λ ⊃ L_λ'. Then • Lambda is a directed partially ordered set, • L_λ is a system of K-extensions over Lambda and L = colim L_λ, • G_λ is an inverse system of finite groups over Lambda, the transition maps are…

nodes.title: Fundamental theorem of infinite Galois theory · Theorem 0BML
nodes.summary: Let L/K be a Galois extension. Let G = Gal(L/K) be the Galois group viewed as a profinite topological group (Lemma [Tag 0BMJ]). Then we have K = L^G and the map (closed subgroups of G) → (subextensions L/M/K), H ↦ L^H is a bijection whose inverse maps M to Gal(L/M). The finite subextensions M correspond exactly to the open subgroups H ⊂ G. The normal closed subgroups H of G correspond exactly to subextensions M Galois over K.

nodes.title: Infinite Galois theory · Lemma 0BMM
nodes.summary: Let L/M/K be a tower of fields. Assume L/K and M/K are Galois. Then we obtain a short exact sequence 1 → Gal(L/M) → Gal(L/K) → Gal(M/K) → 1 of profinite topological groups.

nodes.title: Fundamental theorem of algebra · Lemma 09I5
nodes.summary: The field C is algebraically closed.

nodes.title: Kummer extensions · Lemma 09DX
nodes.summary: Let L/K be a Galois extension of fields whose Galois group is Z/nZ. Assume moreover that the characteristic of K is prime to n and that K contains a primitive nth root of 1. Then L = K[z] with z^n ∈ K.

nodes.title: Kummer extensions · Lemma 0EXN
nodes.summary: Let K be a field with algebraic closure overlineK. Let p be a prime different from the characteristic of K. Let zeta ∈ overlineK be a primitive pth root of 1. Then K(zeta)/K is a Galois extension of degree dividing p - 1.

nodes.title: Kummer extensions · Lemma 0EXP
nodes.summary: [Radical] Let K be a field. Let L/K be a finite extension of degree e which is generated by an element α with a = α^e ∈ K. If every eth root of unity in L is contained in K, then any sub extension L/L'/K is generated by α^d for some d | e.

nodes.title: Artin-Schreier extensions · Lemma 09DY
nodes.summary: Let L/K be a Galois extension of fields of characteristic p > 0 with Galois group Z/pZ. Then L = K[z] with z^p - z ∈ K.

nodes.title: Transcendence · Definition 030E
nodes.summary: Let K/k be a field extension. • A collection of elements (x_i)_i ∈ I of K is called algebraically independent over k if the map k[X_i; i∈ I] → K which maps X_i to x_i is injective. • The field of fractions of a polynomial ring k[x_i; i ∈ I] is denoted k(x_i; i∈ I). • A purely transcendental extension of k is any field extension K/k isomorphic to the field of fractions of a polynomial ring over k. • A transcendence basis of K/k is a collection of elements (x_i)_i ∈ I which…

nodes.title: Transcendence · Lemma 030F
nodes.summary: Let E/F be a field extension. A transcendence basis of E over F exists. Any two transcendence bases have the same cardinality.

nodes.title: Transcendence · Definition 030G
nodes.summary: Let K/k be a field extension. The transcendence degree of K over k is the cardinality of a transcendence basis of K over k. It is denoted trdeg_k(K).

nodes.title: Transcendence · Lemma 030H
nodes.summary: Let L/K/k be field extensions. Then trdeg_k(L) = trdeg_K(L) + trdeg_k(K).

nodes.title: Transcendence · Definition 037I
nodes.summary: Let K/k be a field extension. • The algebraic closure of k in K is the subfield k' of K consisting of elements of K which are algebraic over k. • We say k is algebraically closed in K if every element of K which is algebraic over k is contained in k.

nodes.title: Transcendence · Lemma 0G1M
nodes.summary: Let k'/k be a finite extension of fields. Let k'(x_1, …, x_r)/k(x_1, …, x_r) be the induced extension of purely transcendental extensions. Then [k'(x_1, …, x_r) : k(x_1, …, x_r)] = [k' : k] < ∞.

nodes.title: Transcendence · Lemma 037J
nodes.summary: Let K/k be a finitely generated field extension. The algebraic closure of k in K is finite over k.

nodes.title: Linearly disjoint extensions · Definition 09ID
nodes.summary: Consider a diagram vcenter xymatrix L ar[r] & Ω k ar[r] ar[u] & K ar[u] of field extensions. The compositum of K and L in Ω written KL is the smallest subfield of Ω containing both L and K.

nodes.title: Linearly disjoint extensions · Definition 09IF
nodes.summary: Consider a diagram of fields as in ([Tag 09IE]). We say that K and L are linearly disjoint over k in Ω if the map K ⊗_k L → KL, ∑ x_i ⊗ y_i ↦ ∑ x_i y_i is injective.

nodes.title: Linearly disjoint extensions · Lemma 030M
nodes.summary: Let E/F be a normal algebraic field extension. There exist subextensions E / E_sep /F and E / E_insep / F such that • F ⊂ E_sep is Galois and E_sep ⊂ E is purely inseparable, • F ⊂ E_insep is purely inseparable and E_insep ⊂ E is Galois, • E = E_sep ⊗_F E_insep.

nodes.title: Review · Definition 030J
nodes.summary: Algebraic field extensions. • A field extension K/k is called algebraic if every element of K is algebraic over k. • An algebraic extension k'/k is called separable if every α ∈ k' is separable over k. • An algebraic extension k'/k is called purely inseparable if the characteristic of k is p > 0 and for every element α ∈ k' there exists a power q of p such that α^q ∈ k. • An algebraic extension k'/k is called normal if for every α ∈ k' the minimal polynomial P(T) ∈ k[T]…

nodes.title: Review · Lemma 031V
nodes.summary: Let K be a field of characteristic p > 0. Let L/K be a separable algebraic extension. Let α ∈ L. • If the coefficients of the minimal polynomial of α over K are pth powers in K then α is a pth power in L. • More generally, if P ∈ K[T] is a polynomial such that (a) α is a root of P, (b) P has pairwise distinct roots in an algebraic closure, and (c) all coefficients of P are pth powers, then α is a pth power in L.

nodes.title: Snake lemma · Lemma 07JW
nodes.summary: [Cartan-Eilenberg] Given a commutative diagram xymatrix & X ar[r] ar[d]^α & Y ar[r] ar[d]^β & Z ar[r] ar[d]^γ & 0 0 ar[r] & U ar[r] & V ar[r] & W of abelian groups with exact rows, there is a canonical exact sequence Ker(α) → Ker(β) → Ker(γ) → Coker(α) → Coker(β) → Coker(γ) Moreover: if X → Y is injective, then the first map is injective; if V → W is surjective, then the last map is surjective.

nodes.title: Finite modules and finitely presented modules · Definition 0518
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. • We say M is a finite R-module, or a finitely generated R-module if there exist n ∈ N and x_1, …, x_n ∈ M such that every element of M is an R-linear combination of the x_i. Equivalently, this means there exists a surjection R^⊕ n → M for some n ∈ N. • We say M is a finitely presented R-module or an R-module of finite presentation if there exist integers n, m ∈ N and an exact sequence R^⊕ m → R^⊕ n → M → 0
nodes.section: Finite modules and finitely presented modules

nodes.title: Finite modules and finitely presented modules · Lemma 07JX
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let α : R^⊕ n → M and β : N → M be module maps. If Im(α) ⊂ Im(β), then there exists an R-module map γ : R^⊕ n → N such that α = β ∘ γ.
nodes.section: Finite modules and finitely presented modules

nodes.title: Finite modules and finitely presented modules · Lemma 0519
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let 0 → M_1 → M_2 → M_3 → 0 be a short exact sequence of R-modules. • If M_1 and M_3 are finite R-modules, then M_2 is a finite R-module. • If M_1 and M_3 are finitely presented R-modules, then M_2 is a finitely presented R-module. • If M_2 is a finite R-module, then M_3 is a finite R-module. • If M_2 is a finitely presented R-module and M_1 is a finite R-module, then M_3 is a finitely presented R-module. • If M_3 is a finitely presented R-module and M_2…
nodes.section: Finite modules and finitely presented modules

nodes.title: Finite modules and finitely presented modules · Lemma 00KZ
nodes.summary: Finite modules have filtrations such that successive quotients are cyclic modules. Let R be a ring, and let M be a finite R-module. There exists a filtration by finite R-submodules 0 = M_0 ⊂ M_1 ⊂ … ⊂ M_n = M such that each quotient M_i/M_i - 1 is isomorphic to R/I_i for some ideal I_i of R.
nodes.section: Finite modules and finitely presented modules

nodes.title: Finite modules and finitely presented modules · Lemma 0560
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module. If M is finite as an R-module, then M is finite as an S-module.
nodes.section: Finite modules and finitely presented modules

nodes.title: Ring maps of finite type and of finite presentation · Definition 00F3
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. • We say R → S is of finite type, or that S is a finite type R-algebra if there exist an n ∈ N and an surjection of R-algebras R[x_1, …, x_n] → S. • We say R → S is of finite presentation if there exist integers n, m ∈ N and polynomials f_1, …, f_m ∈ R[x_1, …, x_n] and an isomorphism of R-algebras R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_m) ≅ S.
nodes.section: Ring maps of finite type and of finite presentation

nodes.title: Ring maps of finite type and of finite presentation · Lemma 00F4
nodes.summary: The notions finite type and finite presentation have the following permanence properties. • A composition of ring maps of finite type is of finite type. • A composition of ring maps of finite presentation is of finite presentation. • Given R → S' → S with R → S of finite type, then S' → S is of finite type. • Given R → S' → S, with R → S of finite presentation, and R → S' of finite type, then S' → S is of finite presentation.
nodes.section: Ring maps of finite type and of finite presentation

nodes.title: Ring maps of finite type and of finite presentation · Lemma 00R2
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map of finite presentation. For any surjection α : R[x_1, …, x_n] → S the kernel of α is a finitely generated ideal in R[x_1, …, x_n].
nodes.section: Ring maps of finite type and of finite presentation

nodes.title: Ring maps of finite type and of finite presentation · Lemma 0561
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module. Assume R → S is of finite type and M is finitely presented as an R-module. Then M is finitely presented as an S-module.
nodes.section: Ring maps of finite type and of finite presentation

nodes.title: Finite ring maps · Definition 0563
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. We say φ : R → S is finite if S is finite as an R-module.

nodes.title: Finite ring maps · Lemma 00GJ
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a finite ring map. Let M be an S-module. Then M is finite as an R-module if and only if M is finite as an S-module.

nodes.title: Finite ring maps · Lemma 00GL
nodes.summary: Suppose that R → S and S → T are finite ring maps. Then R → T is finite.

nodes.title: Finite ring maps · Lemma 0D46
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. • If φ is finite, then φ is of finite type. • If S is of finite presentation as an R-module, then φ is of finite presentation.

nodes.title: Colimits · Definition 00D4
nodes.summary: Let (I, ≤) be a preordered set. A system (M_i, μ_ij) of R-modules over I consists of a family of R-modules (M_i)_i∈ I indexed by I and a family of R-module maps (μ_ij : M_i → M_j)_i ≤ j such that for all i ≤ j ≤ k μ_ii = id_M_i μ_ik = μ_jk∘ μ_ij We say (M_i, μ_ij) is a directed system if I is a directed set.

nodes.title: Colimits · Lemma 00D5
nodes.summary: Let (M_i, μ_ij) be a system of R-modules over the preordered set I. The colimit of the system (M_i, μ_ij) is the quotient R-module (bigoplus_i∈ I M_i) /Q where Q is the R-submodule generated by all elements iota_i(x_i) - iota_j(μ_ij(x_i)) where iota_i : M_i → bigoplus_i∈ I M_i is the natural inclusion. We denote the colimit M = colim_i M_i. We denote π : bigoplus_i∈ I M_i → M the projection map and φ_i = π ∘ iota_i : M_i → M.

nodes.title: Colimits · Lemma 00D6
nodes.summary: Let (M_i, μ_ij) be a system of R-modules over the preordered set I. Assume that I is directed. The colimit of the system (M_i, μ_ij) is canonically isomorphic to the module M defined as follows: • as a set let M = (coprod_i ∈ I M_i)/sim where for m ∈ M_i and m' ∈ M_i' we have m sim m' ⇔ μ_ij(m) = μ_i'j(m') for some j ≥ i, i' • as an abelian group for m ∈ M_i and m' ∈ M_i' we define the sum of the classes of m and m' in M to be the class of μ_ij(m) + μ_i'j(m') where j ∈ I…

nodes.title: Colimits · Lemma 00D7
nodes.summary: Let (M_i, μ_ij) be a directed system. Let M = colim M_i with μ_i : M_i → M. Then, μ_i(x_i) = 0 for x_i ∈ M_i if and only if there exists j ≥ i such that μ_ij(x_i) = 0.

nodes.title: Colimits · Definition 00D9
nodes.summary: Let (M_i, μ_ij), (N_i, ν_ij) be systems of R-modules over the same preordered set I. A homomorphism of systems Φ from (M_i, μ_ij) to (N_i, ν_ij) is by definition a family of R-module homomorphisms φ_i : M_i → N_i such that φ_j ∘ μ_ij = ν_ij ∘ φ_i for all i ≤ j.

nodes.title: Colimits · Lemma 00DA
nodes.summary: Let (M_i, μ_ij), (N_i, ν_ij) be systems of R-modules over the same preordered set. A morphism of systems Φ = (φ_i) from (M_i, μ_ij) to (N_i, ν_ij) induces a unique homomorphism colim φ_i : colim M_i → colim N_i such that xymatrix M_i ar[r] ar[d]_φ_i & colim M_i ar[d]^colim φ_i N_i ar[r] & colim N_i commutes for all i ∈ I.

nodes.title: Colimits · Lemma 00DB
nodes.summary: Filtered colimits are exact. Directed colimits are exact. Let I be a directed set. Let (L_i, λ_ij), (M_i, μ_ij), and (N_i, ν_ij) be systems of R-modules over I. Let φ_i : L_i → M_i and ψ_i : M_i → N_i be morphisms of systems over I. Assume that for all i ∈ I the sequence of R-modules xymatrix L_i ar[r]^φ_i & M_i ar[r]^ψ_i & N_i is a complex with homology H_i. Then the R-modules H_i form a system over I, the sequence of R-modules xymatrix colim_i L_i ar[r]^φ & colim_i M_i…

nodes.title: Colimits · Lemma 04B0
nodes.summary: Let I be an index category satisfying the assumptions of Categories, Lemma [Tag 002X]. Then taking colimits of diagrams of abelian groups over I is exact (i.e., the analogue of Lemma [Tag 00DB] holds in this situation).

nodes.title: Localization · Definition 00CN
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring, S a subset of R. We say S is a multiplicative subset of R if 1∈ S and S is closed under multiplication, i.e., s, s' ∈ S ⇒ ss' ∈ S.

nodes.title: Localization · Definition 00CO
nodes.summary: This ring is called the localization of A with respect to S.

nodes.title: Localization · Proposition 00CP
nodes.summary: Let f : A → B be a ring map that sends every element in S to a unit of B. Then there is a unique homomorphism g : S^-1A → B such that the following diagram commutes. xymatrix A ar[rr]^f ar[dr] & & B & S^-1A ar[ur]_g

nodes.title: Localization · Lemma 00CQ
nodes.summary: The localization S^-1A is the zero ring if and only if 0∈ S.

nodes.title: Localization · Lemma 07JY
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let S ⊂ R be a multiplicative subset. The category of S^-1R-modules is equivalent to the category of R-modules N with the property that every s ∈ S acts as an automorphism on N.

nodes.title: Localization · Definition 07JZ
nodes.summary: The S^-1A-module S^-1M is called the localization of M with respect to S.

nodes.title: Localization · Lemma 07K0
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let S ⊂ R a multiplicative subset. Let M, N be R-modules. Assume all the elements of S act as automorphisms on N. Then the canonical map Hom_R(S^-1M, N) → Hom_R(M, N) induced by the localization map, is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Localization · Lemma 00CR
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let S ⊂ R be a multiplicative subset. Let M be an R-module. Then S^-1M = colim_f ∈ S M_f where the preorder on S is given by f ≥ f' ⇔ f = f'f" for some f" ∈ R in which case the map M_f' → M_f is given by m/(f')^e ↦ m(f")^e/f^e.

nodes.title: Localization · Proposition 02C6
nodes.summary: Let overlineS be the image of S in S'^-1A, then (SS')^-1A is isomorphic to overlineS^-1(S'^-1A).

nodes.title: Localization · Proposition 02C7
nodes.summary: View S'^-1M as an A-module, then S^-1(S'^-1M) is isomorphic to (SS')^-1M.

nodes.title: Localization · Proposition 00CS
nodes.summary: Localization is exact. Let Lxrightarrowu Mxrightarrowv N be an exact sequence of R-modules. Then S^-1L → S^-1M → S^-1N is also exact.

nodes.title: Localization · Lemma 02C8
nodes.summary: Localization respects quotients, i.e. if N is a submodule of M, then S^-1(M/N)≃ (S^-1M)/(S^-1N).

nodes.title: Localization · Proposition 00CT
nodes.summary: Let I be an ideal of A, S a multiplicative set of A. Then S^-1I is an ideal of S^-1A and overlineS^-1(A/I) is isomorphic to S^-1A/S^-1I, where overlineS is the image of S in A/I.

nodes.title: Localization · Lemma 00CU
nodes.summary: Any submodule N' of S^-1M is of the form S^-1N for some N⊂ M. Indeed one can take N to be the inverse image of N' in M.

nodes.title: Localization · Lemma 02C9
nodes.summary: Ideals in the localization of a ring are localizations of ideals. Each ideal I' of S^-1A takes the form S^-1I, where one can take I to be the inverse image of I' in A.

nodes.title: Internal Hom · Lemma 0582
nodes.summary: Exactness and Hom_R. Let R be a ring. Let M_1, M_2, M_3 be R-modules. Let M_1 → M_2 and M_2 → M_3 be R-module maps. • M_1 → M_2 → M_3 → 0 is exact if and only if 0 → Hom_R(M_3, N) → Hom_R(M_2, N) → Hom_R(M_1, N) is exact for all R-modules N. • 0 → M_1 → M_2 → M_3 is exact if and only if 0 → Hom_R(N, M_1) → Hom_R(N, M_2) → Hom_R(N, M_3) is exact for all R-modules N.

nodes.title: Internal Hom · Lemma 0583
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be a finitely presented R-module. Let N be an R-module. • For f ∈ R we have Hom_R(M, N)_f = Hom_R_f(M_f, N_f) = Hom_R(M_f, N_f), • for a multiplicative subset S of R we have S^-1Hom_R(M, N) = Hom_S^-1R(S^-1M, S^-1N) = Hom_R(S^-1M, S^-1N).

nodes.title: Characterizing finite and finitely presented modules · Lemma 0G8N
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let N be an R-module. The following are equivalent • N is a finite R-module, • for any filtered colimit M = colim M_i of R-modules the map colim Hom_R(N, M_i) → Hom_R(N, M) is injective.
nodes.section: Characterizing finite and finitely presented modules

nodes.title: Characterizing finite and finitely presented modules · Definition 07N8
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Let n ≥ 0 and x_i ∈ M for i = 1, …, n. A relation between x_1, …, x_n in M is a sequence of elements f_1, …, f_n ∈ R such that ∑_i = 1, …, n f_i x_i = 0.
nodes.section: Characterizing finite and finitely presented modules

nodes.title: Characterizing finite and finitely presented modules · Lemma 00HA
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring and let M be an R-module. Then M is the colimit of a directed system (M_i, μ_ij) of R-modules with all M_i finitely presented R-modules.
nodes.section: Characterizing finite and finitely presented modules

nodes.title: Characterizing finite and finitely presented modules · Lemma 0G8P
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let N be an R-module. The following are equivalent • N is a finitely presented R-module, • for any filtered colimit M = colim M_i of R-modules the map colim Hom_R(N, M_i) → Hom_R(N, M) is bijective.
nodes.section: Characterizing finite and finitely presented modules

nodes.title: Tensor products · Definition 00CW
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring, M, N, P be three R-modules. A mapping f : M × N → P (where M × N is viewed only as Cartesian product of two R-modules) is said to be R-bilinear if for each x ∈ M the mapping y↦ f(x, y) of N into P is R-linear, and for each y∈ N the mapping x↦ f(x, y) is also R-linear.

nodes.title: Tensor products · Lemma 00CX
nodes.summary: Let M, N be R-modules. Then there exists a pair (T, g) where T is an R-module, and g : M × N → T an R-bilinear mapping, with the following universal property: For any R-module P and any R-bilinear mapping f : M × N → P, there exists a unique R-linear mapping tildef : T → P such that f = tildef ∘ g. In other words, the following diagram commutes: xymatrix M × N ar[rr]^f ar[dr]_g & & P & T ar[ur]_tilde f Moreover, if (T, g) and (T', g') are two pairs with this property,…

nodes.title: Tensor products · Lemma 00CY
nodes.summary: Let M, N, P be R-modules, then the bilinear maps (x, y) & ↦ y ⊗ x (x + y, z) & ↦ x ⊗ z + y ⊗ z (r, x) & ↦ rx induce unique isomorphisms M ⊗_R N & → N ⊗_R M, (M⊕ N)⊗_R P & → (M ⊗_R P)⊕(N ⊗_R P), R ⊗_R M & → M

nodes.title: Tensor products · Lemma 00CZ
nodes.summary: Let M_1, …, M_r be R-modules. Then there exists a pair (T, g) consisting of an R-module T and an R-multilinear mapping g : M_1× … × M_r → T with the universal property: For any R-multilinear mapping f : M_1× … × M_r → P there exists a unique R-module homomorphism f' : T → P such that f'∘ g = f. Such a module T is unique up to unique isomorphism. We denote it M_1⊗_R … ⊗_R M_r and we denote the universal multilinear map (m_1, …, m_r) ↦ m_1 ⊗ … ⊗ m_r.

nodes.title: Tensor products · Lemma 00D0
nodes.summary: The homomorphisms (M ⊗_R N)⊗_R P → M ⊗_R N ⊗_R P → M ⊗_R (N ⊗_R P) such that f((x ⊗ y)⊗ z) = x ⊗ y ⊗ z and g(x ⊗ y ⊗ z) = x ⊗ (y ⊗ z), x∈ M, y∈ N, z∈ P are well-defined and are isomorphisms.

nodes.title: Tensor products · Definition 00D1
nodes.summary: An abelian group N is called an (A, B)-bimodule if it is both an A-module and a B-module and for all a ∈ A and b ∈ B the multiplication by a and b commute, so b(an) = a(bn) for all n ∈ N. In this situation we usually write the B-action on the right: so for b ∈ B and n ∈ N the result of multiplying n by b is denoted nb. With this convention the compatibility above is that (ax)b = a(xb) for all a∈ A, b∈ B, x∈ N. The shorthand _AN_B is used to denote an (A, B)-bimodule N.

nodes.title: Tensor products · Lemma 00D2
nodes.summary: For A-module M, B-module P and (A, B)-bimodule N, the modules (M ⊗_A N)⊗_B P and M ⊗_A(N ⊗_B P) can both be given (A, B)-bimodule structure, and moreover (M ⊗_A N)⊗_B P ≅ M ⊗_A(N ⊗_B P).

nodes.title: Tensor products · Lemma 00DE
nodes.summary: For any three R-modules M, N, P, Hom_R(M ⊗_R N, P) ≅ Hom_R(M, Hom_R(N, P))

nodes.title: Tensor products commute with colimits · Lemma 00DD
nodes.summary: Let (M_i, μ_ij) be a system over the preordered set I. Let N be an R-module. Then colim (M_i ⊗ N) ≅ (colim M_i)⊗ N. Moreover, the isomorphism is induced by the homomorphisms μ_i ⊗ 1: M_i ⊗ N → M ⊗ N where M = colim_i M_i with natural maps μ_i : M_i → M.

nodes.title: Tensor products · Lemma 00DF
nodes.summary: Let M_1xrightarrowf M_2xrightarrowg M_3 → 0 be an exact sequence of R-modules and homomorphisms, and let N be any R-module. Then the sequence M_1⊗ Nxrightarrowf ⊗ 1 M_2⊗ N xrightarrowg ⊗ 1 M_3⊗ N → 0 is exact. In other words, the functor - ⊗_R N is right exact, in the sense that tensoring each term in the original right exact sequence preserves the exactness.

nodes.title: Tensor products · Lemma 05BS
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M and N be R-modules. • If N and M are finite, then so is M ⊗_R N. • If N and M are finitely presented, then so is M ⊗_R N.

nodes.title: Tensor products · Lemma 00DK
nodes.summary: Let M be an R-module. Then the S^-1R-modules S^-1M and S^-1R ⊗_R M are canonically isomorphic, and the canonical isomorphism f : S^-1R ⊗_R M → S^-1M is given by f((a/s) ⊗ m) = am/s, ∀ a ∈ R, m ∈ M, s ∈ S

nodes.title: Tensor products · Lemma 00DL
nodes.summary: Let M, N be R-modules, then there is a canonical S^-1R-module isomorphism f : S^-1M ⊗_S^-1RS^-1N → S^-1(M ⊗_R N), given by f((m/s)⊗(n/t)) = (m ⊗ n)/st

nodes.title: Tensor algebra · Lemma 00DN
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. If M is a free R-module, so is each symmetric and exterior power.

nodes.title: Tensor algebra · Lemma 00DO
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M_2 → M_1 → M → 0 be an exact sequence of R-modules. There are exact sequences M_2 ⊗_R Sym^n - 1(M_1) → Sym^n(M_1) → Sym^n(M) → 0 and similarly M_2 ⊗_R wedge^n - 1(M_1) → wedge^n(M_1) → wedge^n(M) → 0

nodes.title: Tensor algebra · Lemma 00DP
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Let x_i, i ∈ I be a given system of generators of M as an R-module. Let n ≥ 2. There exists a canonical exact sequence bigoplus_1 ≤ j_1 < j_2 ≤ n bigoplus_i_1, i_2 ∈ I T^n - 2(M) ⊕ bigoplus_1 ≤ j_1 < j_2 ≤ n bigoplus_i ∈ I T^n - 2(M) → T^n(M) → wedge^n(M) → 0 where the pure tensor m_1 ⊗ … ⊗ m_n - 2 in the first summand maps to underbrace m_1 ⊗ … ⊗ x_i_1 ⊗ … ⊗ x_i_2 ⊗ … ⊗ m_n - 2 _with x_i_1 and x_i_2 occupying slots j_1 and j_2 in…

nodes.title: Tensor algebra · Lemma 0H1C
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Let M be a B-module. Let n > 1. The kernel of the A-linear map M ⊗_A … ⊗_A M → wedge^n_B(M) is generated as an A-module by the elements m_1 ⊗ … ⊗ m_n with m_i = m_j for i not = j, m_1, …, m_n ∈ M and the elements m_1 ⊗ … ⊗ bm_i ⊗ … ⊗ m_n - m_1 ⊗ … ⊗ bm_j ⊗ … ⊗ m_n for i not = j, m_1, …, m_n ∈ M, and b ∈ B.

nodes.title: Tensor algebra · Lemma 00DQ
nodes.summary: Taking tensor algebras commutes with filtered colimits. Let R be a ring. Let M_i be a directed system of R-modules. Then colim_i T(M_i) = T(colim_i M_i) and similarly for the symmetric and exterior algebras.

nodes.title: Tensor algebra · Lemma 0C6F
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring and let S ⊂ R be a multiplicative subset. Then S^-1T_R(M) = T_S^-1R(S^-1M) for any R-module M. Similar for symmetric and exterior algebras.

nodes.title: Base change · Definition 05G4
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module. Let R → R' be any ring map. The base change of φ by R → R' is the ring map R' → S ⊗_R R'. In this situation we often write S' = S ⊗_R R'. The base change of the S-module M is the S'-module M ⊗_R R'.

nodes.title: Base change · Lemma 05G5
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module. Let R → R' be a ring map and let S' = S ⊗_R R' and M' = M ⊗_R R' be the base changes. • If M is a finite S-module, then the base change M' is a finite S'-module. • If M is an S-module of finite presentation, then the base change M' is an S'-module of finite presentation. • If R → S is of finite type, then the base change R' → S' is of finite type. • If R → S is of finite presentation, then the base change R' → S' is of finite…

nodes.title: Base change · Lemma 05DQ
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. The functors Mod_S → Mod_R, N ↦ N_R (restriction) and Mod_R → Mod_S, M ↦ M ⊗_R S (base change) are adjoint functors. In a formula Hom_R(M, N_R) = Hom_S(M ⊗_R S, N)

nodes.title: Base change · Lemma 08YP
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. The functors Mod_S → Mod_R, N ↦ N_R (restriction) and Mod_R → Mod_S, M ↦ Hom_R(S, M) are adjoint functors. In a formula Hom_R(N_R, M) = Hom_S(N, Hom_R(S, M))

nodes.title: Base change · Lemma 08YQ
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Given S-modules M, N and an R-module P we have Hom_R(M ⊗_S N, P) = Hom_S(M, Hom_R(N, P))

nodes.title: Miscellany · Lemma 07K1
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring, I and J two ideals and p a prime ideal containing the product IJ. Then p contains I or J.

nodes.title: Prime avoidance · Lemma 00DS
nodes.summary: 1. In an affine scheme if a finite number of points are contained in an open subset then they are contained in a smaller principal open subset. 2. Affine opens are cofinal among the neighborhoods of a given finite set of an affine scheme Let R be a ring. Let I_i ⊂ R, i = 1, …, r, and J ⊂ R be ideals. Assume • J not⊂ I_i for i = 1, …, r, and • all but two of I_i are prime ideals. Then there exists an x ∈ J, xnot∈ I_i for all i.

nodes.title: Miscellany · Lemma 0EHL
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let x ∈ R, I ⊂ R an ideal, and p_i, i = 1, …, r be prime ideals. Suppose that x + I not ⊂ p_i for i = 1, …, r. Then there exists a y ∈ I such that x + y not ∈ p_i for all i.

nodes.title: Chinese remainder · Lemma 00DT
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. • If I_1, …, I_r are ideals such that I_a + I_b = R when a not = b, then I_1 ∩ … ∩ I_r = I_1I_2… I_r and R/(I_1I_2… I_r) ≅ R/I_1 × … × R/I_r. • If m_1, …, m_r are pairwise distinct maximal ideals then m_a + m_b = R for a not = b and the above applies.

nodes.title: Miscellany · Lemma 07DQ
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let n ≥ m. Let A be an n × m matrix with coefficients in R. Let J ⊂ R be the ideal generated by the m × m minors of A. • For any f ∈ J there exists a m × n matrix B such that BA = f 1_m × m. • If f ∈ R and BA = f 1_m × m for some m × n matrix B, then f^m ∈ J.

nodes.title: Miscellany · Lemma 080R
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let n ≥ m. Let A = (a_ij) be an n × m matrix with coefficients in R, written in block form as A = ( A_1 A_2 ) where A_1 has size m × m. Let B be the adjugate (transpose of cofactor) matrix to A_1. Then AB = ( f 1_m × m C ) where f = det(A_1) and c_ij is (up to sign) the determinant of the m × m minor of A corresponding to the rows 1, …, hat j, …, m, i.

nodes.title: Miscellany · Lemma 05WI
nodes.summary: A map of finite free modules cannot be injective if the source has rank bigger than the target. Let R be a nonzero ring. Let n ≥ 1. Let M be an R-module generated by < n elements. Then any R-module map f : R^⊕ n → M has a nonzero kernel.

nodes.title: Miscellany · Lemma 0FJ7
nodes.summary: The rank of a finite free module is well defined. Let R be a nonzero ring. Let n, m ≥ 0 be integers. If R^⊕ n is isomorphic to R^⊕ m as R-modules, then n = m.

nodes.title: Cayley-Hamilton · Lemma 00DX
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let A = (a_ij) be an n × n matrix with coefficients in R. Let P(x) ∈ R[x] be the characteristic polynomial of A (defined as det(xid_n × n - A)). Then P(A) = 0 in Mat(n × n, R).

nodes.title: Cayley-Hamilton · Lemma 05BT
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be a finite R-module. Let φ : M → M be an endomorphism. Then there exists a monic polynomial P ∈ R[T] such that P(φ) = 0 as an endomorphism of M.

nodes.title: Cayley-Hamilton · Lemma 05G7
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let M be a finite R-module. Let φ : M → M be an endomorphism such that φ(M) ⊂ IM. Then there exists a monic polynomial P = t^n + a_1 t^n - 1 + … + a_n ∈ R[T] such that a_j ∈ I^j and P(φ) = 0 as an endomorphism of M.

nodes.title: Cayley-Hamilton · Lemma 05G8
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be a finite R-module. Let φ : M → M be a surjective R-module map. Then φ is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: The spectrum of a ring · Definition 00DZ
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. • The spectrum of R is the set of prime ideals of R. It is usually denoted Spec(R). • Given a subset T ⊂ R we let V(T) ⊂ Spec(R) be the set of primes containing T, i.e., V(T) = ( p ∈ Spec(R) mid ∀ f∈ T, f∈ p). • Given an element f ∈ R we let D(f) ⊂ Spec(R) be the set of primes not containing f.

nodes.title: The spectrum of a ring · Lemma 00E0
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. • The spectrum of a ring R is empty if and only if R is the zero ring. • Every nonzero ring has a maximal ideal. • Every nonzero ring has a minimal prime ideal. • Given an ideal I ⊂ R and a prime ideal I ⊂ p there exists a prime I ⊂ q ⊂ p such that q is minimal over I. • If T ⊂ R, and if (T) is the ideal generated by T in R, then V((T)) = V(T). • If I is an ideal and sqrtI is its radical, see basic notion ([Tag 00BI]), then V(I) = V(sqrtI). • Given an…

nodes.title: The spectrum of a ring · Definition 00E1
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. The topology on Spec(R) whose closed sets are the sets V(T) is called the Zariski topology. The open subsets D(f) are called the standard opens of Spec(R).

nodes.title: The spectrum of a ring · Lemma 00E2
nodes.summary: Functoriality of the spectrum Suppose that φ : R → R' is a ring homomorphism. The induced map Spec(φ) : Spec(R') → Spec(R), p' ↦ φ^-1( p') is continuous for the Zariski topologies. In fact, for any element f ∈ R we have Spec(φ)^-1(D(f)) = D(φ(f)).

nodes.title: The spectrum of a ring · Lemma 00E3
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let S ⊂ R be a multiplicative subset. The map R → S^-1R induces via the functoriality of Spec a homeomorphism Spec(S^-1R) → ( p ∈ Spec(R) mid S ∩ p = ∅ ) where the topology on the right hand side is that induced from the Zariski topology on Spec(R). The inverse map is given by p ↦ S^-1 p = p(S^-1R).

nodes.title: The spectrum of a ring · Lemma 00E4
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let f ∈ R. The map R → R_f induces via the functoriality of Spec a homeomorphism Spec(R_f) → D(f) ⊂ Spec(R). The inverse is given by p ↦ p · R_f.

nodes.title: The spectrum of a ring · Lemma 00E5
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. The map R → R/I induces via the functoriality of Spec a homeomorphism Spec(R/I) → V(I) ⊂ Spec(R). The inverse is given by p ↦ p / I.

nodes.title: The spectrum of a ring · Lemma 00E8
nodes.summary: The spectrum of a ring is quasi-compact Let R be a ring. The space Spec(R) is quasi-compact.

nodes.title: The spectrum of a ring · Lemma 04PM
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. The topology on X = Spec(R) has the following properties: • X is quasi-compact, • X has a basis for the topology consisting of quasi-compact opens, and • the intersection of any two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact.

nodes.title: Local rings · Definition 07BI
nodes.summary: A local ring is a ring with exactly one maximal ideal. If R is a local ring, then the maximal ideal is often denoted m_R and the field R/ m_R is called the residue field of the local ring R. We often say "let (R, m) be a local ring" or "let (R, m, kappa) be a local ring" to indicate that R is local, m is its unique maximal ideal and kappa = R/ m is its residue field. A local homomorphism of local rings is a ring map φ : R → S such that R and S are local rings and such…

nodes.title: Local rings · Lemma 00E9
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. The following are equivalent: • R is a local ring, • Spec(R) has exactly one closed point, • R has a maximal ideal m and every element of R setminus m is a unit, and • R is not the zero ring and for every x ∈ R either x or 1 - x is invertible or both.

nodes.title: Local rings · Lemma 07BJ
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Assume R and S are local rings. The following are equivalent: • φ is a local ring map, • φ( m_R) ⊂ m_S, • φ^-1( m_S) = m_R, and • for any x ∈ R, if φ(x) is invertible in S, then x is invertible in R.

nodes.title: Local rings · Lemma 00E7
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Let p be a prime of R. The following are equivalent • p is in the image of Spec(S) → Spec(R), • S ⊗_R kappa( p) not = 0, • S_ p/ p S_ p not = 0, • (S/ pS)_ p not = 0, and • p = φ^-1( pS).

nodes.title: The Jacobson radical of a ring · Lemma 0AME
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring with Jacobson radical rad(R). Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. The following are equivalent • I ⊂ rad(R), and • every element of 1 + I is a unit in R. In this case every element of R which maps to a unit of R/I is a unit.
nodes.section: The Jacobson radical of a ring

nodes.title: The Jacobson radical of a ring · Lemma 0B7C
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map such that the induced map Spec(S) → Spec(R) is surjective. Then an element x ∈ R is a unit if and only if φ(x) ∈ S is a unit.
nodes.section: The Jacobson radical of a ring

nodes.title: Nakayama's lemma · Lemma 00DV
nodes.summary: [MatCA] We quote from [MatCA]: "This simple but important lemma is due to T. Nakayama, G. Azumaya and W. Krull. Priority is obscure, and although it is usually called the Lemma of Nakayama, late Prof. Nakayama did not like the name." Let R be a ring with Jacobson radical rad(R). Let M be an R-module. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. • If IM = M and M is finite, then there exists an f ∈ 1 + I such that fM = 0. • If IM = M, M is finite, and I ⊂ rad(R), then M = 0. • If N, N' ⊂ M, M =…

nodes.title: Nakayama's lemma · Lemma 0GLX
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring, let S ⊂ R be a multiplicative subset, let I ⊂ R be an ideal, and let M be a finite R-module. If x_1, …, x_r ∈ M generate S^-1(M/IM) as an S^-1(R/I)-module, then there exists an f ∈ S + I such that x_1, …, x_r generate M_f as an R_f-module.M, then x_1, …, x_r generate M_f for some f ∈ S. (II) I = p is a prime ideal and S = R setminus p. The lemma says if x_1, …, x_r generate M ⊗_R kappa( p) then x_1, …, x_r generate M_f for some f ∈ R, f not ∈ p.

nodes.title: Nakayama's lemma · Lemma 0E8M
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a local homomorphism of local rings. Assume • B is finite as an A-module, • m_B is a finitely generated ideal, • A → B induces an isomorphism on residue fields, and • m_A/ m_A^2 → m_B/ m_B^2 is surjective. Then A → B is surjective.

nodes.title: Open and closed subsets of spectra · Lemma 00EC
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let e ∈ R be an idempotent. In this case Spec(R) = D(e) amalg D(1-e).
nodes.section: Open and closed subsets of spectra

nodes.title: Open and closed subsets of spectra · Lemma 00ED
nodes.summary: Let R_1 and R_2 be rings. Let R = R_1 × R_2. The maps R → R_1, (x, y) ↦ x and R → R_2, (x, y) ↦ y induce continuous maps Spec(R_1) → Spec(R) and Spec(R_2) → Spec(R). The induced map Spec(R_1) amalg Spec(R_2) → Spec(R) is a homeomorphism. In other words, the spectrum of R = R_1× R_2 is the disjoint union of the spectrum of R_1 and the spectrum of R_2.
nodes.section: Open and closed subsets of spectra

nodes.title: Open and closed subsets of spectra · Lemma 00EE
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. For each U ⊂ Spec(R) which is open and closed there exists a unique idempotent e ∈ R such that U = D(e). This induces a 1-1 correspondence between open and closed subsets U ⊂ Spec(R) and idempotents e ∈ R.
nodes.section: Open and closed subsets of spectra

nodes.title: Open and closed subsets of spectra · Lemma 00EF
nodes.summary: Let R be a nonzero ring. Then Spec(R) is connected if and only if R has no nontrivial idempotents.
nodes.section: Open and closed subsets of spectra

nodes.title: Open and closed subsets of spectra · Lemma 00EH
nodes.summary: Let I ⊂ R be a finitely generated ideal of a ring R such that I = I^2. Then • there exists an idempotent e ∈ R such that I = (e), • R/I ≅ R_e' for the idempotent e' = 1 - e ∈ R, and • V(I) is open and closed in Spec(R).
nodes.section: Open and closed subsets of spectra

nodes.title: Connected components of spectra · Lemma 04PP
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let T ⊂ Spec(R) be a subset of the spectrum. The following are equivalent • T is closed and is a union of connected components of Spec(R), • T is an intersection of open and closed subsets of Spec(R), and • T = V(I) where I ⊂ R is an ideal generated by idempotents. Moreover, the ideal in (3) if it exists is unique.

nodes.title: Connected components of spectra · Lemma 00EG
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. A connected component of Spec(R) is of the form V(I), where I is an ideal generated by idempotents such that every idempotent of R either maps to 0 or 1 in R/I.

nodes.title: Glueing properties · Lemma 00HN
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. • For an element x of an R-module M the following are equivalent • x = 0, • x maps to zero in M_ p for all p ∈ Spec(R), • x maps to zero in M_ m for all maximal ideals m of R. In other words, the map M → ∏_ m M_ m is injective. • Given an R-module M the following are equivalent • M is zero, • M_ p is zero for all p ∈ Spec(R), • M_ m is zero for all maximal ideals m of R. • Given a complex M_1 → M_2 → M_3 of R-modules the following are equivalent • M_1 →…

nodes.title: Glueing properties · Lemma 00EO
nodes.summary: Zariski-local properties of modules and algebras Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Let S be an R-algebra. Suppose that f_1, …, f_n is a finite list of elements of R such that ⋃ D(f_i) = Spec(R), in other words (f_1, …, f_n) = R. • If each M_f_i = 0 then M = 0. • If each M_f_i is a finite R_f_i-module, then M is a finite R-module. • If each M_f_i is a finitely presented R_f_i-module, then M is a finitely presented R-module. • Let M → N be a map of R-modules. If M_f_i…

nodes.title: Glueing properties · Lemma 00EP
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Suppose that g_1, …, g_n is a finite list of elements of S such that ⋃ D(g_i) = Spec(S) in other words (g_1, …, g_n) = S. • If each S_g_i is of finite type over R, then S is of finite type over R. • If each S_g_i is of finite presentation over R, then S is of finite presentation over R.

nodes.title: Glueing functions · Lemma 00EK
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let f_1, …, f_n be elements of R generating the unit ideal. Let M be an R-module. The sequence 0 → M xrightarrowα bigoplus_i = 1^n M_f_i xrightarrowβ bigoplus_i, j = 1^n M_f_i f_j is exact, where α(m) = (m/1, …, m/1) and β(m_1/f_1^e_1, …, m_n/f_n^e_n) = (m_i/f_i^e_i - m_j/f_j^e_j)_(i, j).

nodes.title: Glueing functions · Lemma 00EJ
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring, and let f_1, f_2, … f_n∈ R generate the unit ideal in R. Then the following sequence is exact: 0 → R → bigoplus_i R_f_i → bigoplus_i, jR_f_if_j where the maps α : R → bigoplus_i R_f_i and β : bigoplus_i R_f_i → bigoplus_i, j R_f_if_j are defined as α(x) = (fracx1, …, fracx1) and β(fracx_1f_1^r_1, …, fracx_nf_n^r_n) = (fracx_if_i^r_i-fracx_jf_j^r_j in R_f_if_j).

nodes.title: Glueing functions · Lemma 00EM
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. If Spec(R) = U amalg V with both U and V open then R ≅ R_1 × R_2 with U ≅ Spec(R_1) and V ≅ Spec(R_2) via the maps in Lemma [Tag 00ED]. Moreover, both R_1 and R_2 are localizations as well as quotients of the ring R.

nodes.title: Glueing functions · Lemma 0565
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let f_1, …, f_n ∈ R. Let M be an R-module. Then M → bigoplus M_f_i is injective if and only if M → bigoplus_i = 1, …, n M, m ↦ (f_1m, …, f_nm) is injective.

nodes.title: Glueing functions · Lemma 00EQ
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let f_1, …, f_n ∈ R. Suppose we are given the following data: • For each i an R_f_i-module M_i. • For each pair i, j an R_f_if_j-module isomorphism ψ_ij : (M_i)_f_j → (M_j)_f_i. which satisfy the "cocycle condition" that all the diagrams xymatrix (M_i)_f_jf_k ar[rd]_ψ_ij ar[rr]^ψ_ik & & (M_k)_f_if_j & (M_j)_f_if_k ar[ru]_ψ_jk commute (for all triples i, j, k). Given this data define M = Ker( bigoplus_1 ≤ i ≤ n M_i → bigoplus_1 ≤ i, j ≤ n (M_i)_f_j ) where…

nodes.title: Zerodivisors and total rings of fractions · Lemma 00EU
nodes.summary: Let p be a minimal prime of a ring R. Every element of the maximal ideal of R_ p is nilpotent. If R is reduced then R_ p is a field.
nodes.section: Zerodivisors and total rings of fractions

nodes.title: Zerodivisors and total rings of fractions · Lemma 00EW
nodes.summary: Let R be a reduced ring. Then • R is a subring of a product of fields, • R → ∏_ p minimal R_ p is an embedding into a product of fields, • ⋃_ p minimal p is the set of zerodivisors of R.
nodes.section: Zerodivisors and total rings of fractions

nodes.title: Zerodivisors and total rings of fractions · Lemma 02LW
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let S ⊂ R be a multiplicative subset consisting of nonzerodivisors. Then Q(R) ≅ Q(S^-1R). In particular Q(R) ≅ Q(Q(R)).
nodes.section: Zerodivisors and total rings of fractions

nodes.title: Zerodivisors and total rings of fractions · Lemma 02LX
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Assume that R has finitely many minimal primes q_1, …, q_t, and that q_1 ∪ … ∪ q_t is the set of zerodivisors of R. Then the total ring of fractions Q(R) is equal to R_ q_1 × … × R_ q_t.
nodes.section: Zerodivisors and total rings of fractions

nodes.title: Irreducible components of spectra · Lemma 00ES
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. • For a prime p ⊂ R the closure of ( p) in the Zariski topology is V( p). In a formula overline( p) = V( p). • The irreducible closed subsets of Spec(R) are exactly the subsets V( p), with p ⊂ R a prime. • The irreducible components (see Topology, Definition [Tag 004V]) of Spec(R) are exactly the subsets V( p), with p ⊂ R a minimal prime.

nodes.title: Irreducible components of spectra · Lemma 090M
nodes.summary: The spectrum of a ring is a spectral space, see Topology, Definition [Tag 08YG].

nodes.title: Irreducible components of spectra · Lemma 00ET
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let p ⊂ R be a prime. • the set of irreducible closed subsets of Spec(R) passing through p is in one-to-one correspondence with primes q ⊂ R_ p. • The set of irreducible components of Spec(R) passing through p is in one-to-one correspondence with minimal primes q ⊂ R_ p.

nodes.title: Irreducible components of spectra · Lemma 00EV
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let p be a minimal prime of R. Let W ⊂ Spec(R) be a quasi-compact open not containing the point p. Then there exists an f ∈ R, f not ∈ p such that D(f) ∩ W = ∅.

nodes.title: Irreducible components of spectra · Lemma 04MG
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let X = Spec(R) as a topological space. The following are equivalent • X is profinite, • X is Hausdorff, • X is totally disconnected. • every quasi-compact open of X is closed, • there are no nontrivial inclusions between its prime ideals, • every prime ideal is a maximal ideal, • every prime ideal is minimal, • every standard open D(f) ⊂ X is closed, and • add more here.

nodes.title: A meta-observation about prime ideals · Lemma 05K8
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. For a principal ideal J ⊂ R, and for any ideal I ⊂ J we have I = J (I : J).

nodes.title: A meta-observation about prime ideals · Definition 05K9
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let F be a set of ideals of R. We say F is an Oka family if R ∈ F and whenever I ⊂ R is an ideal and (I : a), (I, a) ∈ F for some a ∈ R, then I ∈ F.

nodes.title: A meta-observation about prime ideals · Proposition 05KE
nodes.summary: If F is an Oka family of ideals, then any maximal element of the complement of F is prime.

nodes.title: A meta-observation about prime ideals · Lemma 05KF
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let S be a multiplicative subset of R. An ideal I ⊂ R which is maximal with respect to the property that I ∩ S = ∅ is prime.

nodes.title: A meta-observation about prime ideals · Lemma 05KG
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. • An ideal I ⊂ R maximal with respect to not being finitely generated is prime. • If every prime ideal of R is finitely generated, then every ideal of R is finitely generated.

nodes.title: A meta-observation about prime ideals · Lemma 05KH
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. • An ideal I ⊂ R maximal with respect to not being principal is prime. • If every prime ideal of R is principal, then every ideal of R is principal.

nodes.title: A meta-observation about prime ideals · Lemma 05KI
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. • An ideal maximal among the ideals which do not contain a nonzerodivisor is prime. • If R is nonzero and every nonzero prime ideal in R contains a nonzerodivisor, then R is a domain.

nodes.title: Images of ring maps of finite presentation · Lemma 00F6
nodes.summary: Let U ⊂ Spec(R) be open. The following are equivalent: • U is retrocompact in Spec(R), • U is quasi-compact, • U is a finite union of standard opens, and • there exists a finitely generated ideal I ⊂ R such that X setminus V(I) = U.
nodes.section: Images of ring maps of finite presentation

nodes.title: Images of ring maps of finite presentation · Lemma 00F7
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. The induced continuous map f : Spec(S) → Spec(R) is quasi-compact. For any constructible set E ⊂ Spec(R) the inverse image f^-1(E) is constructible in Spec(S).
nodes.section: Images of ring maps of finite presentation

nodes.title: Images of ring maps of finite presentation · Lemma 0G1P
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. A subset of Spec(R) is constructible if and only if it can be written as a finite union of subsets of the form D(f) ∩ V(g_1, …, g_m) for f, g_1, …, g_m ∈ R.
nodes.section: Images of ring maps of finite presentation

nodes.title: Images of ring maps of finite presentation · Lemma 00F8
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring and let T ⊂ Spec(R) be constructible. Then there exists a ring map R → S of finite presentation such that T is the image of Spec(S) in Spec(R).
nodes.section: Images of ring maps of finite presentation

nodes.title: Images of ring maps of finite presentation · Lemma 00F9
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let f be an element of R. Let S = R_f. Then the image of a constructible subset of Spec(S) is constructible in Spec(R).
nodes.section: Images of ring maps of finite presentation

nodes.title: Images of ring maps of finite presentation · Lemma 00FA
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I be a finitely generated ideal of R. Let S = R/I. Then the image of a constructible subset of Spec(S) is constructible in Spec(R).
nodes.section: Images of ring maps of finite presentation

nodes.title: Images of ring maps of finite presentation · Lemma 00FB
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. The map Spec(R[x]) → Spec(R) is open, and the image of any standard open is a quasi-compact open.
nodes.section: Images of ring maps of finite presentation

nodes.title: Images of ring maps of finite presentation · Lemma 00FC
nodes.summary: Let R → A be a ring homomorphism. Assume A ≅ R^⊕ n as an R-module. Let f ∈ A. The multiplication map m_f: A → A is R-linear and hence has a characteristic polynomial P(T) = T^n + r_n-1T^n-1 + … + r_0 ∈ R[T]. For any prime p ∈ Spec(R), f acts nilpotently on A ⊗_R kappa(p) if and only if p ∈ V(r_0, …, r_n-1).
nodes.section: Images of ring maps of finite presentation

nodes.title: Images of ring maps of finite presentation · Lemma 00FD
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let f, g ∈ R[x] be polynomials. Assume the leading coefficient of g is a unit of R. There exists elements r_i∈ R, i = 1…, n such that the image of D(f) ∩ V(g) in Spec(R) is ⋃_i = 1, …, n D(r_i).
nodes.section: Images of ring maps of finite presentation

nodes.title: Chevalley's Theorem · Theorem 00FE
nodes.summary: Suppose that R → S is of finite presentation. The image of a constructible subset of Spec(S) in Spec(R) is constructible.
nodes.section: Images of ring maps of finite presentation

nodes.title: More on images · Lemma 00FG
