nodes.summary: Let R ⊂ S be an inclusion of domains. Assume that R → S is of finite type. There exists a nonzero f ∈ R, and a nonzero g ∈ S such that R_f → S_fg is of finite presentation.

nodes.title: More on images · Lemma 00FH
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a finite type ring map. Denote X = Spec(R) and Y = Spec(S). Write f : Y → X the induced map of spectra. Let E ⊂ Y = Spec(S) be a constructible set. If a point xi ∈ X is in f(E), then overline(xi) ∩ f(E) contains an open dense subset of overline(xi).

nodes.title: More on images · Lemma 00FI
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. The following are equivalent: • The map Spec(S) → Spec(R) is surjective. • For any ideal I ⊂ R the inverse image of sqrtIS in R is equal to sqrtI. • For any radical ideal I ⊂ R the inverse image of IS in R is equal to I. • For every prime p of R the inverse image of p S in R is p. In this case the same is true after any base change: Given a ring map R → R' the ring map R' → R' ⊗_R S has the equivalent properties (1), (2), (3) as well.

nodes.title: More on images · Lemma 00FJ
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain. Let φ : R → S be a ring map. The following are equivalent: • The ring map R → S is injective. • The image Spec(S) → Spec(R) contains a dense set of points. • There exists a prime ideal q ⊂ S whose inverse image in R is (0).

nodes.title: More on images · Lemma 00FK
nodes.summary: Let R ⊂ S be an injective ring map. Then Spec(S) → Spec(R) hits all the minimal primes.

nodes.title: More on images · Lemma 00FL
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. The following are equivalent: • The kernel of R → S consists of nilpotent elements. • The minimal primes of R are in the image of Spec(S) → Spec(R). • The image of Spec(S) → Spec(R) is dense in Spec(R).

nodes.title: More on images · Lemma 0CAN
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. If a minimal prime p ⊂ R is in the image of Spec(S) → Spec(R), then it is the image of a minimal prime.

nodes.title: More on images · Lemma 0H7L
nodes.summary: Let A ⊂ B be an inclusion of domains inducing an algebraic extension of fraction fields. If J ⊂ B is a nonzero ideal, then A ∩ J is nonzero too. Thus the image of a proper closed subset of Spec(B) is not dense in Spec(A).

nodes.title: Noetherian rings · Lemma 00FN
nodes.summary: Noetherian property is stable by passage to finite type extension and localization. Any finitely generated ring over a Noetherian ring is Noetherian. Any localization of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian.

nodes.title: Noetherian rings · Lemma 0306
nodes.summary: If R is a Noetherian ring, then so is the formal power series ring R[[x_1, …, x_n]].

nodes.title: Noetherian rings · Lemma 00FO
nodes.summary: Any finite type algebra over a field is Noetherian. Any finite type algebra over Z is Noetherian.

nodes.title: Noetherian rings · Lemma 00FP
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. • Any finite R-module is of finite presentation. • Any submodule of a finite R-module is finite. • Any finite type R-algebra is of finite presentation over R.

nodes.title: Noetherian rings · Lemma 00FQ
nodes.summary: If R is a Noetherian ring then Spec(R) is a Noetherian topological space, see Topology, Definition [Tag 0051].

nodes.title: Noetherian rings · Lemma 00FR
nodes.summary: A Noetherian affine scheme has finitely many generic points. If R is a Noetherian ring then Spec(R) has finitely many irreducible components. In other words R has finitely many minimal primes.

nodes.title: Noetherian rings · Lemma 0CY6
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let R → R' be of finite type. If S is Noetherian, then the base change S' = R' ⊗_R S is Noetherian.

nodes.title: Noetherian rings · Lemma 045I
nodes.summary: Let k be a field and let R be a Noetherian k-algebra. If K/k is a finitely generated field extension then K ⊗_k R is Noetherian.

nodes.title: Noetherian rings · Lemma 0BX1
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring and p ⊂ R be a prime. There exists an f ∈ R, f not ∈ p such that R_f → R_ p is injective in each of the following cases • R is a domain, • R is Noetherian, or • R is reduced and has finitely many minimal primes.

nodes.title: Noetherian rings · Lemma 06RN
nodes.summary: Any surjective endomorphism of a Noetherian ring is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Locally nilpotent ideals · Definition 00IL
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. We say I is locally nilpotent if for every x ∈ I there exists an n ∈ N such that x^n = 0. We say I is nilpotent if there exists an n ∈ N such that I^n = 0.

nodes.title: Locally nilpotent ideals · Lemma 0544
nodes.summary: Let R → R' be a ring map and let I ⊂ R be a locally nilpotent ideal. Then IR' is a locally nilpotent ideal of R'.

nodes.title: Locally nilpotent ideals · Lemma 0AMG
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring and let I ⊂ R be a locally nilpotent ideal. An element x of R is a unit if and only if the image of x in R/I is a unit.

nodes.title: Locally nilpotent ideals · Lemma 00IM
nodes.summary: An ideal in a Noetherian ring is nilpotent if each element of the ideal is nilpotent. Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let I, J be ideals of R. Suppose J ⊂ sqrtI. Then J^n ⊂ I for some n. In particular, in a Noetherian ring the notions of "locally nilpotent ideal" and "nilpotent ideal" coincide.

nodes.title: Locally nilpotent ideals · Lemma 00J9
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be a locally nilpotent ideal. Then R → R/I induces a bijection on idempotents.

nodes.title: Locally nilpotent ideals · Lemma 05BU
nodes.summary: Let A be a possibly noncommutative algebra. Let e ∈ A be an element such that x = e^2 - e is nilpotent. Then there exists an idempotent of the form e' = e + x(∑ a_i, je^ix^j) ∈ A with a_i, j ∈ Z.

nodes.title: Locally nilpotent ideals · Lemma 0CAP
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be a locally nilpotent ideal. Let n ≥ 1 be an integer which is invertible in R/I. Then • the nth power map 1 + I → 1 + I, 1 + x ↦ (1 + x)^n is a bijection, • a unit of R is a nth power if and only if its image in R/I is an nth power.

nodes.title: Curiosity · Lemma 02JH
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let S ⊂ R be a multiplicative subset. Assume the image of the map Spec(S^-1R) → Spec(R) is closed. Then S^-1R ≅ R/I for some ideal I ⊂ R.

nodes.title: Curiosity · Lemma 02JI
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let S ⊂ R be a multiplicative subset. Assume the image of the map Spec(S^-1R) → Spec(R) is closed. If R is Noetherian, or Spec(R) is a Noetherian topological space, or S is finitely generated as a monoid, then R ≅ S^-1R × R' for some ring R'.

nodes.title: Hilbert Nullstellensatz · Theorem 00FV
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. • For any maximal ideal m ⊂ k[x_1, …, x_n] the field extension kappa( m)/k is finite. • Any radical ideal I ⊂ k[x_1, …, x_n] is the intersection of maximal ideals containing it. The same is true in any finite type k-algebra.

nodes.title: Hilbert Nullstellensatz · Lemma 00FY
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K be a field. If R ⊂ K and K is of finite type over R, then there exists an f ∈ R such that R_f is a field, and K/R_f is a finite field extension.

nodes.title: Jacobson rings · Definition 00G0
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. We say that R is a Jacobson ring if every radical ideal I is the intersection of the maximal ideals containing it.

nodes.title: Jacobson rings · Lemma 00G1
nodes.summary: Any algebra of finite type over a field is Jacobson.

nodes.title: Jacobson rings · Lemma 00G2
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. If every prime ideal of R is the intersection of the maximal ideals containing it, then R is Jacobson.

nodes.title: Jacobson rings · Lemma 00G3
nodes.summary: A ring R is Jacobson if and only if Spec(R) is Jacobson, see Topology, Definition [Tag 005U].

nodes.title: Jacobson rings · Lemma 034J
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. If R is not Jacobson there exist a prime p ⊂ R, an element f ∈ R such that the following hold • p is not a maximal ideal, • f not ∈ p, • V( p) ∩ D(f) = ( p), and • (R/ p)_f is a field. On the other hand, if R is Jacobson, then for any pair ( p, f) such that (1) and (2) hold the set V( p) ∩ D(f) is infinite.

nodes.title: Jacobson rings · Lemma 00G4
nodes.summary: The ring Z is a Jacobson ring. More generally, let R be a ring such that • R is a domain, • R is Noetherian, • any nonzero prime ideal is a maximal ideal, and • R has infinitely many maximal ideals. Then R is a Jacobson ring.

nodes.title: Jacobson rings · Lemma 00GA
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let m ⊂ R be a maximal ideal. Let q ⊂ S be a prime ideal lying over m such that kappa( q)/kappa( m) is an algebraic field extension. Then q is a maximal ideal of S.

nodes.title: Jacobson rings · Lemma 00FT
nodes.summary: Suppose that k is a field and suppose that V is a nonzero vector space over k. Assume the dimension of V (which is a cardinal number) is smaller than the cardinality of k. Then for any linear operator T : V → V there exists some monic polynomial P(t) ∈ k[t] such that P(T) is not invertible.

nodes.title: Jacobson rings · Theorem 00FU
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a k-algebra generated over k by the elements (x_i)_i ∈ I. Assume the cardinality of I is smaller than the cardinality of k. Then • for all maximal ideals m ⊂ S the field extension kappa( m)/k is algebraic, and • S is a Jacobson ring.

nodes.title: Jacobson rings · Lemma 046V
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a k-algebra. For any field extension K/k whose cardinality is larger than the cardinality of S we have • for every maximal ideal m of S_K the field kappa( m) is algebraic over K, and • S_K is a Jacobson ring.

nodes.title: Jacobson rings · Lemma 00G6
nodes.summary: Let R be a Jacobson ring. Let f ∈ R. The ring R_f is Jacobson and maximal ideals of R_f correspond to maximal ideals of R not containing f.

nodes.title: Jacobson rings · Lemma 00G9
nodes.summary: Let R be a Jacobson ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. The ring R/I is Jacobson and maximal ideals of R/I correspond to maximal ideals of R containing I.

nodes.title: Jacobson rings · Lemma 0CY7
nodes.summary: Let R be a Jacobson ring. Let K be a field. Let R ⊂ K and K is of finite type over R. Then R is a field and K/R is a finite field extension.

nodes.title: Jacobson rings · Proposition 00GB
nodes.summary: Let R be a Jacobson ring. Let R → S be a ring map of finite type. Then • The ring S is Jacobson. • The map Spec(S) → Spec(R) transforms closed points to closed points. • For m' ⊂ S maximal lying over m ⊂ R the field extension kappa( m')/kappa( m) is finite.

nodes.title: Jacobson rings · Lemma 00GC
nodes.summary: Any finite type algebra over Z is Jacobson.

nodes.title: Jacobson rings · Lemma 00GD
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a finite type ring map of Jacobson rings. Denote X = Spec(R) and Y = Spec(S). Write f : Y → X the induced map of spectra. Let E ⊂ Y = Spec(S) be a constructible set. Denote with a subscript _0 the set of closed points of a topological space. • We have f(E)_0 = f(E_0) = X_0 ∩ f(E). • A point xi ∈ X is in f(E) if and only if overline(xi) ∩ f(E_0) is dense in overline(xi).

nodes.title: Jacobson rings · Lemma 00GE
nodes.summary: With notation as above. Assume that R is a Noetherian Jacobson ring. Further assume R → S is of finite type. There is a commutative diagram xymatrix Constr(Y) ar[r]^E ↦ E_0 ar[d]^E ↦ f(E) & Constr(Y_0) ar[d]^E ↦ f(E) Constr(X) ar[r]^E ↦ E_0 & Constr(X_0) where the horizontal arrows are the bijections from Topology, Lemma [Tag 005Y].

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Definition 00GI
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. • An element s ∈ S is integral over R if there exists a monic polynomial P(x) ∈ R[x] such that P^φ(s) = 0, where P^φ(x) ∈ S[x] is the image of P under φ : R[x] → S[x]. • The ring map φ is integral if every s ∈ S is integral over R.

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Lemma 052I
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Let y ∈ S. If there exists a finite R-submodule M of S such that 1 ∈ M and yM ⊂ M, then y is integral over R.

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Lemma 00GK
nodes.summary: A finite ring map is integral.

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Lemma 00GM
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Let s_1, …, s_n be a finite set of elements of S. In this case s_i is integral over R for all i = 1, …, n if and only if there exists an R-subalgebra S' ⊂ S finite over R containing all of the s_i.

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Lemma 02JJ
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. The following are equivalent • R → S is finite, • R → S is integral and of finite type, and • there exist x_1, …, x_n ∈ S which generate S as an algebra over R such that each x_i is integral over R.

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Lemma 00GN
nodes.summary: A composition of integral ring maps is integral Suppose that R → S and S → T are integral ring maps. Then R → T is integral.

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Lemma 00GO
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring homomorphism. The set S' = (s ∈ S mid s is integral over R) is an R-subalgebra of S.

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Lemma 0CY8
nodes.summary: Let R_i→ S_i be ring maps i = 1, …, n. Let R and S denote the product of the R_i and S_i respectively. Then an element s = (s_1, …, s_n) ∈ S is integral over R if and only if each s_i is integral over R_i.

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Definition 00GP
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. The ring S' ⊂ S of elements integral over R, see Lemma [Tag 00GO], is called the integral closure of R in S. If R ⊂ S we say that R is integrally closed in S if R = S'.

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Lemma 0CY9
nodes.summary: Let R_i→ S_i be ring maps i = 1, …, n. Denote the integral closure of R_i in S_i by S'_i. Further let R and S denote the product of the R_i and S_i respectively. Then the integral closure of R in S is the product of the S'_i. In particular R → S is integrally closed if and only if each R_i → S_i is integrally closed.

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Lemma 0307
nodes.summary: Integral closure commutes with localization: If A → B is a ring map, and S ⊂ A is a multiplicative subset, then the integral closure of S^-1A in S^-1B is S^-1B', where B' ⊂ B is the integral closure of A in B.

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Lemma 034K
nodes.summary: An element of an algebra over a ring is integral over the ring if and only if it is locally integral at every prime ideal of the ring. Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Let x ∈ S. The following are equivalent: • x is integral over R, and • for every prime ideal p ⊂ R the element x ∈ S_ p is integral over R_ p.

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Lemma 02JK
nodes.summary: Integrality and finiteness are preserved under base change. Let R → S and R → R' be ring maps. Set S' = R' ⊗_R S. • If R → S is integral so is R' → S'. • If R → S is finite so is R' → S'.

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Lemma 02JL
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let f_1, …, f_n ∈ R generate the unit ideal. • If each R_f_i → S_f_i is integral, so is R → S. • If each R_f_i → S_f_i is finite, so is R → S.

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Lemma 02JM
nodes.summary: Let A → B → C be ring maps. • If A → C is integral so is B → C. • If A → C is finite so is B → C.

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Lemma 0308
nodes.summary: Let A → B → C be ring maps. Let B' be the integral closure of A in B, let C' be the integral closure of B' in C. Then C' is the integral closure of A in C.

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Lemma 00GQ
nodes.summary: Suppose that R → S is an integral ring extension with R ⊂ S. Then φ : Spec(S) → Spec(R) is surjective.

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Lemma 00GR
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K be a field. If R ⊂ K and K is integral over R, then R is a field and K is an algebraic extension. If R ⊂ K and K is finite over R, then R is a field and K is a finite algebraic extension.

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Lemma 00GS
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a k-algebra over k. • If S is a domain and finite dimensional over k, then S is a field. • If S is integral over k and a domain, then S is a field. • If S is integral over k then every prime of S is a maximal ideal (see Lemma [Tag 04MG] for more consequences).

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Lemma 00GT
nodes.summary: Suppose R → S is integral. Let q, q' ∈ Spec(S) be distinct primes having the same image in Spec(R). Then neither q ⊂ q' nor q' ⊂ q.

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Lemma 05DR
nodes.summary: Suppose R → S is finite. Then the fibres of Spec(S) → Spec(R) are finite.

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Lemma 00GU
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map such that S is integral over R. Let p ⊂ p' ⊂ R be primes. Let q be a prime of S mapping to p. Then there exists a prime q' with q ⊂ q' mapping to p'.

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Lemma 0564
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a finite and finitely presented ring map. Let M be an S-module. Then M is finitely presented as an R-module if and only if M is finitely presented as an S-module.

nodes.title: Finite and integral ring extensions · Lemma 052J
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let x, y ∈ R be nonzerodivisors. Let R[x/y] ⊂ R_xy be the R-subalgebra generated by x/y, and similarly for the subalgebras R[y/x] and R[x/y, y/x]. If R is integrally closed in R_x or R_y, then the sequence 0 → R xrightarrow(-1, 1) R[x/y] ⊕ R[y/x] xrightarrow(1, 1) R[x/y, y/x] → 0 is a short exact sequence of R-modules.

nodes.title: Normal rings · Definition 0309
nodes.summary: A domain R is called normal if it is integrally closed in its field of fractions.

nodes.title: Normal rings · Lemma 034L
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. If S is a normal domain, then the integral closure of R in S is a normal domain.

nodes.title: Normal rings · Definition 00GW
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain. • An element g of the fraction field of R is called almost integral over R if there exists an element r ∈ R, rnot = 0 such that rg^n ∈ R for all n ≥ 0. • The domain R is called completely normal if every almost integral element of the fraction field of R is contained in R.

nodes.title: Normal rings · Lemma 00GX
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain with fraction field K. If u, v ∈ K are almost integral over R, then so are u + v and uv. Any element g ∈ K which is integral over R is almost integral over R. If R is Noetherian then the converse holds as well.

nodes.title: Normal rings · Lemma 00GY
nodes.summary: Any localization of a normal domain is normal.

nodes.title: Normal rings · Lemma 00GZ
nodes.summary: A principal ideal domain is normal.

nodes.title: Normal rings · Lemma 00H0
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain with fraction field K. Suppose f = ∑ α_i x^i is an element of K[x]. • If f is integral over R[x] then all α_i are integral over R, and • If f is almost integral over R[x] then all α_i are almost integral over R.

nodes.title: Normal rings · Lemma 030A
nodes.summary: Let R be a normal domain. Then R[x] is a normal domain.

nodes.title: Normal rings · Lemma 0BI0
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian normal domain. Then R[[x]] is a Noetherian normal domain.

nodes.title: Normal rings · Lemma 030B
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain. The following are equivalent: • The domain R is a normal domain, • for every prime p ⊂ R the local ring R_ p is a normal domain, and • for every maximal ideal m the ring R_ m is a normal domain.

nodes.title: Normal rings · Definition 00GV
nodes.summary: A ring R is called normal if for every prime p ⊂ R the localization R_ p is a normal domain (see Definition [Tag 0309]).

nodes.title: Normal rings · Lemma 034M
nodes.summary: A normal ring is integrally closed in its total ring of fractions.

nodes.title: Normal rings · Lemma 037C
nodes.summary: A localization of a normal ring is a normal ring.

nodes.title: Normal rings · Lemma 00H1
nodes.summary: Let R be a normal ring. Then R[x] is a normal ring.

nodes.title: Normal rings · Lemma 0CYA
nodes.summary: A finite product of normal rings is normal.

nodes.title: Normal rings · Lemma 030C
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Assume R is reduced and has finitely many minimal primes. Then the following are equivalent: • R is a normal ring, • R is integrally closed in its total ring of fractions, and • R is a finite product of normal domains.

nodes.title: Normal rings · Lemma 037D
nodes.summary: Let (R_i, φ_ii') be a directed system (Categories, Definition [Tag 00D4]) of rings. If each R_i is a normal ring so is R = colim_i R_i.

nodes.title: Going down for integral over normal · Definition 00H2
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. We say an element g ∈ S is integral over I if there exists a monic polynomial P = x^d + ∑_j < d a_j x^j with coefficients a_j ∈ I^d-j such that P^φ(g) = 0 in S.
nodes.section: Going down for integral over normal

nodes.title: Going down for integral over normal · Lemma 00H3
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let A = ∑ I^nt^n ⊂ R[t] be the subring of the polynomial ring generated by R ⊕ It ⊂ R[t]. An element s ∈ S is integral over I if and only if the element st ∈ S[t] is integral over A.
nodes.section: Going down for integral over normal

nodes.title: Going down for integral over normal · Lemma 00H4
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. The set of elements of S which are integral over I form a R-submodule of S. Furthermore, if s ∈ S is integral over R, and s' is integral over I, then ss' is integral over I.
nodes.section: Going down for integral over normal

nodes.title: Going down for integral over normal · Lemma 00H5
nodes.summary: Suppose φ : R → S is integral. Suppose I ⊂ R is an ideal. Then every element of IS is integral over I.
nodes.section: Going down for integral over normal

nodes.title: Going down for integral over normal · Lemma 00H6
nodes.summary: Let K be a field. Let n, m ∈ N and a_0, …, a_n - 1, b_0, …, b_m - 1 ∈ K. If the polynomial x^n + a_n - 1x^n - 1 + … + a_0 divides the polynomial x^m + b_m - 1 x^m - 1 + … + b_0 in K[x] then • a_0, …, a_n - 1 are integral over any subring R_0 of K containing the elements b_0, …, b_m - 1, and • each a_i lies in sqrt(b_0, …, b_m-1)R for any subring R ⊂ K containing the elements a_0, …, a_n - 1, b_0, …, b_m - 1.
nodes.section: Going down for integral over normal

nodes.title: Going down for integral over normal · Lemma 00H7
nodes.summary: Let R ⊂ S be an inclusion of domains. Assume R is normal. Let g ∈ S be integral over R. Then the minimal polynomial of g has coefficients in R.
nodes.section: Going down for integral over normal

nodes.title: Going down for integral over normal · Proposition 00H8
nodes.summary: Let R ⊂ S be an inclusion of domains. Assume R is normal and S integral over R. Let p ⊂ p' ⊂ R be primes. Let q' be a prime of S with p' = R ∩ q'. Then there exists a prime q with q ⊂ q' such that p = R ∩ q. In other words: the going down property holds for R → S, see Definition [Tag 00HV].
nodes.section: Going down for integral over normal

nodes.title: Flat modules and flat ring maps · Definition 00HB
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. • An R-module M is called flat if whenever N_1 → N_2 → N_3 is an exact sequence of R-modules the sequence M ⊗_R N_1 → M ⊗_R N_2 → M ⊗_R N_3 is exact as well. • An R-module M is called faithfully flat if the complex of R-modules N_1 → N_2 → N_3 is exact if and only if the sequence M ⊗_R N_1 → M ⊗_R N_2 → M ⊗_R N_3 is exact. • A ring map R → S is called flat if S is flat as an R-module. • A ring map R → S is called faithfully flat if S is faithfully flat as…
nodes.section: Flat modules and flat ring maps

nodes.title: Flat modules and flat ring maps · Lemma 0BBY
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I, J ⊂ R be ideals. Let M be a flat R-module. Then IM ∩ JM = (I ∩ J)M.
nodes.section: Flat modules and flat ring maps

nodes.title: Flat modules and flat ring maps · Lemma 05UT
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let (M_i, φ_ii') be a directed system of flat R-modules. Then colim_i M_i is a flat R-module.
nodes.section: Flat modules and flat ring maps

nodes.title: Flat modules and flat ring maps · Lemma 00HC
nodes.summary: A composition of (faithfully) flat ring maps is (faithfully) flat. If R → R' is (faithfully) flat, and M' is a (faithfully) flat R'-module, then M' is a (faithfully) flat R-module.
nodes.section: Flat modules and flat ring maps

nodes.title: Flat modules and flat ring maps · Lemma 00HD
nodes.summary: Let M be an R-module. The following are equivalent: • M is flat over R. • for every injection of R-modules N ⊂ N' the map N ⊗_R M → N'⊗_R M is injective. • for every ideal I ⊂ R the map I ⊗_R M → R ⊗_R M = M is injective. • for every finitely generated ideal I ⊂ R the map I ⊗_R M → R ⊗_R M = M is injective.
nodes.section: Flat modules and flat ring maps

nodes.title: Flat modules and flat ring maps · Lemma 05UU
nodes.summary: Let (R_i, φ_ii') be a system of rings over the directed set I. Let R = colim_i R_i. • If M is an R-module such that M is flat as an R_i-module for all i, then M is flat as an R-module. • For i ∈ I let M_i be a flat R_i-module and for i' ≥ i let f_ii' : M_i → M_i' be a φ_ii'-linear map such that f_i' i" ∘ f_i i' = f_i i". Then M = colim_i ∈ I M_i is a flat R-module.
nodes.section: Flat modules and flat ring maps

nodes.title: Flat modules and flat ring maps · Lemma 00HI
nodes.summary: Suppose that M is (faithfully) flat over R, and that R → R' is a ring map. Then M ⊗_R R' is (faithfully) flat over R'.
nodes.section: Flat modules and flat ring maps

nodes.title: Flat modules and flat ring maps · Lemma 00HJ
nodes.summary: Let R → R' be a faithfully flat ring map. Let M be a module over R, and set M' = R' ⊗_R M. Then M is flat over R if and only if M' is flat over R'.
nodes.section: Flat modules and flat ring maps

nodes.title: Flat modules and flat ring maps · Lemma 0584
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let S → S' be a flat map of R-algebras. Let M be a module over S, and set M' = S' ⊗_S M. • If M is flat over R, then M' is flat over R. • If S → S' is faithfully flat, then M is flat over R if and only if M' is flat over R.
nodes.section: Flat modules and flat ring maps

nodes.title: Flat modules and flat ring maps · Lemma 039V
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module. If M is flat as an R-module and faithfully flat as an S-module, then R → S is flat.
nodes.section: Flat modules and flat ring maps

nodes.title: Equational criterion of flatness · Lemma 00HK
nodes.summary: A module M over R is flat if and only if every relation in M is trivial.
nodes.section: Flat modules and flat ring maps

nodes.title: Flat modules and flat ring maps · Lemma 00HL
nodes.summary: Suppose that R is a ring, 0 → M" → M' → M → 0 a short exact sequence, and N an R-module. If M is flat then N ⊗_R M" → N ⊗_R M' is injective, i.e., the sequence 0 → N ⊗_R M" → N ⊗_R M' → N ⊗_R M → 0 is a short exact sequence.
nodes.section: Flat modules and flat ring maps

nodes.title: Flat modules and flat ring maps · Lemma 00HM
nodes.summary: Suppose that 0 → M' → M → M" → 0 is a short exact sequence of R-modules. If M' and M" are flat so is M. If M and M" are flat so is M'.
nodes.section: Flat modules and flat ring maps

nodes.title: Flat modules and flat ring maps · Lemma 00HO
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. The following are equivalent • M is faithfully flat, and • M is flat and for all R-module homomorphisms α : N → N' we have α = 0 if and only if α ⊗ id_M = 0.
nodes.section: Flat modules and flat ring maps

nodes.title: Flat modules and flat ring maps · Lemma 00HP
nodes.summary: A flat module is faithfully flat if and only if it has nonzero fibers. Let M be a flat R-module. The following are equivalent: • M is faithfully flat, • for every nonzero R-module N, then tensor product M ⊗_R N is nonzero, • for all p ∈ Spec(R) the tensor product M ⊗_R kappa( p) is nonzero, and • for all maximal ideals m of R the tensor product M ⊗_R kappa( m) = M/ mM is nonzero.
nodes.section: Flat modules and flat ring maps

nodes.title: Flat modules and flat ring maps · Lemma 00HQ
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a flat ring map. The following are equivalent: • R → S is faithfully flat, • the induced map on Spec is surjective, and • any closed point x ∈ Spec(R) is in the image of the map Spec(S) → Spec(R).
nodes.section: Flat modules and flat ring maps

nodes.title: Flat modules and flat ring maps · Lemma 00HR
nodes.summary: A flat local ring homomorphism of local rings is faithfully flat.
nodes.section: Flat modules and flat ring maps

nodes.title: Flat modules and flat ring maps · Lemma 00HT
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let S ⊂ R be a multiplicative subset. • The localization S^-1R is a flat R-algebra. • If M is an S^-1R-module, then M is a flat R-module if and only if M is a flat S^-1R-module. • Suppose M is an R-module. Then M is a flat R-module if and only if M_ p is a flat R_ p-module for all primes p of R. • Suppose M is an R-module. Then M is a flat R-module if and only if M_ m is a flat R_ m-module for all maximal ideals m of R. • Suppose R → A is a ring map, M is…
nodes.section: Flat modules and flat ring maps

nodes.title: Flat modules and flat ring maps · Lemma 00HS
nodes.summary: Let R → S be flat. Let p ⊂ p' be primes of R. Let q' ⊂ S be a prime of S mapping to p'. Then there exists a prime q ⊂ q' mapping to p.
nodes.section: Flat modules and flat ring maps

nodes.title: Flat modules and flat ring maps · Lemma 090N
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let (S_i, φ_ii') be a directed system of faithfully flat R-algebras. Then S = colim_i S_i is a faithfully flat R-algebra.
nodes.section: Flat modules and flat ring maps

nodes.title: Supports and annihilators · Definition 00L1
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring and let M be an R-module. The support of M is the set Supp(M) = ( p ∈ Spec(R) mid M_ p not = 0 )

nodes.title: Supports and annihilators · Lemma 0585
nodes.summary: A module over a ring has empty support if and only if it is the trivial module. Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Then M = (0) ⇔ Supp(M) = ∅.

nodes.title: Supports and annihilators · Definition 07T7
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. • Given an element m ∈ M the annihilator of m is the ideal Ann_R(m) = Ann(m) = (f ∈ R mid fm = 0). • The annihilator of M is the ideal Ann_R(M) = Ann(M) = (f ∈ R mid fm = 0 ∀ m ∈ M).

nodes.title: Supports and annihilators · Lemma 07T8
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a flat ring map. Let M be an R-module and m ∈ M. Then Ann_R(m) S = Ann_S(m ⊗ 1). If M is a finite R-module, then Ann_R(M) S = Ann_S(M ⊗_R S).

nodes.title: Supports and annihilators · Lemma 00L2
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring and let M be an R-module. If M is finite, then Supp(M) is closed. More precisely, if I = Ann(M) is the annihilator of M, then V(I) = Supp(M).

nodes.title: Supports and annihilators · Lemma 0BUR
nodes.summary: Let R → R' be a ring map and let M be a finite R-module. Then Supp(M ⊗_R R') is the inverse image of Supp(M).

nodes.title: Supports and annihilators · Lemma 07Z5
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring, let M be an R-module, and let m ∈ M. Then p ∈ V(Ann(m)) if and only if m does not map to zero in M_ p.

nodes.title: Supports and annihilators · Lemma 051B
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring and let M be an R-module. If M is a finitely presented R-module, then Supp(M) is a closed subset of Spec(R) whose complement is quasi-compact.

nodes.title: Supports and annihilators · Lemma 00L3
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring and let M be an R-module. • If M is finite then the support of M/IM is Supp(M) ∩ V(I). • If N ⊂ M, then Supp(N) ⊂ Supp(M). • If Q is a quotient module of M then Supp(Q) ⊂ Supp(M). • If 0 → N → M → Q → 0 is a short exact sequence then Supp(M) = Supp(Q) ∪ Supp(N).

nodes.title: Going up and going down · Definition 00HV
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. • We say a φ : R → S satisfies going up if given primes p ⊂ p' in R and a prime q in S lying over p there exists a prime q' of S such that (a) q ⊂ q', and (b) q' lies over p'. • We say a φ : R → S satisfies going down if given primes p ⊂ p' in R and a prime q' in S lying over p' there exists a prime q of S such that (a) q ⊂ q', and (b) q lies over p.

nodes.title: Going up and going down · Lemma 0407
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. If the induced map φ : Spec(S) → Spec(R) is open, then R → S satisfies going down.

nodes.title: Going up and going down · Lemma 00HW
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. • R → S satisfies going down if and only if generalizations lift along the map Spec(S) → Spec(R), see Topology, Definition [Tag 0063]. • R → S satisfies going up if and only if specializations lift along the map Spec(S) → Spec(R), see Topology, Definition [Tag 0063].

nodes.title: Going up and going down · Lemma 00HX
nodes.summary: Suppose R → S and S → T are ring maps satisfying going down. Then so does R → T. Similarly for going up.

nodes.title: Going up and going down · Lemma 00HY
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let T ⊂ Spec(R) be the image of Spec(S). If T is stable under specialization, then T is closed.

nodes.title: Going up and going down · Lemma 00HZ
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. The following are equivalent: • Going up holds for R → S, and • the map Spec(S) → Spec(R) is closed.

nodes.title: Going up and going down · Lemma 00I0
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let E ⊂ Spec(R) be a constructible subset. • If E is stable under specialization, then E is closed. • If E is stable under generalization, then E is open.

nodes.title: Going up and going down · Proposition 00I1
nodes.summary: Let R → S be flat and of finite presentation. Then Spec(S) → Spec(R) is open. More generally this holds for any ring map R → S of finite presentation which satisfies going down.

nodes.title: Going up and going down · Lemma 037F
nodes.summary: Let k be a field, and let R, S be k-algebras. Let S' ⊂ S be a sub k-algebra, and let f ∈ S' ⊗_k R. In the commutative diagram xymatrix Spec((S ⊗_k R)_f) ar[rd] ar[rr] & & Spec((S' ⊗_k R)_f) ar[ld] & Spec(R) & the images of the diagonal arrows are the same.

nodes.title: Going up and going down · Lemma 037G
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let R and S be k-algebras. The map Spec(S ⊗_k R) → Spec(R) is open.

nodes.title: Going up and going down · Lemma 00EA
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let p ⊂ R be a prime. Assume that • there exists a unique prime q ⊂ S lying over p, and • either • going up holds for R → S, or • going down holds for R → S and there is at most one prime of S above every prime of R. Then S_ p = S_ q.

nodes.title: Going up and going down · Lemma 080T
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let N be a finite S-module flat over R. Endow Supp(N) ⊂ Spec(S) with the induced topology. Then generalizations lift along Supp(N) → Spec(R).

nodes.title: Separable extensions · Definition 030O
nodes.summary: Let K/k be a field extension. • We say K is separably generated over k if there exists a transcendence basis (x_i; i ∈ I) of K/k such that the extension K/k(x_i; i ∈ I) is a separable algebraic extension. • We say K is separable over k if for every subextension k ⊂ K' ⊂ K with K' finitely generated over k, the extension K'/k is separably generated.

nodes.title: Separable extensions · Lemma 030P
nodes.summary: Let K/k be a separable field extension. For any subextension K/K'/k the field extension K'/k is separable.

nodes.title: Separable extensions · Lemma 030Q
nodes.summary: Let K/k be a separably generated, and finitely generated field extension. Set r = trdeg_k(K). Then there exist elements x_1, …, x_r + 1 of K such that • x_1, …, x_r is a transcendence basis of K over k, • K = k(x_1, …, x_r + 1), and • x_r + 1 is separable over k(x_1, …, x_r).

nodes.title: Separable extensions · Lemma 04KM
nodes.summary: Let K/k be a finitely generated field extension. There exists a diagram xymatrix K ar[r] & K' k ar[u] ar[r] & k' ar[u] where k'/k, K'/K are finite purely inseparable field extensions such that K'/k' is a separably generated field extension.

nodes.title: Geometrically reduced algebras · Definition 030S
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a k-algebra. We say S is geometrically reduced over k if for every field extension K/k the K-algebra K ⊗_k S is reduced.

nodes.title: Geometrically reduced algebras · Lemma 030T
nodes.summary: Elementary properties of geometrically reduced algebras. Let k be a field. Let S be a k-algebra. • If S is geometrically reduced over k so is every k-subalgebra. • If all finitely generated k-subalgebras of S are geometrically reduced, then S is geometrically reduced. • A directed colimit of geometrically reduced k-algebras is geometrically reduced. • If S is geometrically reduced over k, then any localization of S is geometrically reduced over k.

nodes.title: Geometrically reduced algebras · Lemma 04KN
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. If R is geometrically reduced over k, and S ⊂ R is a multiplicative subset, then the localization S^-1R is geometrically reduced over k. If R is geometrically reduced over k, then R[x] is geometrically reduced over k.

nodes.title: Geometrically reduced algebras · Lemma 00I3
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let R, S be k-algebras. • If R ⊗_k S is nonreduced, then there exist finitely generated subalgebras R' ⊂ R, S' ⊂ S such that R' ⊗_k S' is not reduced. • If R ⊗_k S contains a nonzero zerodivisor, then there exist finitely generated subalgebras R' ⊂ R, S' ⊂ S such that R' ⊗_k S' contains a nonzero zerodivisor. • If R ⊗_k S contains a nontrivial idempotent, then there exist finitely generated subalgebras R' ⊂ R, S' ⊂ S such that R' ⊗_k S' contains a…

nodes.title: Geometrically reduced algebras · Lemma 034N
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a geometrically reduced k-algebra. Let R be any reduced k-algebra. Then R ⊗_k S is reduced.

nodes.title: Geometrically reduced algebras · Lemma 030U
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a reduced k-algebra. Let K/k be either a separable field extension, or a separably generated field extension. Then K ⊗_k S is reduced.

nodes.title: Geometrically reduced algebras · Lemma 07K2
nodes.summary: Let k be a field and let S be a k-algebra. Assume that S is reduced and that S_ p is geometrically reduced for every minimal prime p of S. Then S is geometrically reduced.

nodes.title: Geometrically reduced algebras · Lemma 0C2X
nodes.summary: Let k'/k be a separable algebraic extension. Then there exists a multiplicative subset S ⊂ k' ⊗_k k' such that the multiplication map k' ⊗_k k' → k' is identified with k' ⊗_k k' → S^-1(k' ⊗_k k').

nodes.title: Geometrically reduced algebras · Lemma 0C2Y
nodes.summary: Let k'/k be a separable algebraic field extension. Let A be an algebra over k'. Then A is geometrically reduced over k if and only if it is geometrically reduced over k'.

nodes.title: Separable extensions, continued · Lemma 0H71
nodes.summary: Let k be a field of characteristic p > 1. Let K/k be a field extension generated by x_1, …, x_n + 1 ∈ K such that • (x_1, …, x_n) is a transcendence base of K/k, • for every k-linearly independent subset (a_1, …, a_m) of K the set (a^p_1, …, a_m^p) is k-linearly independent. Then there is 1 ≤ j ≤ n+1 such that ( x_1, …, widehatx_j, …, x_n+1) is a separating transcendence base for K / k.

nodes.title: Separable extensions, continued · Lemma 030W
nodes.summary: Let k be a field of characteristic p > 0. Let K/k be a field extension. The following are equivalent: • K is separable over k, • for every k-linearly independent subset (a_1, …, a_m) of K the set (a^p_1, …, a_m^p) is k-linearly independent, • the ring K ⊗_k k^1/p is reduced, and • K is geometrically reduced over k.

nodes.title: Separable extensions, continued · Lemma 030X
nodes.summary: A separably generated field extension is separable.

nodes.title: Separable extensions, continued · Lemma 030V
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a k-algebra. The following are equivalent: • k' ⊗_k S is reduced for every finite purely inseparable extension k' of k, • k^1/p ⊗_k S is reduced, • k^perf ⊗_k S is reduced, where k^perf is the perfect closure of k, • overlinek ⊗_k S is reduced, where overlinek is the algebraic closure of k, and • S is geometrically reduced over k.

nodes.title: Perfect fields · Definition 030Y
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. We say k is perfect if every field extension of k is separable over k.

nodes.title: Perfect fields · Lemma 030Z
nodes.summary: A field k is perfect if and only if it is a field of characteristic 0 or a field of characteristic p > 0 such that every element has a pth root.

nodes.title: Perfect fields · Lemma 030R
nodes.summary: Let K/k be a finitely generated field extension. There exists a diagram xymatrix K ar[r] & K' k ar[u] ar[r] & k' ar[u] where k'/k, K'/K are finite purely inseparable field extensions such that K'/k' is a separable field extension. In this situation we can assume that K' = k'K is the compositum, and also that K' = (k' ⊗_k K)_red.

nodes.title: Perfect fields · Lemma 046W
nodes.summary: Every field has a unique perfect closure. For every field k there exists a purely inseparable extension k'/k such that k' is perfect. The field extension k'/k is unique up to unique isomorphism.

nodes.title: Perfect fields · Definition 046X
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. The field extension k'/k of Lemma [Tag 046W] is called the perfect closure of k. Notation k^perf/k.

nodes.title: Perfect fields · Lemma 00I4
nodes.summary: Let k be a perfect field. Any reduced k algebra is geometrically reduced over k. Let R, S be k-algebras. Assume both R and S are reduced. Then the k-algebra R ⊗_k S is reduced.

nodes.title: Universal homeomorphisms · Lemma 0BR6
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a surjective map with locally nilpotent kernel. Then φ induces a homeomorphism of spectra and isomorphisms on residue fields. For any ring map R → R' the ring map R' → R' ⊗_R S is surjective with locally nilpotent kernel.

nodes.title: Universal homeomorphisms · Lemma 0BR7
nodes.summary: [Alper-adequate] Let k'/k be a field extension. The following are equivalent • for each x ∈ k' there exists an n > 0 such that x^n ∈ k, and • k' = k or k and k' have characteristic p > 0 and either k'/k is a purely inseparable extension or k and k' are algebraic extensions of F_p.

nodes.title: Universal homeomorphisms · Lemma 0BR8
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. If • for any x ∈ S there exists n > 0 such that x^n is in the image of φ, and • Ker(φ) is locally nilpotent, then φ induces a homeomorphism on spectra and induces residue field extensions satisfying the equivalent conditions of Lemma [Tag 0BR7].

nodes.title: Universal homeomorphisms · Lemma 0EUH
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Assume • [(a)] S is generated as an R-algebra by elements x such that x^2, x^3 ∈ φ(R), and • [(b)] Ker(φ) is locally nilpotent, Then φ induces isomorphisms on residue fields and a homeomorphism of spectra. For any ring map R → R' the ring map R' → R' ⊗_R S also satisfies (a) and (b).

nodes.title: Universal homeomorphisms · Lemma 0545
nodes.summary: Let p be a prime number. Let n, m > 0 be two integers. There exists an integer a such that (x + y)^p^a, p^a(x + y) ∈ Z[x^p^n, p^nx, y^p^m, p^my].

nodes.title: Universal homeomorphisms · Lemma 0BR9
nodes.summary: Let k'/k be a field extension. Let p be a prime number. The following are equivalent • k' is generated as a field extension of k by elements x such that there exists an n > 0 with x^p^n ∈ k and p^nx ∈ k, and • k = k' or the characteristic of k and k' is p and k'/k is purely inseparable.

nodes.title: Universal homeomorphisms · Lemma 0BRA
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Let p be a prime number. Assume • [(a)] S is generated as an R-algebra by elements x such that there exists an n > 0 with x^p^n ∈ φ(R) and p^nx ∈ φ(R), and • [(b)] Ker(φ) is locally nilpotent, Then φ induces a homeomorphism of spectra and induces residue field extensions satisfying the equivalent conditions of Lemma [Tag 0BR9]. For any ring map R → R' the ring map R' → R' ⊗_R S also satisfies (a) and (b).

nodes.title: Universal homeomorphisms · Lemma 0BRB
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Assume • φ induces an injective map of spectra, • φ induces purely inseparable residue field extensions. Then for any ring map R → R' properties (1) and (2) are true for R' → R' ⊗_R S.

nodes.title: Universal homeomorphisms · Lemma 0BRC
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Assume • φ is integral, • φ induces an injective map of spectra, • φ induces purely inseparable residue field extensions. Then φ induces a homeomorphism from Spec(S) onto a closed subset of Spec(R) and for any ring map R → R' properties (1), (2), (3) are true for R' → R' ⊗_R S.

nodes.title: Universal homeomorphisms · Lemma 0BRD
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Assume • φ is integral, • φ induces an bijective map of spectra, • φ induces purely inseparable residue field extensions. Then φ induces a homeomorphism on spectra and for any ring map R → R' properties (1), (2), (3) are true for R' → R' ⊗_R S.

nodes.title: Universal homeomorphisms · Lemma 09EF
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map such that • the kernel of φ is locally nilpotent, and • S is generated as an R-algebra by elements x such that there exist n > 0 and a polynomial P(T) ∈ R[T] whose image in S[T] is (T - x)^n. Then Spec(S) → Spec(R) is a homeomorphism and R → S induces purely inseparable extensions of residue fields. Moreover, conditions (1) and (2) remain true on arbitrary base change.

nodes.title: Geometrically irreducible algebras · Lemma 00I6
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Assume • [(a)] Spec(R) is irreducible, • [(b)] R → S is flat, • [(c)] R → S is of finite presentation, • [(d)] the fibre rings S ⊗_R kappa( p) have irreducible spectra for a dense collection of primes p of R. Then Spec(S) is irreducible. This is true more generally with (b) + (c) replaced by "the map Spec(S) → Spec(R) is open".

nodes.title: Geometrically irreducible algebras · Lemma 00I7
nodes.summary: Let k be a separably closed field. Let R, S be k-algebras. If R, S have a unique minimal prime, so does R ⊗_k S.

nodes.title: Geometrically irreducible algebras · Lemma 037K
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let R be a k-algebra. The following are equivalent • for every field extension k'/k the spectrum of R ⊗_k k' is irreducible, • for every finite separable field extension k'/k the spectrum of R ⊗_k k' is irreducible, • the spectrum of R ⊗_k overlinek is irreducible where overlinek is the separable algebraic closure of k, and • the spectrum of R ⊗_k overlinek is irreducible where overlinek is the algebraic closure of k.

nodes.title: Geometrically irreducible algebras · Definition 037L
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a k-algebra. We say S is geometrically irreducible over k if for every field extension k'/k the spectrum of S ⊗_k k' is irreducible.

nodes.title: Geometrically irreducible algebras · Lemma 037M
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let R be a k-algebra. If k is separably algebraically closed then R is geometrically irreducible over k if and only if the spectrum of R is irreducible.

nodes.title: Geometrically irreducible algebras · Lemma 037N
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a k-algebra. • If S is geometrically irreducible over k so is every k-subalgebra. • If all finitely generated k-subalgebras of S are geometrically irreducible, then S is geometrically irreducible. • A directed colimit of geometrically irreducible k-algebras is geometrically irreducible.

nodes.title: Geometrically irreducible algebras · Lemma 037O
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a geometrically irreducible k-algebra. Let R be any k-algebra. The map Spec(R ⊗_k S) → Spec(R) induces a bijection on irreducible components.

nodes.title: Geometrically irreducible algebras · Lemma 037P
nodes.summary: Let K/k be a field extension. If k is algebraically closed in K, then K is geometrically irreducible over k.

nodes.title: Geometrically irreducible algebras · Lemma 0G30
nodes.summary: Let K/k be a geometrically irreducible field extension. Let S be a geometrically irreducible K-algebra. Then S is geometrically irreducible over k.

nodes.title: Geometrically irreducible algebras · Lemma 0G31
nodes.summary: Let K/k be a field extension. The following are equivalent • K is geometrically irreducible over k, and • the induced extension K(t)/k(t) of purely transcendental extensions is geometrically irreducible.

nodes.title: Geometrically irreducible algebras · Lemma 0G32
nodes.summary: Let K/L/M be a tower of fields with L/M geometrically irreducible. Let x ∈ K be transcendental over L. Then L(x)/M(x) is geometrically irreducible.

nodes.title: Geometrically irreducible algebras · Lemma 0G33
nodes.summary: Let K/k be a field extension. The following are equivalent • K/k is geometrically irreducible, and • every element α ∈ K separably algebraic over k is in k.

nodes.title: Geometrically irreducible algebras · Lemma 037Q
nodes.summary: Let K/k be a field extension. Consider the subextension K/k'/k consisting of elements separably algebraic over k. Then K is geometrically irreducible over k'. If K/k is a finitely generated field extension, then [k' : k] < ∞.

nodes.title: Geometrically irreducible algebras · Lemma 04KP
nodes.summary: Let K/k be an extension of fields. Let overlinek/k be a separable algebraic closure. Then Gal(overlinek/k) acts transitively on the primes of overlinek ⊗_k K.

nodes.title: Geometrically connected algebras · Lemma 037R
nodes.summary: Let k be a separably algebraically closed field. Let R, S be k-algebras. If Spec(R), and Spec(S) are connected, then so is Spec(R ⊗_k S).

nodes.title: Geometrically connected algebras · Lemma 037S
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let R be a k-algebra. The following are equivalent • for every field extension k'/k the spectrum of R ⊗_k k' is connected, and • for every finite separable field extension k'/k the spectrum of R ⊗_k k' is connected.

nodes.title: Geometrically connected algebras · Definition 037T
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a k-algebra. We say S is geometrically connected over k if for every field extension k'/k the spectrum of S ⊗_k k' is connected.

nodes.title: Geometrically connected algebras · Lemma 037U
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let R be a k-algebra. If k is separably algebraically closed then R is geometrically connected over k if and only if the spectrum of R is connected.

nodes.title: Geometrically connected algebras · Lemma 037V
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a k-algebra. • If S is geometrically connected over k so is every k-subalgebra. • If all finitely generated k-subalgebras of S are geometrically connected, then S is geometrically connected. • A directed colimit of geometrically connected k-algebras is geometrically connected.

nodes.title: Geometrically connected algebras · Lemma 037W
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a geometrically connected k-algebra. Let R be any k-algebra. The map R → R ⊗_k S induces a bijection on idempotents, and the map Spec(R ⊗_k S) → Spec(R) induces a bijection on connected components.

nodes.title: Geometrically integral algebras · Definition 05DX
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a k-algebra. We say S is geometrically integral over k if for every field extension k'/k the ring of S ⊗_k k' is a domain.

nodes.title: Geometrically integral algebras · Lemma 05DY
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a k-algebra. In this case S is geometrically integral over k if and only if S is geometrically irreducible as well as geometrically reduced over k.

nodes.title: Geometrically integral algebras · Lemma 0FWF
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a k-algebra. The following are equivalent • S is geometrically integral over k, • for every finite extension k'/k of fields the ring S ⊗_k k' is a domain, • S ⊗_k overlinek is a domain where overlinek is the algebraic closure of k.

nodes.title: Geometrically integral algebras · Lemma 09P9
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a geometrically integral k-algebra. Let R be a k-algebra and an integral domain. Then R ⊗_k S is an integral domain.

nodes.title: Valuation rings · Definition 00I9
nodes.summary: Valuation rings. • Let K be a field. Let A, B be local rings contained in K. We say that B dominates A if A ⊂ B and m_A = A ∩ m_B. • Let A be a ring. We say A is a valuation ring if A is a local domain and if A is maximal for the relation of domination among local rings contained in the fraction field of A. • Let A be a valuation ring with fraction field K. If R ⊂ K is a subring of K, then we say A is centered on R if R ⊂ A.

nodes.title: Valuation rings · Lemma 00IA
nodes.summary: Let K be a field. Let A ⊂ K be a local subring. Then there exists a valuation ring with fraction field K dominating A.

nodes.title: Valuation rings · Lemma 00IC
nodes.summary: Let A be a valuation ring. Then A is a normal domain.

nodes.title: Valuation rings · Lemma 00IB
nodes.summary: Let A be a valuation ring with maximal ideal m and fraction field K. Let x ∈ K. Then either x ∈ A or x^-1 ∈ A or both.

nodes.title: Valuation rings · Lemma 052K
nodes.summary: Let A ⊂ K be a subring of a field K such that for all x ∈ K either x ∈ A or x^-1 ∈ A or both. Then A is a valuation ring with fraction field K.

nodes.title: Valuation rings · Lemma 0AS4
nodes.summary: Valuation rings are stable under filtered direct limits Let I be a directed set. Let (A_i, φ_ij) be a system of valuation rings over I. Then A = colim A_i is a valuation ring.

nodes.title: Valuation rings · Lemma 052L
nodes.summary: Let L/K be an extension of fields. If B ⊂ L is a valuation ring, then A = K ∩ B is a valuation ring.

nodes.title: Valuation rings · Lemma 0AAV
nodes.summary: Let L/K be an algebraic extension of fields. If B ⊂ L is a valuation ring with fraction field L and not a field, then A = K ∩ B is a valuation ring and not a field.

nodes.title: Valuation rings · Lemma 088Y
nodes.summary: Let A be a valuation ring. For any prime ideal p ⊂ A the quotient A/ p is a valuation ring. The same is true for the localization A_ p and in fact any localization of A.

nodes.title: Valuation rings · Lemma 088Z
nodes.summary: Let A' be a valuation ring with residue field K. Let A be a valuation ring with fraction field K. Then C = (λ ∈ A' mid λ bmod m_A' ∈ A) is a valuation ring.

nodes.title: Valuation rings · Lemma 090P
nodes.summary: Let A be a normal domain with fraction field K. • For every x ∈ K, x not ∈ A there exists a valuation ring A ⊂ V ⊂ K with fraction field K such that x not ∈ V. • If A is local, we can moreover choose V which dominates A. In other words, A is the intersection of all valuation rings in K containing A and if A is local, then A is the intersection of all valuation rings in K dominating A.

nodes.title: Valuation rings · Lemma 00ID
nodes.summary: Let A be a valuation ring with field of fractions K. Set Γ = K^*/A^* (with group law written additively). For γ, γ' ∈ Γ define γ ≥ γ' if and only if γ - γ' is in the image of A - (0) → Γ. Then (Γ, ≥) is a totally ordered abelian group.

nodes.title: Valuation rings · Definition 00IE
nodes.summary: Let A be a valuation ring. • The totally ordered abelian group (Γ, ≥) of Lemma [Tag 00ID] is called the value group of the valuation ring A. • The map v : A - (0) → Γ and also v : K^* → Γ is called the valuation associated to A. • The valuation ring A is called a discrete valuation ring if Γ ≅ Z.

nodes.title: Valuation rings · Lemma 00IF
nodes.summary: Let A be a valuation ring. The valuation v : A -(0) → Γ_≥ 0 has the following properties: • v(a) = 0 ⇔ a ∈ A^*, • v(ab) = v(a) + v(b), • v(a + b) ≥ min(v(a), v(b)) provided a + b not = 0.

nodes.title: Valuation rings · Lemma 090Q
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. The following are equivalent • A is a valuation ring, • A is a local domain and every finitely generated ideal of A is principal.

nodes.title: Valuation rings · Lemma 00IG
nodes.summary: Let (Γ, ≥) be a totally ordered abelian group. Let K be a field. Let v : K^* → Γ be a homomorphism of abelian groups such that v(a + b) ≥ min(v(a), v(b)) for a, b ∈ K with a, b, a + b not zero. Then A = ( x ∈ K mid x = 0 or v(x) ≥ 0 ) is a valuation ring with value group Im(v) ⊂ Γ, with maximal ideal m = ( x ∈ K mid x = 0 or v(x) > 0 ) and with group of units A^* = ( x ∈ K^* mid v(x) = 0 ).

nodes.title: Valuation rings · Lemma 00IH
nodes.summary: Let A be a valuation ring. Ideals in A correspond 1 - 1 with ideals of Γ. This bijection is inclusion preserving, and maps prime ideals to prime ideals.

nodes.title: Valuation rings · Lemma 00II
nodes.summary: A valuation ring is Noetherian if and only if it is a discrete valuation ring or a field.

nodes.title: More Noetherian rings · Lemma 00IK
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Any finite R-module is of finite presentation. Any submodule of a finite R-module is finite. The ascending chain condition holds for R-submodules of a finite R-module.

nodes.title: Artin-Rees · Lemma 00IN
nodes.summary: Suppose that R is Noetherian, I ⊂ R an ideal. Let N ⊂ M be finite R-modules. There exists a constant c > 0 such that I^n M ∩ N = I^n-c(I^cM ∩ N) for all n ≥ c.

nodes.title: More Noetherian rings · Lemma 00IO
nodes.summary: Suppose that 0 → K → M xrightarrowf N is an exact sequence of finitely generated modules over a Noetherian ring R. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Then there exists a c such that f^-1(I^nN) = K + I^n-cf^-1(I^cN) and f(M) ∩ I^nN ⊂ f(I^n - cM) for all n ≥ c.

nodes.title: Krull's intersection theorem · Lemma 00IP
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring. Let I ⊂ R be a proper ideal. Let M be a finite R-module. Then ⋂_n ≥ 0 I^nM = 0.

nodes.title: More Noetherian rings · Lemma 00IQ
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let M be a finite R-module. Let N = ⋂_n I^n M. • For every prime p, I ⊂ p there exists a f ∈ R, f not ∈ p such that N_f = 0. • If I is contained in the Jacobson radical of R, then N = 0.

nodes.title: Artin-Tate · Lemma 00IS
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let S be a finitely generated R-algebra. If T ⊂ S is an R-subalgebra such that S is finitely generated as a T-module, then T is of finite type over R.

nodes.title: Length · Definition 02LY
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. For any R-module M we define the length of M over R by the formula length_R(M) = sup ( n mid ∃ 0 = M_0 ⊂ M_1 ⊂ … ⊂ M_n = M, M_i not = M_i + 1 ).

nodes.title: Length · Lemma 02LZ
nodes.summary: Modules of finite length are finite. Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. If length_R(M) < ∞ then M is a finite R-module.

nodes.title: Length · Lemma 00IV
nodes.summary: Length is additive in short exact sequences. If 0 → M' → M → M" → 0 is a short exact sequence of modules over R then the length of M is the sum of the lengths of M' and M".

nodes.title: Length · Lemma 00IW
nodes.summary: Let R be a local ring with maximal ideal m. If M is an R-module and m^n M not = 0 for all n ≥ 0, then length_R(M) = ∞. In other words, if M has finite length then m^nM = 0 for some n.

nodes.title: Length · Lemma 00IX
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module. We always have length_R(M) ≥ length_S(M). If R → S is surjective then equality holds.

nodes.title: Length · Lemma 00IY
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring with maximal ideal m. Suppose that M is an R-module with m M = 0. Then the length of M as an R-module agrees with the dimension of M as a R/ m vector space. The length is finite if and only if M is a finite R-module.

nodes.title: Length · Lemma 00IZ
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Let S ⊂ R be a multiplicative subset. Then length_R(M) ≥ length_S^-1R(S^-1M).

nodes.title: Length · Lemma 00J0
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring with finitely generated maximal ideal m. (For example R Noetherian.) Suppose that M is a finite R-module with m^n M = 0 for some n. Then length_R(M) < ∞.

nodes.title: Length · Definition 00J1
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. We say M is simple if M not = 0 and every submodule of M is either equal to M or to 0.

nodes.title: Length · Lemma 00J2
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. The following are equivalent: • M is simple, • length_R(M) = 1, and • M ≅ R/ m for some maximal ideal m ⊂ R.

nodes.title: Length · Lemma 00J3
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be a finite length R-module. Choose any maximal chain of submodules 0 = M_0 ⊂ M_1 ⊂ M_2 ⊂ … ⊂ M_n = M with M_i not = M_i-1, i = 1, …, n. Then • n = length_R(M), • each M_i/M_i-1 is simple, • each M_i/M_i-1 is of the form R/ m_i for some maximal ideal m_i, • given a maximal ideal m ⊂ R we have \# (i mid m_i = m) = length_R_ m (M_ m).

nodes.title: Length · Lemma 02M0
nodes.summary: Let A be a local ring with maximal ideal m. Let B be a semi-local ring with maximal ideals m_i, i = 1, …, n. Suppose that A → B is a homomorphism such that each m_i lies over m and such that [kappa( m_i) : kappa( m)] < ∞. Let M be a B-module of finite length. Then length_A(M) = ∑_i = 1, …, n [kappa( m_i) : kappa( m)] length_B_ m_i(M_ m_i), in particular length_A(M) < ∞.

nodes.title: Length · Lemma 02M1
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a flat local homomorphism of local rings. Then for any A-module M we have length_A(M) length_B(B/ m_AB) = length_B(M ⊗_A B). In particular, if length_B(B/ m_AB) < ∞ then M has finite length if and only if M ⊗_A B has finite length.

nodes.title: Length · Lemma 02M2
nodes.summary: Let A → B → C be flat local homomorphisms of local rings. Then length_B(B/ m_A B) length_C(C/ m_B C) = length_C(C/ m_A C)

nodes.title: Artinian rings · Definition 00J5
nodes.summary: A ring R is Artinian if it satisfies the descending chain condition for ideals.

nodes.title: Artinian rings · Lemma 00J6
nodes.summary: Suppose R is a finite dimensional algebra over a field. Then R is Artinian.

nodes.title: Artinian rings · Lemma 00J7
nodes.summary: If R is Artinian then R has only finitely many maximal ideals.

nodes.title: Artinian rings · Lemma 00J8
nodes.summary: Let R be Artinian. The Jacobson radical of R is a nilpotent ideal.

nodes.title: Artinian rings · Lemma 00JA
nodes.summary: Any ring with finitely many maximal ideals and locally nilpotent Jacobson radical is the product of its localizations at its maximal ideals. Also, all primes are maximal.

nodes.title: Artinian rings · Lemma 00JB
nodes.summary: A ring R is Artinian if and only if it has finite length as a module over itself. Any such ring R is both Artinian and Noetherian, any prime ideal of R is a maximal ideal, and R is equal to the (finite) product of its localizations at its maximal ideals.

nodes.title: Homomorphisms essentially of finite type · Definition 00QM
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. • We say that R → S is essentially of finite type if S is the localization of an R-algebra of finite type. • We say that R → S is essentially of finite presentation if S is the localization of an R-algebra of finite presentation.

nodes.title: Homomorphisms essentially of finite type · Lemma 07DS
nodes.summary: The class of ring maps which are essentially of finite type is preserved under composition. Similarly for essentially of finite presentation.

nodes.title: Homomorphisms essentially of finite type · Lemma 0AUF
nodes.summary: The class of ring maps which are essentially of finite type is preserved by base change. Similarly for essentially of finite presentation.

nodes.title: Homomorphisms essentially of finite type · Lemma 07DT
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Assume S is an Artinian local ring with maximal ideal m. Then • R → S is finite if and only if R → S/ m is finite, • R → S is of finite type if and only if R → S/ m is of finite type. • R → S is essentially of finite type if and only if the composition R → S/ m is essentially of finite type.

nodes.title: Homomorphisms essentially of finite type · Lemma 0AUG
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be essentially of finite type with R and S local (but not necessarily φ local). Then there exists an n and a maximal ideal m ⊂ R[x_1, …, x_n] lying over m_R such that S is a localization of a quotient of R[x_1, …, x_n]_ m.

nodes.title: K-groups · Lemma 00JD
nodes.summary: If R is an Artinian local ring then the length function defines a natural abelian group homomorphism length_R : K'_0(R) → Z.

nodes.title: K-groups · Lemma 00JI
nodes.summary: Let R be an Artinian local ring. The map length_R : K'_0(R) → Z of Lemma [Tag 00JD] is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: K-groups · Lemma 00JJ
nodes.summary: Let (R, m) be a local ring. Every finite projective R-module is finite free. The map rank_R : K_0(R) → Z defined by [M] → rank_R(M) is well defined and an isomorphism.

nodes.title: K-groups · Lemma 00JK
nodes.summary: Let R be a local Artinian ring. There is a commutative diagram xymatrix K_0(R) ar[rr] ar[d]_rank_R & & K'_0(R) ar[d]^length_R Z ar[rr]^length_R(R) & & Z where the vertical maps are isomorphisms by Lemmas [Tag 00JI] and [Tag 00JJ].

nodes.title: Graded rings · Lemma 0EKB
nodes.summary: Let S be a graded ring. Let M be a graded S-module. • If S_+M = M and M is finite, then M = 0. • If N, N' ⊂ M are graded submodules, M = N + S_+N', and N' is finite, then M = N. • If N → M is a map of graded modules, N/S_+N → M/S_+M is surjective, and M is finite, then N → M is surjective. • If x_1, …, x_n ∈ M are homogeneous and generate M/S_+M and M is finite, then x_1, …, x_n generate M.

nodes.title: Graded rings · Lemma 0EGH
nodes.summary: Let S be a graded ring, which is finitely generated over S_0. Then for all sufficiently divisible d the algebra S^(d) is generated in degree 1 over S_0.

nodes.title: Graded rings · Lemma 077G
nodes.summary: [Huneke-Swanson] Let R → S be a homomorphism of graded rings. Let S' ⊂ S be the integral closure of R in S. Then S' = bigoplus_d ≥ 0 S' ∩ S_d, i.e., S' is a graded R-subalgebra of S.

nodes.title: Proj of a graded ring · Definition 00JN
nodes.summary: Let S be a graded ring. We define Proj(S) to be the set of homogeneous prime ideals p of S such that S_+ not ⊂ p. The set Proj(S) is a subset of Spec(S) and we endow it with the induced topology. The topological space Proj(S) is called the homogeneous spectrum of the graded ring S.

nodes.title: Proj of a graded ring · Lemma 00JO
nodes.summary: Let S be a Z-graded ring containing a homogeneous invertible element of positive degree. Then the set G ⊂ Spec(S) of Z-graded primes of S (with induced topology) maps homeomorphically to Spec(S_0).

nodes.title: Topology on Proj · Lemma 00JP
nodes.summary: Let S = ⊕_d ≥ 0 S_d be a graded ring. • The sets D_+(f) are open in Proj(S). • We have D_+(ff') = D_+(f) ∩ D_+(f'). • Let g = g_0 + … + g_m be an element of S with g_i ∈ S_i. Then D(g) ∩ Proj(S) = (D(g_0) ∩ Proj(S)) ∪ ⋃_i ≥ 1 D_+(g_i). • Let g_0∈ S_0 be a homogeneous element of degree 0. Then D(g_0) ∩ Proj(S) = ⋃_f ∈ S_d, d≥ 1 D_+(g_0 f). • The open sets D_+(f) form a basis for the topology of Proj(S). • Let f ∈ S be homogeneous of positive degree. The ring S_f has a…

nodes.title: Proj of a graded ring · Lemma 00JR
nodes.summary: Let S be a graded ring. Let M be a graded S-module. Let p be an element of Proj(S). Let f ∈ S be a homogeneous element of positive degree such that f not ∈ p, i.e., p ∈ D_+(f). Let p' ⊂ S_(f) be the element of Spec(S_(f)) corresponding to p as in Lemma [Tag 00JP]. Then S_( p) = (S_(f))_ p' and compatibly M_( p) = (M_(f))_ p'.

nodes.title: Proj of a graded ring · Lemma 00JS
nodes.summary: Suppose S is a graded ring, p_i, i = 1, …, r homogeneous prime ideals and I ⊂ S_+ a graded ideal. Assume I not⊂ p_i for all i. Then there exists a homogeneous element x∈ I of positive degree such that xnot∈ p_i for all i.

nodes.title: Proj of a graded ring · Lemma 00JT
nodes.summary: Let S be a graded ring. Let p ⊂ S be a prime. Let q be the homogeneous ideal of S generated by the homogeneous elements of p. Then q is a prime ideal of S.

nodes.title: Proj of a graded ring · Lemma 00JU
nodes.summary: Let S be a graded ring. • Any minimal prime of S is a homogeneous ideal of S. • Given a homogeneous ideal I ⊂ S any minimal prime over I is homogeneous.

nodes.title: Proj of a graded ring · Lemma 07Z2
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let S be a graded R-algebra. Let f ∈ S_+ be homogeneous. Assume that S is of finite type over R. Then • the ring S_(f) is of finite type over R, and • for any finite graded S-module M the module M_(f) is a finite S_(f)-module.

nodes.title: Proj of a graded ring · Lemma 052N
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let R' be a finite type R-algebra, and let M be a finite R'-module. There exists a graded R-algebra S, a graded S-module N and an element f ∈ S homogeneous of degree 1 such that • R' ≅ S_(f) and M ≅ N_(f) (as modules), • S_0 = R and S is generated by finitely many elements of degree 1 over R, and • N is a finite S-module.

nodes.title: Noetherian graded rings · Lemma 07Z4
nodes.summary: Let S be a graded ring. A set of homogeneous elements f_i ∈ S_+ generates S as an algebra over S_0 if and only if they generate S_+ as an ideal of S.

nodes.title: Noetherian graded rings · Lemma 00JW
nodes.summary: A graded ring S is Noetherian if and only if S_0 is Noetherian and S_+ is finitely generated as an ideal of S.

nodes.title: Noetherian graded rings · Definition 00JX
nodes.summary: Let A be an abelian group. We say that a function f : n ↦ f(n) ∈ A defined for all sufficient large integers n is a numerical polynomial if there exists r ≥ 0, elements a_0, …, a_r∈ A such that f(n) = ∑_i = 0^r binomni a_i for all n gg 0.

nodes.title: Noetherian graded rings · Lemma 00JY
nodes.summary: If A → A' is a homomorphism of abelian groups and if f : n ↦ f(n) ∈ A is a numerical polynomial, then so is the composition.

nodes.title: Noetherian graded rings · Lemma 00JZ
nodes.summary: Suppose that f: n ↦ f(n) ∈ A is defined for all n sufficiently large and suppose that n ↦ f(n) - f(n-1) is a numerical polynomial. Then f is a numerical polynomial.

nodes.title: Noetherian graded rings · Lemma 00K0
nodes.summary: If M is a finitely generated graded S-module, and if S is finitely generated over S_0, then each M_n is a finite S_0-module.

nodes.title: Noetherian graded rings · Proposition 00K1
nodes.summary: Suppose that S is a Noetherian graded ring and M a finite graded S-module. Consider the function Z → K'_0(S_0), n ↦ [M_n] see Lemma [Tag 00K0]. If S_+ is generated by elements of degree 1, then this function is a numerical polynomial.

nodes.title: Noetherian graded rings · Lemma 00K3
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Suppose that I ⊂ k[X_1, …, X_d] is a nonzero graded ideal. Let M = k[X_1, …, X_d]/I. Then the numerical polynomial n ↦ dim_k(M_n) (see Example [Tag 00K2]) has degree < d - 1 (or is zero if d = 1).

nodes.title: Noetherian local rings · Definition 07DU
nodes.summary: Let (R, m) be a local Noetherian ring. An ideal I ⊂ R such that sqrtI = m is called an ideal of definition of R.

nodes.title: Noetherian local rings · Lemma 00K5
nodes.summary: Suppose that M' ⊂ M are finite R-modules with finite length quotient. Then there exists a constants c_1, c_2 such that for all n ≥ c_2 we have c_1 + chi_I, M'(n - c_2) ≤ chi_I, M(n) ≤ c_1 + chi_I, M'(n)

nodes.title: Noetherian local rings · Lemma 00K6
nodes.summary: Suppose that 0 → M' → M → M" → 0 is a short exact sequence of finite R-modules. Then there exists a submodule N ⊂ M' with finite colength l and c ≥ 0 such that chi_I, M(n) = chi_I, M"(n) + chi_I, N(n - c) + l and φ_I, M(n) = φ_I, M"(n) + φ_I, N(n - c) for all n ≥ c.

nodes.title: Noetherian local rings · Lemma 00K7
nodes.summary: Suppose that I, I' are two ideals of definition for the Noetherian local ring R. Let M be a finite R-module. There exists a constant a such that chi_I, M(n) ≤ chi_I', M(an) for n ≥ 1.

nodes.title: Noetherian local rings · Proposition 00K8
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring. Let M be a finite R-module. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal of definition. The Hilbert function φ_I, M and the function chi_I, M are numerical polynomials.

nodes.title: Noetherian local rings · Definition 09CA
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring. Let M be a finite R-module. The Hilbert polynomial of M over R is the element P(t) ∈ Q[t] such that P(n) = φ_M(n) for n gg 0.

nodes.title: Noetherian local rings · Lemma 00K9
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring. Let M be a finite R-module. • The degree of the numerical polynomial φ_I, M is independent of the ideal of definition I. • The degree of the numerical polynomial chi_I, M is independent of the ideal of definition I.

nodes.title: Noetherian local rings · Definition 00KA
nodes.summary: Let R be a local Noetherian ring and M a finite R-module. We denote d(M) the element of (-∞, 0, 1, 2, … ) defined as follows: • If M = 0 we set d(M) = -∞, • if M not = 0 then d(M) is the degree of the numerical polynomial chi_M.

nodes.title: Noetherian local rings · Lemma 00KB
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal of definition. Let M be a finite R-module which does not have finite length. If M' ⊂ M is a submodule with finite colength, then chi_I, M - chi_I, M' is a polynomial of degree < degree of either polynomial.

nodes.title: Noetherian local rings · Lemma 00KC
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal of definition. Let 0 → M' → M → M" → 0 be a short exact sequence of finite R-modules. Then • if M' does not have finite length, then chi_I, M - chi_I, M" - chi_I, M' is a numerical polynomial of degree < the degree of chi_I, M', • max( deg(chi_I, M'), deg(chi_I, M") ) = deg(chi_I, M), and • max(d(M'), d(M")) = d(M),

nodes.title: Dimension · Definition 0GIE
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. A chain of prime ideals is a sequence p_0 ⊂ p_1 ⊂ … ⊂ p_n of prime ideals of R such that p_i not = p_i + 1 for i = 0, …, n - 1. The length of this chain of prime ideals is n.

nodes.title: Dimension · Definition 00KE
nodes.summary: The Krull dimension of the ring R is the Krull dimension of the topological space Spec(R), see Topology, Definition [Tag 0055]. In other words it is the supremum of the integers n≥ 0 such that R has a chain of prime ideals p_0 ⊂ p_1 ⊂ … ⊂ p_n, p_i not = p_i + 1. of length n.

nodes.title: Dimension · Definition 00KF
nodes.summary: The height of a prime ideal p of a ring R is the dimension of the local ring R_ p.

nodes.title: Dimension · Lemma 00KG
nodes.summary: The Krull dimension of R is the supremum of the heights of its (maximal) primes.

nodes.title: Dimension · Lemma 00KH
nodes.summary: A Noetherian ring of dimension 0 is Artinian. Conversely, any Artinian ring is Noetherian of dimension zero.

nodes.title: Dimension · Lemma 00KI
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring. Then dim(R) = 0 ⇔ d(R) = 0.

nodes.title: Dimension · Proposition 00KJ
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. The following are equivalent: • R is Artinian, • R is Noetherian and dim(R) = 0, • R has finite length as a module over itself, • R is a finite product of Artinian local rings, • R is Noetherian and Spec(R) is a finite discrete topological space, • R is a finite product of Noetherian local rings of dimension 0, • R is a finite product of Noetherian local rings R_i with d(R_i) = 0, • R is a finite product of Noetherian local rings R_i whose maximal ideals…

nodes.title: Dimension · Lemma 00KK
nodes.summary: Let R be a local Noetherian ring. The following are equivalent: • dim(R) = 1, • d(R) = 1, • there exists an x ∈ m, x not nilpotent such that V(x) = ( m), • there exists an x ∈ m, x not nilpotent such that m = sqrt(x), and • there exists an ideal of definition generated by 1 element, and no ideal of definition is generated by 0 elements.

nodes.title: Dimension · Proposition 00KQ
nodes.summary: Let R be a local Noetherian ring. Let d ≥ 0 be an integer. The following are equivalent: • dim(R) = d, • d(R) = d, • there exists an ideal of definition generated by d elements, and no ideal of definition is generated by fewer than d elements.

nodes.title: Dimension · Definition 00KU
nodes.summary: Let (R, m) be a Noetherian local ring of dimension d. • A system of parameters of R is a sequence of elements x_1, …, x_d ∈ m which generates an ideal of definition of R, • if there exist x_1, …, x_d ∈ m such that m = (x_1, …, x_d) then we call R a regular local ring and x_1, …, x_d a regular system of parameters.

nodes.title: Dimension · Lemma 00KV
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let x ∈ R. • If p is minimal over (x) then the height of p is 0 or 1. • If p, q ∈ Spec(R) and q is minimal over ( p, x), then there is no prime strictly between p and q.

nodes.title: Dimension · Lemma 0BBZ
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let f_1, …, f_r ∈ R. • If p is minimal over (f_1, …, f_r) then the height of p is ≤ r. • If p, q ∈ Spec(R) and q is minimal over ( p, f_1, …, f_r), then every chain of primes between p and q has length at most r.

nodes.title: Dimension · Lemma 00KW
nodes.summary: Suppose that R is a Noetherian local ring and x∈ m an element of its maximal ideal. Then dim R ≤ dim R/xR + 1. If x is not contained in any of the minimal primes of R then equality holds. (For example if x is a nonzerodivisor.)

nodes.title: Dimension · Lemma 02IE
nodes.summary: Let (R, m) be a Noetherian local ring. Suppose x_1, …, x_d ∈ m generate an ideal of definition and d = dim(R). Then dim(R/(x_1, …, x_i)) = d - i for all i = 1, …, d.

nodes.title: Applications of dimension theory · Lemma 02IG
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local domain of dimension ≥ 2. A nonempty open subset U ⊂ Spec(R) is infinite.

nodes.title: Applications of dimension theory · Lemma 0ALV
nodes.summary: A Noetherian ring with finitely many primes has dimension ≤ 1.

nodes.title: Applications of dimension theory · Lemma 0ALW
nodes.summary: Let S be a nonzero finite type algebra over a field k. The following are equivalent • dim(S) = 0, • S has finitely many primes, • S has finitely many maximal ideals, • Spec(S) satisfies one of the equivalent conditions of Lemma [Tag 04MG], • dim_k(S) < ∞, • S is Artinian, • Spec(S) is a discrete topological space, • add more here.

nodes.title: Applications of dimension theory · Lemma 00KX
nodes.summary: Noetherian Jacobson rings. • Any Noetherian domain R of dimension 1 with infinitely many primes is Jacobson. • Any Noetherian ring such that every prime p is either maximal or contained in infinitely many prime ideals is Jacobson.

nodes.title: Support and dimension of modules · Lemma 00L0
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring, and let M be a finite R-module. There exists a filtration by R-submodules 0 = M_0 ⊂ M_1 ⊂ … ⊂ M_n = M such that each quotient M_i/M_i-1 is isomorphic to R/ p_i for some prime ideal p_i of R.

nodes.title: Support and dimension of modules · Lemma 00L4
nodes.summary: Let R, M, M_i, p_i as in Lemma [Tag 00L0]. Then Supp(M) = ⋃ V( p_i) and in particular p_i ∈ Supp(M).

nodes.title: Support and dimension of modules · Lemma 00L5
nodes.summary: Suppose that R is a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m. Let M be a nonzero finite R-module. Then Supp(M) = ( m) if and only if M has finite length over R.

nodes.title: Support and dimension of modules · Lemma 00L6
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let M be a finite R-module. Then I^nM = 0 for some n ≥ 0 if and only if Supp(M) ⊂ V(I).

nodes.title: Support and dimension of modules · Lemma 00L7
