nodes.summary: Let R, M, M_i, p_i as in Lemma [Tag 00L0]. The minimal elements of the set ( p_i) are the minimal elements of Supp(M). The number of times a minimal prime p occurs is \#(i mid p_i = p) = length_R_ p M_ p.

nodes.title: Support and dimension of modules · Lemma 00L8
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring. Let M be a finite R-module. Then d(M) = dim(Supp(M)) where d(M) is as in Definition [Tag 00KA].

nodes.title: Support and dimension of modules · Lemma 0B51
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let 0 → M' → M → M" → 0 be a short exact sequence of finite R-modules. Then max(dim(Supp(M')), dim(Supp(M"))) = dim(Supp(M)).

nodes.title: Associated primes · Definition 00LA
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. A prime p of R is associated to M if there exists an element m ∈ M whose annihilator is p. The set of all such primes is denoted Ass_R(M) or Ass(M).

nodes.title: Associated primes · Lemma 0586
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Then Ass(M) ⊂ Supp(M).

nodes.title: Associated primes · Lemma 02M3
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let 0 → M' → M → M" → 0 be a short exact sequence of R-modules. Then Ass(M') ⊂ Ass(M) and Ass(M) ⊂ Ass(M') ∪ Ass(M"). Also Ass(M' ⊕ M") = Ass(M') ∪ Ass(M").

nodes.title: Associated primes · Lemma 00LB
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring, and M an R-module. Suppose there exists a filtration by R-submodules 0 = M_0 ⊂ M_1 ⊂ … ⊂ M_n = M such that each quotient M_i/M_i-1 is isomorphic to R/ p_i for some prime ideal p_i of R. Then Ass(M) ⊂ ( p_1, …, p_n).

nodes.title: Associated primes · Lemma 00LC
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let M be a finite R-module. Then Ass(M) is finite.

nodes.title: Associated primes · Proposition 02CE
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let M be a finite R-module. The following sets of primes are the same: • The minimal primes in the support of M. • The minimal primes in Ass(M). • For any filtration 0 = M_0 ⊂ M_1 ⊂ … ⊂ M_n-1 ⊂ M_n = M with M_i/M_i-1 ≅ R/ p_i the minimal primes of the set ( p_i).

nodes.title: Associated primes · Lemma 0587
nodes.summary: Over a Noetherian ring each nonzero module has an associated prime. Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let M be an R-module. Then M = (0) ⇔ Ass(M) = ∅.

nodes.title: Associated primes · Lemma 05BV
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let M be an R-module. Any p ∈ Supp(M) which is minimal among the elements of Supp(M) is an element of Ass(M).

nodes.title: Associated primes · Lemma 00LD
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let M be an R-module. The union ⋃_ q ∈ Ass(M) q is the set of elements of R which are zerodivisors on M.

nodes.title: Associated primes · Lemma 0B52
nodes.summary: Let R is a Noetherian local ring, M a finite R-module, and f ∈ m an element of the maximal ideal of R. Then dim(Supp(M/fM)) ≤ dim(Supp(M)) ≤ dim(Supp(M/fM)) + 1 If f is not in any of the minimal primes of the support of M (for example if f is a nonzerodivisor on M), then equality holds for the right inequality.

nodes.title: Associated primes · Lemma 05BW
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module. Then Spec(φ)(Ass_S(M)) ⊂ Ass_R(M).

nodes.title: Associated primes · Lemma 05DZ
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module. If S is Noetherian, then Spec(φ)(Ass_S(M)) = Ass_R(M).

nodes.title: Associated primes · Lemma 05BY
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I be an ideal. Let M be an R/I-module. Via the canonical injection Spec(R/I) → Spec(R) we have Ass_R/I(M) = Ass_R(M).

nodes.title: Associated primes · Lemma 0310
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Let p ⊂ R be a prime. • If p ∈ Ass(M) then pR_ p ∈ Ass(M_ p). • If p is finitely generated then the converse holds as well.

nodes.title: Associated primes · Lemma 05BZ
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Let S ⊂ R be a multiplicative subset. Via the canonical injection Spec(S^-1R) → Spec(R) we have • Ass_R(S^-1M) = Ass_S^-1R(S^-1M), • Ass_R(M) ∩ Spec(S^-1R) ⊂ Ass_R(S^-1M), and • if R is Noetherian this inclusion is an equality.

nodes.title: Associated primes · Lemma 05C0
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Let S ⊂ R be a multiplicative subset. Assume that every s ∈ S is a nonzerodivisor on M. Then Ass_R(M) = Ass_R(S^-1M).

nodes.title: Associated primes · Lemma 00LL
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m. Let I ⊂ m be an ideal. Let M be a finite R-module. The following are equivalent: • There exists an x ∈ I which is not a zerodivisor on M. • We have I not ⊂ q for all q ∈ Ass(M).

nodes.title: Associated primes · Lemma 0311
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. If R is Noetherian the map M → ∏_ p ∈ Ass(M) M_ p is injective.

nodes.title: Associated primes · Lemma 0GEC
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a finite type k algebra. If dim(S) > 0, then there exists an element f ∈ S which is a nonzerodivisor and a nonunit.

nodes.title: Symbolic powers · Definition 0313
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let p be a prime ideal. For n ≥ 0 the nth symbolic power of p is the ideal p^(n) = Ker(R → R_ p/ p^nR_ p).

nodes.title: Symbolic powers · Lemma 0314
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let p be a prime ideal. Let n > 0. Then Ass(R/ p^(n)) = ( p).

nodes.title: Symbolic powers · Lemma 0BC0
nodes.summary: Let R → S be flat ring map. Let p ⊂ R be a prime such that q = p S is a prime of S. Then p^(n) S = q^(n).

nodes.title: Relative assassin · Lemma 05GB
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let N be an S-module. Let A, A', A_fin, B, and B_fin be the subsets of Spec(S) introduced above. • We always have A = A'. • We always have A_fin ⊂ A, B_fin ⊂ B, A_fin ⊂ A'_fin ⊂ B_fin and A ⊂ B. • If S is Noetherian, then A = A_fin and B = B_fin. • If N is flat over R, then A = A_fin = A'_fin and B = B_fin. • If R is Noetherian and N is flat over R, then all of the sets are equal, i.e., A = A' = A_fin = A'_fin = B = B_fin.

nodes.title: Relative assassin · Definition 05GC
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let N be an S-module. The relative assassin of N over S/R is the set Ass_S/R(N) = ( q ⊂ S mid q ∈ Ass_S(N ⊗_R kappa( p)) with p = R ∩ q). This is the set named A in Lemma [Tag 05GB].

nodes.title: Relative assassin · Lemma 0312
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let M be an R-module, and let N be an S-module. If N is flat as R-module, then Ass_S(M ⊗_R N) ⊃ ⋃_ p ∈ Ass_R(M) Ass_S(N/ pN) and if R is Noetherian then we have equality.

nodes.title: Relative assassin · Lemma 05C1
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let N be an S-module. Assume N is flat as an R-module and R is a domain with fraction field K. Then Ass_S(N) = Ass_S(N ⊗_R K) = Ass_S ⊗_R K(N ⊗_R K) via the canonical inclusion Spec(S ⊗_R K) ⊂ Spec(S).

nodes.title: Relative assassin · Lemma 05C2
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let M be an R-module, and let N be an S-module. Assume N is flat as R-module. Then Ass_S(M ⊗_R N) ⊃ ⋃_ p ∈ Ass_R(M) Ass_S ⊗_R kappa( p)(N ⊗_R kappa( p)) where we use Remark [Tag 00E6] to think of the spectra of fibre rings as subsets of Spec(S). If R is Noetherian then this inclusion is an equality.

nodes.title: Weakly associated primes · Definition 0547
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. A prime p of R is weakly associated to M if there exists an element m ∈ M such that p is minimal among the prime ideals containing the annihilator Ann(m) = (f ∈ R mid fm = 0). The set of all such primes is denoted WeakAss_R(M) or WeakAss(M).

nodes.title: Weakly associated primes · Lemma 0566
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Let p be a prime of R. The following are equivalent: • p is weakly associated to M, • pR_ p is weakly associated to M_ p, and • M_ p contains an element whose annihilator has radical equal to pR_ p.

nodes.title: Weakly associated primes · Lemma 0EMA
nodes.summary: For a reduced ring the weakly associated primes of the ring are the minimal primes.

nodes.title: Weakly associated primes · Lemma 0548
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let 0 → M' → M → M" → 0 be a short exact sequence of R-modules. Then WeakAss(M') ⊂ WeakAss(M) and WeakAss(M) ⊂ WeakAss(M') ∪ WeakAss(M").

nodes.title: Weakly associated primes · Lemma 0588
nodes.summary: Every nonzero module has a weakly associated prime. Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Then M = (0) ⇔ WeakAss(M) = ∅

nodes.title: Weakly associated primes · Lemma 0589
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Then Ass(M) ⊂ WeakAss(M) ⊂ Supp(M).

nodes.title: Weakly associated primes · Lemma 05C3
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. The union ⋃_ q ∈ WeakAss(M) q is the set of elements of R which are zerodivisors on M.

nodes.title: Weakly associated primes · Lemma 05C4
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Any p ∈ Supp(M) which is minimal among the elements of Supp(M) is an element of WeakAss(M).

nodes.title: Weakly associated primes · Lemma 058A
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Let p be a prime ideal of R which is finitely generated. Then p ∈ Ass(M) ⇔ p ∈ WeakAss(M). In particular, if R is Noetherian, then Ass(M) = WeakAss(M).

nodes.title: Weakly associated primes · Lemma 05C6
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module. Then we have Spec(φ)(WeakAss_S(M)) ⊃ WeakAss_R(M).

nodes.title: Weakly associated primes · Lemma 05E1
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module. Denote f : Spec(S) → Spec(R) the associated map on spectra. If φ is a finite ring map, then WeakAss_R(M) = f(WeakAss_S(M)).

nodes.title: Weakly associated primes · Lemma 05C8
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I be an ideal. Let M be an R/I-module. Via the canonical injection Spec(R/I) → Spec(R) we have WeakAss_R/I(M) = WeakAss_R(M).

nodes.title: Weakly associated primes · Lemma 05C9
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Let S ⊂ R be a multiplicative subset. Via the canonical injection Spec(S^-1R) → Spec(R) we have WeakAss_R(S^-1M) = WeakAss_S^-1R(S^-1M) and WeakAss(M) ∩ Spec(S^-1R) = WeakAss(S^-1M).

nodes.title: Weakly associated primes · Lemma 05CA
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Let S ⊂ R be a multiplicative subset. Assume that every s ∈ S is a nonzerodivisor on M. Then WeakAss(M) = WeakAss(S^-1M).

nodes.title: Weakly associated primes · Lemma 05CB
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. The map M → ∏_ p ∈ WeakAss(M) M_ p is injective.

nodes.title: Weakly associated primes · Lemma 05CC
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let N be an S-module. Assume N is flat as an R-module and R is a domain with fraction field K. Then WeakAss_S(N) = WeakAss_S ⊗_R K(N ⊗_R K) via the canonical inclusion Spec(S ⊗_R K) ⊂ Spec(S).

nodes.title: Weakly associated primes · Lemma 0CUB
nodes.summary: Let K/k be a field extension. Let R be a k-algebra. Let M be an R-module. Let q ⊂ R ⊗_k K be a prime lying over p ⊂ R. If q is weakly associated to M ⊗_k K, then p is weakly associated to M.

nodes.title: Embedded primes · Definition 02M5
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. • The associated primes of M which are not minimal among the associated primes of M are called the embedded associated primes of M. • The embedded primes of R are the embedded associated primes of R as an R-module.

nodes.title: Embedded primes · Lemma 02M6
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let M be a finite R-module. Consider the set of R-submodules ( K ⊂ M mid Supp(K) nowhere dense in Supp(M) ). This set has a maximal element K and the quotient M' = M/K has the following properties • Supp(M) = Supp(M'), • M' has no embedded associated primes, • for any f ∈ R which is contained in all embedded associated primes of M we have M_f ≅ M'_f.

nodes.title: Embedded primes · Lemma 02M7
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let M be a finite R-module. For any f ∈ R we have (M')_f = (M_f)' where M → M' and M_f → (M_f)' are the quotients constructed in Lemma [Tag 02M6].

nodes.title: Embedded primes · Lemma 02M8
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let M be a finite R-module without embedded associated primes. Let I = (x ∈ R mid xM = 0). Then the ring R/I has no embedded primes.

nodes.title: Regular sequences · Definition 00LF
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. A sequence of elements f_1, …, f_r of R is called an M-regular sequence if the following conditions hold: • f_i is a nonzerodivisor on M/(f_1, …, f_i - 1)M for each i = 1, …, r, and • the module M/(f_1, …, f_r)M is not zero. If I is an ideal of R and f_1, …, f_r ∈ I then we call f_1, …, f_r an M-regular sequence in I. If M = R, we call f_1, …, f_r simply a regular sequence (in I).

nodes.title: Regular sequences · Lemma 00LJ
nodes.summary: Let R be a local Noetherian ring. Let M be a finite R-module. Let x_1, …, x_c be an M-regular sequence. Then any permutation of the x_i is a regular sequence as well.

nodes.title: Regular sequences · Lemma 00LM
nodes.summary: Flat local ring homomorphisms preserve and reflect regular sequences. Let R, S be local rings. Let R → S be a flat local ring homomorphism. Let x_1, …, x_r be a sequence in R. Let M be an R-module. The following are equivalent • x_1, …, x_r is an M-regular sequence in R, and • the images of x_1, …, x_r in S form a M ⊗_R S-regular sequence.

nodes.title: Regular sequences · Lemma 061L
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let M be a finite R-module. Let p be a prime. Let x_1, …, x_r be a sequence in R whose image in R_ p forms an M_ p-regular sequence. Then there exists a g ∈ R, g not ∈ p such that the image of x_1, …, x_r in R_g forms an M_g-regular sequence.

nodes.title: Regular sequences · Lemma 065K
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let I be an ideal generated by a regular sequence f_1, …, f_n in A. Let g_1, …, g_m ∈ A be elements whose images overlineg_1, …, overlineg_m form a regular sequence in A/I. Then f_1, …, f_n, g_1, …, g_m is a regular sequence in A.

nodes.title: Regular sequences · Lemma 0F1T
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let 0 → M_1 → M_2 → M_3 → 0 be a short exact sequence of R-modules. Let f_1, …, f_r ∈ R. If f_1, …, f_r is M_1-regular and M_3-regular, then f_1, …, f_r is M_2-regular.

nodes.title: Regular sequences · Lemma 07DV
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Let f_1, …, f_r ∈ R and e_1, …, e_r > 0 integers. Then f_1, …, f_r is an M-regular sequence if and only if f_1^e_1, …, f_r^e_r is an M-regular sequence.

nodes.title: Regular sequences · Lemma 07DW
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let f_1, …, f_r ∈ R which do not generate the unit ideal. The following are equivalent: • any permutation of f_1, …, f_r is a regular sequence, • any subsequence of f_1, …, f_r (in the given order) is a regular sequence, and • f_1x_1, …, f_rx_r is a regular sequence in the polynomial ring R[x_1, …, x_r].

nodes.title: Quasi-regular sequences · Definition 061P
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. A sequence of elements f_1, …, f_c of R is called M-quasi-regular if ([Tag 061N]) is an isomorphism. If M = R, we call f_1, …, f_c simply a quasi-regular sequence.

nodes.title: Quasi-regular sequences · Lemma 00LN
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. • A regular sequence f_1, …, f_c of R is a quasi-regular sequence. • Suppose that M is an R-module and that f_1, …, f_c is an M-regular sequence. Then f_1, …, f_c is an M-quasi-regular sequence.

nodes.title: Quasi-regular sequences · Lemma 065L
nodes.summary: Let R → R' be a flat ring map. Let M be an R-module. Suppose that f_1, …, f_r ∈ R form an M-quasi-regular sequence. Then the images of f_1, …, f_r in R' form a M ⊗_R R'-quasi-regular sequence.

nodes.title: Quasi-regular sequences · Lemma 061Q
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let M be a finite R-module. Let p be a prime. Let x_1, …, x_c be a sequence in R whose image in R_ p forms an M_ p-quasi-regular sequence. Then there exists a g ∈ R, g not ∈ p such that the image of x_1, …, x_c in R_g forms an M_g-quasi-regular sequence.

nodes.title: Quasi-regular sequences · Lemma 061R
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Let f_1, …, f_c ∈ R be an M-quasi-regular sequence. For any i the sequence overlinef_i + 1, …, overlinef_c of overlineR = R/(f_1, …, f_i) is an overlineM = M/(f_1, …, f_i)M-quasi-regular sequence.

nodes.title: Quasi-regular sequences · Lemma 061S
nodes.summary: Let (R, m) be a local Noetherian ring. Let M be a nonzero finite R-module. Let f_1, …, f_c ∈ m be an M-quasi-regular sequence. Then f_1, …, f_c is an M-regular sequence.

nodes.title: Quasi-regular sequences · Lemma 065N
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let J = (f_1, …, f_r) be an ideal of R. Let M be an R-module. Set overlineR = R/⋂_n ≥ 0 J^n, overlineM = M/⋂_n ≥ 0 J^nM, and denote overlinef_i the image of f_i in overlineR. Then f_1, …, f_r is M-quasi-regular if and only if overlinef_1, …, overlinef_r is overlineM-quasi-regular.

nodes.title: Blow up algebras · Definition 052Q
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. • The blowup algebra, or the Rees algebra, associated to the pair (R, I) is the graded R-algebra Bl_I(R) = bigoplus_n ≥ 0 I^n = R ⊕ I ⊕ I^2 ⊕ … where the summand I^n is placed in degree n. • Let a ∈ I be an element. Denote a^(1) the element a seen as an element of degree 1 in the Rees algebra. Then the affine blowup algebra R[fracIa] is the algebra (Bl_I(R))_(a^(1)) constructed in Section [Tag 00JM].

nodes.title: Blow up algebras · Lemma 07Z3
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring, I ⊂ R an ideal, and a ∈ I. Let R' = R[fracIa] be the affine blowup algebra. Then • the image of a in R' is a nonzerodivisor, • IR' = aR', and • (R')_a = R_a.

nodes.title: Blow up algebras · Lemma 0BIP
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal and a ∈ I. Set J = IS and let b ∈ J be the image of a. Then S[fracJb] is the quotient of S ⊗_R R[fracIa] by the ideal of elements annihilated by some power of b.

nodes.title: Blow up algebras · Lemma 0G8S
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I = (a_1, …, a_n) be an ideal of R. Let a = a_1. Then there is a surjection R[x_2, …, x_n]/(a x_2 - a_2, …, a x_n - a_n) → textstyleR[fracIa] whose kernel is the a-power torsion in the source.

nodes.title: Blow up algebras · Lemma 080U
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring, I ⊂ R an ideal, and a ∈ I. Set R' = R[fracIa]. If f ∈ R is such that V(f) = V(I), then f maps to a nonzerodivisor in R' and R'_f = R'_a = R_a.

nodes.title: Blow up algebras · Lemma 0BBI
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring, I ⊂ R an ideal, a ∈ I, and f ∈ R. Set R' = R[fracIa] and R" = R[fracfIfa]. Then there is a surjective R-algebra map R' → R" whose kernel is the set of f-power torsion elements of R'.

nodes.title: Blow up algebras · Lemma 052S
nodes.summary: Being reduced is invariant under blowup If R is reduced then every (affine) blowup algebra of R is reduced.

nodes.title: Blow up algebras · Lemma 052R
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain, I ⊂ R an ideal, and a ∈ I a nonzero element. Then the affine blowup algebra R[fracIa] is a domain.

nodes.title: Blow up algebras · Lemma 052T
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let a ∈ I. If a is not contained in any minimal prime of R, then Spec(R[fracIa]) → Spec(R) has dense image.

nodes.title: Blow up algebras · Lemma 052M
nodes.summary: Let (R, m) be a local domain with fraction field K. Let R ⊂ A ⊂ K be a valuation ring which dominates R. Then A = colim R[textstylefracIa] is a directed colimit of affine blowups R → R[fracIa] with the following properties • a ∈ I ⊂ m, • I is finitely generated, and • the fibre ring of R → R[fracIa] at m is not zero.

nodes.title: Ext groups · Lemma 00LP
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. • There exists an exact complex … → F_2 → F_1 → F_0 → M → 0. with F_i free R-modules. • If R is Noetherian and M finite over R, then we can choose the complex such that F_i is finite free. In other words, we can find an exact complex … → R^⊕ n_2 → R^⊕ n_1 → R^⊕ n_0 → M → 0.

nodes.title: Ext groups · Definition 00LQ
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. • A (left) resolution F_bullet → M of M is an exact complex … → F_2 → F_1 → F_0 → M → 0 of R-modules. • A resolution of M by free R-modules is a resolution F_bullet → M where each F_i is a free R-module. • A resolution of M by finite free R-modules is a resolution F_bullet → M where each F_i is a finite free R-module.

nodes.title: Ext groups · Lemma 00LR
nodes.summary: Any two homotopic maps of complexes induce the same maps on (co)homology groups.

nodes.title: Ext groups · Lemma 00LS
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M → N be a map of R-modules. Let N_bullet → N be an arbitrary resolution. Let … → F_2 → F_1 → F_0 → M be a complex of R-modules where each F_i is a free R-module. Then • there exists a map of complexes F_bullet → N_bullet such that xymatrix F_0 ar[r] ar[d] & M ar[d] N_0 ar[r] & N is commutative, and • any two maps α, β : F_bullet → N_bullet as in (1) are homotopic.

nodes.title: Ext groups · Lemma 00LT
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M_1, M_2, N be R-modules. Suppose that F_bullet is a free resolution of the module M_1, and G_bullet is a free resolution of the module M_2. Let φ : M_1 → M_2 be a module map. Let α : F_bullet → G_bullet be a map of complexes inducing φ on M_1 = Coker(d_F, 1) → M_2 = Coker(d_G, 1), see Lemma [Tag 00LS]. Then the induced maps H^i(α) : H^i(Hom_R(F_bullet, N)) → H^i(Hom_R(G_bullet, N)) are independent of the choice of α. If φ is an isomorphism, so are…

nodes.title: Ext groups · Lemma 00LU
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Let 0 → N' → N → N" → 0 be a short exact sequence. Then we get a long exact sequence 0 → Hom_R(M, N') → Hom_R(M, N) → Hom_R(M, N") phantom0 → Ext^1_R(M, N') → Ext^1_R(M, N) → Ext^1_R(M, N") → …

nodes.title: Ext groups · Lemma 065P
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let N be an R-module. Let 0 → M' → M → M" → 0 be a short exact sequence. Then we get a long exact sequence 0 → Hom_R(M", N) → Hom_R(M, N) → Hom_R(M', N) phantom0 → Ext^1_R(M", N) → Ext^1_R(M, N) → Ext^1_R(M', N) → …

nodes.title: Ext groups · Lemma 00LV
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M, N be R-modules. Any x∈ R such that either xN = 0, or xM = 0 annihilates each of the modules Ext^i_R(M, N).

nodes.title: Ext groups · Lemma 08YR
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let M, N be finite R-modules. Then Ext^i_R(M, N) is a finite R-module for all i.

nodes.title: Depth · Definition 00LI
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring, and I ⊂ R an ideal. Let M be a finite R-module. The I-depth of M, denoted depth_I(M), is defined as follows: • if IM not = M, then depth_I(M) is the supremum in (0, 1, 2, …, ∞) of the lengths of M-regular sequences in I, • if IM = M we set depth_I(M) = ∞. If (R, m) is local we call depth_ m(M) simply the depth of M.

nodes.title: Depth · Lemma 0AUI
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring, I ⊂ R an ideal, and M a finite R-module. Then depth_I(M) is equal to the supremum of the lengths of sequences f_1, …, f_r ∈ I such that f_i is a nonzerodivisor on M/(f_1, …, f_i - 1)M.

nodes.title: Depth · Lemma 00LK
nodes.summary: Let (R, m) be a Noetherian local ring. Let M be a nonzero finite R-module. Then dim(Supp(M)) ≥ depth(M).

nodes.title: Depth · Lemma 0AUJ
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring, I ⊂ R an ideal, and M a finite nonzero R-module such that IM not = M. Then depth_I(M) < ∞.

nodes.title: Depth · Lemma 00LW
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m. Let M be a nonzero finite R-module. Then depth(M) is equal to the smallest integer i such that Ext^i_R(R/ m, M) is nonzero.

nodes.title: Depth · Lemma 00LX
nodes.summary: Let R be a local Noetherian ring. Let 0 → N' → N → N" → 0 be a short exact sequence of nonzero finite R-modules. • depth(N) ≥ min(depth(N'), depth(N")) • depth(N") ≥ min(depth(N), depth(N') - 1) • depth(N') ≥ min(depth(N), depth(N") + 1)

nodes.title: Depth · Lemma 090R
nodes.summary: Let R be a local Noetherian ring and M a nonzero finite R-module. • If x ∈ m is a nonzerodivisor on M, then depth(M/xM) = depth(M) - 1. • Any M-regular sequence x_1, …, x_r can be extended to an M-regular sequence of length depth(M).

nodes.title: Depth · Lemma 0CN5
nodes.summary: Let (R, m) be a local Noetherian ring and M a finite R-module. Let x ∈ m, p ∈ Ass(M), and q minimal over p + (x). Then q ∈ Ass(M/x^nM) for some n ≥ 1.

nodes.title: Depth · Lemma 0BK4
nodes.summary: Let (R, m) be a local Noetherian ring and M a finite R-module. For p ∈ Ass(M) we have dim(R/ p) ≥ depth(M).

nodes.title: Depth · Lemma 0FCC
nodes.summary: Let R be a local Noetherian ring and M a finite R-module. For a prime ideal p ⊂ R we have depth(M_ p) + dim(R/ p) ≥ depth(M).

nodes.title: Depth · Lemma 0AUK
nodes.summary: Let (R, m) be a Noetherian local ring. Let R → S be a finite ring map. Let m_1, …, m_n be the maximal ideals of S. Let N be a finite S-module. Then min_i = 1, …, n depth(N_ m_i) = depth_ m(N)

nodes.title: Functorialities for Ext · Lemma 087N
nodes.summary: Given a flat ring map R → R', an R-module M, and an R'-module N' the natural map Ext^i_R'(M ⊗_R R', N') → Ext^i_R(M, N') is an isomorphism for i ≥ 0.

nodes.title: An application of Ext groups · Lemma 02HO
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical of R. Let N → M be a homomorphism of finite R-modules. Suppose that there exists arbitrarily large n such that N/I^nN → M/I^nM is a split injection. Then N → M is a split injection.

nodes.title: Tor groups and flatness · Lemma 00LZ
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M_1, M_2, N be R-modules. Suppose that F_bullet is a free resolution of the module M_1 and that G_bullet is a free resolution of the module M_2. Let φ : M_1 → M_2 be a module map. Let α : F_bullet → G_bullet be a map of complexes inducing φ on M_1 = Coker(d_F, 1) → M_2 = Coker(d_G, 1), see Lemma [Tag 00LS]. Then the induced maps H_i(α) : H_i(F_bullet ⊗_R N) → H_i(G_bullet ⊗_R N) are independent of the choice of α. If φ is an isomorphism, so are all…

nodes.title: Tor groups and flatness · Lemma 00M0
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring and let M be an R-module. Suppose that 0 → N' → N → N" → 0 is a short exact sequence of R-modules. There exists a long exact sequence Tor_1^R(M, N') → Tor_1^R(M, N) → Tor_1^R(M, N") → M ⊗_R N' → M ⊗_R N → M ⊗_R N" → 0

nodes.title: Tor groups and flatness · Lemma 00M1
nodes.summary: Let (A_bullet, bullet, d, δ) be a double complex such that • Each row A_bullet, j is a resolution of R(A)_j. • Each column A_i, bullet is a resolution of U(A)_i. Then there are canonical isomorphisms H_i(R(A)_bullet) ≅ H_i(U(A)_bullet). The isomorphisms are functorial with respect to morphisms of double complexes with the properties above.

nodes.title: Tor groups and flatness · Lemma 00M3
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. For any i ≥ 0 the functors Mod_R × Mod_R → Mod_R, (M, N) ↦ Tor_i^R(M, N) and (M, N) ↦ Tor_i^R(N, M) are canonically isomorphic.

nodes.title: Tor groups and flatness · Lemma 0AZ4
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let M, N be finite R-modules. Then Tor_p^R(M, N) is a finite R-module for all p.

nodes.title: Tor groups and flatness · Lemma 00M5
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. The following are equivalent: • The module M is flat over R. • For all i > 0 the functor Tor_i^R(M, -) is zero. • The functor Tor_1^R(M, -) is zero. • For all ideals I ⊂ R we have Tor_1^R(M, R/I) = 0. • For all finitely generated ideals I ⊂ R we have Tor_1^R(M, R/I) = 0.

nodes.title: Functorialities for Tor · Lemma 00M8
nodes.summary: Given a flat ring map R → R' and R-modules M, N the natural R-module map Tor_i^R(M, N)⊗_R R' → Tor_i^R'(M ⊗_R R', N ⊗_R R') is an isomorphism for all i.

nodes.title: Functorialities for Tor · Lemma 0BNF
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M = colim M_i be a filtered colimit of R-modules. Let N be an R-module. Then Tor_n^R(M, N) = colim Tor_n^R(M_i, N) for all n.

nodes.title: Projective modules · Definition 05CE
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. An R-module P is projective if and only if the functor Hom_R(P, -) : Mod_R → Mod_R is an exact functor.

nodes.title: Projective modules · Lemma 05CF
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let P be an R-module. The following are equivalent • P is projective, • P is a direct summand of a free R-module, and • Ext^1_R(P, M) = 0 for every R-module M.

nodes.title: Projective modules · Lemma 0G8T
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let P be a finite R-module. If Ext^1_R(P, M) = 0 for every finite R-module M, then P is projective.

nodes.title: Projective modules · Lemma 065Q
nodes.summary: A direct sum of projective modules is projective.

nodes.title: Projective modules · Lemma 07LV
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be a nilpotent ideal. Let overlineP be a projective R/I-module. Then there exists a projective R-module P such that P/IP ≅ overlineP.

nodes.title: Projective modules · Lemma 0D47
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be a locally nilpotent ideal. Let overlineP be a finite projective R/I-module. Then there exists a finite projective R-module P such that P/IP ≅ overlineP.

nodes.title: Projective modules · Lemma 05CG
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let M be an R-module. Assume • I is nilpotent, • M/IM is a projective R/I-module, • M is a flat R-module. Then M is a projective R-module.

nodes.title: Projective modules · Lemma 0H7M
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I, J ⊂ R be ideals such that I ∩ J = 0. Let P be an R-module such that P/IP is a projective R/I-module and P/JP is a projective R/J-module. Then P is a projective R-module.

nodes.title: Finite projective modules · Definition 00NW
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring and M an R-module. • We say that M is locally free if we can cover Spec(R) by standard opens D(f_i), i ∈ I such that M_f_i is a free R_f_i-module for all i ∈ I. • We say that M is finite locally free if we can choose the covering such that each M_f_i is finite free. • We say that M is finite locally free of rank r if we can choose the covering such that each M_f_i is isomorphic to R_f_i^⊕ r.

nodes.title: Finite projective modules · Lemma 00NX
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring and let M be an R-module. The following are equivalent • M is finitely presented and R-flat, • M is finite projective, • M is a direct summand of a finite free R-module, • M is finitely presented and for all p ∈ Spec(R) the localization M_ p is free, • M is finitely presented and for all maximal ideals m ⊂ R the localization M_ m is free, • M is finite and locally free, • M is finite locally free, and • M is finite, for every prime p the module M_ p is…

nodes.title: Finite projective modules · Lemma 0FWG
nodes.summary: Let R be a reduced ring and let M be an R-module. Then the equivalent conditions of Lemma [Tag 00NX] are also equivalent to • [(9)] M is finite and the function ρ_M : Spec(R) → Z, p ↦ dim_kappa( p) M ⊗_R kappa( p) is locally constant in the Zariski topology.

nodes.title: Finite projective modules · Lemma 00NZ
nodes.summary: (Warning: see Remark [Tag 00NY].) Suppose R is a local ring, and M is a finite flat R-module. Then M is finite free.

nodes.title: Finite projective modules · Lemma 00O1
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a flat local homomorphism of local rings. Let M be a finite R-module. Then M is finite projective over R if and only if M ⊗_R S is finite projective over S.

nodes.title: Finite projective modules · Lemma 02M9
nodes.summary: Let R be a semi-local ring. Let M be a finite locally free module. If M has constant rank, then M is free. In particular, if R has connected spectrum, then M is free.

nodes.title: Finite projective modules · Lemma 03C1
nodes.summary: Let R be a local ring with maximal ideal m and infinite residue field. Let R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module and let N ⊂ M be an R-submodule. Assume • S is semi-local and mS is contained in the Jacobson radical of S, • M is a finite free S-module, and • N generates M as an S-module. Then N contains an S-basis of M.

nodes.title: Finite projective modules · Lemma 0DVB
nodes.summary: Let R be ring. Let L, M, N be R-modules. The canonical map Hom_R(M, N) ⊗_R L → Hom_R(M, N ⊗_R L) is an isomorphism if M is finite projective.

nodes.title: Open loci defined by module maps · Lemma 05GE
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let φ : M → N be a map of R-modules with N a finite R-module. Then we have the equality U & = ( p ⊂ R mid φ_ p : M_ p → N_ p is surjective) & = ( p ⊂ R mid φ ⊗ kappa( p) : M ⊗ kappa( p) → N ⊗ kappa( p) is surjective) and U is an open subset of Spec(R). Moreover, for any f ∈ R such that D(f) ⊂ U the map M_f → N_f is surjective.
nodes.section: Open loci defined by module maps

nodes.title: Open loci defined by module maps · Lemma 05GF
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let φ : M → N be a map of R-modules with M finite and N finitely presented. Then U = ( p ⊂ R mid φ_ p : M_ p → N_ p is an isomorphism) is an open subset of Spec(R).
nodes.section: Open loci defined by module maps

nodes.title: Open loci defined by module maps · Lemma 0GWM
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let p ⊂ R be a prime. Let M be a finitely presented R-module. If M_ p is free, then there is an f ∈ R, f not ∈ p such that M_f is a free R_f-module.
nodes.section: Open loci defined by module maps

nodes.title: Open loci defined by module maps · Lemma 00O0
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let φ : P_1 → P_2 be a map of finite projective modules. Then • The set U of primes p ∈ Spec(R) such that φ ⊗ kappa( p) is injective is open and for any f∈ R such that D(f) ⊂ U we have • P_1, f → P_2, f is injective, and • the module Coker(φ)_f is finite projective over R_f. • The set W of primes p ∈ Spec(R) such that φ ⊗ kappa( p) is surjective is open and for any f∈ R such that D(f) ⊂ W we have • P_1, f → P_2, f is surjective, and • the module Ker(φ)_f…
nodes.section: Open loci defined by module maps

nodes.title: Characterizing flatness · Lemma 058D
nodes.summary: Let M be an R-module. The following are equivalent: • M is flat. • If f: R^n → M is a module map and x ∈ Ker(f), then there are module maps h: R^n → R^m and g: R^m → M such that f = g ∘ h and x ∈ Ker(h). • Suppose f: R^n → M is a module map, N ⊂ Ker(f) any submodule, and h: R^n → R^m a map such that N ⊂ Ker(h) and f factors through h. Then given any x ∈ Ker(f) we can find a map h': R^n → R^m' such that N + Rx ⊂ Ker(h') and f factors through h'. • If f: R^n → M is a module…

nodes.title: Characterizing flatness · Lemma 058E
nodes.summary: Let M be an R-module. Then M is flat if and only if the following condition holds: if P is a finitely presented R-module and f: P → M a module map, then there is a free finite R-module F and module maps h: P → F and g: F → M such that f = g ∘ h.

nodes.title: Characterizing flatness · Lemma 058F
nodes.summary: Let M be an R-module. Then M is flat if and only if the following condition holds: for every finitely presented R-module P, if N → M is a surjective R-module map, then the induced map Hom_R(P, N) → Hom_R(P, M) is surjective.

nodes.title: Lazard's theorem · Theorem 058G
nodes.summary: Let M be an R-module. Then M is flat if and only if it is the colimit of a directed system of free finite R-modules.

nodes.title: Universally injective module maps · Definition 058I
nodes.summary: Let f: M → N be a map of R-modules. Then f is called universally injective if for every R-module Q, the map f ⊗_R id_Q: M ⊗_R Q → N ⊗_R Q is injective. A sequence 0 → M_1 → M_2 → M_3 → 0 of R-modules is called universally exact if it is exact and M_1 → M_2 is universally injective.

nodes.title: Universally injective module maps · Theorem 058K
nodes.summary: Let 0 → M_1 xrightarrowf_1 M_2 xrightarrowf_2 M_3 → 0 be an exact sequence of R-modules. The following are equivalent: • The sequence 0 → M_1 → M_2 → M_3 → 0 is universally exact. • For every finitely presented R-module Q, the sequence 0 → M_1 ⊗_R Q → M_2 ⊗_R Q → M_3 ⊗_R Q → 0 is exact. • Given elements x_i ∈ M_1 (i = 1, …, n), y_j ∈ M_2 (j = 1, …, m), and a_ij ∈ R (i = 1, …, n, j = 1, …, m) such that for all i f_1(x_i) = ∑_j a_ij y_j, there exists z_j ∈ M_1 (j =1, …, m)…

nodes.title: Universally injective module maps · Lemma 058L
nodes.summary: Let 0 → M_1 → M_2 → M_3 → 0 be an exact sequence of R-modules. Suppose M_3 is of finite presentation. Then 0 → M_1 → M_2 → M_3 → 0 is universally exact if and only if it is split.

nodes.title: Universally injective module maps · Lemma 058M
nodes.summary: Let M be an R-module. Then M is flat if and only if any exact sequence of R-modules 0 → M_1 → M_2 → M → 0 is universally exact.

nodes.title: Universally injective module maps · Lemma 058P
nodes.summary: Let 0 → M_1 → M_2 → M_3 → 0 be a universally exact sequence of R-modules, and suppose M_2 is flat. Then M_1 and M_3 are flat.

nodes.title: Universally injective module maps · Lemma 05CH
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M → M' be a universally injective R-module map. Then for any R-module N the map M ⊗_R N → M' ⊗_R N is universally injective.

nodes.title: Universally injective module maps · Lemma 05CI
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. A composition of universally injective R-module maps is universally injective.

nodes.title: Universally injective module maps · Lemma 05CJ
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M → M' and M' → M" be R-module maps. If their composition M → M" is universally injective, then M → M' is universally injective.

nodes.title: Universally injective module maps · Lemma 05CL
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let M → M' be a map of S-modules. The following are equivalent • M → M' is universally injective as a map of R-modules, • for each prime q of S the map M_ q → M'_ q is universally injective as a map of R-modules, • for each maximal ideal m of S the map M_ m → M'_ m is universally injective as a map of R-modules, • for each prime q of S the map M_ q → M'_ q is universally injective as a map of R_ p-modules, where p is the inverse image of q in R,…

nodes.title: Universally injective module maps · Lemma 05CM
nodes.summary: Let φ : A → B be a ring map. Let S ⊂ A and S' ⊂ B be multiplicative subsets such that φ(S) ⊂ S'. Let M → M' be a map of B-modules. • If M → M' is universally injective as a map of A-modules, then (S')^-1M → (S')^-1M' is universally injective as a map of A-modules and as a map of S^-1A-modules. • If M and M' are (S')^-1B-modules, then M → M' is universally injective as a map of A-modules if and only if it is universally injective as a map of S^-1A-modules.

nodes.title: Universally injective module maps · Lemma 0AS5
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring and let M → M' be a map of R-modules. If M' is flat, then M → M' is universally injective if and only if M/IM → M'/IM' is injective for every finitely generated ideal I of R.

nodes.title: Universally injective module maps · Lemma 0H9I
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map which is universally injective as a map of R-modules. Then the functor M ↦ M ⊗_R S on R-modules reflects injections, surjections, and isomorphisms.

nodes.title: Universally injective module maps · Lemma 05CK
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a faithfully flat ring map. Then R → S is universally injective as a map of R-modules. In particular R ∩ IS = I for any ideal I ⊂ R.

nodes.title: Descent for finite projective modules · Lemma 058R
nodes.summary: Let M be an R-module. Then M is finite projective if and only if M is finitely presented and flat.

nodes.title: Descent for finite projective modules · Lemma 03C4
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a faithfully flat ring map. Let M be an R-module. Then • if the S-module M ⊗_R S is of finite type, then M is of finite type, • if the S-module M ⊗_R S is of finite presentation, then M is of finite presentation, • if the S-module M ⊗_R S is flat, then M is flat, and • add more here as needed.

nodes.title: Descent for finite projective modules · Proposition 058S
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a faithfully flat ring map. Let M be an R-module. If the S-module M ⊗_R S is finite projective, then M is finite projective.

nodes.title: Transfinite dévissage of modules · Definition 058U
nodes.summary: Let M be an R-module. A direct sum dévissage of M is a family of submodules (M_α)_α ∈ S, indexed by an ordinal S and increasing (with respect to inclusion), such that: • [(0)] M_0 = 0; • [(1)] M = ⋃_α M_α; • [(2)] if α ∈ S is a limit ordinal, then M_α = ⋃_β < α M_β; • [(3)] if α + 1 ∈ S, then M_α is a direct summand of M_α + 1. If moreover • [(4)] M_α + 1/M_α is countably generated for α + 1 ∈ S, then (M_α)_α ∈ S is called a Kaplansky dévissage of M.

nodes.title: Transfinite dévissage of modules · Lemma 058V
nodes.summary: Let M be an R-module. If (M_α)_α ∈ S is a direct sum dévissage of M, then M ≅ bigoplus_α + 1 ∈ S M_α + 1/M_α.

nodes.title: Transfinite dévissage of modules · Lemma 058W
nodes.summary: Let M be an R-module. Then M is a direct sum of countably generated R-modules if and only if it admits a Kaplansky dévissage.

nodes.title: Transfinite dévissage of modules · Theorem 058X
nodes.summary: Suppose M is a direct sum of countably generated R-modules. If P is a direct summand of M, then P is also a direct sum of countably generated R-modules.

nodes.title: Transfinite dévissage of modules · Theorem 058Y
nodes.summary: Any projective module is a direct sum of countably generated projective modules. If P is a projective R-module, then P is a direct sum of countably generated projective R-modules.

nodes.title: Projective modules over a local ring · Lemma 0590
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Then every projective R-module is free if and only if every countably generated projective R-module is free.
nodes.section: Projective modules over a local ring

nodes.title: Projective modules over a local ring · Lemma 0591
nodes.summary: Let M be a countably generated R-module with the following property: if M = N ⊕ N' with N' a finite free R-module, then any element of N is contained in a free direct summand of N. Then M is free.
nodes.section: Projective modules over a local ring

nodes.title: Projective modules over a local ring · Lemma 0592
nodes.summary: Let P be a projective module over a local ring R. Then any element of P is contained in a free direct summand of P.
nodes.section: Projective modules over a local ring

nodes.title: Projective modules over a local ring · Theorem 0593
nodes.summary: Projective modules over local rings are free. If P is a projective module over a local ring R, then P is free.
nodes.section: Projective modules over a local ring

nodes.title: Mittag-Leffler systems · Definition 0595
nodes.summary: Let (A_i, φ_ji) be a directed inverse system of sets over I. Then we say (A_i, φ_ji) is Mittag-Leffler if for each i ∈ I, the family φ_ji(A_j) ⊂ A_i for j ≥ i stabilizes. Explicitly, this means that for each i ∈ I, there exists j ≥ i such that for k ≥ j we have φ_ki(A_k) = φ_ji( A_j). If (A_i, φ_ji) is a directed inverse system of modules over a ring R, we say that it is Mittag-Leffler if the underlying inverse system of sets is Mittag-Leffler.

nodes.title: Mittag-Leffler systems · Lemma 0597
nodes.summary: Let (A_i, φ_ji) be a directed inverse system over I. Suppose I is countable. If (A_i, φ_ji) is Mittag-Leffler and the A_i are nonempty, then lim A_i is nonempty.

nodes.title: Mittag-Leffler systems · Lemma 0598
nodes.summary: Let 0 → A_i xrightarrowf_i B_i xrightarrowg_i C_i → 0 be an exact sequence of directed inverse systems of abelian groups over I. Suppose I is countable. If (A_i) is Mittag-Leffler, then 0 → lim A_i → lim B_i → lim C_i→ 0 is exact.

nodes.title: Inverse systems · Lemma 03CA
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let 0 → K_i → L_i → M_i → 0 be short exact sequences of R-modules, i ≥ 1 which fit into maps of short exact sequences xymatrix 0 ar[r] & K_i ar[r] & L_i ar[r] & M_i ar[r] & 0 0 ar[r] & K_i + 1 ar[r] ar[u] & L_i + 1 ar[r] ar[u] & M_i + 1 ar[r] ar[u] & 0 If for every i there exists a c = c(i) ≥ i such that Im(K_c → K_i) = Im(K_j → K_i) for all j ≥ c, then the sequence 0 → lim K_i → lim L_i → lim M_i → 0 is exact.

nodes.title: Mittag-Leffler modules · Definition 059A
nodes.summary: Let (M_i, f_ij) be a directed system of R-modules. We say that (M_i, f_ij) is a Mittag-Leffler directed system of modules if each M_i is an R-module of finite presentation and if for every R-module N, the inverse system (Hom_R(M_i, N), Hom_R(f_ij, N)) is Mittag-Leffler.

nodes.title: Mittag-Leffler modules · Definition 059B
nodes.summary: Let f: M → N and g: M → M' be maps of R-modules. Then we say g dominates f if for any R-module Q, we have Ker(f ⊗_R id_Q) ⊂ Ker(g ⊗_R id_Q).

nodes.title: Mittag-Leffler modules · Lemma 059C
nodes.summary: Let f: M → N and g: M → M' be maps of R-modules. Then g dominates f if and only if for any finitely presented R-module Q, we have Ker(f ⊗_R id_Q) ⊂ Ker(g ⊗_R id_Q).

nodes.title: Mittag-Leffler modules · Lemma 0AUM
nodes.summary: Let f : M → N and g : M → M' be maps of R-modules. Consider the pushout of f and g, xymatrix M ar[r]_f ar[d]_g & N ar[d]^g' M' ar[r]^f' & N' Then g dominates f if and only if f' is universally injective.

nodes.title: Mittag-Leffler modules · Lemma 059D
nodes.summary: Let f: M → N and g: M → M' be maps of R-modules. Suppose Coker(f) is of finite presentation. Then g dominates f if and only if g factors through f, i.e. there exists a module map h: N → M' such that g = h ∘ f.

nodes.title: Mittag-Leffler modules · Proposition 059E
nodes.summary: Let M be an R-module. Let (M_i, f_ij) be a directed system of finitely presented R-modules, indexed by I, such that M = colim M_i. Let f_i: M_i → M be the canonical map. The following are equivalent: • For every finitely presented R-module P and module map f: P → M, there exists a finitely presented R-module Q and a module map g: P → Q such that g and f dominate each other, i.e., Ker(f ⊗_R id_N) = Ker(g ⊗_R id_N) for every R-module N. • For each i ∈ I, there exists j ≥ i…

nodes.title: Mittag-Leffler modules · Definition 059F
nodes.summary: Let M be an R-module. We say that M is Mittag-Leffler if the equivalent conditions of Proposition [Tag 059E] hold.

nodes.title: Mittag-Leffler modules · Lemma 05CN
nodes.summary: If R is a ring and M, N are Mittag-Leffler modules over R, then M ⊗_R N is a Mittag-Leffler module.

nodes.title: Mittag-Leffler modules · Lemma 05CP
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring and M an R-module. Then M is Mittag-Leffler if and only if for every finite free R-module F and module map f: F → M, there exists a finitely presented R-module Q and a module map g : F → Q such that g and f dominate each other, i.e., Ker(f ⊗_R id_N) = Ker(g ⊗_R id_N) for every R-module N.

nodes.title: Mittag-Leffler modules · Lemma 05CQ
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a finite and finitely presented ring map. Let M be an S-module. If M is a Mittag-Leffler module over S then M is a Mittag-Leffler module over R.

nodes.title: Mittag-Leffler modules · Lemma 05CR
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let S = R/I for some finitely generated ideal I. Let M be an S-module. Then M is a Mittag-Leffler module over R if and only if M is a Mittag-Leffler module over S.

nodes.title: Interchanging direct products with tensor · Proposition 059J
nodes.summary: Let M be an R-module. The following are equivalent: • M is finitely generated. • For every family (Q_α)_α ∈ A of R-modules, the canonical map M ⊗_R ( ∏_α Q_α ) → ∏_α (M ⊗_R Q_α) is surjective. • For every R-module Q and every set A, the canonical map M ⊗_R Q^A → (M ⊗_R Q)^A is surjective. • For every set A, the canonical map M ⊗_R R^A → M^A is surjective.

nodes.title: Interchanging direct products with tensor · Proposition 059K
nodes.summary: Let M be an R-module. The following are equivalent: • M is finitely presented. • For every family (Q_α)_α ∈ A of R-modules, the canonical map M ⊗_R ( ∏_α Q_α ) → ∏_α (M ⊗_R Q_α) is bijective. • For every R-module Q and every set A, the canonical map M ⊗_R Q^A → (M ⊗_R Q)^A is bijective. • For every set A, the canonical map M ⊗_R R^A → M^A is bijective.

nodes.title: Interchanging direct products with tensor · Lemma 059L
nodes.summary: Let M be an R-module, P a finitely presented R-module, and f: P → M a map. Let Q be an R-module and suppose x ∈ Ker(P ⊗ Q → M ⊗ Q). Then there exists a finitely presented R-module P' and a map f': P → P' such that f factors through f' and x ∈ Ker(P ⊗ Q → P' ⊗ Q).

nodes.title: Interchanging direct products with tensor · Proposition 059M
nodes.summary: Let M be an R-module. The following are equivalent: • M is Mittag-Leffler. • For every family (Q_α)_α ∈ A of R-modules, the canonical map M ⊗_R ( ∏_α Q_α ) → ∏_α (M ⊗_R Q_α) is injective.

nodes.title: Interchanging direct products with tensor · Lemma 0AS6
nodes.summary: Let M be a flat Mittag-Leffler module over R. Let F be an R-module and let x ∈ F ⊗_R M. Then there exists a smallest submodule F' ⊂ F such that x ∈ F' ⊗_R M. Also, F' is a finite R-module.

nodes.title: Interchanging direct products with tensor · Lemma 059N
nodes.summary: Let 0 → M_1 → M_2 → M_3 → 0 be a universally exact sequence of R-modules. Then: • If M_2 is Mittag-Leffler, then M_1 is Mittag-Leffler. • If M_1 and M_3 are Mittag-Leffler, then M_2 is Mittag-Leffler.

nodes.title: Interchanging direct products with tensor · Lemma 0EGI
nodes.summary: Let M_1 → M_2 → M_3 → 0 be an exact sequence of R-modules. If M_1 is finitely generated and M_2 is Mittag-Leffler, then M_3 is Mittag-Leffler.

nodes.title: Interchanging direct products with tensor · Lemma 0AS7
nodes.summary: If M = colim M_i is the colimit of a directed system of Mittag-Leffler R-modules M_i with universally injective transition maps, then M is Mittag-Leffler.

nodes.title: Interchanging direct products with tensor · Lemma 059P
nodes.summary: If M = bigoplus_i ∈ I M_i is a direct sum of R-modules, then M is Mittag-Leffler if and only if each M_i is Mittag-Leffler.

nodes.title: Interchanging direct products with tensor · Lemma 05CT
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module. If S is Mittag-Leffler as an R-module, and M is flat and Mittag-Leffler as an S-module, then M is Mittag-Leffler as an R-module.

nodes.title: Coherent rings · Definition 05CV
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. • We say M is a coherent module if it is finitely generated and every finitely generated submodule of M is finitely presented over R. • We say R is a coherent ring if it is coherent as a module over itself.

nodes.title: Coherent rings · Lemma 05CW
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. • A finite submodule of a coherent module is coherent. • Let φ : N → M be a homomorphism from a finite module to a coherent module. Then Ker(φ) is finite, Im(φ) is coherent, and Coker(φ) is coherent. • Let φ : N → M be a homomorphism of coherent modules. Then Ker(φ) and Coker(φ) are coherent modules. • Given a short exact sequence of R-modules 0 → M_1 → M_2 → M_3 → 0 if two out of three are coherent so is the third.

nodes.title: Coherent rings · Lemma 05CX
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. If R is coherent, then a module is coherent if and only if it is finitely presented.

nodes.title: Coherent rings · Lemma 05CY
nodes.summary: A Noetherian ring is a coherent ring.

nodes.title: Coherent rings · Proposition 05CZ
nodes.summary: This is [Chase]. Let R be a ring. The following are equivalent • R is coherent, • any product of flat R-modules is flat, and • for every set A the module R^A is flat.

nodes.title: Examples and non-examples of Mittag-Leffler modules · Lemma 059S
nodes.summary: Let M be a flat R-module. The following are equivalent • M is Mittag-Leffler, and • if F is a finite free R-module and x ∈ F ⊗_R M, then there exists a smallest submodule F' of F such that x ∈ F' ⊗_R M.
nodes.section: Examples and non-examples of Mittag-Leffler modules

nodes.title: Examples and non-examples of Mittag-Leffler modules · Lemma 05D0
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring and A a set. Then M = R^A is a flat and Mittag-Leffler R-module.
nodes.section: Examples and non-examples of Mittag-Leffler modules

nodes.title: Examples and non-examples of Mittag-Leffler modules · Lemma 059T
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring and n a positive integer. Then the R-module M = R[[t_1, …, t_n]] is flat and Mittag-Leffler.
nodes.section: Examples and non-examples of Mittag-Leffler modules

nodes.title: Countably generated Mittag-Leffler modules · Lemma 059W
nodes.summary: Let M be an R-module. Write M = colim_i ∈ I M_i where (M_i, f_ij) is a directed system of finitely presented R-modules. If M is Mittag-Leffler and countably generated, then there is a directed countable subset I' ⊂ I such that M ≅ colim_i ∈ I' M_i.

nodes.title: Countably generated Mittag-Leffler modules · Lemma 05D2
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Assume M is Mittag-Leffler and countably generated. For any R-module map f : P → M with P finitely generated there exists an endomorphism α : M → M such that • α : M → M factors through a finitely presented R-module, and • α ∘ f = f.

nodes.title: Characterizing projective modules · Lemma 059X
nodes.summary: Let M be an R-module. If M is flat, Mittag-Leffler, and countably generated, then M is projective.

nodes.title: Characterizing projective modules · Theorem 059Z
nodes.summary: Let M be an R-module. Then M is projective if and only if • M is flat, • M is Mittag-Leffler, • M is a direct sum of countably generated R-modules.

nodes.title: Characterizing projective modules · Lemma 05A0
nodes.summary: Let f: M → N be universally injective map of R-modules. Suppose M is a direct sum of countably generated R-modules, and suppose N is flat and Mittag-Leffler. Then M is projective.

nodes.title: Characterizing projective modules · Lemma 05A1
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring and let M be a R-module. Suppose M is a direct sum of countably generated R-modules, and suppose there is a universally injective map M → R[[t_1, …, t_n]] for some n. Then M is projective.

nodes.title: Ascending properties of modules · Lemma 05A3
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let M be an R-module. Then: • If M is flat, then the S-module M ⊗_R S is flat. • If M is Mittag-Leffler, then the S-module M ⊗_R S is Mittag-Leffler. • If M is a direct sum of countably generated R-modules, then the S-module M ⊗_R S is a direct sum of countably generated S-modules. • If M is projective, then the S-module M ⊗_R S is projective.

nodes.title: Descending properties of modules · Lemma 05A5
nodes.summary: Email from Juan Pablo Acosta Lopez dated 12/20/14. Let R → S be a faithfully flat ring map. Let M be an R-module. If the S-module M ⊗_R S is Mittag-Leffler, then M is Mittag-Leffler.

nodes.title: Descending properties of modules · Lemma 0GVD
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a faithfully flat ring map. Let M be an R-module. If the S-module M ⊗_R S is countably generated, then M is countably generated.

nodes.title: Descending properties of modules · Lemma 05A6
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a faithfully flat ring map. Let M be an R-module. If the S-module M ⊗_R S is countably generated and projective, then M is countably generated and projective.

nodes.title: Descending properties of modules · Lemma 05A7
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map, let M be an R-module, and let Q be a countably generated S-submodule of M ⊗_R S. Then there exists a countably generated R-submodule P of M such that Im(P ⊗_R S → M ⊗_R S) contains Q.

nodes.title: Descending properties of modules · Lemma 05A8
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map, and let M be an R-module. Suppose M ⊗_R S = bigoplus_i ∈ I Q_i is a direct sum of countably generated S-modules Q_i. If N is a countably generated submodule of M, then there is a countably generated submodule N' of M such that N' ⊃ N and Im(N' ⊗_R S → M ⊗_R S) = bigoplus_i ∈ I' Q_i for some subset I' ⊂ I.

nodes.title: Descending properties of modules · Theorem 05A9
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a faithfully flat ring map. Let M be an R-module. If the S-module M ⊗_R S is projective, then M is projective.

nodes.title: Completion · Lemma 0315
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let φ : M → N be a map of R-modules. • If M/IM → N/IN is surjective, then M^wedge → N^wedge is surjective. • If M → N is surjective, then M^wedge → N^wedge is surjective. • If 0 → K → M → N → 0 is a short exact sequence of R-modules and N is flat, then 0 → K^wedge → M^wedge → N^wedge → 0 is a short exact sequence. • The map M ⊗_R R^wedge → M^wedge is surjective for any finite R-module M.

nodes.title: Completion · Definition 0317
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let M be an R-module. We say M is I-adically complete if the map M → M^wedge = lim_n M/I^nM is an isomorphism. We say R is I-adically complete if R is I-adically complete as an R-module.

nodes.title: Completion · Lemma 05GG
nodes.summary: [Matlis]. The slick proof given here is from an email of Bjorn Poonen dated Nov 5, 2016. Let R be a ring. Let I be a finitely generated ideal of R. Let M be an R-module. Then • the completion M^wedge is I-adically complete, and • I^nM^wedge = Ker(M^wedge → M/I^nM) = (I^nM)^wedge for all n ≥ 1. In particular R^wedge is I-adically complete, I^nR^wedge = (I^n)^wedge, and R^wedge/I^nR^wedge = R/I^n.

nodes.title: Completion · Lemma 0BNG
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let 0 → M → N → Q → 0 be an exact sequence of R-modules such that Q is annihilated by a power of I. Then completion produces an exact sequence 0 → M^wedge → N^wedge → Q → 0.

nodes.title: Completion · Lemma 0318
nodes.summary: Taken from an unpublished note of Lenstra and de Smit. Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let M be an R-module. Denote K_n = Ker(M^wedge → M/I^nM). Then M^wedge is I-adically complete if and only if K_n is equal to I^nM^wedge for all n ≥ 1.

nodes.title: Completion · Lemma 05GI
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring, let I ⊂ R be an ideal, and let R^wedge = lim R/I^n. • any element of R^wedge which maps to a unit of R/I is a unit, • any element of 1 + I maps to an invertible element of R^wedge, • any element of 1 + IR^wedge is invertible in R^wedge, and • the ideals IR^wedge and Ker(R^wedge → R/I) are contained in the Jacobson radical of R^wedge.

nodes.title: Completion · Lemma 090S
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let I = (f_1, …, f_r) be a finitely generated ideal. If M → lim M/f_i^nM is surjective for each i, then M → lim M/I^nM is surjective.

nodes.title: Completion · Lemma 090T
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let I ⊂ J ⊂ A be ideals. If M is J-adically complete and I is finitely generated, then M is I-adically complete.

nodes.title: Completion · Lemma 0319
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I, J be ideals of R. Assume there exist integers c, d > 0 such that I^c ⊂ J and J^d ⊂ I. Then completion with respect to I agrees with completion with respect to J for any R-module. In particular an R-module M is I-adically complete if and only if it is J-adically complete.

nodes.title: Completion · Lemma 031A
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I be an ideal of R. Let M be an I-adically complete R-module, and let K ⊂ M be an R-submodule. The following are equivalent • K = ⋂ (K + I^nM) and • M/K is I-adically complete.

nodes.title: Completion · Lemma 031B
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I be an ideal of R. Let M be an R-module. If (a) R is I-adically complete, (b) M is a finite R-module, and (c) ⋂ I^nM = (0), then M is I-adically complete.

nodes.title: Completion · Lemma 031D
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let M be an R-module. Assume • R is I-adically complete, • ⋂_n ≥ 1 I^nM = (0), and • M/IM is a finite R/I-module. Then M is a finite R-module.

nodes.title: Completion for Noetherian rings · Lemma 00MA
nodes.summary: Let I be an ideal of a Noetherian ring R. Denote ^wedge completion with respect to I. • If K → N is an injective map of finite R-modules, then the map on completions K^wedge → N^wedge is injective. • If 0 → K → N → M → 0 is a short exact sequence of finite R-modules, then 0 → K^wedge → N^wedge → M^wedge → 0 is a short exact sequence. • If M is a finite R-module, then M^wedge = M ⊗_R R^wedge.

nodes.title: Completion for Noetherian rings · Lemma 00MB
nodes.summary: Let I be an ideal of a Noetherian ring R. Denote ^wedge completion with respect to I. • The ring map R → R^wedge is flat. • The functor M ↦ M^wedge is exact on the category of finitely generated R-modules.

nodes.title: Completion for Noetherian rings · Lemma 00MC
nodes.summary: Let I be an ideal of a Noetherian ring R. Denote R^wedge the completion of R with respect to I. If I is contained in the Jacobson radical of R, then the ring map R → R^wedge is faithfully flat. In particular, if (R, m) is a Noetherian local ring, then the completion lim_n R/ m^n is faithfully flat.

nodes.title: Completion for Noetherian rings · Lemma 031C
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let I be an ideal of R. Let M be an R-module. Then the completion M^wedge of M with respect to I is I-adically complete, I^n M^wedge = (I^nM)^wedge, and M^wedge/I^nM^wedge = M/I^nM.

nodes.title: Completion for Noetherian rings · Lemma 05GH
nodes.summary: Let I be an ideal of a ring R. Assume • R/I is a Noetherian ring, • I is finitely generated. Then the completion R^wedge of R with respect to I is a Noetherian ring complete with respect to IR^wedge.

nodes.title: Completion for Noetherian rings · Lemma 0316
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let I be an ideal of R. The completion R^wedge of R with respect to I is Noetherian.

nodes.title: Completion for Noetherian rings · Lemma 0394
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a local homomorphism of local rings (R, m) and (S, n). Let R^wedge, resp. S^wedge be the completion of R, resp. S with respect to m, resp. n. If m and n are finitely generated and dim_kappa( m) S/ mS < ∞, then • S^wedge is equal to the m-adic completion of S, and • S^wedge is a finite R^wedge-module.

nodes.title: Completion for Noetherian rings · Lemma 07N9
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let R → S be a finite ring map. Let p ⊂ R be a prime and let q_1, …, q_m be the primes of S lying over p (Lemma [Tag 05DR]). Then R_ p^wedge ⊗_R S = (S_ p)^wedge = S_ q_1^wedge × … × S_ q_m^wedge where the (S_ p)^wedge is the completion with respect to p and the local rings R_ p and S_ q_i are completed with respect to their maximal ideals.

nodes.title: Completion for Noetherian rings · Lemma 05D3
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let 0 → K → P → M → 0 be a short exact sequence of R-modules. If M is flat over R and M/IM is a projective R/I-module, then the sequence of I-adic completions 0 → K^wedge → P^wedge → M^wedge → 0 is a split exact sequence.

nodes.title: Completion for Noetherian rings · Lemma 0DYC
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian ring. Let I, J ⊂ A be ideals. If A is I-adically complete and A/I is J-adically complete, then A is J-adically complete.

nodes.title: Taking limits of modules · Lemma 0G1Q
nodes.summary: Let I ⊂ A be a finitely generated ideal of a ring. Let (M_n) be an inverse system of A-modules with I^n M_n = 0. Then M = lim M_n is I-adically complete.

nodes.title: Taking limits of modules · Lemma 09B8
nodes.summary: Let I ⊂ A be a finitely generated ideal of a ring. Let (M_n) be an inverse system of A-modules with M_n = M_n + 1/I^nM_n + 1. Set M = lim M_n. Then M/I^nM = M_n and M is I-adically complete.

nodes.title: Taking limits of modules · Lemma 0EKC
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian graded ring. Let I ⊂ A_+ be a homogeneous ideal. Let (N_n) be an inverse system of finite graded A-modules with N_n = N_n + 1/I^n N_n + 1. Then there is a finite graded A-module N such that N_n = N/I^nN as graded modules for all n.

nodes.title: Taking limits of modules · Lemma 0EKD
nodes.summary: Let A be a graded ring. Let I ⊂ A_+ be a homogeneous ideal. Denote A' = lim A/I^n. Let (G_n) be an inverse system of graded A-modules with G_n annihilated by I^n. Let M be a graded A-module and let φ_n : M → G_n be a compatible system of graded A-module maps. If the induced map φ : M ⊗_A A' → lim G_n is an isomorphism, then M_d → lim G_n, d is an isomorphism for all d ∈ Z.

nodes.title: Criteria for flatness · Lemma 00ME
nodes.summary: Suppose that R → S is a local homomorphism of local rings with S Noetherian. Denote m the maximal ideal of R. Let M be a flat R-module and N a finite S-module. Let u : N → M be a map of R-modules. If overlineu : N/ m N → M/ m M is injective then u is injective. In this case M/u(N) is flat over R.

nodes.title: Criteria for flatness · Lemma 00MF
nodes.summary: Suppose that R → S is a flat and local ring homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Denote m the maximal ideal of R. Suppose f ∈ S is a nonzerodivisor in S/ mS. Then S/fS is flat over R, and f is a nonzerodivisor in S.

nodes.title: Criteria for flatness · Lemma 00MG
nodes.summary: Suppose that R → S is a flat and local ring homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Denote m the maximal ideal of R. Suppose f_1, …, f_c is a sequence of elements of S such that the images overlinef_1, …, overlinef_c form a regular sequence in S/ mS. Then f_1, …, f_c is a regular sequence in S and each of the quotients S/(f_1, …, f_i) is flat over R.

nodes.title: Criteria for flatness · Lemma 00MH
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Let m be the maximal ideal of R. Let M be a nonzero finite S-module. Suppose that (a) M/ mM is a free S/ mS-module, and (b) M is flat over R. Then M is free and S is flat over R.

nodes.title: Criteria for flatness · Lemma 00MI
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a local homomorphism of local Noetherian rings. Let m be the maximal ideal of R. Let 0 → F_e → F_e-1 → … → F_0 be a finite complex of finite S-modules. Assume that each F_i is R-flat, and that the complex 0 → F_e/ m F_e → F_e-1/ m F_e-1 → … → F_0 / m F_0 is exact. Then 0 → F_e → F_e-1 → … → F_0 is exact, and moreover the module Coker(F_1 → F_0) is R-flat.

nodes.title: Criteria for flatness · Lemma 00MJ
nodes.summary: Let R be a local ring with maximal ideal m and residue field kappa = R/ m. Let M be an R-module. If Tor_1^R(kappa, M) = 0, then for every finite length R-module N we have Tor_1^R(N, M) = 0.

nodes.title: Local criterion for flatness · Lemma 00MK
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a local homomorphism of local Noetherian rings. Let m be the maximal ideal of R, and let kappa = R/ m. Let M be a finite S-module. If Tor_1^R(kappa, M) = 0, then M is flat over R.

nodes.title: Criteria for flatness · Lemma 051C
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let M be an R-module. If M/IM is flat over R/I and Tor_1^R(R/I, M) = 0 then • M/I^nM is flat over R/I^n for all n ≥ 1, and • for any module N which is annihilated by I^m for some m ≥ 0 we have Tor_1^R(N, M) = 0. In particular, if I is nilpotent, then M is flat over R.

nodes.title: Criteria for flatness · Lemma 0AS8
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let M be an R-module. • If M/IM is flat over R/I and M ⊗_R I/I^2 → IM/I^2M is injective, then M/I^2M is flat over R/I^2. • If M/IM is flat over R/I and M ⊗_R I^n/I^n + 1 → I^nM/I^n + 1M is injective for n = 1, …, k, then M/I^k + 1M is flat over R/I^k + 1.

nodes.title: Variant of the local criterion · Lemma 00ML
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Let I not = R be an ideal in R. Let M be a finite S-module. If Tor_1^R(M, R/I) = 0 and M/IM is flat over R/I, then M is flat over R.

nodes.title: Criteria for flatness · Lemma 0523
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let M be an S-module. Assume • R is a Noetherian ring, • S is a Noetherian ring, • M is a finite S-module, and • for each n ≥ 1 the module M/I^n M is flat over R/I^n. Then for every q ∈ V(IS) the localization M_ q is flat over R. In particular, if S is local and IS is contained in its maximal ideal, then M is flat over R.

nodes.title: Criteria for flatness · Lemma 00MM
nodes.summary: Let R → R' → R" be ring maps. Let M be an R-module. Suppose that M ⊗_R R' is flat over R'. Then the natural map Tor_1^R(M, R') ⊗_R' R" → Tor_1^R(M, R") is onto.

nodes.title: Criteria for flatness · Lemma 00MN
nodes.summary: Let R → R' be a ring map. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal and I' = IR'. Let M be an R-module and set M' = M ⊗_R R'. The natural map Tor_1^R(R'/I', M) → Tor_1^R'(R'/I', M') is surjective.

nodes.title: Criteria for flatness · Lemma 00MO
nodes.summary: Let xymatrix S ar[r] & S' R ar[r] ar[u] & R' ar[u] be a commutative diagram of local homomorphisms of local Noetherian rings. Let I ⊂ R be a proper ideal. Let M be a finite S-module. Denote I' = IR' and M' = M ⊗_S S'. Assume that • S' is a localization of the tensor product S ⊗_R R', • M/IM is flat over R/I, • Tor_1^R(M, R/I) → Tor_1^R'(M', R'/I') is zero. Then M' is flat over R'.

nodes.title: Crit\`ere de platitude par fibres; Noetherian case · Lemma 00MP
nodes.summary: Let R, S, S' be Noetherian local rings and let R → S → S' be local ring homomorphisms. Let m ⊂ R be the maximal ideal. Let M be an S'-module. Assume • The module M is finite over S'. • The module M is not zero. • The module M/ m M is a flat S/ m S-module. • The module M is a flat R-module. Then S is flat over R and M is a flat S-module.

nodes.title: Criteria for flatness · Lemma 0H7N
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring, let M be an A-module, and let f ∈ A. If • f is a nonzerodivisor on A and M, • M_f is a flat A_f-module, and • M/fM is a flat A/fA-module, Then M is a flat A-module. Same with "flat" replaced by "faithfully flat".

nodes.title: Criteria for flatness · Lemma 0H7P
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring, let M be an A-module. Let I = (f_1, …, f_r) be an ideal of A generated by r ≥ 1 elements. If • M_f_i is a flat A_f_i-module for i = 1, …, r, • M/IM is a flat A/I-module, • Tor_i^A(M, A/I) = 0 for i = 1, …, r + 1. Then M is a flat A-module. Same with "flat" replaced by "faithfully flat".

nodes.title: Base change and flatness · Lemma 00MQ
nodes.summary: Let xymatrix S ar[r] & S' R ar[r] ar[u] & R' ar[u] be a commutative diagram of local homomorphisms of local rings. Assume that S' is a localization of the tensor product S ⊗_R R'. Let M be an S-module and set M' = S' ⊗_S M. • If M is flat over R then M' is flat over R'. • If M' is flat over R' and R → R' is flat then M is flat over R. In particular we have • [(3)] If S is flat over R then S' is flat over R'. • [(4)] If R' → S' and R → R' are flat then S is flat over R.

nodes.title: Base change and flatness · Lemma 0GEB
nodes.summary: Consider a commutative diagram of local rings and local homomorphisms xymatrix S ar[r] & S' R ar[r] ar[u] & R' ar[u] Let M be a finite S-module. Assume that • the horizontal arrows are flat ring maps • M is flat over R, • m_R R' = m_R', • R' and S' are Noetherian. Then M' = M ⊗_S S' is flat over R'.

nodes.title: Flatness criteria over Artinian rings · Lemma 051F
nodes.summary: Let (R, m) be a local ring with nilpotent maximal ideal m. Let M be a flat R-module. If A is a set and x_α ∈ M, α ∈ A is a collection of elements of M, then the following are equivalent: • (overlinex_α)_α ∈ A forms a basis for the vector space M/ mM over R/ m, and • (x_α)_α ∈ A forms a basis for M over R.

nodes.title: Flatness criteria over Artinian rings · Lemma 051G
nodes.summary: Let R be a local ring with nilpotent maximal ideal. Let M be an R-module. The following are equivalent • M is flat over R, • M is a free R-module, and • M is a projective R-module.

nodes.title: Flatness criteria over Artinian rings · Lemma 051H
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let M be an R-module. Let A be a set and let x_α ∈ M, α ∈ A be a collection of elements of M. Assume • I is nilpotent, • (overlinex_α)_α ∈ A forms a basis for M/IM over R/I, and • Tor_1^R(R/I, M) = 0. Then M is free on (x_α)_α ∈ A over R.

nodes.title: Flatness criteria over Artinian rings · Lemma 051I
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → R' be a ring map. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let M be an R-module. Assume • M/IM is flat over R/I, and • R' ⊗_R M is flat over R'. Set I_2 = φ^-1(φ(I^2)R'). Then M/I_2M is flat over R/I_2.

nodes.title: Flatness criteria over Artinian rings · Lemma 051J
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → R' be a ring map. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let M be an R-module. Assume • I is nilpotent, • R → R' is injective, • M/IM is flat over R/I, and • R' ⊗_R M is flat over R'. Then M is flat over R.

nodes.title: Flatness criteria over Artinian rings · Lemma 051K
nodes.summary: Let R be an Artinian local ring. Let M be an R-module. Let I ⊂ R be a proper ideal. The following are equivalent • M is flat over R, and • M/IM is flat over R/I and Tor_1^R(R/I, M) = 0.

nodes.title: Flatness criteria over Artinian rings · Lemma 051L
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let M be an R-module. Assume • R is Artinian • R → S is injective, and • M ⊗_R S is a flat S-module. Then M is a flat R-module.

nodes.title: Crit\`ere de platitude par fibres: Nilpotent case · Lemma 06A5
nodes.summary: Let xymatrix S ar[rr] & & S' & R ar[lu] ar[ru] be a commutative diagram in the category of rings. Let I ⊂ R be a nilpotent ideal and M an S'-module. Assume • The module M/IM is a flat S/IS-module. • The module M is a flat R-module. Then M is a flat S-module and S_ q is flat over R for every q ⊂ S such that M ⊗_S kappa( q) is nonzero.

nodes.title: What makes a complex exact? · Lemma 00MT
nodes.summary: Suppose R is a ring. Let … xrightarrowφ_i + 1 R^n_i xrightarrowφ_i R^n_i-1 xrightarrowφ_i-1 … be a complex of finite free R-modules. Suppose that for some i some matrix coefficient of the map φ_i is invertible. Then the displayed complex is isomorphic to the direct sum of a complex … → R^n_i + 2 xrightarrowφ_i + 2 R^n_i + 1 → R^n_i - 1 → R^n_i - 1 - 1 → R^n_i - 2 xrightarrowφ_i - 2 R^n_i - 3 → … and the complex … → 0 → R → R → 0 → … where the map R → R is the identity map.

nodes.title: What makes a complex exact? · Lemma 00MY
nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 00MS]. Suppose R is a local Noetherian ring with maximal ideal m. Assume m ∈ Ass(R), in other words R has depth 0. Suppose that 0 → R^n_e → R^n_e-1 → … → R^n_0 is exact at R^n_e, …, R^n_1. Then the complex is isomorphic to a direct sum of trivial complexes.

nodes.title: What makes a complex exact? · Lemma 00MU
nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 00MS]. Let R be a Artinian local ring. Suppose that 0 → R^n_e → R^n_e-1 → … → R^n_0 is exact at R^n_e, …, R^n_1. Then the complex is isomorphic to a direct sum of trivial complexes.

nodes.title: What makes a complex exact? · Definition 00MV
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Suppose that φ : R^m → R^n is a map of finite free modules. • The rank of φ is the maximal r such that wedge^r φ : wedge^r R^m → wedge^r R^n is nonzero. • We let I(φ) ⊂ R be the ideal generated by the r × r minors of the matrix of φ, where r is the rank as defined above.

nodes.title: What makes a complex exact? · Lemma 00MW
nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 00MS], suppose the complex is isomorphic to a direct sum of trivial complexes. Then we have • the maps φ_i have rank r_i = n_i - n_i + 1 + … + (-1)^e-i-1 n_e-1 + (-1)^e-i n_e, • for all i, 1 ≤ i ≤ e - 1 we have rank(φ_i + 1) + rank(φ_i) = n_i, • each I(φ_i) = R.

nodes.title: What makes a complex exact? · Lemma 00MZ
nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 00MS]. Suppose R is a local ring with maximal ideal m. Suppose that 0 → R^n_e → R^n_e-1 → … → R^n_0 is exact at R^n_e, …, R^n_1. Let x ∈ m be a nonzerodivisor. The complex 0 → (R/xR)^n_e → … → (R/xR)^n_1 is exact at (R/xR)^n_e, …, (R/xR)^n_2.

nodes.title: Acyclicity lemma · Lemma 00N0
nodes.summary: [Peskine-Szpiro] Let R be a local Noetherian ring. Let 0 → M_e → M_e-1 → … → M_0 be a complex of finite R-modules. Assume depth(M_i) ≥ i. Let i be the largest index such that the complex is not exact at M_i. If i > 0 then Ker(M_i → M_i-1)/Im(M_i + 1 → M_i) has depth ≥ 1.

nodes.title: What makes a complex exact? · Proposition 00N1
nodes.summary: [WhatExact] In Situation [Tag 00MS], suppose R is a local Noetherian ring. The following are equivalent • 0 → R^n_e → R^n_e-1 → … → R^n_0 is exact at R^n_e, …, R^n_1, and • for all i, 1 ≤ i ≤ e the following two conditions are satisfied: • rank(φ_i) = r_i where r_i = n_i - n_i + 1 + … + (-1)^e-i-1 n_e-1 + (-1)^e-i n_e, • I(φ_i) = R, or I(φ_i) contains a regular sequence of length i.

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay modules · Definition 00N3
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring. Let M be a finite R-module. We say M is Cohen-Macaulay if dim(Supp(M)) = depth(M).

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay modules · Lemma 00N4
nodes.summary: Notation and assumptions as above. If g is good with respect to (M, f_1, …, f_d), then (a) g is a nonzerodivisor on M, and (b) M/gM is Cohen-Macaulay with maximal regular sequence f_1, …, f_d - 1.

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay modules · Lemma 00N5
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring. Let M be a Cohen-Macaulay module over R. Suppose g ∈ m is such that dim(Supp(M) ∩ V(g)) = dim(Supp(M)) - 1. Then (a) g is a nonzerodivisor on M, and (b) M/gM is Cohen-Macaulay of depth one less.

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay modules · Proposition 00N6
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring, with maximal ideal m. Let M be a Cohen-Macaulay module over R whose support has dimension d. Suppose that g_1, …, g_c are elements of m such that dim(Supp(M/(g_1, …, g_c)M)) = d - c. Then g_1, …, g_c is an M-regular sequence, and can be extended to a maximal M-regular sequence.

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay modules · Lemma 0C6G
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m. Let M be a finite R-module. Let x ∈ m be a nonzerodivisor on M. Then M is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if M/xM is Cohen-Macaulay.

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay modules · Lemma 0AAD
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a surjective homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Let N be a finite S-module. Then N is Cohen-Macaulay as an S-module if and only if N is Cohen-Macaulay as an R-module.

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay modules · Lemma 0BUS
nodes.summary: [EGA] Let R be a Noetherian local ring. Let M be a finite Cohen-Macaulay R-module. If p ∈ Ass(M), then dim(R/ p) = dim(Supp(M)) and p is a minimal prime in the support of M. In particular, M has no embedded associated primes.

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay modules · Definition 00NF
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring. A finite module M over R is called a maximal Cohen-Macaulay module if depth(M) = dim(R).

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay modules · Lemma 0AAE
nodes.summary: In a local Cohen-Macaulay ring, any maximal chain of prime ideals has length equal to the dimension. Let R be a Noetherian local ring. Assume there exists a Cohen-Macaulay module M with Spec(R) = Supp(M). Then any maximal chain of prime ideals p_0 ⊂ p_1 ⊂ … ⊂ p_n has length n = dim(R).

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay modules · Lemma 0AAF
nodes.summary: Suppose R is a Noetherian local ring. Assume there exists a Cohen-Macaulay module M with Spec(R) = Supp(M). Then for a prime p ⊂ R we have dim(R) = dim(R_ p) + dim(R/ p).

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay modules · Lemma 0AAG
nodes.summary: Suppose R is a Noetherian local ring. Let M be a Cohen-Macaulay module over R. For any prime p ⊂ R the module M_ p is Cohen-Macaulay over R_ p.

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay modules · Definition 0AAH
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let M be a finite R-module. We say M is Cohen-Macaulay if M_ p is a Cohen-Macaulay module over R_ p for all primes p of R.

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay modules · Lemma 0AAI
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let M be a Cohen-Macaulay module over R. Then M ⊗_R R[x_1, …, x_n] is a Cohen-Macaulay module over R[x_1, …, x_n].

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay rings · Definition 00N8
nodes.summary: A Noetherian local ring R is called Cohen-Macaulay if it is Cohen-Macaulay as a module over itself.

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay rings · Lemma 02JN
