nodes.summary: Regular sequences in Cohen-Macaulay local rings are characterized by cutting out something of the correct dimension. Let R be a Noetherian local Cohen-Macaulay ring with maximal ideal m . Let x_1, …, x_c ∈ m be elements. Then x_1, …, x_c is a regular sequence ⇔ dim(R/(x_1, …, x_c)) = dim(R) - c If so x_1, …, x_c can be extended to a regular sequence of length dim(R) and each quotient R/(x_1, …, x_i) is a Cohen-Macaulay ring of dimension dim(R) - i.

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay rings · Lemma 00N9
nodes.summary: Let R be Noetherian local. Suppose R is Cohen-Macaulay of dimension d. Any maximal chain of ideals p_0 ⊂ p_1 ⊂ … ⊂ p_n has length n = d.

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay rings · Lemma 00NA
nodes.summary: Suppose R is a Noetherian local Cohen-Macaulay ring of dimension d. For any prime p ⊂ R we have dim(R) = dim(R_ p) + dim(R/ p).

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay rings · Lemma 00NB
nodes.summary: Suppose R is a Cohen-Macaulay local ring. For any prime p ⊂ R the ring R_ p is Cohen-Macaulay as well.

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay rings · Definition 00NC
nodes.summary: A Noetherian ring R is called Cohen-Macaulay if all its local rings are Cohen-Macaulay.

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay rings · Lemma 00ND
nodes.summary: Suppose R is a Noetherian Cohen-Macaulay ring. Any polynomial algebra over R is Cohen-Macaulay.

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay rings · Lemma 00NE
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local Cohen-Macaulay ring of dimension d. Let 0 → K → R^⊕ n → M → 0 be an exact sequence of R-modules. Then either M = 0, or depth(K) > depth(M), or depth(K) = depth(M) = d.

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay rings · Lemma 00NG
nodes.summary: Let R be a local Noetherian Cohen-Macaulay ring of dimension d. Let M be a finite R-module of depth e. There exists an exact complex 0 → K → F_d-e-1 → … → F_0 → M → 0 with each F_i finite free and K maximal Cohen-Macaulay.

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay rings · Lemma 06LC
nodes.summary: Let φ : A → B be a map of local rings. Assume that B is Noetherian and Cohen-Macaulay and that m_B = sqrtφ( m_A) B. Then there exists a sequence of elements f_1, …, f_dim(B) in A such that φ(f_1), …, φ(f_dim(B)) is a regular sequence in B.

nodes.title: Catenary rings · Definition 00NI
nodes.summary: A ring R is said to be catenary if for any pair of prime ideals p ⊂ q, there exists an integer bounding the lengths of all finite chains of prime ideals p = p_0 ⊂ p_1 ⊂ … ⊂ p_e = q and all maximal such chains have the same length.

nodes.title: Catenary rings · Lemma 02IH
nodes.summary: A ring R is catenary if and only if the topological space Spec(R) is catenary (see Topology, Definition [Tag 02I1]).

nodes.title: Catenary rings · Definition 00NL
nodes.summary: A Noetherian ring R is said to be universally catenary if every R-algebra of finite type is catenary.

nodes.title: Catenary rings · Lemma 00NJ
nodes.summary: Any localization of a catenary ring is catenary. Any localization of a Noetherian universally catenary ring is universally catenary.

nodes.title: Catenary rings · Lemma 0ECE
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian universally catenary ring. Any A-algebra essentially of finite type over A is universally catenary.

nodes.title: Catenary rings · Lemma 0AUN
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. The following are equivalent • R is catenary, • R_ p is catenary for all prime ideals p, • R_ m is catenary for all maximal ideals m. Assume R is Noetherian. The following are equivalent • R is universally catenary, • R_ p is universally catenary for all prime ideals p, • R_ m is universally catenary for all maximal ideals m.

nodes.title: Catenary rings · Lemma 00NK
nodes.summary: Any quotient of a catenary ring is catenary. Any quotient of a Noetherian universally catenary ring is universally catenary.

nodes.title: Catenary rings · Lemma 0AUP
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. • R is catenary if and only if R/ p is catenary for every minimal prime p. • R is universally catenary if and only if R/ p is universally catenary for every minimal prime p.

nodes.title: Catenary rings · Lemma 00NM
nodes.summary: A Noetherian Cohen-Macaulay ring is universally catenary. More generally, if R is a Noetherian ring and M is a Cohen-Macaulay R-module with Supp(M) = Spec(R), then R is universally catenary.

nodes.title: Catenary rings · Lemma 0ECF
nodes.summary: Let (A, m) be a Noetherian local ring. The following are equivalent • A is catenary, and • p ↦ dim(A/ p) is a dimension function on Spec(A).

nodes.title: Regular local rings · Lemma 00NO
nodes.summary: Let (R, m, kappa) be a regular local ring of dimension d. The graded ring bigoplus m^n / m^n + 1 is isomorphic to the graded polynomial algebra kappa[X_1, …, X_d].

nodes.title: Regular local rings · Lemma 00NP
nodes.summary: Any regular local ring is a domain.

nodes.title: Regular local rings · Lemma 00NQ
nodes.summary: Let R be a regular local ring and let x_1, …, x_d be a minimal set of generators for the maximal ideal m. Then x_1, …, x_d is a regular sequence, and each R/(x_1, …, x_c) is a regular local ring of dimension d - c. In particular R is Cohen-Macaulay.

nodes.title: Regular local rings · Lemma 00NR
nodes.summary: Let R be a regular local ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal such that R/I is a regular local ring as well. Then there exists a minimal set of generators x_1, …, x_d for the maximal ideal m of R such that I = (x_1, …, x_c) for some 0 ≤ c ≤ d.

nodes.title: Regular local rings · Lemma 00NS
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring. Let x ∈ m. Let M be a finite R-module such that x is a nonzerodivisor on M and M/xM is free over R/xR. Then M is free over R.

nodes.title: Regular local rings · Lemma 00NT
nodes.summary: Let R be a regular local ring. Any maximal Cohen-Macaulay module over R is free.

nodes.title: Regular local rings · Lemma 00NU
nodes.summary: Suppose R is a Noetherian local ring. Let x ∈ m be a nonzerodivisor such that R/xR is a regular local ring. Then R is a regular local ring. More generally, if x_1, …, x_r is a regular sequence in R such that R/(x_1, …, x_r) is a regular local ring, then R is a regular local ring.

nodes.title: Regular local rings · Lemma 07DX
nodes.summary: Let (R_i, φ_ii') be a directed system of local rings whose transition maps are local ring maps. If each R_i is a regular local ring and R = colim R_i is Noetherian, then R is a regular local ring.

nodes.title: Epimorphisms of rings · Lemma 04VN
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. The following are equivalent • R → S is an epimorphism, • the two ring maps S → S ⊗_R S are equal, • either of the ring maps S → S ⊗_R S is an isomorphism, and • the ring map S ⊗_R S → S is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Epimorphisms of rings · Lemma 04VP
nodes.summary: The composition of two epimorphisms of rings is an epimorphism.

nodes.title: Epimorphisms of rings · Lemma 04VQ
nodes.summary: If R → S is an epimorphism of rings and R → R' is any ring map, then R' → R' ⊗_R S is an epimorphism.

nodes.title: Epimorphisms of rings · Lemma 04VR
nodes.summary: If A → B → C are ring maps and A → C is an epimorphism, so is B → C.

nodes.title: Epimorphisms of rings · Lemma 04VS
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. The following are equivalent: • R → S is an epimorphism, and • R_ p → S_ p is an epimorphism for each prime p of R.

nodes.title: Epimorphisms of rings · Lemma 04VT
nodes.summary: A ring map is surjective if and only if it is a finite epimorphism. Let R → S be a ring map. The following are equivalent • R → S is an epimorphism and finite, and • R → S is surjective.

nodes.title: Epimorphisms of rings · Lemma 04VU
nodes.summary: A faithfully flat epimorphism is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Epimorphisms of rings · Lemma 04VV
nodes.summary: If k → S is an epimorphism and k is a field, then S = k or S = 0.

nodes.title: Epimorphisms of rings · Lemma 04VW
nodes.summary: Let R → S be an epimorphism of rings. Then • Spec(S) → Spec(R) is injective, and • for q ⊂ S lying over p ⊂ R we have kappa( p) = kappa( q).

nodes.title: Epimorphisms of rings · Lemma 04VX
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M, N be R-modules. Let (x_i)_i ∈ I be a set of generators of M. Let (y_j)_j ∈ J be a set of generators of N. Let (m_j)_j ∈ J be a family of elements of M with m_j = 0 for all but finitely many j. Then ∑_j ∈ J m_j ⊗ y_j = 0 in M ⊗_R N is equivalent to the following: There exist a_i, j ∈ R with a_i, j = 0 for all but finitely many pairs (i, j) such that m_j & = ∑_i ∈ I a_i, j x_i for all j ∈ J, 0 & = ∑_j ∈ J a_i, j y_j for all i ∈ I.

nodes.title: Epimorphisms of rings · Lemma 04VY
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Let g ∈ S. The following are equivalent: • g ⊗ 1 = 1 ⊗ g in S ⊗_R S, and • there exist n ≥ 0 and elements y_i, z_j ∈ S and x_i, j ∈ R for 1 ≤ i, j ≤ n such that • g = ∑_i, j ≤ n x_i, j y_i z_j, • for each j we have ∑ x_i, jy_i ∈ φ(R), and • for each i we have ∑ x_i, jz_j ∈ φ(R).

nodes.title: Epimorphisms of rings · Lemma 04W0
nodes.summary: Let R → S be an epimorphism of rings. Then the cardinality of S is at most the cardinality of R. In a formula: |S| ≤ |R|.

nodes.title: Epimorphisms of rings · Lemma 08YS
nodes.summary: For a ring homomorphism R → S the following are equivalent • R → S is an epimorphism of rings, • for any S-modules N_1, N_2 we have Hom_S(N_1, N_2) = Hom_R(N_1, N_2), and • the restriction functor Mod_S → Mod_R is fully faithful.

nodes.title: Pure ideals · Definition 04PR
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. We say that I ⊂ R is pure if the quotient ring R/I is flat over R.

nodes.title: Pure ideals · Lemma 04PS
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. The following are equivalent: • I is pure, • for every ideal J ⊂ R we have J ∩ I = IJ, • for every finitely generated ideal J ⊂ R we have J ∩ I = JI, • for every x ∈ R we have (x) ∩ I = xI, • for every x ∈ I we have x = yx for some y ∈ I, • for every x_1, …, x_n ∈ I there exists a y ∈ I such that x_i = yx_i for all i = 1, …, n, • for every prime p of R we have IR_ p = 0 or IR_ p = R_ p, • Supp(I) = Spec(R) setminus V(I), • I is the…

nodes.title: Pure ideals · Lemma 04PT
nodes.summary: Pure ideals are determined by their vanishing locus. Let R be a ring. If I, J ⊂ R are pure ideals, then V(I) = V(J) implies I = J.

nodes.title: Pure ideals · Lemma 04PU
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. The rule I ↦ V(I) determines a bijection (I ⊂ R pure) ↔ (Z ⊂ Spec(R) closed and closed under generalizations)

nodes.title: Pure ideals · Lemma 05KK
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. The following are equivalent • I is pure and finitely generated, • I is generated by an idempotent, • I is pure and V(I) is open, and • R/I is a projective R-module.

nodes.title: Pure ideals · Lemma 052U
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. The following are equivalent: • every Z ⊂ Spec(R) which is closed and closed under generalizations is also open, and • any finite flat R-module is finite locally free.

nodes.title: Schanuel's lemma · Lemma 00O3
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Suppose that 0 → K xrightarrowc_1 P_1 xrightarrowp_1 M → 0 and 0 → L xrightarrowc_2 P_2 xrightarrowp_2 M → 0 are two short exact sequences, with P_i projective. Then K ⊕ P_2 ≅ L ⊕ P_1. More precisely, there exist a commutative diagram xymatrix 0 ar[r] & K ⊕ P_2 ar[r]_(c_1, id) ar[d] & P_1 ⊕ P_2 ar[r]_(p_1, 0) ar[d] & M ar[r] ar@=[d] & 0 0 ar[r] & P_1 ⊕ L ar[r]^(id, c_2) & P_1 ⊕ P_2 ar[r]^(0, p_2) & M ar[r] & 0 whose vertical arrows…

nodes.title: Rings of finite global dimension · Definition 00O4
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. We say M has finite projective dimension if it has a finite length resolution by projective R-modules. The minimal length of such a resolution is called the projective dimension of M.

nodes.title: Rings of finite global dimension · Lemma 00O5
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Suppose that M is an R-module of projective dimension d. Suppose that F_e → F_e-1 → … → F_0 → M → 0 is exact with F_i projective and e ≥ d - 1. Then the kernel of F_e → F_e-1 is projective (or the kernel of F_0 → M is projective in case e = 0).

nodes.title: Rings of finite global dimension · Lemma 0CXC
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Let d ≥ 0. The following are equivalent • M has projective dimension ≤ d, • there exists a resolution 0 → P_d → P_d - 1 → … → P_0 → M → 0 with P_i projective, • for some resolution … → P_2 → P_1 → P_0 → M → 0 with P_i projective we have Ker(P_d - 1 → P_d - 2) is projective if d ≥ 2, or Ker(P_0 → M) is projective if d = 1, or M is projective if d = 0, • for any resolution … → P_2 → P_1 → P_0 → M → 0 with P_i projective we have Ker(P_d…

nodes.title: Rings of finite global dimension · Lemma 0CXD
nodes.summary: Let R be a local ring. Let M be an R-module. Let d ≥ 0. The equivalent conditions (1) -- (4) of Lemma [Tag 0CXC] are also equivalent to • [(5)] there exists a resolution 0 → P_d → P_d - 1 → … → P_0 → M → 0 with P_i free.

nodes.title: Rings of finite global dimension · Lemma 0CXE
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let M be a finite R-module. Let d ≥ 0. The equivalent conditions (1) -- (4) of Lemma [Tag 0CXC] are also equivalent to • [(6)] there exists a resolution 0 → P_d → P_d - 1 → … → P_0 → M → 0 with P_i finite projective.

nodes.title: Rings of finite global dimension · Lemma 0CXF
nodes.summary: Let R be a local Noetherian ring. Let M be a finite R-module. Let d ≥ 0. The equivalent conditions (1) -- (4) of Lemma [Tag 0CXC], condition (5) of Lemma [Tag 0CXD], and condition (6) of Lemma [Tag 0CXE] are also equivalent to • [(7)] there exists a resolution 0 → F_d → F_d - 1 → … → F_0 → M → 0 with F_i finite free.

nodes.title: Rings of finite global dimension · Lemma 065R
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Let n ≥ 0. The following are equivalent • M has projective dimension ≤ n, • Ext^i_R(M, N) = 0 for all R-modules N and all i ≥ n + 1, and • Ext^n + 1_R(M, N) = 0 for all R-modules N.

nodes.title: Rings of finite global dimension · Lemma 065S
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let 0 → M' → M → M" → 0 be a short exact sequence of R-modules. • If M has projective dimension ≤ n and M" has projective dimension ≤ n + 1, then M' has projective dimension ≤ n. • If M' and M" have projective dimension ≤ n then M has projective dimension ≤ n. • If M' has projective dimension ≤ n and M has projective dimension ≤ n + 1 then M" has projective dimension ≤ n + 1.

nodes.title: Rings of finite global dimension · Definition 00O6
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. The ring R is said to have finite global dimension if there exists an integer n such that every R-module has a resolution by projective R-modules of length at most n. The minimal such n is then called the global dimension of R.

nodes.title: Rings of finite global dimension · Lemma 0D1U
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Suppose we have a module M = ⋃_e ∈ E M_e where the M_e are submodules well-ordered by inclusion. Assume the quotients M_e/⋃_e' < e M_e' have projective dimension ≤ n. Then M has projective dimension ≤ n.

nodes.title: Rings of finite global dimension · Lemma 065T
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. The following are equivalent • R has finite global dimension ≤ n, • every finite R-module has projective dimension ≤ n, and • every cyclic R-module R/I has projective dimension ≤ n.

nodes.title: Rings of finite global dimension · Lemma 00O8
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Let S ⊂ R be a multiplicative subset. • If M has projective dimension ≤ n, then S^-1M has projective dimension ≤ n over S^-1R. • If R has finite global dimension ≤ n, then S^-1R has finite global dimension ≤ n.

nodes.title: Regular rings and global dimension · Proposition 00O7
nodes.summary: Let R be a regular local ring of dimension d. Every finite R-module M of depth e has a finite free resolution 0 → F_d-e → … → F_0 → M → 0. In particular a regular local ring has global dimension ≤ d.

nodes.title: Regular rings and global dimension · Lemma 00O9
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let n ≥ 0 be an integer. Then R has finite global dimension ≤ n if and only if for all maximal ideals m of R the ring R_ m has global dimension ≤ n.

nodes.title: Regular rings and global dimension · Lemma 00OA
nodes.summary: Suppose that R is a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m and residue field kappa. In this case the projective dimension of kappa is ≥ dim_kappa m / m^2.

nodes.title: Regular rings and global dimension · Lemma 00OB
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring. Suppose that the residue field kappa has finite projective dimension n over R. In this case dim(R) ≥ n.

nodes.title: Regular rings and global dimension · Proposition 00OC
nodes.summary: Let (R, m, kappa) be a Noetherian local ring. The following are equivalent • kappa has finite projective dimension as an R-module, • R has finite global dimension, • R is a regular local ring. Moreover, in this case the global dimension of R equals dim(R) = dim_kappa( m/ m^2).

nodes.title: Regular rings and global dimension · Lemma 0AFS
nodes.summary: A Noetherian local ring R is a regular local ring if and only if it has finite global dimension. In this case R_ p is a regular local ring for all primes p.

nodes.title: Regular rings and global dimension · Definition 00OD
nodes.summary: A Noetherian ring R is said to be regular if all the localizations R_ p at primes are regular local rings.

nodes.title: Regular rings and global dimension · Lemma 00OE
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. The following are equivalent: • R has finite global dimension n, • R is a regular ring of dimension n, • there exists an integer n such that all the localizations R_ m at maximal ideals are regular of dimension ≤ n with equality for at least one m, and • there exists an integer n such that all the localizations R_ p at prime ideals are regular of dimension ≤ n with equality for at least one p.

nodes.title: Regular rings and global dimension · Lemma 00OF
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a local homomorphism of local Noetherian rings. Assume that R → S is flat and that S is regular. Then R is regular.

nodes.title: Auslander-Buchsbaum · Proposition 090V
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring. Let M be a nonzero finite R-module which has finite projective dimension pd_R(M). Then we have depth(R) = pd_R(M) + depth(M)

nodes.title: Homomorphisms and dimension · Lemma 00OH
nodes.summary: Suppose R → S is a ring map satisfying either going up, see Definition [Tag 00HV], or going down see Definition [Tag 00HV]. Assume in addition that Spec(S) → Spec(R) is surjective. Then dim(R) ≤ dim(S).

nodes.title: Homomorphisms and dimension · Lemma 00OI
nodes.summary: Suppose that R → S is a ring map with the going up property, see Definition [Tag 00HV]. If q ⊂ S is a maximal ideal. Then the inverse image of q in R is a maximal ideal too.

nodes.title: Homomorphisms and dimension · Lemma 00OJ
nodes.summary: Suppose that R → S is a ring map such that S is integral over R. Then dim (R) ≥ dim(S), and every closed point of Spec(S) maps to a closed point of Spec(R).

nodes.title: Homomorphisms and dimension · Lemma 00OK
nodes.summary: Suppose R ⊂ S and S integral over R. Then dim(R) = dim(S).

nodes.title: Homomorphisms and dimension · Definition 00OL
nodes.summary: Suppose that R → S is a ring map. Let q ⊂ S be a prime lying over the prime p of R. The local ring of the fibre at q is the local ring S_ q/ pS_ q = (S/ pS)_ q = (S ⊗_R kappa( p))_ q

nodes.title: Homomorphisms and dimension · Lemma 00OM
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a homomorphism of Noetherian rings. Let q ⊂ S be a prime lying over the prime p. Then dim(S_ q) ≤ dim(R_ p) + dim(S_ q/ pS_ q).

nodes.title: Homomorphisms and dimension · Lemma 00ON
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a homomorphism of Noetherian rings. Let q ⊂ S be a prime lying over the prime p. Assume the going down property holds for R → S (for example if R → S is flat, see Lemma [Tag 00HS]). Then dim(S_ q) = dim(R_ p) + dim(S_ q/ pS_ q).

nodes.title: Homomorphisms and dimension · Lemma 031E
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a local homomorphism of local Noetherian rings. Assume • R is regular, • S/ m_RS is regular, and • R → S is flat. Then S is regular.

nodes.title: Homomorphisms and dimension · Lemma 00R5
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Assume R Cohen-Macaulay. If S is finite flat over R, or if S is flat over R and dim(S) ≤ dim(R), then S is Cohen-Macaulay and dim(R) = dim(S).

nodes.title: The dimension formula · Lemma 02IJ
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let q be a prime of S lying over the prime p of R. Assume that • R is Noetherian, • R → S is of finite type, • R, S are domains, and • R ⊂ S. Then we have height( q) ≤ height( p) + trdeg_R(S) - trdeg_kappa( p) kappa( q) with equality if R is universally catenary.

nodes.title: The dimension formula · Lemma 02MA
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Assume • A ⊂ B is an extension of domains, • the induced extension of fraction fields is finite, • A is Noetherian, and • A → B is of finite type. Let p ⊂ A be a prime of height 1. Then there are at most finitely many primes of B lying over p and they all have height 1.

nodes.title: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields · Lemma 00OP
nodes.summary: Let m be a maximal ideal in k[x_1, …, x_n]. The ideal m is generated by n elements. The dimension of k[x_1, …, x_n]_ m is n. Hence k[x_1, …, x_n]_ m is a regular local ring of dimension n.
nodes.section: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields

nodes.title: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields · Proposition 00OQ
nodes.summary: A polynomial algebra in n variables over a field is a regular ring. It has global dimension n. All localizations at maximal ideals are regular local rings of dimension n.
nodes.section: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields

nodes.title: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields · Lemma 00OR
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let p ⊂ q ⊂ k[x_1, …, x_n] be a pair of primes. Any maximal chain of primes between p and q has length height( q) - height( p).
nodes.section: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields

nodes.title: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields · Lemma 00OS
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a finite type k-algebra which is an integral domain. Then dim(S) = dim(S_ m) for any maximal ideal m of S. In words: every maximal chain of primes has length equal to the dimension of S.
nodes.section: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields

nodes.title: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields · Lemma 00OT
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a finite type k-algebra. Let X = Spec(S). Let p ⊂ S be a prime ideal and let x ∈ X be the corresponding point. The following numbers are equal • dim_x(X), • max dim(Z) where the maximum is over those irreducible components Z of X passing through x, and • min dim(S_ m) where the minimum is over maximal ideals m with p ⊂ m.
nodes.section: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields

nodes.title: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields · Lemma 00OU
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a finite type k-algebra. Let X = Spec(S). Let m ⊂ S be a maximal ideal and let x ∈ X be the associated closed point. Then dim_x(X) = dim(S_ m).
nodes.section: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields

nodes.title: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields · Lemma 00OV
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a finite type k algebra. Assume that S is Cohen-Macaulay. Then Spec(S) = coprod T_d is a finite disjoint union of open and closed subsets T_d with T_d equidimensional (see Topology, Definition [Tag 0058]) of dimension d. Equivalently, S is a product of rings S_d, d = 0, …, dim(S) such that every maximal ideal m of S_d has height d.
nodes.section: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields

nodes.title: Noether normalization · Lemma 051M
nodes.summary: Let n ∈ N. Let N be a finite nonempty set of multi-indices ν = (ν_1, …, ν_n). Given e = (e_1, …, e_n) we set e · ν = ∑ e_iν_i. Then for e_1 gg e_2 gg … gg e_n-1 gg e_n we have: If ν, ν' ∈ N then (e · ν = e · ν') ⇔ (ν = ν')

nodes.title: Noether normalization · Lemma 051N
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let g ∈ R[x_1, …, x_n] be an element which is nonconstant, i.e., g not ∈ R. For e_1 gg e_2 gg … gg e_n-1 gg e_n = 1 the polynomial g(x_1 + x_n^e_1, x_2 + x_n^e_2, …, x_n - 1 + x_n^e_n - 1, x_n) = ax_n^d + lower order terms in x_n where d > 0 and a ∈ R is one of the nonzero coefficients of g.

nodes.title: Noether normalization · Lemma 00OX
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S = k[x_1, …, x_n]/I for some proper ideal I. If I not = 0, then there exist y_1, …, y_n-1 ∈ k[x_1, …, x_n] such that S is finite over k[y_1, …, y_n-1]. Moreover we may choose y_i to be in the Z-subalgebra of k[x_1, …, x_n] generated by x_1, …, x_n.

nodes.title: Noether normalization · Lemma 00OY
nodes.summary: Noether normalization Let k be a field. Let S = k[x_1, …, x_n]/I for some ideal I. If I ≠ (1), there exist r≥ 0, and y_1, …, y_r ∈ k[x_1, …, x_n] such that (a) the map k[y_1, …, y_r] → S is injective where the source is the polynomial ring on y_1, …, y_r, and (b) the map k[y_1, …, y_r] → S is finite. In this case the integer r is the dimension of S. Moreover we may choose y_i to be in the Z-subalgebra of k[x_1, …, x_n] generated by x_1, …, x_n.

nodes.title: Noether normalization · Lemma 00OZ
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a finite type k algebra and denote X = Spec(S). Let q be a prime of S, and let x ∈ X be the corresponding point. There exists a g ∈ S, g not ∈ q such that dim(S_g) = dim_x(X) =: d and such that there exists a finite injective map k[y_1, …, y_d] → S_g.

nodes.title: Noether normalization · Lemma 051P
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let q ⊂ k[x_1, …, x_n] be a prime ideal. Set r = trdeg_k kappa( q). Then there exists a finite ring map φ : k[y_1, …, y_n] → k[x_1, …, x_n] such that φ^-1( q) = (y_r + 1, …, y_n).

nodes.title: Noether normalization · Lemma 07NA
nodes.summary: Let R → S be an injective finite type ring map. Assume R is a domain. Then there exists an integer d and a factorization R → R[y_1, …, y_d] → S' → S by injective maps such that S' is finite over R[y_1, …, y_d] and such that S'_f ≅ S_f for some nonzero f ∈ R.

nodes.title: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields, reprise · Lemma 00P0
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a finite type k algebra which is an integral domain. Let K be the field of fractions of S. Let r = trdeg(K/k) be the transcendence degree of K over k. Then dim(S) = r. Moreover, the local ring of S at every maximal ideal has dimension r.
nodes.section: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields, reprise

nodes.title: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields, reprise · Lemma 06RP
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a finite type k-algebra. Let q ⊂ q' ⊂ S be distinct prime ideals. Then trdeg_k kappa( q') < trdeg_k kappa( q).
nodes.section: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields, reprise

nodes.title: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields, reprise · Lemma 00P1
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a finite type k algebra. Let X = Spec(S). Let p ⊂ S be a prime ideal, and let x ∈ X be the corresponding point. Then we have dim_x(X) = dim(S_ p) + trdeg_k kappa( p).
nodes.section: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields, reprise

nodes.title: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields, reprise · Lemma 00P2
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S' → S be a surjection of finite type k algebras. Let p ⊂ S be a prime ideal, and let p' be the corresponding prime ideal of S'. Let X = Spec(S), resp. X' = Spec(S'), and let x ∈ X, resp. x'∈ X' be the point corresponding to p, resp. p'. Then dim_x' X' - dim_x X = height( p') - height( p).

nodes.title: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields, reprise · Lemma 00P3
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a finite type k-algebra. Let K/k be a field extension. Then dim(S) = dim(K ⊗_k S).
nodes.section: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields, reprise

nodes.title: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields, reprise · Lemma 00P4
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a finite type k-algebra. Set X = Spec(S). Let K/k be a field extension. Set S_K = K ⊗_k S, and X_K = Spec(S_K). Let q ⊂ S be a prime corresponding to x ∈ X and let q_K ⊂ S_K be a prime corresponding to x_K ∈ X_K lying over q. Then dim_x X = dim_x_K X_K.
nodes.section: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields, reprise

nodes.title: Dimension of finite type algebras over fields, reprise · Lemma 0CWE
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a finite type k-algebra. Let K/k be a field extension. Set S_K = K ⊗_k S. Let q ⊂ S be a prime and let q_K ⊂ S_K be a prime lying over q. Then dim (S_K ⊗_S kappa( q))_ q_K = dim (S_K)_ q_K - dim S_ q = trdeg_k kappa( q) - trdeg_K kappa( q_K) Moreover, given q we can always choose q_K such that the number above is zero.

nodes.title: Dimension of graded algebras over a field · Lemma 00P6
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a graded k-algebra generated over k by finitely many elements of degree 1. Assume S_0 = k. Let P(T) ∈ Q[T] be the polynomial such that dim(S_d) = P(d) for all d gg 0. See Proposition [Tag 00K1]. Then • The irrelevant ideal S_+ is a maximal ideal m. • Any minimal prime of S is a homogeneous ideal and is contained in S_+ = m. • We have dim(S) = deg(P) + 1 = dim_xSpec(S) (with the convention that deg(0) = -1) where x is the point corresponding to…

nodes.title: Generic flatness · Lemma 051R
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module. Assume • R is Noetherian, • R is a domain, • R → S is of finite type, and • M is a finite type S-module. Then there exists a nonzero f ∈ R such that M_f is a free R_f-module.

nodes.title: Generic flatness · Lemma 051S
nodes.summary: Generic freeness. Let R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module. Assume • R is a domain, • R → S is of finite presentation, and • M is an S-module of finite presentation. Then there exists a nonzero f ∈ R such that M_f is a free R_f-module.

nodes.title: Generic flatness · Lemma 051T
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module. Assume • R is a domain, • R → S is of finite type, and • M is a finite type S-module. Then there exists a nonzero f ∈ R such that • [(a)] M_f and S_f are free as R_f-modules, and • [(b)] S_f is a finitely presented R_f-algebra and M_f is a finitely presented S_f-module.

nodes.title: Generic flatness · Lemma 051W
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let 0 → M_1 → M_2 → M_3 → 0 be a short exact sequence of S-modules. Then U(R → S, M_1) ∩ U(R → S, M_3) ⊂ U(R → S, M_2).

nodes.title: Generic flatness · Lemma 051X
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module. Let f ∈ R. Using the identification Spec(R_f) = D(f) we have U(R_f → S_f, M_f) = D(f) ∩ U(R → S, M).

nodes.title: Generic flatness · Lemma 051Y
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module. Let U ⊂ Spec(R) be a dense open. Assume there is a covering U = ⋃_i ∈ I D(f_i) of opens such that U(R_f_i → S_f_i, M_f_i) is dense in D(f_i) for each i ∈ I. Then U(R → S, M) is dense in Spec(R).

nodes.title: Generic flatness · Lemma 051Z
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module. Assume • R → S is of finite type, • M is a finite S-module, and • R is reduced. Then there exists a subset U ⊂ Spec(R) such that • U is open and dense in Spec(R), • for every u ∈ U there exists an f ∈ R such that u ∈ D(f) ⊂ U and such that we have • M_f and S_f are free over R_f, • S_f is a finitely presented R_f-algebra, and • M_f is a finitely presented S_f-module.

nodes.title: Around Krull-Akizuki · Lemma 00P8
nodes.summary: Let R be a local Noetherian domain with fraction field K. Assume R is not a field. Then there exist R ⊂ R' ⊂ K with • R' local Noetherian of dimension 1, • R → R' a local ring map, i.e., R' dominates R, and • R → R' essentially of finite type.

nodes.title: Koll\'ar · Lemma 0BHZ
nodes.summary: This is taken from a forthcoming paper by J\'anos Koll\'ar entitled "Variants of normality for Noetherian schemes". Let (R, m) be a local Noetherian ring. Then exactly one of the following holds: • (R, m) is Artinian, • (R, m) is regular of dimension 1, • depth(R) ≥ 2, or • there exists a finite ring map R → R' which is not an isomorphism whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of m such that m is not an associated prime of R' and R' not = 0.

nodes.title: Around Krull-Akizuki · Lemma 00P9
nodes.summary: Let R be a local ring with maximal ideal m. Assume R is Noetherian, has dimension 1, and that dim( m/ m^2) > 1. Then there exists a ring map R → R' such that • R → R' is finite, • R → R' is not an isomorphism, • the kernel and cokernel of R → R' are annihilated by a power of m, and • m is not an associated prime of R'.

nodes.title: Around Krull-Akizuki · Lemma 00PD
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. The following are equivalent. • The ring A is a discrete valuation ring. • The ring A is a valuation ring and Noetherian but not a field. • The ring A is a regular local ring of dimension 1. • The ring A is a Noetherian local domain with maximal ideal m generated by a single nonzero element. • The ring A is a Noetherian local normal domain of dimension 1. In this case if π is a generator of the maximal ideal of A, then every nonzero element of A can be…

nodes.title: Around Krull-Akizuki · Definition 09DZ
nodes.summary: Let A be a discrete valuation ring. A uniformizer is an element π ∈ A which generates the maximal ideal of A.

nodes.title: Around Krull-Akizuki · Lemma 00PE
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain with fraction field K. Let M be an R-submodule of K^⊕ r. Assume R is local Noetherian of dimension 1. For any nonzero x ∈ R we have length_R(R/xR) < ∞ and length_R(M/xM) ≤ r · length_R(R/xR).

nodes.title: Around Krull-Akizuki · Lemma 031F
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a homomorphism of domains inducing an injection of fraction fields K ⊂ L. If R is Noetherian local of dimension 1 and [L : K] < ∞ then • each prime ideal n_i of S lying over the maximal ideal m of R is maximal, • there are finitely many of these, and • [kappa( n_i) : kappa( m)] < ∞ for each i.

nodes.title: Around Krull-Akizuki · Lemma 00PF
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain with fraction field K. Let M be an R-submodule of K^⊕ r. Assume R is Noetherian of dimension 1. For any nonzero x ∈ R we have length_R(M/xM) < ∞.

nodes.title: Krull-Akizuki · Lemma 00PG
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain with fraction field K. Let L/K be a finite extension of fields. Assume R is Noetherian and dim(R) = 1. In this case any ring A with R ⊂ A ⊂ L is Noetherian.

nodes.title: Around Krull-Akizuki · Lemma 00PH
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local domain with fraction field K. Assume that R is not a field. Let L/K be a finitely generated field extension. Then there exists discrete valuation ring A with fraction field L which dominates R.

nodes.title: Factorization · Definition 034P
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain. • Elements x, y ∈ R are called associates if there exists a unit u ∈ R^* such that x = uy. • An element x ∈ R is called irreducible if it is nonzero, not a unit and whenever x = yz, y, z ∈ R, then y is either a unit or an associate of x. • An element x ∈ R is called prime if the ideal generated by x is a prime ideal.

nodes.title: Factorization · Lemma 034Q
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain. Let x, y ∈ R. Then x, y are associates if and only if (x) = (y).

nodes.title: Factorization · Lemma 034R
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain. Consider the following conditions: • The ring R satisfies the ascending chain condition for principal ideals. • Every nonzero, nonunit element a ∈ R has a factorization a = b_1 … b_k with each b_i an irreducible element of R. Then (1) implies (2).

nodes.title: Factorization · Definition 034S
nodes.summary: A unique factorization domain, abbreviated UFD, is a domain R such that if x ∈ R is a nonzero, nonunit, then x has a factorization into irreducibles, and if x = a_1 … a_m = b_1 … b_n are factorizations into irreducibles then n = m and there exists a permutation σ : (1, …, n) → (1, …, n) such that a_i and b_σ(i) are associates.

nodes.title: Factorization · Lemma 034T
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain. Assume every nonzero, nonunit factors into irreducibles. Then R is a UFD if and only if every irreducible element is prime.

nodes.title: Factorization · Lemma 0AFT
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian domain. Then R is a UFD if and only if every height 1 prime ideal is principal.

nodes.title: Nagata's criterion for factoriality · Lemma 0AFU
nodes.summary: [Nagata-UFD] Let A be a domain. Let S ⊂ A be a multiplicative subset generated by prime elements. Let x ∈ A be irreducible. Then • the image of x in S^-1A is irreducible or a unit, and • x is prime if and only if the image of x in S^-1A is a prime element or a unit in S^-1A. Moreover, then A is a UFD if and only if every nonzero nonunit element of A has a factorization into irreducibles and S^-1A is a UFD.

nodes.title: Factorization · Lemma 0BUD
nodes.summary: A UFD satisfies the ascending chain condition for principal ideals.

nodes.title: Factorization · Lemma 0BUE
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain. Assume R has the ascending chain condition for principal ideals. Then the same property holds for a polynomial ring over R.

nodes.title: Factorization · Lemma 0BC1
nodes.summary: A polynomial ring over a UFD is a UFD. In particular, if k is a field, then k[x_1, …, x_n] is a UFD.

nodes.title: Factorization · Lemma 0AFV
nodes.summary: A unique factorization domain is normal.

nodes.title: Factorization · Definition 034U
nodes.summary: A principal ideal domain, abbreviated PID, is a domain R such that every ideal is a principal ideal.

nodes.title: Factorization · Lemma 034V
nodes.summary: A principal ideal domain is a unique factorization domain.

nodes.title: Factorization · Definition 034W
nodes.summary: A Dedekind domain is a domain R such that every nonzero ideal I ⊂ R can be written as a product I = p_1 … p_r of nonzero prime ideals uniquely up to permutation of the p_i.

nodes.title: Factorization · Lemma 0AUQ
nodes.summary: A PID is a Dedekind domain.

nodes.title: Factorization · Lemma 09ME
nodes.summary: A product of ideals is an invertible module iff both factors are. Let A be a ring. Let I and J be nonzero ideals of A such that IJ = (f) for some nonzerodivisor f ∈ A. Then I and J are finitely generated ideals and finitely locally free of rank 1 as A-modules.

nodes.title: Factorization · Lemma 034X
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. The following are equivalent • R is a Dedekind domain, • R is a Noetherian domain and for every nonzero maximal ideal m the local ring R_ m is a discrete valuation ring, and • R is a Noetherian, normal domain, and dim(R) ≤ 1.

nodes.title: Factorization · Lemma 09IG
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian domain of dimension 1 with fraction field K. Let L/K be a finite extension. Let B be the integral closure of A in L. Then B is a Dedekind domain and Spec(B) → Spec(A) is surjective, has finite fibres, and induces finite residue field extensions.

nodes.title: Orders of vanishing · Lemma 02MC
nodes.summary: Let R be a semi-local Noetherian ring of dimension 1. If a, b ∈ R are nonzerodivisors then length_R(R/(ab)) = length_R(R/(a)) + length_R(R/(b)) and these lengths are finite.

nodes.title: Orders of vanishing · Definition 02MD
nodes.summary: Suppose that K is a field, and R ⊂ K is a local Noetherian subring of dimension 1 with fraction field K. In this case we define the order of vanishing along R ord_R : K^* → Z by the rule ord_R(x) = length_R(R/(x)) if x ∈ R and we set ord_R(x/y) = ord_R(x) - ord_R(y) for x, y ∈ R both nonzero.

nodes.title: Orders of vanishing · Definition 02ME
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local domain of dimension 1 with fraction field K. Let V be a finite dimensional K-vector space. A lattice in V is a finite R-submodule M ⊂ V such that V = K ⊗_R M.

nodes.title: Orders of vanishing · Lemma 02MF
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local domain of dimension 1 with fraction field K. Let V be a finite dimensional K-vector space. • If M is a lattice in V and M ⊂ M' ⊂ V is an R-submodule of V containing M then the following are equivalent • M' is a lattice, • length_R(M'/M) is finite, and • M' is finitely generated. • If M is a lattice in V and M' ⊂ M is an R-submodule of M then M' is a lattice if and only if length_R(M/M') is finite. • If M, M' are lattices in V, then so are M ∩…

nodes.title: Orders of vanishing · Definition 02MG
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local domain of dimension 1 with fraction field K. Let V be a finite dimensional K-vector space. Let M, M' be two lattices in V. The distance between M and M' is the integer d(M, M') = length_R(M/M ∩ M') - length_R(M'/M ∩ M') of Lemma [Tag 02MF] part (5).

nodes.title: Orders of vanishing · Lemma 02MH
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local domain of dimension 1 with fraction field K. Let V be a finite dimensional K-vector space. This distance function has the property that d(M, M") = d(M, M') + d(M', M") whenever given three lattices M, M', M" of V. In particular we have d(M, M') = - d(M', M).

nodes.title: Orders of vanishing · Lemma 02MI
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local domain of dimension 1 with fraction field K. Let V be a finite dimensional K-vector space. Let φ : V → V be a K-linear isomorphism. For any lattice M ⊂ V we have d(M, φ(M)) = ord_R(det(φ))

nodes.title: Orders of vanishing · Lemma 02MJ
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Assume • A is a Noetherian local domain of dimension 1, • A ⊂ B is a finite extension of domains. Let L/K be the corresponding finite extension of fraction fields. Let y ∈ L^* and x = Nm_L/K(y). In this situation B is semi-local. Let m_i, i = 1, …, n be the maximal ideals of B. Then ord_A(x) = ∑_i [kappa( m_i) : kappa( m_A)] ord_B_ m_i(y) where ord is defined as in Definition [Tag 02MD].

nodes.title: Quasi-finite maps · Lemma 00PJ
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a finite type k-algebra. Let q be a prime of S. The following are equivalent: • q is an isolated point of Spec(S), • S_ q is finite over k, • there exists a g ∈ S, g not∈ q such that D(g) = ( q ), • dim_ q Spec(S) = 0, • q is a closed point of Spec(S) and dim(S_ q) = 0, and • the field extension kappa( q)/k is finite and dim(S_ q) = 0. In this case S = S_ q × S' for some finite type k-algebra S'. Also, the element g as in (3) has the property S_…

nodes.title: Quasi-finite maps · Lemma 00PK
nodes.summary: Equivalent conditions for isolated points in fibres Let R → S be a ring map of finite type. Let q ⊂ S be a prime lying over p ⊂ R. Let F = Spec(S ⊗_R kappa( p)) be the fibre of Spec(S) → Spec(R), see Remark [Tag 00E6]. Denote overline q ∈ F the point corresponding to q. The following are equivalent • overline q is an isolated point of F, • S_ q/ pS_ q is finite over kappa( p), • there exists a g ∈ S, g not ∈ q such that the only prime of D(g) mapping to p is q, •…

nodes.title: Quasi-finite maps · Definition 00PL
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a finite type ring map. Let q ⊂ S be a prime. • If the equivalent conditions of Lemma [Tag 00PK] are satisfied then we say R → S is quasi-finite at q. • We say a ring map A → B is quasi-finite if it is of finite type and quasi-finite at all primes of B.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite maps · Lemma 0H8X
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a finite type ring map and p be a prime ideal of R. Then the following are equivalent: • R → S is quasi-finite at all primes of S lying over p, • S ⊗_R kappa( p) is a finite kappa( p)-algebra, and • Spec(S ⊗_R kappa( p)) is a finite set.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite maps · Lemma 00PM
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a finite type ring map. Then R → S is quasi-finite if and only if for all primes p ⊂ R the ring S ⊗_R kappa( p) is finite over kappa( p).

nodes.title: Quasi-finite maps · Lemma 077H
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a finite type ring map. Let q ⊂ S be a prime lying over p ⊂ R. Let f ∈ R, f not ∈ p and g ∈ S, g not ∈ q. Then R → S is quasi-finite at q if and only if R_f → S_fg is quasi-finite at qS_fg.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite maps · Lemma 00PN
nodes.summary: Let xymatrix S ar[r] & S' & & q ar@-[r] & q' R ar[u] ar[r] & R' ar[u] & & p ar@-[r] ar@-[u] & p' ar@-[u] be a commutative diagram of rings with primes as indicated. Assume R → S of finite type, and S ⊗_R R' → S' surjective. If R → S is quasi-finite at q, then R' → S' is quasi-finite at q'.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite maps · Lemma 00PO
nodes.summary: A composition of quasi-finite ring maps is quasi-finite.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite maps · Lemma 00PP
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map of finite type. Let R → R' be any ring map. Set S' = R' ⊗_R S. • The set ( q' mid R' → S' quasi-finite at q') is the inverse image of the corresponding set of Spec(S) under the canonical map Spec(S') → Spec(S). • If Spec(R') → Spec(R) is surjective, then R → S is quasi-finite if and only if R' → S' is quasi-finite. • Any base change of a quasi-finite ring map is quasi-finite.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite maps · Lemma 0C6H
nodes.summary: Let A → B and B → C be ring homomorphisms such that A → C is of finite type. Let r be a prime of C lying over q ⊂ B and p ⊂ A. If A → C is quasi-finite at r, then B → C is quasi-finite at r.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite maps · Lemma 02ML
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map of finite type. Let p ⊂ R be a minimal prime. Assume that there are at most finitely many primes of S lying over p. Then there exists a g ∈ R, g not ∈ p such that the ring map R_g → S_g is finite.

nodes.title: Zariski's Main Theorem · Lemma 00PQ
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Suppose t ∈ S satisfies the relation φ(a_0) + φ(a_1)t + … + φ(a_n) t^n = 0. Then φ(a_n)t is integral over R.

nodes.title: Zariski's Main Theorem · Lemma 00PT
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let φ : R[x] → S be a ring map. Let t ∈ S. Assume that (a) t is integral over R[x], and (b) there exists a monic p ∈ R[x] such that t φ(p) ∈ Im(φ). Then there exists a q ∈ R[x] such that t - φ(q) is integral over R.

nodes.title: Zariski's Main Theorem · Lemma 00PV
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let φ : R[x] → S be a ring map. Let t ∈ S. Assume t is integral over R[x]. Let p ∈ R[x], p = a_0 + a_1x + … + a_k x^k such that t φ(p) ∈ Im(φ). Then there exists a q ∈ R[x] and n ≥ 0 such that φ(a_k)^n t - φ(q) is integral over R.

nodes.title: Zariski's Main Theorem · Lemma 00PX
nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 00PW]. Suppose u ∈ S, a_0, …, a_k ∈ R, u φ(a_0 + a_1x + … + a_k x^k) ∈ J. Then there exists an m ≥ 0 such that u φ(a_k)^m ∈ J.

nodes.title: Zariski's Main Theorem · Lemma 00PY
nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 00PW]. Suppose u ∈ S, a_0, …, a_k ∈ R, u φ(a_0 + a_1x + … + a_k x^k) ∈ sqrtJ. Then u φ(a_i) ∈ sqrtJ for all i.

nodes.title: Zariski's Main Theorem · Definition 00PZ
nodes.summary: Given an inclusion of rings R ⊂ S and an element x ∈ S we say that x is strongly transcendental over R if whenever u(a_0 + a_1 x + … + a_k x^k) = 0 with u ∈ S and a_i ∈ R, then we have ua_i = 0 for all i.

nodes.title: Zariski's Main Theorem · Lemma 00Q0
nodes.summary: Suppose R ⊂ S is an inclusion of reduced rings and suppose that x ∈ S is strongly transcendental over R. Let q ⊂ S be a minimal prime and let p = R ∩ q. Then the image of x in S/ q is strongly transcendental over the subring R/ p.

nodes.title: Zariski's Main Theorem · Lemma 00Q1
nodes.summary: Suppose R⊂ S is an inclusion of domains and let x ∈ S. Assume x is (strongly) transcendental over R and that S is finite over R[x]. Then R → S is not quasi-finite at any prime of S.

nodes.title: Zariski's Main Theorem · Lemma 00Q2
nodes.summary: Suppose R ⊂ S is an inclusion of reduced rings. Assume x ∈ S be strongly transcendental over R, and S finite over R[x]. Then R → S is not quasi-finite at any prime of S.

nodes.title: Zariski's Main Theorem · Lemma 00Q8
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let S = R[x]/I. Let q ⊂ S be a prime. Assume R → S is quasi-finite at q. Let S' ⊂ S be the integral closure of R in S. Then there exists an element g ∈ S', g not∈ q such that S'_g ≅ S_g.

nodes.title: Zariski's Main Theorem · Theorem 00Q9
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let R → S be a finite type R-algebra. Let S' ⊂ S be the integral closure of R in S. Let q ⊂ S be a prime of S. If R → S is quasi-finite at q then there exists a g ∈ S', g not ∈ q such that S'_g ≅ S_g.

nodes.title: Zariski's Main Theorem · Lemma 00QA
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a finite type ring map. The set of points q of Spec(S) at which S/R is quasi-finite is open in Spec(S).

nodes.title: Zariski's Main Theorem · Lemma 00QB
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a finite type ring map. Suppose that S is quasi-finite over R. Let S' ⊂ S be the integral closure of R in S. Then • Spec(S) → Spec(S') is a homeomorphism onto an open subset, • if g ∈ S' and D(g) is contained in the image of the map, then S'_g ≅ S_g, and • there exists a finite R-algebra S" ⊂ S' such that (1) and (2) hold for the ring map S" → S.

nodes.title: Applications of Zariski's Main Theorem · Lemma 02MM
nodes.summary: Let A ⊂ B be an extension of domains. Assume • A is a local Noetherian ring of dimension 1, • A → B is of finite type, and • the induced extension L/K of fraction fields is finite. Then B is semi-local. Let x ∈ m_A, x not = 0. Let m_i, i = 1, …, n be the maximal ideals of B. Then [L : K]ord_A(x) ≥ ∑_i [kappa( m_i) : kappa( m_A)] ord_B_ m_i(x) where ord is defined as in Definition [Tag 02MD]. We have equality if and only if A → B is finite.

nodes.title: Applications of Zariski's Main Theorem · Lemma 052V
nodes.summary: Let (R, m_R) → (S, m_S) be a local homomorphism of local rings. Assume • R → S is essentially of finite type, • kappa( m_R) ⊂ kappa( m_S) is finite, and • dim(S/ m_RS) = 0. Then S is the localization of a finite R-algebra.

nodes.title: Applications of Zariski's Main Theorem · Lemma 07NC
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map, q a prime of S lying over p in R. If • R is Noetherian, • R → S is of finite type, and • R → S is quasi-finite at q, then R_ p^wedge ⊗_R S = S_ q^wedge × B for some R_ p^wedge-algebra B.

nodes.title: Dimension of fibres · Definition 00QD
nodes.summary: Suppose that R → S is of finite type, and let q ⊂ S be a prime lying over a prime p of R. We define the relative dimension of S/R at q, denoted dim_ q(S/R), to be the dimension of Spec(S ⊗_R kappa( p)) at the point corresponding to q. We let dim(S/R) be the supremum of dim_ q(S/R) over all q. This is called the relative dimension of S/R.

nodes.title: Dimension of fibres · Lemma 00QE
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a finite type ring map. Let q ⊂ S be a prime. Suppose that dim_ q(S/R) = n. There exists a g ∈ S, g not∈ q such that S_g is quasi-finite over a polynomial algebra R[t_1, …, t_n].

nodes.title: Dimension of fibres · Lemma 0520
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let q ⊂ S be a prime lying over the prime p of R. Assume • R → S is of finite type, • dim_ q(S/R) = n, and • trdeg_kappa( p)kappa( q) = r. Then there exist f ∈ R, f not ∈ p, g ∈ S, g not∈ q and a quasi-finite ring map φ : R_f[x_1, …, x_n] → S_g such that φ^-1( qS_g) = ( p, x_r + 1, …, x_n)R_f[x_1, …, x_n]

nodes.title: Dimension of fibres · Lemma 00QF
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a finite type ring map. Let q ⊂ S be a prime lying over p ⊂ R. If R → S is quasi-finite at q, then dim(S_ q) ≤ dim(R_ p).

nodes.title: Dimension of fibres · Lemma 00QG
nodes.summary: A quasi-finite cover of affine n-space has dimension at most n. Let k be a field. Let S be a finite type k-algebra. Suppose there is a quasi-finite k-algebra map k[t_1, …, t_n] ⊂ S. Then dim(S) ≤ n.

nodes.title: Dimension of fibres · Lemma 00QH
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a finite type ring map. Let q ⊂ S be a prime. Suppose that dim_ q(S/R) = n. There exists an open neighbourhood V of q in Spec(S) such that dim_ q'(S/R) ≤ n for all q' ∈ V.

nodes.title: Dimension of fibres · Lemma 00QI
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a finite type ring map. Let R → R' be any ring map. Set S' = R' ⊗_R S and denote f : Spec(S') → Spec(S) the associated map on spectra. Let n ≥ 0. The inverse image f^-1(( q ∈ Spec(S) mid dim_ q(S/R) ≤ n)) is equal to ( q' ∈ Spec(S') mid dim_ q'(S'/R') ≤ n).

nodes.title: Dimension of fibres · Lemma 00QJ
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring homomorphism of finite presentation. Let n ≥ 0. The set V_n = ( q ∈ Spec(S) mid dim_ q(S/R) ≤ n) is a quasi-compact open subset of Spec(S).

nodes.title: Dimension of fibres · Lemma 00QK
nodes.summary: Let R be a valuation ring with residue field k and field of fractions K. Let S be a domain containing R such that S is of finite type over R. If S ⊗_R k is not the zero ring then dim(S ⊗_R k) = dim(S ⊗_R K) In fact, Spec(S ⊗_R k) is equidimensional.

nodes.title: Algebras and modules of finite presentation · Lemma 00QP
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let R → R' be a faithfully flat ring map. Set S' = R'⊗_R S. Then R → S is of finite type if and only if R' → S' is of finite type.

nodes.title: Algebras and modules of finite presentation · Lemma 00QQ

nodes.title: Algebras and modules of finite presentation · Lemma 05N5

Set R' = S^-1(R/I) = S^-1R/S^-1I. • For any finite R'-module M' there exists a finite R-module M such that S^-1(M/IM) ≅ M'. • For any finitely presented R'-module M' there exists a finitely presented R-module M such that S^-1(M/IM) ≅ M'.
nodes.section: Algebras and modules of finite presentation

nodes.section: Algebras and modules of finite presentation

nodes.title: Algebras and modules of finite presentation · Lemma 00QS

nodes.section: Algebras and modules of finite presentation

nodes.title: Algebras and modules of finite presentation · Lemma 087P
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let S → S' be an R-algebra map. Let IS ⊂ q ⊂ S be a prime ideal. Assume that • S → S' is surjective, • S_ q/IS_ q → S'_ q/IS'_ q is an isomorphism, • S is of finite type over R, • S' of finite presentation over R, and • S'_ q is flat over R. Then S_g → S'_g is an isomorphism for some g ∈ S, g not ∈ q.

The following are equivalent • φ is of finite presentation, • for every directed system A_λ of R-algebras the map colim_λ Hom_R(S, A_λ) → Hom_R(S, colim_λ A_λ) is bijective, and • for every directed system A_λ of R-algebras the map colim_λ Hom_R(S, A_λ) → Hom_R(S, colim_λ A_λ) is surjective.

nodes.title: More flatness criteria · Lemma 00R4
nodes.summary: Miracle flatness Let R → S be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Assume • R is regular, • S Cohen-Macaulay, • dim(S) = dim(R) + dim(S/ m_R S). Then R → S is flat.

nodes.title: More flatness criteria · Lemma 07DY
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Assume that R is a regular local ring and that a regular system of parameters maps to a regular sequence in S. Then R → S is flat.

nodes.title: More flatness criteria · Lemma 00R6
nodes.summary: Let R → S, M, Lambda, R_λ → S_λ, M_λ be as in Lemma [Tag 00QX]. Assume that M is flat over R. Then for some λ ∈ Lambda the module M_λ is flat over R_λ.

nodes.title: More flatness criteria · Lemma 046Y
nodes.summary: Suppose that R → S is a local homomorphism of local rings. Denote m the maximal ideal of R. Let u : M → N be a map of S-modules. Assume • S is essentially of finite presentation over R, • M, N are finitely presented over S, • N is flat over R, and • overlineu : M/ mM → N/ mN is injective. Then u is injective, and N/u(M) is flat over R.

nodes.title: More flatness criteria · Lemma 046Z
nodes.summary: Suppose that R → S is a local ring homomorphism of local rings. Denote m the maximal ideal of R. Suppose • S is essentially of finite presentation over R, • S is flat over R, and • f ∈ S is a nonzerodivisor in S/ mS. Then S/fS is flat over R, and f is a nonzerodivisor in S.

nodes.title: More flatness criteria · Lemma 0470
nodes.summary: Suppose that R → S is a local ring homomorphism of local rings. Denote m the maximal ideal of R. Suppose • R → S is essentially of finite presentation, • R → S is flat, and • f_1, …, f_c is a sequence of elements of S such that the images overlinef_1, …, overlinef_c form a regular sequence in S/ mS. Then f_1, …, f_c is a regular sequence in S and each of the quotients S/(f_1, …, f_i) is flat over R.

nodes.title: More flatness criteria · Lemma 0471
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a local homomorphism of local rings. Let I not = R be an ideal in R. Let M be an S-module. Assume • S is essentially of finite presentation over R, • M is of finite presentation over S, • Tor_1^R(M, R/I) = 0, and • M/IM is flat over R/I. Then M is flat over R.

nodes.title: Crit\`ere de platitude par fibres · Lemma 00R7
nodes.summary: Let R, S, S' be local rings and let R → S → S' be local ring homomorphisms. Let M be an S'-module. Let m ⊂ R be the maximal ideal. Assume • The ring maps R → S and R → S' are essentially of finite presentation. • The module M is of finite presentation over S'. • The module M is not zero. • The module M/ mM is a flat S/ mS-module. • The module M is a flat R-module. Then S is flat over R and M is a flat S-module.

nodes.title: More flatness criteria · Lemma 05UV
nodes.summary: Let R, S, S' be local rings and let R → S → S' be local ring homomorphisms. Let M be an S'-module. Let m ⊂ R be the maximal ideal. Assume • R → S' is essentially of finite presentation, • R → S is essentially of finite type, • M is of finite presentation over S', • M is not zero, • M/ mM is a flat S/ mS-module, and • M is a flat R-module. Then S is essentially of finite presentation and flat over R and M is a flat S-module.

Assume • R → S is of finite type, • R → S' is of finite presentation, • M is a finitely presented S'-module, • M/IM is flat as a S/IS-module, and • M is flat as an R-module. nodes.summary: Let S be a finite type algebra over a field k. Let φ : k[y_1, …, y_d] → S be a quasi-finite ring map. As subsets of Spec(S) we have ( q mid S_ q flat over k[y_1, …, y_d]) = ( q mid S_ q CM and dim_ q(S/k) = d) For notation see Definition [Tag 00QD].

nodes.title: Openness of Cohen-Macaulay loci · Lemma 00RF
nodes.summary: Let S be a finite type algebra over a field k. The set of primes q such that S_ q is Cohen-Macaulay is open in S.

nodes.title: Openness of Cohen-Macaulay loci · Lemma 00RG
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a finite type k algebra. The set of Cohen-Macaulay primes forms a dense open U ⊂ Spec(S).

nodes.title: Openness of Cohen-Macaulay loci · Lemma 00RH
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let R → S be of finite presentation and flat. For any d ≥ 0 the set ( q ∈ Spec(S) such that setting p = R ∩ q the fibre ring S_ q/ pS_ q is Cohen-Macaulay and dim_ q(S/R) = d ) is open in Spec(S).

nodes.title: Openness of Cohen-Macaulay loci · Lemma 00RI
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let R → S be flat of finite presentation. The set of primes q such that the fibre ring S_ q ⊗_R kappa( p), with p = R ∩ q is Cohen-Macaulay is open and dense in every fibre of Spec(S) → Spec(R).

nodes.title: Openness of Cohen-Macaulay loci · Lemma 00RJ
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a finite type k-algebra. Let K/k be a field extension, and set S_K = K ⊗_k S. Let q ⊂ S be a prime of S. Let q_K ⊂ S_K be a prime of S_K lying over q. Then S_ q is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if (S_K)_ q_K is Cohen-Macaulay.

nodes.title: Openness of Cohen-Macaulay loci · Lemma 00RK
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let R → S be of finite type. Let R → R' be any ring map. Set S' = R' ⊗_R S. Denote f : Spec(S') → Spec(S) the map associated to the ring map S → S'. Set W equal to the set of primes q such that the fibre ring S_ q ⊗_R kappa( p), p = R ∩ q is Cohen-Macaulay, and let W' denote the analogue for S'/R'. Then W' = f^-1(W).

nodes.title: Openness of Cohen-Macaulay loci · Lemma 00RL
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let R → S be a ring map which is (a) flat, (b) of finite presentation, (c) has Cohen-Macaulay fibres. Then we can write S = S_0 × … × S_n as a product of R-algebras S_d such that each S_d satisfies (a), (b), (c) and has all fibres equidimensional of dimension d.

nodes.title: Differentials · Definition 00RN
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map and let M be an S-module. A derivation, or more precisely an R-derivation into M is a map D : S → M which is additive, annihilates elements of φ(R), and satisfies the Leibniz rule: D(ab) = aD(b) + bD(a).

nodes.title: Differentials · Definition 07BK
nodes.summary: The pair (Ω_S/R, d) is called the module of K\"ahler differentials or the module of differentials of S over R.

nodes.title: Differentials · Lemma 00RO
nodes.summary: Maps out of the module of differentials are the same as derivations. The module of differentials of S over R has the following universal property. The map Hom_S(Ω_S/R, M) → Der_R(S, M), α ↦ α ∘ d is an isomorphism of functors.

nodes.title: Differentials · Lemma 00RP
nodes.summary: Suppose that R → S is surjective. Then Ω_S/R = 0.

nodes.title: Differentials · Lemma 031G
nodes.summary: Let I be a directed set. Let (R_i → S_i, φ_ii') be a system of ring maps over I, see Categories, Section [Tag 002Z]. Then we have Ω_S/R = colim_i Ω_S_i/R_i. where R → S = colim (R_i → S_i).

nodes.title: Differentials · Lemma 00RR
nodes.summary: In diagram ([Tag 00RQ]), suppose that S → S' is surjective with kernel I ⊂ S. Then Ω_S/R → Ω_S'/R' is surjective with kernel generated as an S-module by the elements da, where a ∈ S is such that φ(a) ∈ β(R'). (This includes in particular the elements d(i), i ∈ I.)

nodes.title: Differentials · Lemma 00RS
nodes.summary: Let A → B → C be ring maps. Then there is a canonical exact sequence C ⊗_B Ω_B/A → Ω_C/A → Ω_C/B → 0 of C-modules.

nodes.title: Differentials · Lemma 00RT
nodes.summary: Let φ : A → B be a ring map. • If S ⊂ A is a multiplicative subset mapping to invertible elements of B, then Ω_B/A = Ω_B/S^-1A. • If S ⊂ B is a multiplicative subset then S^-1Ω_B/A = Ω_S^-1B/A.

nodes.title: Differentials · Lemma 00RU
nodes.summary: In diagram ([Tag 00RQ]), suppose that S → S' is surjective with kernel I ⊂ S, and assume that R' = R. Then there is a canonical exact sequence of S'-modules I/I^2 → Ω_S/R ⊗_S S' → Ω_S'/R → 0 The leftmost map is characterized by the rule that f ∈ I maps to df ⊗ 1.

nodes.title: Differentials · Lemma 02HP
nodes.summary: In diagram ([Tag 00RQ]), suppose that S → S' is surjective with kernel I ⊂ S, and assume that R' = R. Moreover, assume that there exists an R-algebra map S' → S which is a right inverse to S → S'. Then the exact sequence of S'-modules of Lemma [Tag 00RU] turns into a short exact sequence 0 → I/I^2 → Ω_S/R ⊗_S S' → Ω_S'/R → 0 which is even a split short exact sequence.

nodes.title: Differentials · Lemma 02HQ
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let I ⊂ S be an ideal. Let n ≥ 1 be an integer. Set S' = S/I^n + 1. The map Ω_S/R → Ω_S'/R induces an isomorphism Ω_S/R ⊗_S S/I^n → Ω_S'/R ⊗_S' S/I^n.

nodes.title: Differentials · Lemma 00RV
nodes.summary: Suppose that we have ring maps R → R' and R → S. Set S' = S ⊗_R R', so that we obtain a diagram ([Tag 00RQ]). Then the canonical map defined above induces an isomorphism Ω_S/R ⊗_R R' = Ω_S'/R'.

nodes.title: Differentials · Lemma 00RW
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let J = Ker(S ⊗_R S → S) be the kernel of the multiplication map. There is a canonical isomorphism of S-modules Ω_S/R → J/J^2, a d b ↦ a ⊗ b - ab ⊗ 1.

nodes.title: Differentials · Lemma 00RX
nodes.summary: If S = R[x_1, …, x_n], then Ω_S/R is a finite free S-module with basis dx_1, …, dx_n.

nodes.title: Differentials · Lemma 00RY
nodes.summary: Suppose R → S is of finite presentation. Then Ω_S/R is a finitely presented S-module.

nodes.title: Differentials · Lemma 00RZ
nodes.summary: Suppose R → S is of finite type. Then Ω_S/R is finitely generated S-module.

nodes.title: The de Rham complex · Lemma 0H8Y
nodes.summary: Suppose that we have ring maps A → A' and A → B. Set B' = B ⊗_A A', so that we obtain a diagram as above. Then the canonical map defined above induces an isomorphism Ω^bullet_B/A ⊗_A A' = Ω^bullet_B'/A' of complexes.

nodes.title: The de Rham complex · Lemma 07HY
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Let π : Ω_B/A → Ω be a surjective B-module map. Denote d : B → Ω the composition of π with the universal derivation d_B/A : B → Ω_B/A. Set Ω^i = wedge_B^i(Ω). Assume that the kernel of π is generated, as a B-module, by elements ω ∈ Ω_B/A such that d_B/A(ω) ∈ Ω_B/A^2 maps to zero in Ω^2. Then there is a de Rham complex Ω^0 → Ω^1 → Ω^2 → … whose differential is defined by the rule d : Ω^p → Ω^p + 1, d(f_0df_1 wedge … wedge df_p) = df_0 wedge df_1…

nodes.title: Finite order differential operators · Definition 09CI
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let M, N be S-modules. Let k ≥ 0 be an integer. We inductively define a differential operator D : M → N of order k to be an R-linear map such that for all g ∈ S the map m ↦ D(gm) - gD(m) is a differential operator of order k - 1. For the base case k = 0 we define a differential operator of order 0 to be an S-linear map.

nodes.title: Finite order differential operators · Lemma 09CJ
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let L, M, N be S-modules. If D : L → M and D' : M → N are differential operators of order k and k', then D' ∘ D is a differential operator of order k + k'.

nodes.title: Finite order differential operators · Lemma 09CK
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module. Let k ≥ 0. There exists an S-module P^k_S/R(M) and a canonical isomorphism Diff^k_S/R(M, N) = Hom_S(P^k_S/R(M), N) functorial in the S-module N.

nodes.title: Finite order differential operators · Definition 09CL
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module. The module P^k_S/R(M) constructed in Lemma [Tag 09CK] is called the module of principal parts of order k of M.

nodes.title: Finite order differential operators · Lemma 09CN
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module. There is a canonical short exact sequence 0 → Ω_S/R ⊗_S M → P^1_S/R(M) → M → 0 functorial in M called the sequence of principal parts.

nodes.title: Finite order differential operators · Lemma 0H8Z
nodes.summary: Suppose that we have ring maps A → A' and A → B and a B-module M. Set B' = B ⊗_A A' and view M' = M ⊗_A A' as a B'-module. The map of Remark [Tag 09CP] induces an isomorphism P^k_B/A(M) ⊗_A A' = P^k_B'/A'(M').

nodes.title: Finite order differential operators · Lemma 0H90
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module. Let J = Ker(S ⊗_R S → S) be the kernel of the multiplication map. There is a canonical isomorphism of S-modules P^k_S/R(M) → (S ⊗_R M)/J^k + 1(S ⊗_R M) where s ∈ S acts on the target via multiplication by s ⊗ 1 and such that the universal differential operators of order k to the map given by m ↦ class of 1 ⊗ m.

nodes.title: Finite order differential operators · Lemma 0G34
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. The differentials d : Ω^i_B/A → Ω^i + 1_B/A are differential operators of order 1.

nodes.title: Finite order differential operators · Lemma 0G35
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Let g_i ∈ B, i ∈ I be a set of generators for B as an A-algebra. Let M, N be B-modules. Let D : M → N be an A-linear map. In order to show that D is a differential operator of order k it suffices to show that D ∘ g_i - g_i ∘ D is a differential operator of order k - 1 for i ∈ I.

nodes.title: Finite order differential operators · Lemma 0G36
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Let M, N be B-modules. Let S ⊂ B be a multiplicative subset. Any differential operator D : M → N of order k extends uniquely to a differential operator E : S^-1M → S^-1N of order k.

nodes.title: Finite order differential operators · Lemma 0G37
nodes.summary: Let R → A and R → B be ring maps. Let M and M' be A-modules. Let D : M → M' be a differential operator of order k with respect to R → A. Let N be any B-module. Then the map D ⊗ id_N : M ⊗_R N → M' ⊗_R N is a differential operator of order k with respect to B → A ⊗_R B.

nodes.title: The naive cotangent complex · Definition 07BN
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. The naive cotangent complex NL_S/R is the chain complex ([Tag 07BM]) NL_S/R = (I/I^2 → Ω_R[S]/R ⊗_R[S] S) with I/I^2 placed in (homological) degree 1 and Ω_R[S]/R ⊗_R[S] S placed in degree 0. We will denote H_1(L_S/R) = H_1(NL_S/R) in the literature. the homology in degree 1.

nodes.title: The naive cotangent complex · Lemma 00S1
nodes.summary: Suppose given a diagram ([Tag 06RQ]). Let α : P → S and α' : P' → S' be presentations. • There exists a morphism of presentations from α to α'. • Any two morphisms of presentations induce homotopic morphisms of complexes NL(α) → NL(α'). • The construction is compatible with compositions of morphisms of presentations (see proof for exact statement). • If R → R' and S → S' are isomorphisms, then for any map φ of presentations from α to α' the induced map NL(α) → NL(α') is a…

nodes.title: The naive cotangent complex · Lemma 08Q1
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a polynomial algebra. Then NL_B/A is homotopy equivalent to the chain complex (0 → Ω_B/A) with Ω_B/A in degree 0.

nodes.title: Jacobi-Zariski sequence · Lemma 00S2
nodes.summary: Let A → B → C be ring maps. Choose a presentation α : A[x_s, s ∈ S] → B with kernel I. Choose a presentation β : B[y_t, t ∈ T] → C with kernel J. Let γ : A[x_s, y_t] → C be the induced presentation of C with kernel K. Then we get a canonical commutative diagram xymatrix 0 ar[r] & Ω_A[x_s]/A ⊗ C ar[r] & Ω_A[x_s, y_t]/A ⊗ C ar[r] & Ω_B[y_t]/B ⊗ C ar[r] & 0 & I/I^2 ⊗ C ar[r] ar[u] & K/K^2 ar[r] ar[u] & J/J^2 ar[r] ar[u] & 0 with exact rows. We get the following exact…

nodes.title: The naive cotangent complex · Lemma 07BP
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a surjective ring map with kernel I. Then NL_B/A is homotopy equivalent to the chain complex (I/I^2 → 0) with I/I^2 in degree 1. In particular H_1(L_B/A) = I/I^2.

nodes.title: The naive cotangent complex · Lemma 065V
nodes.summary: Let A → B → C be ring maps. Assume A → C is surjective (so also B → C is). Denote I = Ker(A → C) and J = Ker(B → C). Then the sequence I/I^2 → J/J^2 → Ω_B/A ⊗_B B/J → 0 is exact.

nodes.title: Flat base change · Lemma 00S4
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let α : P → S be a presentation. Let R → R' be a flat ring map. Let α' : P ⊗_R R' → S' = S ⊗_R R' be the induced presentation. Then NL(α) ⊗_R R' = NL(α) ⊗_S S' = NL(α'). In particular, the canonical map NL_S/R ⊗_S S' → NL_S ⊗_R R'/R' is a homotopy equivalence if R → R' is flat.

nodes.title: The naive cotangent complex · Lemma 07BQ
nodes.summary: Let R_λ → S_λ be a system of ring maps over the directed set Lambda. Set R = colim R_λ and S = colim S_λ. Then NL_S/R = colim NL_S_λ/R_λ.

nodes.title: The naive cotangent complex · Lemma 07BR
nodes.summary: If S ⊂ A is a multiplicative subset of A, then NL_S^-1A/A is homotopy equivalent to the zero complex.

nodes.title: The naive cotangent complex · Lemma 07BS
nodes.summary: Let S ⊂ A is a multiplicative subset of A. Let S^-1A → B be a ring map. Then NL_B/A → NL_B/S^-1A is a homotopy equivalence.

nodes.title: The naive cotangent complex · Lemma 08JZ
nodes.summary: The formation of the naive cotangent complex commutes with localization at an element. Let A → B be a ring map. Let g ∈ B. Suppose α : P → B is a presentation with kernel I. Then a presentation of B_g over A is the map β : P[x] → B_g extending α and sending x to 1/g. The kernel J of β is generated by I and the element f x - 1 where f ∈ P is an element mapped to g ∈ B by α. In this situation we have • J/J^2 = (I/I^2)_g ⊕ B_g (f x - 1), • Ω_P[x]/A ⊗_P[x] B_g = Ω_P/A ⊗_P B_g…

nodes.title: The naive cotangent complex · Lemma 00S7
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Let S ⊂ B be a multiplicative subset. The canonical map NL_B/A ⊗_B S^-1B → NL_S^-1B/A is a quasi-isomorphism.

nodes.title: The naive cotangent complex · Lemma 00S3
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let A_1 → A_0, and B_1 → B_0 be two term complexes. Suppose that there exist morphisms of complexes φ : A_bullet → B_bullet and ψ : B_bullet → A_bullet such that φ ∘ ψ and ψ ∘ φ are homotopic to the identity maps. Then A_1 ⊕ B_0 ≅ B_1 ⊕ A_0 as R-modules.

nodes.title: The naive cotangent complex · Lemma 00S5
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map of finite type. For any presentations α : R[x_1, …, x_n] → S, and β : R[y_1, …, y_m] → S we have I/I^2 ⊕ S^⊕ m ≅ J/J^2 ⊕ S^⊕ n as S-modules where I = Ker(α) and J = Ker(β).

nodes.title: The naive cotangent complex · Lemma 00S6
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map of finite type. Let g ∈ S. For any presentations α : R[x_1, …, x_n] → S, and β : R[y_1, …, y_m] → S_g we have (I/I^2)_g ⊕ S^⊕ m_g ≅ J/J^2 ⊕ S_g^⊕ n as S_g-modules where I = Ker(α) and J = Ker(β).

nodes.title: Local complete intersections · Definition 00S9
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a finite type k-algebra. • We say that S is a global complete intersection over k if there exists a presentation S = k[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c) such that dim(S) = n - c. • We say that S is a local complete intersection over k if there exists a covering Spec(S) = ⋃ D(g_i) such that each of the rings S_g_i is a global complete intersection over k. We will also use the convention that the zero ring is a global complete intersection over k.

nodes.title: Local complete intersections · Lemma 00SA
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a finite type k-algebra. Let g ∈ S. • If S is a global complete intersection so is S_g. • If S is a local complete intersection so is S_g.

nodes.title: Local complete intersections · Lemma 00SB
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a finite type k-algebra. If S is a local complete intersection, then S is a Cohen-Macaulay ring.

nodes.title: Local complete intersections · Lemma 00SC
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a finite type k-algebra. Let q be a prime of S. Choose any presentation S = k[x_1, …, x_n]/I. Let q' be the prime of k[x_1, …, x_n] corresponding to q. Set c = height( q') - height( q), in other words dim_ q(S) = n - c (see Lemma [Tag 00P2]). The following are equivalent • There exists a g ∈ S, g not ∈ q such that S_g is a global complete intersection over k. • The ideal I_ q' ⊂ k[x_1, …, x_n]_ q' can be generated by c elements. • The conormal…

nodes.title: Local complete intersections · Definition 00SD
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a local k-algebra essentially of finite type over k. We say S is a complete intersection (over k) if there exists a local k-algebra R and elements f_1, …, f_c ∈ m_R such that • R is essentially of finite type over k, • R is a regular local ring, • f_1, …, f_c form a regular sequence in R, and • S ≅ R/(f_1, …, f_c) as k-algebras.

nodes.title: Local complete intersections · Lemma 00SE
nodes.summary: Let A → B → C be surjective local ring homomorphisms. Assume A and B are regular local rings. The following are equivalent • Ker(A → C) is generated by a regular sequence, • Ker(A → C) is generated by dim(A) - dim(C) elements, • Ker(B → C) is generated by a regular sequence, and • Ker(B → C) is generated by dim(B) - dim(C) elements.

nodes.title: Local complete intersections · Lemma 00SF
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a local k-algebra essentially of finite type over k. The following are equivalent: • S is a complete intersection over k, • for any surjection R → S with R a regular local ring essentially of finite presentation over k the ideal Ker(R → S) can be generated by a regular sequence, • for some surjection R → S with R a regular local ring essentially of finite presentation over k the ideal Ker(R → S) can be generated by dim(R) - dim(S) elements, •…

nodes.title: Local complete intersections · Lemma 00SG
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a finite type k-algebra. Let q be a prime of S. The following are equivalent: • The local ring S_ q is a complete intersection ring (Definition [Tag 00SD]). • There exists a g ∈ S, g not ∈ q such that S_g is a local complete intersection over k. • There exists a g ∈ S, g not ∈ q such that S_g is a global complete intersection over k. • For any presentation S = k[x_1, …, x_n]/I with q' ⊂ k[x_1, …, x_n] corresponding to q any of the equivalent…

nodes.title: Local complete intersections · Lemma 00SH
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let S be a finite type k-algebra. The following are equivalent: • The ring S is a local complete intersection over k. • All local rings of S are complete intersection rings over k. • All localizations of S at maximal ideals are complete intersection rings over k.

nodes.title: Local complete intersections · Lemma 00SI
nodes.summary: Let K/k be a field extension. Let S be a finite type algebra over k. Let q_K be a prime of S_K = K ⊗_k S and let q be the corresponding prime of S. Then S_ q is a complete intersection over k (Definition [Tag 00SD]) if and only if (S_K)_ q_K is a complete intersection over K.

nodes.title: Local complete intersections · Lemma 00SJ
nodes.summary: Let k → K be a field extension. Let S be a finite type k-algebra. Then S is a local complete intersection over k if and only if S ⊗_k K is a local complete intersection over K.

nodes.title: Local complete intersections · Lemma 02JP
nodes.summary: Let xymatrix B & S ar[l] A ar[u] & R ar[l] ar[u] be a commutative square of local rings. Assume • R and overlineS = S/ m_R S are regular local rings, • A = R/I and B = S/J for some ideals I, J, • J ⊂ S and overlineJ = J/ m_R ∩ J ⊂ overlineS are generated by regular sequences, and • A → B and R → S are flat. Then I is generated by a regular sequence.

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Definition 00SL
nodes.summary: A ring map R → S is called syntomic, or we say S is a flat local complete intersection over R if it is flat, of finite presentation, and if all of its fibre rings S ⊗_R kappa( p) are local complete intersections, see Definition [Tag 00S9].

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Lemma 00SM
nodes.summary: Being syntomic is fpqc local on the base. Let R → S be a ring map. Let R → R' be a faithfully flat ring map. Set S' = R'⊗_R S. Then R → S is syntomic if and only if R' → S' is syntomic.

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Lemma 00SN
nodes.summary: Any base change of a syntomic map is syntomic.

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Lemma 00SO
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Suppose we have g_1, … g_m ∈ S which generate the unit ideal such that each R → S_g_i is syntomic. Then R → S is syntomic.

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Definition 00SP
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. We say that R → S is a relative global complete intersection if there exists a presentation S = R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c) and every nonempty fibre of Spec(S) → Spec(R) has dimension n - c. We will say "let S = R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c) be a relative global complete intersection" to indicate this situation.

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Lemma 07CF
nodes.summary: Let S be a finitely presented R-algebra which has a presentation S = R[x_1, …, x_n]/I such that I/I^2 is free over S. Then S has a presentation S = R[y_1, …, y_m]/(f_1, …, f_c) such that (f_1, …, f_c)/(f_1, …, f_c)^2 is free with basis given by the classes of f_1, …, f_c.

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Lemma 00SS
nodes.summary: Let S = R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c) be a relative global complete intersection (Definition [Tag 00SP]) • For any R → R' the base change R' ⊗_R S = R'[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c) is a relative global complete intersection. • For any g ∈ S which is the image of h ∈ R[x_1, …, x_n] the ring S_g = R[x_1, …, x_n, x_n + 1]/(f_1, …, f_c, hx_n + 1 - 1) is a relative global complete intersection. • If R → S factors as R → R_f → S for some f ∈ R. Then the ring S = R_f[x_1, …,…

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Lemma 00ST
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let S = R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c).
