nodes.title: Fibre products of rings, I · Lemma 00IT
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let A → B and C → B be R-algebra maps. Assume • R is Noetherian, • A, B, C are of finite type over R, • A → B is surjective, and • B is finite over C. Then A ×_B C is of finite type over R.

nodes.title: Fibre products of rings, I · Lemma 08NI
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let I be a finite set. Suppose given a cartesian diagram xymatrix ∏ B_i & ∏ A_i ar[l]^∏ φ_i Q ar[u]^∏ ψ_i & P ar[u] ar[l] with ψ_i and φ_i surjective, and Q, A_i, B_i of finite type over R. Then P is of finite type over R.

nodes.title: Fibre products of rings, I · Lemma 01Z8
nodes.summary: Suppose given a cartesian diagram of rings xymatrix R & R' ar[l]^t B ar[u]_s & B'ar[u] ar[l] i.e., B' = B ×_R R'. If h ∈ B' corresponds to g ∈ B and f ∈ R' such that s(g) = t(f), then the diagram xymatrix R_s(g) = R_t(f) & (R')_f ar[l]^-t B_g ar[u]_s & (B')_h ar[u] ar[l] is cartesian too.

nodes.title: Fibre products of rings, I · Lemma 0D2F
nodes.summary: Given a commutative diagram of rings xymatrix R & R' ar[l] B ar[u] & B' ar[u] ar[l] the functor ([Tag 0D2E]) has a right adjoint, namely the functor F : (N, M', φ) ↦ N ×_φ M' (see proof for elucidation).

nodes.title: Fibre products of rings, II · Lemma 0B7J
nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 08KH] we have Spec(B') = Spec(B) amalg_Spec(A) Spec(A') as topological spaces.

nodes.title: Fibre products of rings, II · Lemma 0E1S
nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 08KH] if B → A is integral, then B' → A' is integral.

nodes.title: Fibre products of rings, II · Lemma 07RU
nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 08KH] the functor ([Tag 08KI]) has a right adjoint, namely the functor F : (N, M', φ) ↦ N ×_φ, M M' where M = M'/IM'. Moreover, the composition of F with ([Tag 08KI]) is the identity functor on Mod_B ×_Mod_A Mod_A'. In other words, setting N' = N ×_φ, M M' we have N' ⊗_B' B = N and N' ⊗_B' A' = M'.

nodes.title: Fibre products of rings, II · Lemma 08IG
nodes.summary: In the situation of Lemma [Tag 07RU] for a B'-module L' the adjunction map L' → (L' ⊗_B' B) ×_(L' ⊗_B' A) (L' ⊗_B' A') is surjective but in general not injective.

nodes.title: Fibre products of rings, II · Lemma 08KJ
nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 08KH] let (N_1, M'_1, φ_1) → (N_2, M'_2, φ_2) be a morphism of Mod_B ×_Mod_A Mod_A' with N_1 → N_2 and M'_1 → M'_2 surjective. Then N_1 ×_φ_1, M_1 M'_1 → N_2 ×_φ_2, M_2 M'_2 where M_1 = M'_1/IM'_1 and M_2 = M'_2/IM'_2 is surjective.

nodes.title: Fibre products of rings, II · Lemma 0D2H
nodes.summary: Let A, A', B, B', I, M, M', N, φ be as in Lemma [Tag 07RU]. If N finite over B and M' finite over A', then N' = N ×_φ, M M' is finite over B'.

nodes.title: Fibre products of rings, II · Lemma 0D2I
nodes.summary: With A, A', B, B', I as in Situation [Tag 08KH]. • Let (N, M', φ) be an object of Mod_B ×_Mod_A Mod_A'. If M' is flat over A' and N is flat over B, then N' = N ×_φ, M M' is flat over B'. • If L' is a flat B'-module, then L' = (L ⊗_B' B) ×_(L ⊗_B' A) (L ⊗_B' A'). • The category of flat B'-modules is equivalent to the full subcategory of Mod_B ×_Mod_A Mod_A' consisting of triples (N, M', φ) with N flat over B and M' flat over A'.

nodes.title: Fibre products of rings, II · Lemma 0D2J
nodes.summary: Let A, A', B, B', I be as in Situation [Tag 08KH]. The category of finite projective B'-modules is equivalent to the full subcategory of Mod_B ×_Mod_A Mod_A' consisting of triples (N, M', φ) with N finite projective over B and M' finite projective over A'.

nodes.title: Fibre products of rings, III · Lemma 08KM
nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 08KK] the functor ([Tag 08KL]) has a right adjoint, namely the functor F : (N, M', φ) ↦ N ×_φ, M M' where M = M'/IM'. Moreover, the composition of F with ([Tag 08KL]) is the identity functor on Mod_D ×_Mod_C Mod_C'. In other words, setting N' = N ×_φ, M M' we have N' ⊗_D' D = N and N' ⊗_D' C' = M'.

nodes.title: Fibre products of rings, III · Lemma 08KN
nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 08KK] the map JD' → IC' is surjective where J = Ker(B' → B).

nodes.title: Fibre products of rings, III · Lemma 08IH
nodes.summary: Let A, A', B, B', C, C', D, D', I, M', M, N, φ be as in Lemma [Tag 08KM]. If N finite over D and M' finite over C', then N' = N ×_φ, M M' is finite over D'.

nodes.title: Fibre products of rings, III · Lemma 07RW
nodes.summary: With A, A', B, B', C, C', D, D', I as in Situation [Tag 08KK]. • Let (N, M', φ) be an object of Mod_D ×_Mod_C Mod_C'. If M' is flat over A' and N is flat over B, then N' = N ×_φ, M M' is flat over B'. • If L' is a D'-module flat over B', then L' = (L ⊗_D' D) ×_(L ⊗_D' C) (L ⊗_D' C'). • The category of D'-modules flat over B' is equivalent to the categories of objects (N, M', φ) of Mod_D ×_Mod_C Mod_C' with N flat over B and M' flat over A'.

nodes.title: Fibre products of rings, III · Lemma 08KP
nodes.summary: Let A, A', B, B', C, C', D, D', I, M', M, N, φ be as in Lemma [Tag 08KM]. If • N is finitely presented over D and flat over B, • M' finitely presented over C' and flat over A', and • the ring map B' → D' factors as B' → D" → D' with B' → D" flat and D" → D' of finite presentation, then N' = N ×_M M' is finitely presented over D'.

nodes.title: Fibre products of rings, III · Lemma 08KQ
nodes.summary: Let A, A', B, B', I be as in Situation [Tag 08KH]. Let (D, C', φ) be a system consisting of an B-algebra D, a A'-algebra C' and an isomorphism D ⊗_B A → C'/IC' = C. Set D' = D ×_C C' (as in Lemma [Tag 07RU]). Then • B' → D' is finite type if and only if B → D and A' → C' are finite type, • B' → D' is flat if and only if B → D and A' → C' are flat, • B' → D' is flat and of finite presentation if and only if B → D and A' → C' are flat and of finite presentation, • B' → D'…

nodes.title: Fitting ideals · Lemma 07Z7
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let A be an n × m matrix with coefficients in R. Let I_r(A) be the ideal generated by the r × r-minors of A with the convention that I_0(A) = R and I_r(A) = 0 if r > min(n, m). Then • I_0(A) ⊃ I_1(A) ⊃ I_2(A) ⊃ …, • if B is an (n + n') × m matrix, and A is the first n rows of B, then I_r + n'(B) ⊂ I_r(A), • if C is an n × n matrix then I_r(CA) ⊂ I_r(A). • If A is a block matrix ( A_1 & 0 0 & A_2 ) then I_r(A) = ∑_r_1 + r_2 = r I_r_1(A_1) I_r_2(A_2). • Add…

nodes.title: Fitting ideals · Lemma 07Z8
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be a finite R-module. Choose a presentation bigoplus_j ∈ J R → R^⊕ n → M → 0. of M. Let A = (a_ij)_i = 1, …, n, j ∈ J be the matrix of the map bigoplus_j ∈ J R → R^⊕ n. The ideal Fit_k(M) generated by the (n - k) × (n - k) minors of A is independent of the choice of the presentation.

nodes.title: Fitting ideals · Definition 07Z9
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be a finite R-module. Let k ≥ 0. The kth Fitting ideal of M is the ideal Fit_k(M) constructed in Lemma [Tag 07Z8]. Set Fit_-1(M) = 0.

nodes.title: Fitting ideals · Lemma 07ZA
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be a finite R-module. • If M can be generated by n elements, then Fit_n(M) = R. • Given a second finite R-module M' we have Fit_0(M ⊕ M') = Fit_0(M)Fit_0(M') and more generally Fit_l(M ⊕ M') = ∑_k + k' = l Fit_k(M)Fit_k'(M') • If R → R' is a ring map, then Fit_k(M ⊗_R R') is the ideal of R' generated by the image of Fit_k(M). • If M is of finite presentation, then Fit_k(M) is a finitely generated ideal. • If M → M' is a surjection, then Fit_k(M) ⊂…

nodes.title: Fitting ideals · Lemma 07ZC
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be a finite R-module. Let k ≥ 0. Let p ⊂ R be a prime ideal. The following are equivalent • Fit_k(M) not ⊂ p, • dim_kappa( p) M ⊗_R kappa( p) ≤ k, • M_ p can be generated by k elements over R_ p, and • M_f can be generated by k elements over R_f for some f ∈ R, f not ∈ p.

nodes.title: Fitting ideals · Lemma 07ZD
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be a finite R-module. Let r ≥ 0. The following are equivalent • M is finite locally free of rank r (Algebra, Definition [Tag 00NW]), • Fit_r - 1(M) = 0 and Fit_r(M) = R, and • Fit_k(M) = 0 for k < r and Fit_k(M) = R for k ≥ r.

nodes.title: Fitting ideals · Lemma 080Z
nodes.summary: Let R be a local ring. Let M be a finite R-module. Let k ≥ 0. Assume that Fit_k(M) = (f) for some f ∈ R. Let M' be the quotient of M by (x ∈ M mid fx = 0). Then M' can be generated by k elements.

nodes.title: Fitting ideals · Lemma 0F7M
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be a finitely presented R-module. Let k ≥ 0. Assume that Fit_k(M) = (f) for some nonzerodivisor f ∈ R and Fit_k - 1(M) = 0. Then • M has projective dimension ≤ 1, • M' = Ker(f : M → M) is the f-power torsion submodule of M, • M' has projective dimension ≤ 1, • M/M' is finite locally free of rank k, and • M ≅ M/M' ⊕ M'.

nodes.title: Lifting · Lemma 07LX
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring, let I ⊂ A be an ideal, let overlineu ∈ A/I be an invertible element. There exists an étale ring map A → A' which induces an isomorphism A/I → A'/IA' and an invertible element u' ∈ A' lifting overlineu.

nodes.title: Lifting · Lemma 07LY
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring, let I ⊂ A be an ideal, let overlinee ∈ A/I be an idempotent. There exists an étale ring map A → A' which induces an isomorphism A/I → A'/IA' and an idempotent e' ∈ A' lifting overlinee.

nodes.title: Lifting · Lemma 07LZ
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring, let I ⊂ A be an ideal. Let Spec(A/I) = coprod_j ∈ J overlineU_j be a finite disjoint open covering. Then there exists an étale ring map A → A' which induces an isomorphism A/I → A'/IA' and a finite disjoint open covering Spec(A') = coprod_j ∈ J U'_j lifting the given covering.

nodes.title: Lifting · Lemma 07M0
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map and J ⊂ B an ideal. If A → B is étale at every prime of V(J), then there exists a g ∈ B mapping to an invertible element of B/J such that A' = B_g is étale over A.

nodes.title: Lifting · Lemma 0ALH
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring, let I ⊂ A be an ideal. Let f ∈ A[x] be a monic polynomial. Let overlinef = overlineg overlineh be a factorization of f in A/I[x] such that overlineg and overlineh are monic and generate the unit ideal in A/I[x]. Then there exists an étale ring map A → A' which induces an isomorphism A/I → A'/IA' and a factorization f = g' h' in A'[x] with g', h' monic lifting the given factorization over A/I.

nodes.title: Lifting · Lemma 07M1
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring, let I ⊂ A be an ideal. Let f ∈ A[x] be a monic polynomial. Let overlinef = overlineg overlineh be a factorization of f in A/I[x] and assume • the leading coefficient of overlineg is an invertible element of A/I, and • overlineg, overlineh generate the unit ideal in A/I[x]. Then there exists an étale ring map A → A' which induces an isomorphism A/I → A'/IA' and a factorization f = g' h' in A'[x] lifting the given factorization over A/I.

nodes.title: Lifting · Lemma 07M3
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal of R and let J ⊂ S be an ideal of S. If the closure of the image of V(J) in Spec(R) is disjoint from V(I), then there exists an element f ∈ R which maps to 1 in R/I and to an element of J in S.

nodes.title: Lifting · Lemma 09XG
nodes.summary: Let I be an ideal of a ring A. Let A → B be an integral ring map. Let b ∈ B map to an idempotent in B/IB. Then there exists a monic f ∈ A[x] with f(b) = 0 and f bmod I = x^d(x - 1)^d for some d ≥ 1.

nodes.title: Lifting · Lemma 07M4
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring, let I ⊂ A be an ideal. Let A → B be an integral ring map. Let overlinee ∈ B/IB be an idempotent. Then there exists an étale ring map A → A' which induces an isomorphism A/I → A'/IA' and an idempotent e' ∈ B ⊗_A A' lifting overlinee.

nodes.title: Lifting · Lemma 07M5
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring, let I ⊂ A be an ideal. Let overlineP be a finite projective A/I-module. Then there exists an étale ring map A → A' which induces an isomorphism A/I → A'/IA' and a finite projective A'-module P' lifting overlineP.

nodes.title: Lifting · Lemma 07EV
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let 0 → K → A^⊕ m → M → 0 be a sequence of A-modules. Consider the A-algebra C = Sym^*_A(M) with its presentation α : A[y_1, …, y_m] → C coming from the surjection A^⊕ m → M. Then NL(α) = (K ⊗_A C → bigoplus_j = 1, …, m C dy_j) (see Algebra, Section [Tag 00S0]) in particular Ω_C/A = M ⊗_A C.

nodes.title: Lifting · Lemma 07M6
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let M be an A-module. Then C = Sym_A^*(M) is smooth over A if and only if M is a finite projective A-module.

nodes.title: Lifting · Lemma 07M7
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring, let I ⊂ A be an ideal. Consider a commutative diagram xymatrix B ar[rd] A ar[u] ar[r] & A/I where B is a smooth A-algebra. Then there exists an étale ring map A → A' which induces an isomorphism A/I → A'/IA' and an A-algebra map B → A' lifting the ring map B → A/I.

nodes.title: Zariski pairs · Definition 0ELY
nodes.summary: A Zariski pair is a pair (A, I) such that I is contained in the Jacobson radical of A.

nodes.title: Zariski pairs · Lemma 09XF
nodes.summary: Let (A, I) be a Zariski pair. Then the map from idempotents of A to idempotents of A/I is injective.

nodes.title: Zariski pairs · Lemma 0ELZ
nodes.summary: Let (A, I) be a Zariski pair. Let A → B be a flat, integral, finitely presented ring map such that A/I → B/IB is an isomorphism. Then A → B is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Zariski pairs · Lemma 0EM0
nodes.summary: Let (A, I) be a Zariski pair. Let A → B be a finite ring map. Assume • B/IB = B_1 × B_2 is a product of A/I-algebras • A/I → B_1/IB_1 is surjective, • b ∈ B maps to (1, 0) in the product. Then there exists a monic f ∈ A[x] with f(b) = 0 and f bmod I = (x - 1)x^d for some d ≥ 1.

nodes.title: Zariski pairs · Lemma 0GED
nodes.summary: Let (A, I) be a Zariski pair with A Noetherian. Let f ∈ I. Then A_f is a Jacobson ring.

nodes.title: Henselian pairs · Definition 09XE
nodes.summary: A henselian pair is a pair (A, I) satisfying • I is contained in the Jacobson radical of A, and • for any monic polynomial f ∈ A[T] and factorization overlinef = g_0h_0 with g_0, h_0 ∈ A/I[T] monic generating the unit ideal in A/I[T], there exists a factorization f = gh in A[T] with g, h monic and g_0 = overlineg and h_0 = overlineh.

nodes.title: Henselian pairs · Lemma 0ALI
nodes.summary: Let (A, I) be a pair with I locally nilpotent. Then the functor B ↦ B/IB induces an equivalence between the category of étale algebras over A and the category of étale algebras over A/I. Moreover, the pair is henselian.

nodes.title: Henselian pairs · Lemma 0CT7
nodes.summary: Let A = lim A_n where (A_n) is an inverse system of rings whose transition maps are surjective and have locally nilpotent kernels. Then (A, I_n) is a henselian pair, where I_n = Ker(A → A_n).

nodes.title: Henselian pairs · Lemma 0ALJ
nodes.summary: Let (A, I) be a pair. If A is I-adically complete, then the pair is henselian.

nodes.title: Henselian pairs · Lemma 09XH
nodes.summary: Let (A, I) be a pair. Let A → B be a finite type ring map such that B/IB = C_1 × C_2 with A/I → C_1 finite. Let B' be the integral closure of A in B. Then we can write B'/IB' = C_1 × C'_2 such that the map B'/IB' → B/IB preserves product decompositions and there exists a g ∈ B' mapping to (1, 0) in C_1 × C'_2 with B'_g → B_g an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Henselian pairs · Lemma 09XI
nodes.summary: [Henselian] and [Gabber-henselian] Let (A, I) be a pair. The following are equivalent • (A, I) is a henselian pair, • given an étale ring map A → A' and an A-algebra map σ : A' → A/I, there exists an A-algebra map A' → A lifting σ, • for any finite A-algebra B the map B → B/IB induces a bijection on idempotents, • for any integral A-algebra B the map B → B/IB induces a bijection on idempotents, and • (Gabber) I is contained in the Jacobson radical of A and every monic…

nodes.title: Henselian pairs · Lemma 09XJ
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let I, J ⊂ A be ideals with V(I) = V(J). Then (A, I) is henselian if and only if (A, J) is henselian.

nodes.title: Henselian pairs · Lemma 09XK
nodes.summary: Let (A, I) be a henselian pair and let A → B be an integral ring map. Then (B, IB) is a henselian pair.

nodes.title: Henselian pairs · Lemma 0DYD
nodes.summary: Let I ⊂ J ⊂ A be ideals of a ring A. The following are equivalent • (A, I) and (A/I, J/I) are henselian pairs, and • (A, J) is an henselian pair.

nodes.title: Henselian pairs · Lemma 0G1R
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring and let (A, I) and (A, I') be henselian pairs. Then (A, I + I') is an henselian pair.

nodes.title: Henselian pairs · Lemma 0ATD
nodes.summary: Let J be a set and let ( (A_j, I_j))_j ∈ J be a collection of pairs. Then (∏_j ∈ J A_j, ∏_j∈ J I_j) is Henselian if and only if so is each (A_j, I_j).

nodes.title: Henselian pairs · Lemma 0EM6
nodes.summary: The property of being Henselian is preserved under limits of pairs. More precisely, let J be a preordered set and let (A_j, I_j) be an inverse system of henselian pairs over J. Then A = lim A_j equipped with the ideal I = lim I_j is a henselian pair (A, I).

nodes.title: Henselian pairs · Lemma 0FWT
nodes.summary: The property of being Henselian is preserved under filtered colimits of pairs. More precisely, let J be a directed set and let (A_j, I_j) be a system of henselian pairs over J. Then A = colim A_j equipped with the ideal I = colim I_j is a henselian pair (A, I).

nodes.title: Henselian pairs · Lemma 0G1S
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. There exists a largest ideal I ⊂ A such that (A, I) is a henselian pair.

nodes.title: Henselian pairs · Lemma 09Y6
nodes.summary: Let (A, I) be a henselian pair. Let p ⊂ A be a prime ideal. Then V( p + I) is connected.

nodes.title: Henselization of pairs · Lemma 0A02
nodes.summary: The inclusion functor category of henselian pairs → category of pairs has a left adjoint (A, I) ↦ (A^h, I^h).

nodes.title: Henselization of pairs · Lemma 0AGU
nodes.summary: Let (A, I) be a pair. Let (A^h, I^h) be as in Lemma [Tag 0A02]. Then A → A^h is flat, I^h = IA^h and A/I^n → A^h/I^nA^h is an isomorphism for all n.

nodes.title: Henselization of pairs · Lemma 0A03
nodes.summary: Compatibility henselization of pairs and of local rings. The functor of Lemma [Tag 0A02] associates to a local ring (A, m) its henselization.

nodes.title: Henselization of pairs · Lemma 0AGV
nodes.summary: The henselization of a Noetherian pair is a Noetherian pair with the same completion Let (A, I) be a pair with A Noetherian. Let (A^h, I^h) be as in Lemma [Tag 0A02]. Then the map of I-adic completions A^wedge → (A^h)^wedge is an isomorphism. Moreover, A^h is Noetherian, the maps A → A^h → A^wedge are flat, and A^h → A^wedge is faithfully flat.

nodes.title: Henselization of pairs · Lemma 0A04
nodes.summary: Let (A, I) = colim (A_i, I_i) be a filtered colimit of pairs. The functor of Lemma [Tag 0A02] gives A^h = colim A_i^h and I^h = colim I_i^h.

nodes.title: Henselization of pairs · Lemma 0F0L
nodes.summary: The henselization of a pair only depends on the radical of the ideal Let A be a ring with ideals I and J. If V(I) = V(J) then the functor of Lemma [Tag 0A02] produces the same ring for the pair (A, I) as for the pair (A, J).

nodes.title: Henselization of pairs · Lemma 0DYE
nodes.summary: Henselization commutes with integral base change Let (A, I) → (B, J) be a map of pairs such that V(J) = V(IB). Let (A^h , I^h) → (B^h, J^h) be the induced map on henselizations (Lemma [Tag 0A02]). If A → B is integral, then the induced map A^h ⊗_A B → B^h is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Henselization of pairs · Lemma 0H7Q
nodes.summary: Let I_1, I_2, dots, I_n ⊂ A be ideals in a ring A. Suppose I_i + I_j = A for i not = j, 1 ≤ i, j ≤ n. Denote A^h the henselization of the pair (A, I_1 ∩ … ∩ I_n) and A_i^h the henselization of the pair (A, I_i). Then the natural morphism A^h → ∏_i = 1, …, n A^h_i is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Lifting and henselian pairs · Lemma 0D4A
nodes.summary: Let (R, I) be a henselian pair. The map P → P/IP induces a bijection between the sets of isomorphism classes of finite projective R-modules and finite projective R/I-modules. In particular, any finite projective R/I-module is isomorphic to P/IP for some finite projective R-module P.

nodes.title: Lifting and henselian pairs · Lemma 09ZL
nodes.summary: Let (A, I) be a henselian pair. The functor B → B/IB determines an equivalence between finite étale A-algebras and finite étale A/I-algebras.

nodes.title: Lifting and henselian pairs · Lemma 0H74
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring and S a smooth R-algebra. Assume that A is an R-algebra and (A,I) is a henselian pair. Then any R-algebra map S → A/I can be lifted to an R-algebra map S → A.

nodes.title: Lifting and henselian pairs · Lemma 0D4B
nodes.summary: Let A = lim A_n be a limit of an inverse system (A_n) of rings. Suppose given A_n-modules M_n and A_n + 1-module maps M_n + 1 → M_n. Assume • the transition maps A_n + 1 → A_n are surjective with locally nilpotent kernels, • M_1 is a finite projective A_1-module, • M_n is a finite flat A_n-module, and • the maps induce isomorphisms M_n + 1 ⊗_A_n + 1 A_n → M_n. Then M = lim M_n is a finite projective A-module and M ⊗_A A_n → M_n is an isomorphism for all n.

nodes.title: Absolute integral closure · Definition 0DCL
nodes.summary: A ring A is absolutely integrally closed if every monic f ∈ A[T] is a product of linear factors.

nodes.title: Absolute integral closure · Lemma 0DCM
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. The following are equivalent • A is absolutely integrally closed, and • any monic f ∈ A[T] has a root in A.

nodes.title: Absolute integral closure · Lemma 0DCN
nodes.summary: Let A be absolutely integrally closed. • Any quotient ring A/I of A is absolutely integrally closed. • Any localization S^-1A is absolutely integrally closed.

nodes.title: Absolute integral closure · Lemma 0DCP
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let S ⊂ A be a multiplicative subset consisting of nonzerodivisors. If S^-1A is absolutely integrally closed and A ⊂ S^-1A is integrally closed in S^-1A, then A is absolutely integrally closed.

nodes.title: Absolute integral closure · Lemma 0DCQ
nodes.summary: Let A be a normal domain. Then A is absolutely integrally closed if and only if its fraction field is algebraically closed.

nodes.title: Absolute integral closure · Lemma 0DCR
nodes.summary: For any ring A there exists an extension A ⊂ B such that • B is a filtered colimit of finite free A-algebras, • B is free as an A-module, and • B is absolutely integrally closed.

nodes.title: Absolute integral closure · Lemma 0DCS
nodes.summary: Let A be absolutely integrally closed. Let p ⊂ A be a prime. Then the local ring A_ p is strictly henselian.

nodes.title: Absolute integral closure · Lemma 0DCT
nodes.summary: Let A be absolutely integrally closed. Let I ⊂ A be an ideal. Then (A, I) is a henselian pair if (and only if) the following conditions hold • I is contained in the Jacobson radical of A, • A → A/I induces a bijection on idempotents.

nodes.title: Auto-associated rings · Definition 05GM
nodes.summary: A ring R is said to be auto-associated if R is local and its maximal ideal m is weakly associated to R.

nodes.title: Auto-associated rings · Lemma 05GN
nodes.summary: An auto-associated ring R has the following property: (P) Every proper finitely generated ideal I ⊂ R has a nonzero annihilator.

nodes.title: Auto-associated rings · Lemma 05GP
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring having property (P) of Lemma [Tag 05GN]. Let u : N → M be a homomorphism of projective R-modules. Then u is universally injective if and only if u is injective.

nodes.title: Auto-associated rings · Lemma 05GQ
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. The following are equivalent • R has property (P) of Lemma [Tag 05GN], • any injective map of projective R-modules is universally injective, • if u : N → M is injective and N, M are finite projective R-modules then Coker(u) is a finite projective R-module, • if N ⊂ M and N, M are finite projective as R-modules, then N is a direct summand of M, and • any injective map R → R^⊕ n is a split injection.

nodes.title: Auto-associated rings · Lemma 00MX
nodes.summary: Let (R, m) be a local ring. Suppose that φ : R^m → R^n is a map of finite free modules. The following are equivalent • φ is injective, • the rank of φ is m and the annihilator of I(φ) in R is zero. If R is Noetherian these are also equivalent to • [(3)] the rank of φ is m and either I(φ) = R or it contains a nonzerodivisor. Here the rank of φ and I(φ) are defined as in Algebra, Definition [Tag 00MV].

nodes.title: Auto-associated rings · Lemma 0EWY
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Suppose that φ : R^n → R^n be an injective map of finite free modules of the same rank. Then Hom_R(Coker(φ), R) = 0.

nodes.title: Flattening stratification · Lemma 0522
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Let I_1, I_2 be ideals of R. If M/I_1M is flat over R/I_1 and M/I_2M is flat over R/I_2, then M/(I_1 ∩ I_2)M is flat over R/(I_1 ∩ I_2).

nodes.title: Flattening over an Artinian ring · Lemma 0524
nodes.summary: Let R be an Artinian ring. Let M be an R-module. Then there exists a smallest ideal I ⊂ R such that M/IM is flat over R/I.

nodes.title: Flattening over an Artinian ring · Lemma 0525
nodes.summary: Let R be an Artinian ring. Let M be an R-module. Let I ⊂ R be the smallest ideal I ⊂ R such that M/IM is flat over R/I. Then I has the following universal property: For every ring map φ : R → R' we have R' ⊗_R M is flat over R' ⇔ we have φ(I) = 0.

nodes.title: Flattening over a closed subset of the base · Lemma 052X
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let M be an S-module. Let R → R' be a ring map and IR' ⊂ I' ⊂ R' an ideal. If ([Tag 052W]) holds for (R → S, I, M), then ([Tag 052W]) holds for (R' → S ⊗_R R', I', M ⊗_R R').
nodes.section: Flattening over a closed subset of the base

nodes.title: Flattening over a closed subset of the base · Lemma 05LL
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let M be an S-module. Let R → R' be a ring map and IR' ⊂ I' ⊂ R' an ideal such that • the map V(I') → V(I) induced by Spec(R') → Spec(R) is surjective, and • R'_ p' is flat over R for all primes p' ∈ V(I'). If ([Tag 052W]) holds for (R' → S ⊗_R R', I', M ⊗_R R'), then ([Tag 052W]) holds for (R → S, I, M).
nodes.section: Flattening over a closed subset of the base

nodes.title: Flattening over a closed subset of the base · Lemma 05LM
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map of finite presentation. Let M be an S-module of finite presentation. Let R' = colim_λ ∈ Lambda R_λ be a directed colimit of R-algebras. Let I_λ ⊂ R_λ be ideals such that I_λ R_μ ⊂ I_μ for all μ ≥ λ and set I' = colim_λ I_λ. If ([Tag 052W]) holds for (R' → S ⊗_R R', I', M ⊗_R R'), then there exists a λ ∈ Lambda such that ([Tag 052W]) holds for (R_λ → S ⊗_R R_λ, I_λ, M ⊗_R R_λ).
nodes.section: Flattening over a closed subset of the base

nodes.title: Flattening over a closed subsets of source and base · Lemma 05LR
nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 05LP] let R' → R" be an R-algebra map. Let I' ⊂ R' and I'R" ⊂ I" ⊂ R" be ideals. If ([Tag 05LQ]) holds for (R', I'), then ([Tag 05LQ]) holds for (R", I").
nodes.section: Flattening over a closed subsets of source and base

nodes.title: Flattening over a closed subsets of source and base · Lemma 05LS
nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 05LP] let R' → R" be an R-algebra map. Let I' ⊂ R' and I'R" ⊂ I" ⊂ R" be ideals. Assume • the map V(I") → V(I') induced by Spec(R") → Spec(R') is surjective, and • R"_ p" is flat over R' for all primes p" ∈ V(I"). If ([Tag 05LQ]) holds for (R", I"), then ([Tag 05LQ]) holds for (R', I').
nodes.section: Flattening over a closed subsets of source and base

nodes.title: Flattening over a closed subsets of source and base · Lemma 05LT
nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 05LP] assume R → S is essentially of finite presentation and M is an S-module of finite presentation. Let R' = colim_λ ∈ Lambda R_λ be a directed colimit of R-algebras. Let I_λ ⊂ R_λ be ideals such that I_λ R_μ ⊂ I_μ for all μ ≥ λ and set I' = colim_λ I_λ. If ([Tag 05LQ]) holds for (R', I'), then there exists a λ ∈ Lambda such that ([Tag 05LQ]) holds for (R_λ, I_λ).
nodes.section: Flattening over a closed subsets of source and base

nodes.title: Flattening over a closed subsets of source and base · Lemma 05LU
nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 05LP]. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Assume • R is a Noetherian ring, • S is a Noetherian ring, • M is a finite S-module, and • for each n ≥ 1 and any prime q ∈ V(J + IS) the module (M/I^n M)_ q is flat over R/I^n. Then ([Tag 05LQ]) holds for (R, I), i.e., for every prime q ∈ V(J + IS) the localization M_ q is flat over R.
nodes.section: Flattening over a closed subsets of source and base

nodes.title: Flattening over a Noetherian complete local ring · Lemma 0526
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let M be an S-module. Assume • (R, m) is a complete local Noetherian ring, • S is a Noetherian ring, and • M is finite over S. Then there exists an ideal I ⊂ m such that • (M/IM)_ q is flat over R/I for all primes q of S/IS lying over m, and • if J ⊂ R is an ideal such that (M/JM)_ q is flat over R/J for all primes q lying over m, then I ⊂ J. In other words, I is the smallest ideal of R such that ([Tag 052W]) holds for (overlineR → overlineS,…
nodes.section: Flattening over a Noetherian complete local ring

nodes.title: Flattening over a Noetherian complete local ring · Lemma 0527
nodes.summary: With notation R → S, M, and I and assumptions as in Lemma [Tag 0526]. Consider a local homomorphism of local rings φ : (R, m) → (R', m') such that R' is Noetherian. Then the following are equivalent • condition ([Tag 052W]) holds for (R' → S ⊗_R R', m', M ⊗_R R'), and • φ(I) = 0.
nodes.section: Flattening over a Noetherian complete local ring

nodes.title: Flattening over a Noetherian complete local ring · Lemma 0528
nodes.summary: With notation R → S, M, and I and assumptions as in Lemma [Tag 0526]. In addition assume that R → S is of finite type. Then for any local homomorphism of local rings φ : (R, m) → (R', m') the following are equivalent • condition ([Tag 052W]) holds for (R' → S ⊗_R R', m', M ⊗_R R'), and • φ(I) = 0.
nodes.section: Flattening over a Noetherian complete local ring

nodes.title: Descent of flatness along integral maps · Lemma 052Z
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let P(T) be a monic polynomial with coefficients in R. Let α ∈ R be such that P(α) = 0. Then P(T) = (T - α)Q(T) for some monic polynomial Q(T) ∈ R[T].
nodes.section: Descent of flatness along integral maps

nodes.title: Descent of flatness along integral maps · Lemma 0530
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let P(T) be a monic polynomial with coefficients in R. There exists a finite free ring map R → R' such that P(T) = (T - α)Q(T) for some α ∈ R' and some monic polynomial Q(T) ∈ R'[T].
nodes.section: Descent of flatness along integral maps

nodes.title: Descent of flatness along integral maps · Lemma 0531
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a finite ring map. There exists a finite free ring extension R ⊂ R' such that S ⊗_R R' is a quotient of a ring of the form R'[T_1, …, T_n]/(P_1(T_1), …, P_n(T_n)) with P_i(T) = ∏_j = 1, …, d_i (T - α_ij) for some α_ij ∈ R'.
nodes.section: Descent of flatness along integral maps

nodes.title: Descent of flatness along integral maps · Lemma 0532
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let S = R[T_1, …, T_n]/J. Assume J contains elements of the form P_i(T_i) with P_i(T) = ∏_j = 1, …, d_i (T - α_ij) for some α_ij ∈ R. For underlinek = (k_1, …, k_n) with 1 ≤ k_i ≤ d_i consider the ring map Φ_underlinek : R[T_1, …, T_n] → R, T_i ↦ α_ik_i Set J_underlinek = Φ_underlinek(J). Then the image of Spec(S) → Spec(R) is equal to V(⋂ J_underlinek).
nodes.section: Descent of flatness along integral maps

nodes.title: Descent of flatness along integral maps · Lemma 0533
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a finite injective homomorphism of Noetherian rings. Let M be an R-module. If M ⊗_R S is a flat S-module, then M is a flat R-module.
nodes.section: Descent of flatness along integral maps

nodes.title: Descent of flatness along integral maps · Lemma 0534
nodes.summary: Let R → S be an injective integral ring map. Let M be a finitely presented module over R[x_1, …, x_n]. If M ⊗_R S is flat over S, then M is flat over R.
nodes.section: Descent of flatness along integral maps

nodes.title: Descent of flatness along integral maps · Lemma 0H7R
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a finite injective homomorphism of Noetherian rings. Let P be an R-module. If P ⊗_R S is a projective S-module, then P is a projective R-module.
nodes.section: Descent of flatness along integral maps

nodes.title: Torsion free modules · Definition 0536
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain. Let M be an R-module. • We say an element x ∈ M is torsion if there exists a nonzero f ∈ R such that fx = 0. • We say M is torsion free if the only torsion element of M is 0. • We say M is a torsion module if every element of M is torsion.

nodes.title: Torsion free modules · Lemma 0537
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain. Let M be an R-module. The set of torsion elements M_tors of M is the kernel of the map M → M ⊗_R K. Thus M_tors is an R-submodule of M. The quotient module M/M_tors is torsion free.

nodes.title: Torsion free modules · Lemma 0AUR
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain. Let M be a torsion free R-module. For any multiplicative set S ⊂ R the module S^-1M is a torsion free S^-1R-module.

nodes.title: Torsion free modules · Lemma 0AXM
nodes.summary: Let R → R' be a flat homomorphism of domains. If M is a torsion free R-module, then M ⊗_R R' is a torsion free R'-module.

nodes.title: Torsion free modules · Lemma 0AUS
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain. Let 0 → M → M' → M" → 0 be a short exact sequence of R-modules. If M and M" are torsion free, then M' is torsion free.

nodes.title: Torsion free modules · Lemma 0AUT
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain. Let M be an R-module. Then M is torsion free if and only if M_ m is a torsion free R_ m-module for all maximal ideals m of R.

nodes.title: Torsion free modules · Lemma 0AUU
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain. Let M be a finite R-module. Then M is torsion free if and only if M is a submodule of a finite free module.

nodes.title: Torsion free modules · Lemma 0AUV
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian domain. Let M be a nonzero finite R-module. The following are equivalent • M is torsion free, • M is a submodule of a finite free module, • (0) is the only associated prime of M, • (0) is in the support of M and M has property (S_1), and • (0) is in the support of M and M has no embedded associated prime.

nodes.title: Torsion free modules · Lemma 0538
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain. Any flat R-module is torsion free.

nodes.title: Torsion free modules · Lemma 0539
nodes.summary: Let A be a valuation ring. An A-module M is flat over A if and only if M is torsion free.

nodes.title: Torsion free modules · Lemma 0AUW
nodes.summary: Let A be a Dedekind domain (for example a discrete valuation ring or more generally a PID). • An A-module is flat if and only if it is torsion free. • A finite torsion free A-module is finite locally free. • A finite torsion free A-module is finite free if A is a PID.

nodes.title: Torsion free modules · Lemma 0AUX
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain. Let M, N be R-modules. If N is torsion free, so is Hom_R(M, N).

nodes.title: Ranks of modules · Definition 0H9U
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain with fraction field K. The rank of an R-module M is dim_K(M ⊗_R K).

nodes.title: Ranks of modules · Lemma 0H9V
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain. If M → M' is a map of R-modules whose kernel and cokernel are torsion, then the rank of M equals the rank of M'.

nodes.title: Ranks of modules · Lemma 0H9W
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain. Let 0 → M → M' → M" → 0 be a short exact sequence of R-modules. Then the rank of M' is the sum of the ranks of M and M".

nodes.title: Ranks of modules · Lemma 0H9X
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain. Let M and N be R-modules. • The rank of M ⊗_R N is the product of the ranks of M and N. • If M is a finitely presented R-module, then the rank of Hom_R(M, N) is the product of the ranks of M and N.

nodes.title: Ranks of modules · Lemma 0H9Y
nodes.summary: Let R ⊂ R' be an extension of domains. If M is an R-module, then the rank of M over R is equal to the rank of M ⊗_R R' over R'.

nodes.title: Ranks of modules · Lemma 0H9Z
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain. Let M be a finite R-module. Then • M has finite rank r ≥ 0, • there is a map M → R^⊕ r whose kernel and cokernel are torsion modules, • there is an f ∈ R, f not = 0 such that M_f is free of rank r, and • there is an injective map R^⊕ r → M whose cokernel is a torsion module.

nodes.title: Reflexive modules · Definition 0AUZ
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain. We say an R-module M is reflexive if the natural map j : M → Hom_R(Hom_R(M, R), R) which sends m ∈ M to the map sending φ ∈ Hom_R(M, R) to φ(m) ∈ R is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Reflexive modules · Lemma 0AV0
nodes.summary: Let R be a domain and let M be an R-module. • If M is reflexive, then M is torsion free. • If M is finite, then the kernel and cokernel of j : M → Hom_R(Hom_R(M, R), R) are torsion modules. • If M is finite, then j is injective if and only if M is torsion free.

nodes.title: Reflexive modules · Lemma 0B36
nodes.summary: Let R be a discrete valuation ring and let M be a finite R-module. Then the map j : M → Hom_R(Hom_R(M, R), R) is surjective.

nodes.title: Reflexive modules · Lemma 0AV1
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian domain. Let M be a finite R-module. The following are equivalent: • M is reflexive, • M_ p is a reflexive R_ p-module for all primes p ⊂ R, and • M_ m is a reflexive R_ m-module for all maximal ideals m of R.

nodes.title: Reflexive modules · Lemma 0EB8
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian domain. Let 0 → M → M' → M" an exact sequence of finite R-modules. If M' is reflexive and M" is torsion free, then M is reflexive.

nodes.title: Reflexive modules · Lemma 0AV2
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian domain. Let M be a finite R-module. The following are equivalent • M is reflexive, • there exists a short exact sequence 0 → M → F → N → 0 with F finite free and N torsion free.

nodes.title: Reflexive modules · Lemma 0EB9
nodes.summary: Let R → R' be a flat homomorphism of Noetherian domains. If M is a finite reflexive R-module, then M ⊗_R R' is a finite reflexive R'-module.

nodes.title: Reflexive modules · Lemma 0AV3
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian domain. Let M be a finite R-module. Let N be a finite reflexive R-module. Then Hom_R(M, N) is reflexive.

nodes.title: Reflexive modules · Definition 0AV4
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian domain. Let M be a finite R-module. The module M^** = Hom_R(Hom_R(M, R), R) is called the reflexive hull of M.

nodes.title: Reflexive modules · Lemma 0AV5
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring. Let M, N be finite R-modules. • If N has depth ≥ 1, then Hom_R(M, N) has depth ≥ 1. • If N has depth ≥ 2, then Hom_R(M, N) has depth ≥ 2.

nodes.title: Reflexive modules · Lemma 0AV6
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let M, N be finite R-modules. • If N has property (S_1), then Hom_R(M, N) has property (S_1). • If N has property (S_2), then Hom_R(M, N) has property (S_2). • If R is a domain, N is torsion free and (S_2), then Hom_R(M, N) is torsion free and has property (S_2).

nodes.title: Reflexive modules · Lemma 0AV7
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let φ : M → N be a map of R-modules. Assume that for every prime p of R at least one of the following happens • M_ p → N_ p is injective, or • p not ∈ Ass(M). Then φ is injective.

nodes.title: Reflexive modules · Lemma 0AV8
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let φ : M → N be a map of R-modules. Assume M is finite and that for every prime p of R one of the following happens • M_ p → N_ p is an isomorphism, or • depth(M_ p) ≥ 2 and p not ∈ Ass(N). Then φ is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Reflexive modules · Lemma 0AV9
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian domain. Let φ : M → N be a map of R-modules. Assume M is finite, N is torsion free, and that for every prime p of R one of the following happens • M_ p → N_ p is an isomorphism, or • depth(M_ p) ≥ 2. Then φ is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Reflexive modules · Lemma 0AVA
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian domain. Let M be a finite R-module. The following are equivalent • M is reflexive, • for every prime p of R one of the following happens • M_ p is a reflexive R_ p-module, or • depth(M_ p) ≥ 2.

nodes.title: Reflexive modules · Lemma 0EBA
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian domain. Let M be a finite reflexive R-module. Let p ⊂ R be a prime ideal. • If depth(R_ p) ≥ 2, then depth(M_ p) ≥ 2. • If R is (S_2), then M is (S_2).

nodes.title: Reflexive modules · Lemma 0AVB
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian normal domain with fraction field K. Let M be a finite R-module. The following are equivalent • M is reflexive, • M is torsion free and has property (S_2), • M is torsion free and M = ⋂_height( p) = 1 M_ p where the intersection happens in M_K = M ⊗_R K.

nodes.title: Reflexive modules · Lemma 0AVC
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian normal domain. Let M be a finite R-module. Then the reflexive hull of M is the intersection M^** = ⋂_height( p) = 1 M_ p/(M_ p)_tors = ⋂_height( p) = 1 (M/M_tors)_ p taken in M ⊗_R K.

nodes.title: Reflexive modules · Lemma 0BM4
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian normal domain with fraction field K. Let L be a finite extension of K. If the integral closure B of A in L is finite over A, then B is reflexive as an A-module.

nodes.title: Content ideals · Definition 0ASA
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let M be a flat A-module. Let x ∈ M. If the set of ideals I in A such that x ∈ IM has a smallest element, we call it the content ideal of x.

nodes.title: Content ideals · Lemma 0ASB
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let M be a flat A-module. Let x ∈ M. The content ideal of x, if it exists, is finitely generated.

nodes.title: Content ideals · Lemma 0ASC
nodes.summary: Let (A, m) be a local ring. Let u : M → N be a map of flat A-modules such that overlineu : M/ m M → N/ m N is injective. If x ∈ M has content ideal I, then u(x) has content ideal I as well.

nodes.title: Content ideals · Lemma 0ASD
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let M be a flat Mittag-Leffler module. Then every element of M has a content ideal.

nodes.title: Flatness and finiteness conditions · Lemma 053A
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let S = R[x_1, …, x_n] be a polynomial ring over R. Let M be an S-module. Assume • there exist finitely many primes p_1, …, p_m of R such that the map R → ∏ R_ p_j is injective, • M is a finite S-module, • M flat over R, and • for every prime p of R the module M_ p is of finite presentation over S_ p. Then M is of finite presentation over S.

nodes.title: Flatness and finiteness conditions · Lemma 053B
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring homomorphism. Assume • there exist finitely many primes p_1, …, p_m of R such that the map R → ∏ R_ p_j is injective, • R → S is of finite type, • S flat over R, and • for every prime p of R the ring S_ p is of finite presentation over R_ p. Then S is of finite presentation over R.

nodes.title: Flatness and finiteness conditions · Lemma 053C
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let S = R[x_1, …, x_n] be a graded polynomial algebra over R, i.e., deg(x_i) > 0 but not necessarily equal to 1. Let M be a graded S-module. Assume • R is a local ring, • M is a finite S-module, and • M is flat over R. Then M is finitely presented as an S-module.

nodes.title: Flatness and finiteness conditions · Lemma 053D
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let S = bigoplus_n ≥ 0 S_n be a graded R-algebra. Let M = bigoplus_d ∈ Z M_d be a graded S-module. Assume S is finitely generated as an R-algebra, assume S_0 is a finite R-algebra, and assume there exist finitely many primes p_j, i = 1, …, m such that R → ∏ R_ p_j is injective. • If S is flat over R, then S is a finitely presented R-algebra. • If M is flat as an R-module and finite as an S-module, then M is finitely presented as an S-module.

nodes.title: Flatness and finiteness conditions · Lemma 053E
nodes.summary: [Nagata-Finitely] Let A be a valuation ring. Let A → B be a ring map of finite type. Let M be a finite B-module. • If B is flat over A, then B is a finitely presented A-algebra. • If M is flat as an A-module, then M is finitely presented as a B-module.

nodes.title: Flatness and finiteness conditions · Lemma 0GSE
nodes.summary: Let A be a valuation ring. Let A → B be a local homomorphism which is essentially of finite type. Let M be a finite B-module. • If B is flat over A, then B is essentially of finite presentation over A. • If M is flat as an A-module, then M is finitely presented as a B-module.

nodes.title: Blowing up and flatness · Definition 053H
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal and a ∈ I. Let R[fracIa] be the affine blowup algebra, see Algebra, Definition [Tag 052Q]. Let M be an R-module. The strict transform of M along R → R[fracIa] is the R[fracIa]-module M' = (M ⊗_R R[textstylefracIa])/a-power torsion

nodes.title: Blowing up and flatness · Lemma 053I
nodes.summary: Let (R, m) be a local domain with fraction field K. Let S be a finite type R-algebra. Let M be a finite S-module. For every valuation ring A ⊂ K dominating R there exists an ideal I ⊂ m and a nonzero element a ∈ I such that • I is finitely generated, • A has center on R[fracIa], • the fibre ring of R → R[fracIa] at m is not zero, and • the strict transform S_I, a of S along R → R[fracIa] is flat and of finite presentation over R, and the strict transform M_I, a of M along…

nodes.title: Blowing up and flatness · Lemma 0CZM
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be a finite R-module. Let k ≥ 0 and I = Fit_k(M). For every a ∈ I with R' = R[fracIa] the strict transform M' = (M ⊗_R R')/a-power torsion has Fit_k(M') = R'.

nodes.title: Blowing up and flatness · Lemma 0CZN
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be a finite R-module. Let k ≥ 0 and I = Fit_k(M). Assume that M_ p is free of rank k for every p not ∈ V(I). Then for every a ∈ I with R' = R[fracIa] the strict transform M' = (M ⊗_R R')/a-power torsion is locally free of rank k.

nodes.title: Blowing up and flatness · Lemma 0BBJ
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be a finite R-module. Let f ∈ R be an element such that M_f is finite locally free of rank r. Then there exists a finitely generated ideal I ⊂ R with V(f) = V(I) such that for all a ∈ I with R' = R[fracIa] the strict transform M' = (M ⊗_R R')/a-power torsion is locally free of rank r.

nodes.title: Completion and flatness · Lemma 05BC
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let A be a set. Assume R is Noetherian and complete with respect to I. There is a canonical map (bigoplus_α ∈ A R)^wedge → ∏_α ∈ A R from the I-adic completion of the direct sum into the product which is universally injective.

nodes.title: Completion and flatness · Lemma 06LE
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let A be a set. Assume R is Noetherian. The completion (bigoplus_α ∈ A R)^wedge is a flat R-module.

nodes.title: Completion and flatness · Lemma 0911
nodes.summary: This is [quillenhomology]; note that the author forgot the word "strict" in the statement although it was clearly intended. Let A be a Noetherian ring. Let I be an ideal of A. Let M be a finite A-module. For every p > 0 there exists a c > 0 such that Tor_p^A(M, A/I^n) → Tor_p^A(M, A/I^n - c) is zero for all n ≥ c.

nodes.title: Completion and flatness · Lemma 0912
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian ring. Let I be an ideal of A. Let (M_n) be an inverse system of A-modules such that • M_n is a flat A/I^n-module, • M_n + 1 → M_n is surjective. Then M = lim M_n is a flat A-module and Q ⊗_A M = lim Q ⊗_A M_n for every finite A-module Q.

nodes.title: Completion and flatness · Lemma 0AGW
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let M be an R-module. Assume • I is finitely generated, • R/I is Noetherian, • M/IM is flat over R/I, • Tor_1^R(M, R/I) = 0. Then the I-adic completion R^wedge is a Noetherian ring and M^wedge is flat over R^wedge.

nodes.title: The Koszul complex · Definition 0622
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let φ : E → R be an R-module map. The Koszul complex K_bullet(φ) associated to φ is the commutative differential graded algebra defined as follows: • the underlying graded algebra is the exterior algebra K_bullet(φ) = wedge(E), • the differential d : K_bullet(φ) → K_bullet(φ) is the unique derivation such that d(e) = φ(e) for all e ∈ E = K_1(φ).

nodes.title: The Koszul complex · Definition 0623
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring and let f_1, …, f_r ∈ R. The Koszul complex on f_1, …, f_r is the Koszul complex associated to the map (f_1, …, f_r) : R^⊕ r → R. Notation K_bullet(f_bullet), K_bullet(f_1, …, f_r), K_bullet(R, f_1, …, f_r), or K_bullet(R, f_bullet).

nodes.title: The Koszul complex · Lemma 0624
nodes.summary: Let φ : E → R and φ' : E' → R be R-module maps. Let ψ : E → E' be an R-module map such that φ' ∘ ψ = φ. Then ψ induces a homomorphism of differential graded algebras K_bullet(φ) → K_bullet(φ').

nodes.title: The Koszul complex · Lemma 0625
nodes.summary: Let f_1, …, f_r ∈ R be a sequence. Let (x_ij) be an invertible r × r-matrix with coefficients in R. Then the complexes K_bullet(f_bullet) and K_bullet(∑ x_1jf_j, ∑ x_2jf_j, …, ∑ x_rjf_j) are isomorphic.

nodes.title: The Koszul complex · Lemma 0626
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let φ : E → R be an R-module map. Let e ∈ E with image f = φ(e) in R. Then f = de + ed as endomorphisms of K_bullet(φ).

nodes.title: The Koszul complex · Lemma 0663
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let f_1, …, f_r ∈ R be a sequence. Multiplication by f_i on K_bullet(f_bullet) is homotopic to zero, and in particular the cohomology modules H_i(K_bullet(f_bullet)) are annihilated by the ideal (f_1, …, f_r).

nodes.title: The Koszul complex · Lemma 0628
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let φ : E → R be an R-module map. Let f ∈ R. Set E' = E ⊕ R and define φ' : E' → R by φ on E and multiplication by f on R. The complex K_bullet(φ') is isomorphic to the cone of the map of complexes f : K_bullet(φ) → K_bullet(φ).

nodes.title: The Koszul complex · Lemma 0629
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let f_1, …, f_r be a sequence of elements of R. The complex K_bullet(f_1, …, f_r) is isomorphic to the cone of the map of complexes f_r : K_bullet(f_1, …, f_r - 1) → K_bullet(f_1, …, f_r - 1).

nodes.title: The Koszul complex · Lemma 062A
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let A_bullet be a complex of R-modules. Let f, g ∈ R. Let C(f)_bullet be the cone of f : A_bullet → A_bullet. Define similarly C(g)_bullet and C(fg)_bullet. Then C(fg)_bullet is homotopy equivalent to the cone of a map C(f)_bullet[1] → C(g)_bullet

nodes.title: The Koszul complex · Lemma 062B
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let φ : E → R be an R-module map. Let f, g ∈ R. Set E' = E ⊕ R and define φ'_f, φ'_g, φ'_fg : E' → R by φ on E and multiplication by f, g, fg on R. The complex K_bullet(φ'_fg) is homotopy equivalent to the cone of a map of complexes K_bullet(φ'_f)[1] → K_bullet(φ'_g).

nodes.title: The Koszul complex · Lemma 062C
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let f_1, …, f_r - 1 be a sequence of elements of R. Let f, g ∈ R. The complex K_bullet(f_1, …, f_r - 1, fg) is homotopy equivalent to the cone of a map of complexes K_bullet(f_1, …, f_r - 1, f)[1] → K_bullet(f_1, …, f_r - 1, g)

nodes.title: The Koszul complex · Lemma 0664
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let f_1, …, f_r, g_1, …, g_s be elements of R. Then there is an isomorphism of Koszul complexes K_bullet(R, f_1, …, f_r, g_1, …, g_s) = Tot(K_bullet(R, f_1, …, f_r) ⊗_R K_bullet(R, g_1, …, g_s)).

nodes.title: The extended alternating v Cech complex · Lemma 0G6G
nodes.summary: The extended alternating v Cech complexes defined above are complexes of R-modules.
nodes.section: The extended alternating v Cech complex

nodes.title: The extended alternating v Cech complex · Lemma 0G6H
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let f_1, …, f_r ∈ R. Let M be an R-module. The extended alternating v Cech complex of M is the tensor product over R of M with the extended alternating v Cech complex of R.
nodes.section: The extended alternating v Cech complex

nodes.title: The extended alternating v Cech complex · Lemma 0G6I
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let f_1, …, f_r ∈ R. Let M be an R-module. Let R → S be a ring map, denote g_1, …, g_r ∈ S the images of f_1, …, f_r, and set N = M ⊗_R S. The extended alternating v Cech complex constructed using S, g_1, …, g_r, and N is the tensor product of the extended alternating v Cech complex of M with S over R.
nodes.section: The extended alternating v Cech complex

nodes.title: The extended alternating v Cech complex · Lemma 0G6J
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let f_1, …, f_r ∈ R. Let M be an R-module. If there exists an i ∈ (1, …, r) such that f_i is a unit, then the extended alternating v Cech complex of M is homotopy equivalent to 0.
nodes.section: The extended alternating v Cech complex

nodes.title: The extended alternating v Cech complex · Lemma 0G6K
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let f_1, …, f_r ∈ R. Let M be an R-module. Let H^q be the qth cohomology module of the extended alternation v Cech complex of M. Then • H^q = 0 if q not ∈ [0, r], • for x ∈ H^i there exists an n ≥ 1 such that f_i^n x = 0 for i = 1, …, r, • the support of H^q is contained in V(f_1, …, f_r), • if there is an f ∈ (f_1, …, f_r) which acts invertibly on M, then H^q = 0.
nodes.section: The extended alternating v Cech complex

nodes.title: The extended alternating v Cech complex · Lemma 0913
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let f_1, …, f_r ∈ R. The extended alternating v Cech complex R → bigoplus_i_0 R_f_i_0 → bigoplus_i_0 < i_1 R_f_i_0f_i_1 → … → R_f_1… f_r is a colimit of the Koszul complexes K(R, f_1^n, …, f_r^n); see proof for a precise statement.
nodes.section: The extended alternating v Cech complex

nodes.title: Koszul regular sequences · Definition 062E
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let r ≥ 0 and let f_1, …, f_r ∈ R be a sequence of elements. Let M be an R-module. The sequence f_1, …, f_r is called • M-Koszul-regular if H_i(K_bullet(f_1, …, f_r) ⊗_R M) = 0 for all i not = 0, • M-H_1-regular if H_1(K_bullet(f_1, …, f_r) ⊗_R M) = 0, • Koszul-regular if H_i(K_bullet(f_1, …, f_r)) = 0 for all i not = 0, and • H_1-regular if H_1(K_bullet(f_1, …, f_r)) = 0.

nodes.title: Koszul regular sequences · Lemma 062F
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring, M an R-module, and f_1, …, f_r ∈ R such that for i = 1, …, r multiplication by f_i is injective on M/(f_1, …, f_i - 1)M. Then f_1, …, f_r is M-Koszul regular. In particular, an M-regular sequence is M-Koszul-regular and any regular sequence is Koszul-regular.

nodes.title: Koszul regular sequences · Lemma 0CEM
nodes.summary: A M-Koszul-regular sequence is M-H_1-regular. A Koszul-regular sequence is H_1-regular.

nodes.title: Koszul regular sequences · Lemma 062G
nodes.summary: Let f_1, …, f_r - 1 ∈ R be a sequence and f, g ∈ R. Let M be an R-module. • If f_1, …, f_r - 1, f and f_1, …, f_r - 1, g are M-H_1-regular then f_1, …, f_r - 1, fg is M-H_1-regular too. • If f_1, …, f_r - 1, f and f_1, …, f_r - 1, g are M-Koszul-regular then f_1, …, f_r - 1, fg is M-Koszul-regular too.

nodes.title: Koszul regular sequences · Lemma 062H
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a flat ring map. Let f_1, …, f_r ∈ R. Let M be an R-module and set N = M ⊗_R S. • If f_1, …, f_r in R is an M-H_1-regular sequence, then φ(f_1), …, φ(f_r) is an N-H_1-regular sequence in S. • If f_1, …, f_r is an M-Koszul-regular sequence in R, then φ(f_1), …, φ(f_r) is an N-Koszul-regular sequence in S.

nodes.title: Koszul regular sequences · Lemma 062I
nodes.summary: An M-H_1-regular sequence is M-quasi-regular.

nodes.title: Koszul regular sequences · Lemma 09CC
nodes.summary: Let (R, m) be a Noetherian local ring. Let M be a nonzero finite R-module. Let f_1, …, f_r ∈ m. The following are equivalent • f_1, …, f_r is an M-regular sequence, • f_1, …, f_r is a M-Koszul-regular sequence, • f_1, …, f_r is an M-H_1-regular sequence, • f_1, …, f_r is an M-quasi-regular sequence. In particular the sequence f_1, …, f_r is a regular sequence in R if and only if it is a Koszul regular sequence, if and only if it is a H_1-regular sequence, if and only if…

nodes.title: Koszul regular sequences · Lemma 0665
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let I ⊂ A be an ideal. Let g_1, …, g_m be a sequence in A whose image in A/I is H_1-regular. Then I ∩ (g_1, …, g_m) = I(g_1, …, g_m).

nodes.title: Koszul regular sequences · Lemma 0666
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let I ⊂ J ⊂ A be ideals. Assume that J/I ⊂ A/I is generated by an H_1-regular sequence. Then I ∩ J^2 = IJ.

nodes.title: Koszul regular sequences · Lemma 0667
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let I be an ideal generated by a quasi-regular sequence f_1, …, f_n in A. Let g_1, …, g_m ∈ A be elements whose images overlineg_1, …, overlineg_m form an H_1-regular sequence in A/I. Then f_1, …, f_n, g_1, …, g_m is a quasi-regular sequence in A.

nodes.title: Koszul regular sequences · Lemma 0668
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let I be an ideal generated by an H_1-regular sequence f_1, …, f_n in A. Let g_1, …, g_m ∈ A be elements whose images overlineg_1, …, overlineg_m form an H_1-regular sequence in A/I. Then f_1, …, f_n, g_1, …, g_m is an H_1-regular sequence in A.

nodes.title: Koszul regular sequences · Lemma 068L
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let f_1, …, f_n, g_1, …, g_m ∈ A be an H_1-regular sequence. Then the images overlineg_1, …, overlineg_m in A/(f_1, …, f_n) form an H_1-regular sequence.

nodes.title: Koszul regular sequences · Lemma 0669
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let I be an ideal generated by a Koszul-regular sequence f_1, …, f_n in A. Let g_1, …, g_m ∈ A be elements whose images overlineg_1, …, overlineg_m form a Koszul-regular sequence in A/I. Then f_1, …, f_n, g_1, …, g_m is a Koszul-regular sequence in A.

nodes.title: Koszul regular sequences · Lemma 068M
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let f_1, …, f_n, g_1, …, g_m ∈ A. If both f_1, …, f_n and f_1, …, f_n, g_1, …, g_m are Koszul-regular sequences in A, then overlineg_1, …, overlineg_m in A/(f_1, …, f_n) form a Koszul-regular sequence.

nodes.title: Koszul regular sequences · Lemma 066A
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I be an ideal generated by f_1, …, f_r ∈ R. • If I can be generated by a quasi-regular sequence of length r, then f_1, …, f_r is a quasi-regular sequence. • If I can be generated by an H_1-regular sequence of length r, then f_1, …, f_r is an H_1-regular sequence. • If I can be generated by a Koszul-regular sequence of length r, then f_1, …, f_r is a Koszul-regular sequence.

nodes.title: Koszul regular sequences · Lemma 068P
nodes.summary: This is a particular case of [McCoy] Let R be a ring. Let a_1, …, a_n ∈ R be elements such that R → R^⊕ n, x ↦ (xa_1, …, xa_n) is injective. Then the element ∑ a_i t_i of the polynomial ring R[t_1, …, t_n] is a nonzerodivisor.

nodes.title: Koszul regular sequences · Lemma 068Q
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let f_1, …, f_n be a Koszul-regular sequence in R such that (f_1, …, f_n) not = R. Consider the faithfully flat, smooth ring map R → S = R[(t_ij)_i ≤ j, t_11^-1, t_22^-1, …, t_nn^-1] For 1 ≤ i ≤ n set g_i = ∑_i ≤ j t_ij f_j ∈ S. Then g_1, …, g_n is a regular sequence in S and (f_1, …, f_n)S = (g_1, …, g_n).

nodes.title: More on Koszul regular sequences · Lemma 0G6L
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let f_1, …, f_r ∈ R be an Koszul-regular sequence. Then the extended alternating v Cech complex R → bigoplus_i_0 R_f_i_0 → bigoplus_i_0 < i_1 R_f_i_0f_i_1 → … → R_f_1… f_r from Section [Tag 0G6F] only has cohomology in degree r.

nodes.title: More on Koszul regular sequences · Lemma 0BIQ
nodes.summary: Let a, a_2, …, a_r be an H_1-regular sequence in a ring R (for example a Koszul regular sequence or a regular sequence, see Lemmas [Tag 062F] and [Tag 0CEM]). With I = (a, a_2, …, a_r) the blowup algebra R' = R[fracIa] is isomorphic to R" = R[y_2, …, y_r]/(a y_i - a_i).

nodes.title: More on Koszul regular sequences · Lemma 063Q
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Let f_1, …, f_r be a sequence in B such that B/(f_1, …, f_r) is A-flat. Let A → A' be a ring map. Then the canonical map H_1(K_bullet(B, f_1, …, f_r)) ⊗_A A' → H_1(K_bullet(B', f'_1, …, f'_r)) is surjective. Here B' = B ⊗_A A' and f_i' ∈ B' is the image of f_i.

nodes.title: More on Koszul regular sequences · Lemma 0CEP
nodes.summary: Let A → B and A → A' be ring maps. Set B' = B ⊗_A A'. Let f_1, …, f_r ∈ B. Assume B/(f_1, …, f_r)B is flat over A • If f_1, …, f_r is a quasi-regular sequence, then the image in B' is a quasi-regular sequence. • If f_1, …, f_r is a H_1-regular sequence, then the image in B' is a H_1-regular sequence.

nodes.title: More on Koszul regular sequences · Lemma 0CEQ
nodes.summary: Let A' → B' be a ring map. Let I ⊂ A' be an ideal. Set A = A'/I and B = B'/IB'. Let f'_1, …, f'_r ∈ B'. Assume • A' → B' is flat and of finite presentation, • I is locally nilpotent, • the images f_1, …, f_r ∈ B form a quasi-regular sequence, • B/(f_1, …, f_r) is flat over A. Then B'/(f'_1, …, f'_r) is flat over A'.

nodes.title: More on Koszul regular sequences · Lemma 0CER
nodes.summary: Let A' → B' be a ring map. Let I ⊂ A' be an ideal. Set A = A'/I and B = B'/IB'. Let f'_1, …, f'_r ∈ B'. Assume • A' → B' is flat and of finite presentation (for example smooth), • I is locally nilpotent, • the images f_1, …, f_r ∈ B form a quasi-regular sequence, • B/(f_1, …, f_r) is smooth over A. Then B'/(f'_1, …, f'_r) is smooth over A'.

nodes.title: Regular ideals · Definition 07CV
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring and let I ⊂ R be an ideal. • We say I is a regular ideal if for every p ∈ V(I) there exists a g ∈ R, g not ∈ p and a regular sequence f_1, …, f_r ∈ R_g such that I_g is generated by f_1, …, f_r. • We say I is a Koszul-regular ideal if for every p ∈ V(I) there exists a g ∈ R, g not ∈ p and a Koszul-regular sequence f_1, …, f_r ∈ R_g such that I_g is generated by f_1, …, f_r. • We say I is a H_1-regular ideal if for every p ∈ V(I) there exists a g ∈ R, g not…

nodes.title: Regular ideals · Lemma 07CW
nodes.summary: A quasi-regular ideal is finitely generated.

nodes.title: Regular ideals · Lemma 08RK
nodes.summary: Let I ⊂ R be a quasi-regular ideal of a ring. Then I/I^2 is a finite projective R/I-module.

nodes.title: Regular ideals · Lemma 068N
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a faithfully flat ring map. Let I ⊂ A be an ideal. If IB is a Koszul-regular (resp. H_1-regular, resp. quasi-regular) ideal in B, then I is a Koszul-regular (resp. H_1-regular, resp. quasi-regular) ideal in A.

nodes.title: Regular ideals · Lemma 07CX
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let I ⊂ J ⊂ A be ideals. Assume that J/I ⊂ A/I is a H_1-regular ideal. Then I ∩ J^2 = IJ.

nodes.title: Local complete intersection maps · Lemma 07CZ
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a finite type ring map. If for some presentation α : A[x_1, …, x_n] → B the kernel I is a Koszul-regular ideal then for any presentation β : A[y_1, …, y_m] → B the kernel J is a Koszul-regular ideal.

nodes.title: Local complete intersection maps · Definition 07D0
nodes.summary: A ring map A → B is called a local complete intersection if it is of finite type and for some (equivalently any) presentation B = A[x_1, …, x_n]/I the ideal I is Koszul-regular.

nodes.title: Local complete intersection maps · Lemma 07D1
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let g_1, …, g_m ∈ S generate the unit ideal. If each R → S_g_j is a local complete intersection so is R → S.

nodes.title: Local complete intersection maps · Lemma 07D2
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. If R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c) is a relative global complete intersection, then f_1, …, f_c is a Koszul regular sequence.

nodes.title: Local complete intersection maps · Lemma 07D3
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. The following are equivalent • R → S is syntomic (Algebra, Definition [Tag 00SL]), and • R → S is flat and a local complete intersection.

nodes.title: Local complete intersection maps · Lemma 07D4
nodes.summary: Let A → B → C be ring maps. Assume B → C is a local complete intersection homomorphism. Choose a presentation α : A[x_s, s ∈ S] → B with kernel I. Choose a presentation β : B[y_1, …, y_m] → C with kernel J. Let γ : A[x_s, y_t] → C be the induced presentation of C with kernel K. Then we get a canonical commutative diagram xymatrix 0 ar[r] & Ω_A[x_s]/A ⊗ C ar[r] & Ω_A[x_s, y_t]/A ⊗ C ar[r] & Ω_B[y_t]/B ⊗ C ar[r] & 0 0 ar[r] & I/I^2 ⊗ C ar[r] ar[u] & K/K^2 ar[r] ar[u] &…

nodes.title: Local complete intersection maps · Lemma 07D5
nodes.summary: Let A → B → C be ring maps. If B → C is a filtered colimit of local complete intersection homomorphisms then the conclusion of Lemma [Tag 07D4] remains valid.

nodes.title: Local complete intersection maps · Lemma 0D08
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a local homomorphism of local rings. Let A^h → B^h, resp. A^sh → B^sh be the induced map on henselizations, resp. strict henselizations (Algebra, Lemma [Tag 04GS], resp. Lemma [Tag 04GU]). Then NL_B/A ⊗_B B^h → NL_B^h/A^h and NL_B/A ⊗_B B^sh → NL_B^sh/A^sh induce isomorphisms on cohomology groups.

nodes.title: Cartier equality · Lemma 07E1
nodes.summary: Let K/k be a finitely generated field extension. Then Ω_K/k and H_1(L_K/k) are finite dimensional and trdeg_k(K) = dim_K Ω_K/k - dim_K H_1(L_K/k).

nodes.title: Cartier's equality and geometric regularity · Lemma 07E2
nodes.summary: Let M/L/K be field extensions. Then the Jacobi-Zariski sequence 0 → H_1(L_L/K) ⊗_L M → H_1(L_M/K) → H_1(L_M/L) → Ω_L/K ⊗_L M → Ω_M/K → Ω_M/L → 0 is exact.

nodes.title: Cartier's equality and geometric regularity · Lemma 07E3
nodes.summary: Given a commutative diagram of fields xymatrix K ar[r] & K' k ar[u] ar[r] & k' ar[u] with k'/k and K'/K finitely generated field extensions the kernel and cokernel of the maps α : Ω_K/k ⊗_K K' → Ω_K'/k' and β : H_1(L_K/k) ⊗_K K' → H_1(L_K'/k') are finite dimensional and dim Ker(α) - dim Coker(α) -dim Ker(β) + dim Coker(β) = trdeg_k(k') - trdeg_K(K')

nodes.title: Geometric regularity · Proposition 07E5
nodes.summary: Let k be a field of characteristic p > 0. Let (A, m, K) be a Noetherian local k-algebra. The following are equivalent • A is geometrically regular over k, • for all k ⊂ k' ⊂ k^1/p finite over k the ring A ⊗_k k' is regular, • A is regular and the canonical map H_1(L_K/k) → m/ m^2 is injective, and • A is regular and the map Ω_k/F_p ⊗_k K → Ω_A/F_p ⊗_A K is injective.

nodes.title: Geometric regularity · Lemma 07E6
nodes.summary: Let k be a field of characteristic p > 0. Let (A, m, K) be a Noetherian local k-algebra. Assume A is geometrically regular over k. Let K/F/k be a finitely generated subextension. Let φ : k[y_1, …, y_m] → A be a k-algebra map such that y_i maps to an element of F in K and such that dy_1, …, dy_m map to a basis of Ω_F/k. Set p = φ^-1( m). Then k[y_1, …, y_m]_ p → A is flat and A/ pA is regular.

nodes.title: Topological rings · Definition 07E8
nodes.summary: [EGA1] Let R be a ring and let M be an R-module. • We say R is a topological ring if R is endowed with a topology such that both addition and multiplication are continuous as maps R × R → R where R × R has the product topology. In this case we say M is a topological module if M is endowed with a topology such that addition M × M → M and scalar multiplication R × M → M are continuous. • A homomorphism of topological modules is just a continuous R-module map. A homomorphism…

nodes.title: Topological rings and modules · Lemma 07E9
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Let I ⊂ R and J ⊂ S be ideals and endow R with the I-adic topology and S with the J-adic topology. Then φ is a homomorphism of topological rings if and only if φ(I^n) ⊂ J for some n ≥ 1.

nodes.title: Baire category theorem · Lemma 0CQU
nodes.summary: Let M be a topological abelian group. Assume M is linearly topologized, complete, and has a countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods of 0. If U_n ⊂ M, n ≥ 1 are open dense subsets, then ⋂_n ≥ 1 U_n is dense.

nodes.title: Topological rings and modules · Lemma 0CQV
nodes.summary: With same assumptions as Lemma [Tag 0CQU] if M = ⋃_n ≥ 1 N_n for some closed subgroups N_n, then N_n is open for some n.

nodes.title: Open mapping lemma · Lemma 0CQW
nodes.summary: Let u : N → M be a continuous map of topologized abelian groups. Assume that M separated and that N is complete, linearly topologized, and has a countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods of 0. Then exactly one of the following holds • u is open, or • for some open subgroup N' ⊂ N the image u(N') is nowhere dense in M.

nodes.title: Formally smooth maps of topological rings · Definition 07EB
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a homomorphism of topological rings with R and S linearly topologized. We say S is formally smooth over R if for every commutative solid diagram xymatrix S ar[r] ar@-->[rd] & A/J R ar[r] ar[u] & A ar[u] of homomorphisms of topological rings where A is a discrete ring and J ⊂ A is an ideal of square zero, a dotted arrow exists which makes the diagram commute.

Then the following are equivalent • φ is formally smooth for the m-adic topology on R and the n-adic topology on S, and • φ is…

nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let n ⊂ S be an ideal. If the equivalent conditions (2)(a) and (2)(b) of Lemma [Tag 07EC] hold, then we say R → S is formally smooth for the n-adic topology.

nodes.title: Formally smooth maps of topological rings · Lemma 07ED
nodes.summary: Let (R, m) and (S, n) be rings endowed with finitely generated ideals. Endow R and S with the m-adic and n-adic topologies. Let R → S be a homomorphism of topological rings. The following are equivalent • R → S is formally smooth for the n-adic topology, • R → S^wedge is formally smooth for the n^wedge-adic topology, • R^wedge → S^wedge is formally smooth for the n^wedge-adic topology. Here R^wedge and S^wedge are the m-adic and n-adic completions of R and S.

Then there exists a dotted arrow in the category of topological…

nodes.title: Formally smooth maps of topological rings · Lemma 07EE
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Let n ⊂ n' ⊂ S be ideals. If R → S is formally smooth for the n-adic topology, then R → S is formally smooth for the n'-adic topology.
nodes.section: Formally smooth maps of topological rings

nodes.title: Formally smooth maps of topological rings · Lemma 07EF
nodes.summary: A composition of formally smooth continuous homomorphisms of linearly topologized rings is formally smooth.
nodes.section: Formally smooth maps of topological rings

nodes.title: Formally smooth maps of topological rings · Lemma 07EG
nodes.summary: Let R, S be rings. Let n ⊂ S be an ideal. Let R → S be formally smooth for the n-adic topology. Let R → R' be any ring map. Then R' → S' = S ⊗_R R' is formally smooth in the n' = nS'-adic topology.

nodes.title: Formally smooth maps of topological rings · Lemma 07EH
nodes.summary: Let R, S be rings. Let n ⊂ S be an ideal. Let R → R' be a ring map. Set S' = S ⊗_R R' and n' = nS. If • the map R → R' embeds R as a direct summand of R' as an R-module, and • R' → S' is formally smooth for the n'-adic topology, then R → S is formally smooth in the n-adic topology.

nodes.summary: Let (R, m) → (S, n) be a local homomorphism of local rings. The following are equivalent • R → S is formally smooth in the n-adic topology, • for every solid commutative diagram xymatrix S ar[r] ar@-->[rd] & A/J R ar[r] ar[u] & A ar[u] of local homomorphisms of local rings where J ⊂ A is an ideal of square zero, m_A^n = 0 for some n > 0, and S → A/J induces an isomorphism on residue fields, a dotted arrow exists which makes the diagram commute. If S is Noetherian these…
nodes.section: Formally smooth maps of local rings

nodes.title: Formally smooth maps of local rings · Lemma 07EI
nodes.summary: Let k be a field and let (A, m, K) be a Noetherian local k-algebra. If k → A is formally smooth for the m-adic topology, then A is a regular local ring.
nodes.section: Formally smooth maps of local rings

nodes.title: Formally smooth maps of local rings · Lemma 0C34
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let (A, m, kappa) be a complete local k-algebra. If kappa/k is separable, then there exists a k-algebra map kappa → A such that kappa → A → kappa is id_kappa.

nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let (A, m, kappa) be a complete local k-algebra. If kappa/k is separable and A regular, then there exists an isomorphism of A ≅ kappa[[t_1, …, t_d]] as k-algebras.
nodes.section: Formally smooth maps of local rings

nodes.title: Formally smooth maps of local rings · Lemma 07EJ
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let (A, m, K) be a regular local k-algebra such that K/k is separable. Then k → A is formally smooth in the m-adic topology.

nodes.title: Formally smooth maps of local rings · Lemma 07VH
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a finite type ring map with A Noetherian. Let q ⊂ B be a prime ideal lying over p ⊂ A. The following are equivalent • A → B is smooth at q, and • A_ p → B_ q is formally smooth in the q-adic topology.

nodes.title: Some results on power series rings · Lemma 07NL
nodes.summary: Let K be a field of characteristic 0 and A = K[[x_1, …, x_n]]. Let L be a field of characteristic p > 0 and B = L[[x_1, …, x_n]]. Let Lambda be a Cohen ring. Let C = Lambda[[x_1, …, x_n]]. • Q → A is formally smooth in the m_A-adic topology. • F_p → B is formally smooth in the m_B-adic topology. • Z → C is formally smooth in the m_C-adic topology.

nodes.title: Some results on power series rings · Lemma 07NM
nodes.summary: Let K be a field and A = K[[x_1, …, x_n]]. Let Lambda be a Cohen ring and let B = Lambda[[x_1, …, x_n]]. • If y_1, …, y_n ∈ A is a regular system of parameters then K[[y_1, …, y_n]] → A is an isomorphism. • If z_1, …, z_r ∈ A form part of a regular system of parameters for A, then r ≤ n and A/(z_1, …, z_r) ≅ K[[y_1, …, y_n - r]]. • If p, y_1, …, y_n ∈ B is a regular system of parameters then Lambda[[y_1, …, y_n]] → B is an isomorphism. • If p, z_1, …, z_r ∈ B form part of…

nodes.title: Some results on power series rings · Lemma 07NN
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a local homomorphism of Noetherian complete local rings. Then there exists a commutative diagram xymatrix S ar[r] & B R ar[u] ar[r] & A ar[u] with the following properties: • the horizontal arrows are surjective, • if the characteristic of A/ m_A is zero, then S and R are power series rings over fields, • if the characteristic of A/ m_A is p > 0, then S and R are power series rings over Cohen rings, and • R → S maps a regular system of parameters of R to part…

nodes.title: Some results on power series rings · Lemma 09Q8
nodes.summary: Let S → R and S' → R be surjective maps of complete Noetherian local rings. Then S ×_R S' is a complete Noetherian local ring.

nodes.title: Geometric regularity and formal smoothness · Theorem 07EL
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let (A, m, K) be a Noetherian local k-algebra. If the characteristic of k is zero then the following are equivalent • A is a regular local ring, and • k → A is formally smooth in the m-adic topology. If the characteristic of k is p > 0 then the following are equivalent • A is geometrically regular over k, • k → A is formally smooth in the m-adic topology. • for all k ⊂ k' ⊂ k^1/p finite over k the ring A ⊗_k k' is regular, • A is regular and the…

nodes.title: Geometric regularity and formal smoothness · Lemma 07NP
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Assume A → B is formally smooth in the m_B-adic topology. Then A → B is flat.

nodes.title: Geometric regularity and formal smoothness · Lemma 0DYH
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Assume A → B is formally smooth in the m_B-adic topology. Let K be the residue field of B. Then the Jacobi-Zariski sequence for A → B → K gives an exact sequence 0 → H_1(NL_K/A) → m_B/ m_B^2 → Ω_B/A ⊗_B K → Ω_K/A → 0

nodes.title: Geometric regularity and formal smoothness · Proposition 07NQ
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Let k be the residue field of A and overlineB = B ⊗_A k the special fibre. The following are equivalent • A → B is flat and overlineB is geometrically regular over k, • A → B is flat and k → overlineB is formally smooth in the m_overlineB-adic topology, and • A → B is formally smooth in the m_B-adic topology.

nodes.title: Geometric regularity and formal smoothness · Lemma 07NR
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian complete local ring with residue field k. Let B be a Noetherian complete local k-algebra. Assume k → B is formally smooth in the m_B-adic topology. Then there exists a Noetherian complete local ring C and a local homomorphism A → C which is formally smooth in the m_C-adic topology such that C ⊗_A k ≅ B.

nodes.title: Regular ring maps · Definition 07BZ
nodes.summary: A ring map R → Lambda is regular if it is flat and for every prime p ⊂ R the fibre ring Lambda ⊗_R kappa( p) = Lambda_ p/ pLambda_ p is Noetherian and geometrically regular over kappa( p).

nodes.title: Regular is a local property · Lemma 07C0
nodes.summary: Let R → Lambda be a ring map with Lambda Noetherian. The following are equivalent • R → Lambda is regular, • R_ p → Lambda_ q is regular for all q ⊂ Lambda lying over p ⊂ R, and • R_ m → Lambda_ m' is regular for all maximal ideals m' ⊂ Lambda lying over m in R.

nodes.title: Regular maps and base change · Lemma 07C1
nodes.summary: Let R → Lambda be a regular ring map. For any finite type ring map R → R' the base change R' → Lambda ⊗_R R' is regular too.

nodes.title: Composition of regular maps · Lemma 07QI
nodes.summary: Let A → B and B → C be regular ring maps. If the fibre rings of A → C are Noetherian, then A → C is regular.

nodes.title: Regular ring maps · Lemma 07EP
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let (A_i, φ_ii') be a directed system of smooth R-algebras. Set Lambda = colim A_i. If the fibre rings Lambda ⊗_R kappa( p) are Noetherian for all p ⊂ R, then R → Lambda is regular.

nodes.title: Regular ring maps · Lemma 07EQ
nodes.summary: Let K/k be a field extension. Then k → K is a regular ring map if and only if K is a separable field extension of k.

nodes.title: Regular ring maps · Lemma 07NT
nodes.summary: Let A → B → C be ring maps. If A → C is regular and B → C is flat and surjective on spectra, then A → B is regular.

nodes.title: Ascending properties along regular ring maps · Lemma 07QK
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Assume • φ is regular, • S is Noetherian, and • R is Noetherian and reduced. Then S is reduced.
nodes.section: Ascending properties along regular ring maps

nodes.title: Ascending properties along regular ring maps · Lemma 0BFK
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Assume • φ is regular, • S is Noetherian, and • R is Noetherian and normal. Then S is normal.
nodes.section: Ascending properties along regular ring maps

nodes.title: Ascending properties along regular ring maps · Lemma 0H7S
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Assume • φ is regular, • S is Noetherian, and • R is Noetherian and regular. Then S is regular.
nodes.section: Ascending properties along regular ring maps

nodes.title: Ascending properties along regular ring maps · Lemma 0H7T
nodes.summary: Let φ : R → S be a ring map. Assume • φ is regular, • S is Noetherian, and • R is Noetherian and Cohen-Macaulay. Then S is Cohen-Macaulay.
nodes.section: Ascending properties along regular ring maps

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under completion · Lemma 07NV
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian local ring. Then dim(A) = dim(A^wedge).

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under completion · Lemma 07NW
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian local ring. Then depth(A) = depth(A^wedge).
