nodes.title: Permanence of properties under completion · Lemma 07NX
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian local ring. Then A is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if A^wedge is so.

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under completion · Lemma 07NY
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian local ring. Then A is regular if and only if A^wedge is so.

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under completion · Lemma 0AP1
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian local ring. Then A is a discrete valuation ring if and only if A^wedge is so.

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under completion · Lemma 07NZ
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian local ring. • If A^wedge is reduced, then so is A. • In general A reduced does not imply A^wedge is reduced. • If A is Nagata, then A is reduced if and only if A^wedge is reduced.

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under completion · Lemma 0FIZ
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian local ring. If A^wedge is normal, then so is A.

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under completion · Lemma 0C4G
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Then the induced map of completions A^wedge → B^wedge is flat if and only if A → B is flat.

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under completion · Lemma 0AGX
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings such that m_A B = m_B and kappa( m_A) = kappa( m_B). Then A → B induces an isomorphism A^wedge → B^wedge of completions.

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under étale maps · Lemma 0AGZ
nodes.summary: If A → B is an étale ring map and q is a prime of B lying over p ⊂ A, then A_ p is Noetherian if and only if B_ q is Noetherian.
nodes.section: Permanence of properties under étale maps

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under étale maps · Lemma 07QP
nodes.summary: If A → B is an étale ring map and q is a prime of B lying over p ⊂ A, then dim(A_ p) = dim(B_ q).
nodes.section: Permanence of properties under étale maps

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under étale maps · Lemma 0AH0
nodes.summary: If A → B is an étale ring map and q is a prime of B lying over p ⊂ A, then A_ p is regular if and only if B_ q is regular.
nodes.section: Permanence of properties under étale maps

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under étale maps · Lemma 0AP2
nodes.summary: If A → B is an étale ring map and A is a Dedekind domain, then B is a finite product of Dedekind domains. In particular, the localizations B_ q for q ⊂ B maximal are discrete valuation rings.
nodes.section: Permanence of properties under étale maps

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under henselization · Lemma 07QM
nodes.summary: Let (R, m, kappa) be a local ring. Then we have the following • R → R^h → R^sh are faithfully flat ring maps, • m R^h = m^h and m R^sh = m^h R^sh = m^sh, • R/ m^n = R^h/ m^nR^h for all n, • there exist elements x_i ∈ R^sh such that R^sh/ m^nR^sh is a free R/ m^n-module on x_i bmod m^nR^sh.

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under henselization · Lemma 07QN
nodes.summary: Let (R, m, kappa) be a local ring. Then • R → R^h, R^h → R^sh, and R → R^sh are formally étale, • R → R^h, R^h → R^sh, resp. R → R^sh are formally smooth in the m^h, m^sh, resp. m^sh-topology.

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under henselization · Lemma 06LJ
nodes.summary: [EGA] Let R be a local ring. The following are equivalent • R is Noetherian, • R^h is Noetherian, and • R^sh is Noetherian. In this case we have • [(a)] (R^h)^wedge and (R^sh)^wedge are Noetherian complete local rings, • [(b)] R^wedge → (R^h)^wedge is an isomorphism, • [(c)] R^h → (R^h)^wedge and R^sh → (R^sh)^wedge are flat, • [(d)] R^wedge → (R^sh)^wedge is formally smooth in the m_(R^sh)^wedge-adic topology, • [(e)] (R^wedge)^sh = R^wedge ⊗_R^h R^sh, and • [(f)]…

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under henselization · Lemma 06DH
nodes.summary: Reducedness passes to the (strict) henselization. Let R be a local ring. The following are equivalent: R is reduced, the henselization R^h of R is reduced, and the strict henselization R^sh of R is reduced.

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under henselization · Lemma 0ASE
nodes.summary: Let R be a local ring. Let nil(R) denote the ideal of nilpotent elements of R. Then nil(R)R^h = nil(R^h) and nil(R)R^sh = nil(R^sh).

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under henselization · Lemma 06DI
nodes.summary: Let R be a local ring. The following are equivalent: R is a normal domain, the henselization R^h of R is a normal domain, and the strict henselization R^sh of R is a normal domain.

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under henselization · Lemma 06LK
nodes.summary: Given any local ring R we have dim(R) = dim(R^h) = dim(R^sh).

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under henselization · Lemma 06LL
nodes.summary: Given a Noetherian local ring R we have depth(R) = depth(R^h) = depth(R^sh).

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under henselization · Lemma 06LM
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring. The following are equivalent: R is Cohen-Macaulay, the henselization R^h of R is Cohen-Macaulay, and the strict henselization R^sh of R is Cohen-Macaulay.

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under henselization · Lemma 06LN
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring. The following are equivalent: R is a regular local ring, the henselization R^h of R is a regular local ring, and the strict henselization R^sh of R is a regular local ring.

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under henselization · Lemma 0AP3
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring. Then R is a discrete valuation ring if and only if R^h is a discrete valuation ring if and only if R^sh is a discrete valuation ring.

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under henselization · Lemma 0AH1
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let B be a filtered colimit of étale A-algebras. Let p be a prime of A. If B is Noetherian, then there are finitely many primes q_1, …, q_r lying over p, we have B ⊗_A kappa( p) = ∏ kappa( q_i), and each of the field extensions kappa( q_i)/kappa( p) is separable algebraic.

nodes.title: Permanence of properties under henselization · Lemma 07QQ
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring. Let p ⊂ R be a prime. Then R^h ⊗_R kappa( p) = ∏_i = 1, …, t kappa( q_i) resp. R^sh ⊗_R kappa( p) = ∏_i = 1, …, s kappa( r_i) where q_1, …, q_t, resp. r_1, …, r_s are the prime of R^h, resp. R^sh lying over p. Moreover, the field extensions kappa( q_i)/kappa( p) resp. kappa( r_i)/kappa( p) are separable algebraic.

nodes.title: Field extensions, revisited · Definition 07P1
nodes.summary: Let p be a prime number. Let k → K be an extension of fields of characteristic p. Denote kK^p the compositum of k and K^p in K. • A subset (x_i) ⊂ K is called p-independent over k if the elements x^E = ∏ x_i^e_i where 0 ≤ e_i < p are linearly independent over kK^p. • A subset (x_i) of K is called a p-basis of K over k if the elements x^E form a basis of K over kK^p.

nodes.title: Field extensions, revisited · Lemma 07P2
nodes.summary: Let K/k be a field extension. Assume k has characteristic p > 0. Let (x_i) be a subset of K. The following are equivalent • the elements (x_i) are p-independent over k, and • the elements dx_i are K-linearly independent in Ω_K/k. Any p-independent collection can be extended to a p-basis of K over k. In particular, the field K has a p-basis over k. Moreover, the following are equivalent: • [(a)] (x_i) is a p-basis of K over k, and • [(b)] dx_i is a basis of the K-vector…

nodes.title: Field extensions, revisited · Lemma 07P3
nodes.summary: Let K/k be a field extension. Let (K_α)_α ∈ A be a collection of subfields of K with the following properties • k ⊂ K_α for all α ∈ A, • k = ⋂_α ∈ A K_α, • for α, α' ∈ A there exists an α" ∈ A such that K_α" ⊂ K_α ∩ K_α'. Then for n ≥ 1 and V ⊂ K^⊕ n a K-vector space we have V ∩ k^⊕ n not = 0 if and only if V ∩ K_α^⊕ n not = 0 for all α ∈ A.

nodes.title: Field extensions, revisited · Lemma 07P4
nodes.summary: Let K be a field of characteristic p. Let (K_α)_α ∈ A be a collection of subfields of K with the following properties • K^p ⊂ K_α for all α ∈ A, • K^p = ⋂_α ∈ A K_α, • for α, α' ∈ A there exists an α" ∈ A such that K_α" ⊂ K_α ∩ K_α'. Then • the intersection of the kernels of the maps Ω_K/F_p → Ω_K/K_α is zero, • for any finite extension L/K we have L^p = ⋂_α ∈ A L^pK_α.

nodes.title: Field extensions, revisited · Lemma 07P5
nodes.summary: Let k be a field of characteristic p > 0. Let (x_i)_i ∈ I be a p-basis for k. Let n, m ≥ 0. Let K be the fraction field of A = k[[x_1, …, x_n]][y_1, …, y_m]. Let J be a finite subset of I. Consider the subfield k/k_J/k^p generated by k^p and x_i with i ∈ I setminus J. The fraction fields K_J of A_J = k_J[[x_1^p, …, x_n^p]][y_1^p, …, y_m^p] form a family of subfields of K as in Lemma [Tag 07P4]. Moreover, each of the ring extensions A_J ⊂ A is finite.

nodes.title: The singular locus · Definition 07P7
nodes.summary: [MatCA] Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let X = Spec(R). • We say R is J-0 if Reg(X) contains a nonempty open. • We say R is J-1 if Reg(X) is open. • We say R is J-2 if any finite type R-algebra is J-1.

nodes.title: The singular locus · Lemma 07P8
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let X = Spec(R). The ring R is J-1 if and only if V( p) ∩ Reg(X) contains a nonempty open subset of V( p) for all p ∈ Reg(X).

nodes.title: The singular locus · Lemma 07P9
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let X = Spec(R). Assume that for all primes p ⊂ R the ring R/ p is J-0. Then R is J-1.

nodes.title: The singular locus · Lemma 07PA
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Assume that • R is a Noetherian domain, • R → S is injective and of finite type, and • S is a domain and J-0. Then R is J-0.

nodes.title: The singular locus · Lemma 07PB
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a ring map. Assume that • R is a Noetherian domain and J-0, • R → S is injective and of finite type, and • S is a domain, and • the induced extension of fraction fields is separable. Then S is J-0.

nodes.title: The singular locus · Lemma 07PC
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. The following are equivalent • R is J-2, • every finite type R-algebra which is a domain is J-0, • every finite R-algebra is J-1, • for every prime p and every finite purely inseparable extension L/kappa( p) there exists a finite R-algebra R' which is a domain, which is J-0, and whose field of fractions is L.

nodes.title: Regularity and derivations · Lemma 07PE
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let D : R → R be a derivation. • For any ideal I ⊂ R the derivation D extends canonically to a derivation D^wedge : R^wedge → R^wedge on the I-adic completion. • For any multiplicative subset S ⊂ R the derivation D extends uniquely to the localization S^-1R of R. If R ⊂ R' is a finite type extension of rings such that R_g ≅ R'_g for some g ∈ R which is a nonzerodivisor in R', then g^ND extends to R' for some N ≥ 0.

nodes.title: Regularity and derivations · Lemma 07PF
nodes.summary: The Jacobian criterion for hypersurfaces, done right. Let R be a regular ring. Let f ∈ R. Assume there exists a derivation D : R → R such that D(f) is a unit of R/(f). Then R/(f) is regular.

nodes.title: Regularity and derivations · Lemma 0GEE
nodes.summary: Let (R, m, kappa) be a regular local ring. Let m ≥ 1. Let f_1, …, f_m ∈ m. Assume there exist derivations D_1, …, D_m : R → R such that det_1 ≤ i, j ≤ m(D_i(f_j)) is a unit of R. Then R/(f_1, …, f_m) is regular and f_1, …, f_m is a regular sequence.

nodes.title: Regularity and derivations · Lemma 07PG
nodes.summary: Let R be a regular ring. Let f ∈ R. Assume there exists a derivation D : R → R such that D(f) is a unit of R. Then R[z]/(z^n - f) is regular for any integer n ≥ 1. More generally, R[z]/(p(z) - f) is regular for any p ∈ Z[z].

nodes.title: Regularity and derivations · Lemma 07PH
nodes.summary: Let p be a prime number. Let B be a domain with p = 0 in B. Let f ∈ B be an element which is not a pth power in the fraction field of B. If B is of finite type over a Noetherian complete local ring, then there exists a derivation D : B → B such that D(f) is not zero.

nodes.title: Regularity and derivations · Lemma 07PI
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian complete local domain. Then A is J-0.

nodes.title: Regularity and derivations · Proposition 07PJ
nodes.summary: The following types of rings are J-2: • fields, • Noetherian complete local rings, • Z, • Noetherian local rings of dimension 1, • Nagata rings of dimension 1, • Dedekind domains with fraction field of characteristic zero, • finite type ring extensions of any of the above.

nodes.title: Formal smoothness and regularity · Lemma 07PL
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Let D : A → A be a derivation. Assume that B is complete and A → B is formally smooth in the m_B-adic topology. Then there exists an extension D' : B → B of D.

nodes.title: Formal smoothness and regularity · Proposition 07PM
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a local homomorphism of Noetherian complete local rings. Let k be the residue field of A and overlineB = B ⊗_A k the special fibre. The following are equivalent • A → B is regular, • A → B is flat and overlineB is geometrically regular over k, • A → B is flat and k → overlineB is formally smooth in the m_overlineB-adic topology, and • A → B is formally smooth in the m_B-adic topology.

nodes.title: André · Theorem 0H7U
nodes.summary: The implication (4) ⇒ (1) is the main result of [Andre-smooth]. Let A → B be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Let k be the residue field of A and overlineB = B ⊗_A k the special fibre. Assume A → A^wedge is regular. The following are equivalent • A → B is regular, • A → B is flat and overlineB is geometrically regular over k, • A → B is flat and k → overlineB is formally smooth in the m_overlineB-adic topology, and • A → B is formally smooth in the m_B-adic…

nodes.title: G-rings · Definition 07GH
nodes.summary: A ring R is called a G-ring if R is Noetherian and for every prime p of R the ring map R_ p → (R_ p)^wedge is regular.

nodes.title: G-rings · Lemma 07PN
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Then R is a G-ring if and only if for every pair of primes q ⊂ p ⊂ R the algebra (R/ q)_ p^wedge ⊗_R/ q kappa( q) is geometrically regular over kappa( q).

nodes.title: G-rings · Lemma 07PP
nodes.summary: Let R → R' be a finite type map of Noetherian rings and let xymatrix q' ar[r] & p' ar[r] & R' q ar[r] ar@-[u] & p ar[r] ar@-[u] & R ar[u] be primes. Assume R → R' is quasi-finite at p'. • If the formal fibre R_ p^wedge ⊗_R kappa( q) is geometrically regular over kappa( q), then the formal fibre (R'_ p')^wedge ⊗_R' kappa( q') is geometrically regular over kappa( q'). • If the formal fibres of R_ p are geometrically regular, then the formal fibres of R'_ p' are…

nodes.title: G-rings · Lemma 07PQ
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Then R is a G-ring if and only if for every finite free ring map R → S the formal fibres of S are regular rings.

nodes.title: G-rings · Lemma 07PR
nodes.summary: Let k be a field of characteristic p. Let A = k[[x_1, …, x_n]][y_1, …, y_m] and denote K the fraction field of A. Let p ⊂ A be a prime. Then A_ p^wedge ⊗_A K is geometrically regular over K.

nodes.title: G-rings · Proposition 07PS
nodes.summary: A Noetherian complete local ring is a G-ring.

nodes.title: G-rings · Lemma 07PT
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Then R is a G-ring if and only if R_ m has geometrically regular formal fibres for every maximal ideal m of R.

nodes.title: G-rings · Lemma 07QR
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring which is a G-ring. Then the henselization R^h and the strict henselization R^sh are G-rings.

nodes.title: G-rings · Lemma 07PU
nodes.summary: Let p be a prime number. Let A be a Noetherian complete local domain with fraction field K of characteristic p. Let q ⊂ A[x] be a maximal ideal lying over the maximal ideal of A and let (0) not = r ⊂ q be a prime lying over (0) ⊂ A. Then A[x]_ q^wedge ⊗_A[x] kappa( r) is geometrically regular over kappa( r).

nodes.title: G-rings · Proposition 07PV
nodes.summary: Let R be a G-ring. If R → S is essentially of finite type then S is a G-ring.

nodes.title: G-rings · Proposition 07PX
nodes.summary: The following types of rings are G-rings: • fields, • Noetherian complete local rings, • Z, • Dedekind domains with fraction field of characteristic zero, • finite type ring extensions of any of the above.

nodes.title: G-rings · Lemma 0A41
nodes.summary: Let (A, m) be a henselian local ring. Then A is a filtered colimit of a system of henselian local G-rings with local transition maps.

nodes.title: G-rings · Lemma 0AH2
nodes.summary: [MatCA] Let A be a G-ring. Let I ⊂ A be an ideal and let A^wedge be the completion of A with respect to I. Then A → A^wedge is regular.

nodes.title: G-rings · Lemma 0AH3
nodes.summary: Being a G-ring is stable under Henselizations along ideals [Greco] Let A be a G-ring. Let I ⊂ A be an ideal. Let (A^h, I^h) be the henselization of the pair (A, I), see Lemma [Tag 0A02]. Then A^h is a G-ring.

nodes.title: Properties of formal fibres · Lemma 0BIS
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let P be a property as above. Then R is a P-ring if and only if for every pair of primes q ⊂ p ⊂ R the kappa( q)-algebra (R/ q)_ p^wedge ⊗_R/ q kappa( q) has property P.

nodes.title: Properties of formal fibres · Lemma 0BK8
nodes.summary: Let R → Lambda be a homomorphism of Noetherian rings. Assume P has property (B). The following are equivalent • the fibres of R → Lambda have P, • the fibres of R_ p → Lambda_ q have P for all q ⊂ Lambda lying over p ⊂ R, and • the fibres of R_ m → Lambda_ m' have P for all maximal ideals m' ⊂ Lambda lying over m in R.

nodes.title: Properties of formal fibres · Lemma 0BIT
nodes.summary: Let R → R' be a finite type map of Noetherian rings and let xymatrix q' ar[r] & p' ar[r] & R' q ar[r] ar@-[u] & p ar[r] ar@-[u] & R ar[u] be primes. Assume R → R' is quasi-finite at p'. Assume P satisfies (A) and (B). • If kappa( q) → R_ p^wedge ⊗_R kappa( q) has P, then kappa( q') → (R'_ p')^wedge ⊗_R' kappa( q') has P. • If the formal fibres of R_ p have P, then the formal fibres of R'_ p' have P. • If R → R' is quasi-finite and R is a P-ring, then R' is a P-ring.

nodes.title: Properties of formal fibres · Lemma 0BIU
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Assume P satisfies (C) and (D). Then R is a P-ring if and only if the formal fibres of R_ m have P for every maximal ideal m of R.

nodes.title: Properties of formal fibres · Proposition 0BIV
nodes.summary: Let R be a P-ring where P satisfies (A), (B), (C), and (D). If R → S is essentially of finite type then S is a P-ring.

nodes.title: Properties of formal fibres · Lemma 0BK9
nodes.summary: Let A be a P-ring where P satisfies (B) and (D). Let I ⊂ A be an ideal and let A^wedge be the completion of A with respect to I. Then the fibres of A → A^wedge have P.

nodes.title: Properties of formal fibres · Lemma 0BKA
nodes.summary: Henselization of a ring inherits good properties of formal fibers Let A be a P-ring where P satisfies (B), (C), (D), and (E). Let I ⊂ A be an ideal. Let (A^h, I^h) be the henselization of the pair (A, I), see Lemma [Tag 0A02]. Then A^h is a P-ring.

nodes.title: Properties of formal fibres · Lemma 0C36
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian local ring which is a P-ring where P satisfies (B), (C), (D), and (E). Then the henselization R^h and the strict henselization R^sh are P-rings.

nodes.title: Properties of formal fibres · Lemma 0BIW
nodes.summary: Properties (A), (B), (C), (D), and (E) hold for P(k → R) ="R is geometrically reduced over k".

nodes.title: Properties of formal fibres · Lemma 0BIX
nodes.summary: Properties (A), (B), (C), (D), and (E) hold for P(k → R) ="R is geometrically normal over k".

nodes.title: Properties of formal fibres · Lemma 0BIY
nodes.summary: Fix n ≥ 1. Properties (A), (B), (C), (D), and (E) hold for P(k → R) ="R has (S_n)".

nodes.title: Properties of formal fibres · Lemma 0BJ9
nodes.summary: Properties (A), (B), (C), (D), and (E) hold for P(k → R) ="R is Cohen-Macaulay".

nodes.title: Properties of formal fibres · Lemma 0BIZ
nodes.summary: Fix n ≥ 0. Properties (A), (B), (C), (D), and (E) hold for P(k → R) ="R ⊗_k k' has (R_n) for all finite extensions k'/k".

nodes.title: Excellent rings · Definition 07QT
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. • We say R is quasi-excellent if R is Noetherian, a G-ring, and J-2. • We say R is excellent if R is quasi-excellent and universally catenary.

nodes.title: Excellent rings · Lemma 07QU
nodes.summary: Any localization of a finite type ring over a (quasi-)excellent ring is (quasi-)excellent.

nodes.title: Excellent rings · Proposition 07QW
nodes.summary: The following types of rings are excellent: • fields, • Noetherian complete local rings, • Z, • Dedekind domains with fraction field of characteristic zero, • finite type ring extensions of any of the above.

nodes.title: Excellent rings · Lemma 0BJ0
nodes.summary: Let (A, m) be a Noetherian local ring. The following are equivalent • A is Nagata, and • the formal fibres of A are geometrically reduced.

nodes.title: Excellent rings · Lemma 07QV
nodes.summary: A quasi-excellent ring is Nagata.

nodes.title: Excellent rings · Lemma 0C23
nodes.summary: Let (A, m) be a Noetherian local ring. If A is normal and the formal fibres of A are normal (for example if A is excellent or quasi-excellent), then A^wedge is normal.

nodes.title: Injective abelian groups · Lemma 01D7
nodes.summary: An abelian group J is an injective object in the category of abelian groups if and only if J is divisible.

nodes.title: Injective modules · Definition 0AVD
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. An R-module J is injective if and only if the functor Hom_R(-, J) : Mod_R → Mod_R is an exact functor.

nodes.title: Injective modules · Lemma 0AUL
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let A be the abelian category of R-modules. There is a canonical isomorphism Ext_A(M, N) = Ext^1_R(M, N) compatible with the long exact sequences of Algebra, Lemmas [Tag 00LU] and [Tag 065P] and the 6-term exact sequences of Homology, Lemma [Tag 05E2].

nodes.title: Injective modules · Lemma 0AVE
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let J be an R-module. The following are equivalent • J is injective, • Ext^1_R(M, J) = 0 for every R-module M.

nodes.title: Injective modules · Lemma 0AVF
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let J be an R-module. The following are equivalent • J is injective, • Ext^1_R(R/I, J) = 0 for every ideal I ⊂ R, and • for an ideal I ⊂ R and module map I → J there exists an extension R → J.

nodes.title: Injective modules · Definition 01D9
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. • For any R-module M over R we denote M^vee = Hom(M, Q/Z) with its natural R-module structure. We think of M ↦ M^vee as a contravariant functor from the category of R-modules to itself. • For any R-module M we denote F(M) = bigoplus_m ∈ M R[m] the free module with basis given by the elements [m] with m ∈ M. We let F(M)→ M, ∑ f_i [m_i] ↦ ∑ f_i m_i be the natural surjection of R-modules. We think of M ↦ (F(M) → M) as a functor from the category of R-modules…

nodes.title: Injective modules · Lemma 01DA
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. The functor M ↦ M^vee is exact.

nodes.title: Injective modules · Lemma 01DB
nodes.summary: For any R-module M the evaluation map ev : M → (M^vee)^vee is injective.

nodes.title: Injective modules · Lemma 01DC
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. For every R-module M the R-module J(M) is injective.

nodes.title: Injective modules · Lemma 01DD
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. The construction above defines a covariant functor M ↦ (M → J(M)) from the category of R-modules to the category of arrows of R-modules such that for every module M the output M → J(M) is an injective map of M into an injective R-module J(M).

nodes.title: Derived categories of modules · Lemma 0915
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a flat ring map. If I^bullet is a K-injective complex of S-modules, then I^bullet is K-injective as a complex of R-modules.

nodes.title: Derived categories of modules · Lemma 0916
nodes.summary: Let R → S be an epimorphism of rings. Let I^bullet be a complex of S-modules. If I^bullet is K-injective as a complex of R-modules, then I^bullet is a K-injective complex of S-modules.

nodes.title: Derived categories of modules · Lemma 0917
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. If I^bullet is a K-injective complex of A-modules, then Hom_A(B, I^bullet) is a K-injective complex of B-modules.

nodes.title: Tensor products of complexes · Lemma 0FNI
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. The category Comp(R) of complexes of R-modules endowed with the functor (L^bullet, M^bullet) ↦ Tot(L^bullet ⊗_R M^bullet) and associativity and commutativity constraints as above is a symmetric monoidal category.

nodes.title: Tensor products of complexes · Lemma 064I
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let P^bullet be a complex of R-modules. Let α, β : L^bullet → M^bullet be homotopic maps of complexes. Then α and β induce homotopic maps Tot(α ⊗ id_P), Tot(β ⊗ id_P) : Tot(L^bullet ⊗_R P^bullet) → Tot(M^bullet ⊗_R P^bullet). In particular the construction L^bullet ↦ Tot(L^bullet ⊗_R P^bullet) defines an endo-functor of the homotopy category of complexes.

nodes.title: Tensor products of complexes · Lemma 0GWP
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. The homotopy category K(R) of complexes of R-modules endowed with the functor (L^bullet, M^bullet) ↦ Tot(L^bullet ⊗_R M^bullet) and associativity and commutativity constraints as above is a symmetric monoidal category.

nodes.title: Tensor products of complexes · Lemma 064J
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let P^bullet be a complex of R-modules. The functors K(R) → K(R), L^bullet ↦ Tot(P^bullet ⊗_R L^bullet) and K(R) → K(R), L^bullet ↦ Tot(L^bullet ⊗_R P^bullet) are exact functors of triangulated categories.

nodes.title: Derived tensor product · Definition 06XZ
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. A complex K^bullet is called K-flat if for every acyclic complex M^bullet the total complex Tot(M^bullet ⊗_R K^bullet) is acyclic.

nodes.title: Derived tensor product · Lemma 06Y0
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K^bullet be a K-flat complex. Then the functor K(R) → K(R), L^bullet ↦ Tot(L^bullet ⊗_R K^bullet) transforms quasi-isomorphisms into quasi-isomorphisms.

nodes.title: Derived tensor product · Lemma 06Y1
nodes.summary: Let R → R' be a ring map. If K^bullet is a K-flat complex of R-modules, then K^bullet ⊗_R R' is a K-flat complex of R'-modules.

nodes.title: Derived tensor product · Lemma 0795
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. If K^bullet, L^bullet are K-flat complexes of R-modules, then Tot(K^bullet ⊗_R L^bullet) is a K-flat complex of R-modules.

nodes.title: Derived tensor product · Lemma 06Y2
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let (K_1^bullet, K_2^bullet, K_3^bullet) be a distinguished triangle in K(R). If two out of three of K_i^bullet are K-flat, so is the third.

nodes.title: Derived tensor product · Lemma 0BYH
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let 0 → K_1^bullet → K_2^bullet → K_3^bullet → 0 be a short exact sequence of complexes. If K_3^n is flat for all n ∈ Z and two out of three of K_i^bullet are K-flat, so is the third.

nodes.title: Derived tensor product · Lemma 064K
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let P^bullet be a bounded above complex of flat R-modules. Then P^bullet is K-flat.

nodes.title: Derived tensor product · Lemma 06Y3
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K_1^bullet → K_2^bullet → … be a system of K-flat complexes. Then colim_i K_i^bullet is K-flat. More generally any filtered colimit of K-flat complexes is K-flat.

nodes.title: Derived tensor product · Lemma 0E8F
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K^bullet be a complex of R-modules. If K^bullet ⊗_R M is acyclic for all finitely presented R-modules M, then K^bullet is K-flat.

nodes.title: Derived tensor product · Lemma 06Y4
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. For any complex M^bullet there exists a K-flat complex K^bullet whose terms are flat R-modules and a quasi-isomorphism K^bullet → M^bullet which is termwise surjective.

nodes.title: Derived tensor product · Lemma 064L
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let α : P^bullet → Q^bullet be a quasi-isomorphism of K-flat complexes of R-modules. For every complex L^bullet of R-modules the induced map Tot(id_L ⊗ α) : Tot(L^bullet ⊗_R P^bullet) → Tot(L^bullet ⊗_R Q^bullet) is a quasi-isomorphism.

nodes.title: Derived tensor product · Definition 064M
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M^bullet be an object of D(R). The derived tensor product - ⊗_R^L M^bullet : D(R) → D(R) is the exact functor of triangulated categories described above.

nodes.title: Derived tensor product · Lemma 0BYI
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K^bullet, L^bullet be complexes of R-modules. There is a canonical isomorphism K^bullet ⊗_R^L L^bullet → L^bullet ⊗_R^L K^bullet functorial in both complexes which uses a sign of (-1)^pq for the map K^p ⊗_R L^q → L^q ⊗_R K^p (see proof for explanation).

nodes.title: Derived tensor product · Lemma 0BYJ
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K^bullet, L^bullet, M^bullet be complexes of R-modules. There is a canonical isomorphism (K^bullet ⊗_R^L L^bullet) ⊗_R^L M^bullet = K^bullet ⊗_R^L (L^bullet ⊗_R^L M^bullet) functorial in all three complexes.

nodes.title: Derived tensor product · Lemma 0G6M
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let a : K^bullet → L^bullet be a map of complexes of R-modules. If K^bullet is K-flat, then there exist a complex N^bullet and maps of complexes b : K^bullet → N^bullet and c : N^bullet → L^bullet such that • N^bullet is K-flat, • c is a quasi-isomorphism, • a is homotopic to c ∘ b. If the terms of K^bullet are flat, then we may choose N^bullet, b, and c such that the same is true for N^bullet.

nodes.title: Derived change of rings · Lemma 06Y6
nodes.summary: The construction above is independent of choices and defines an exact functor of triangulated categories - ⊗_R^L N^bullet : D(R) → D(A). There is a functorial isomorphism E^bullet ⊗_R^L N^bullet = (E^bullet ⊗_R^L A) ⊗_A^L N^bullet for E^bullet in D(R).

nodes.title: Derived change of rings · Lemma 0BYK
nodes.summary: Let R → A be a ring map. Let f : L^bullet → N^bullet be a map of complexes of A-modules. Then f induces a transformation of functors 1 ⊗ f : - ⊗_A^L L^bullet → - ⊗_A^L N^bullet If f is a quasi-isomorphism, then 1 ⊗ f is an isomorphism of functors.

nodes.title: Derived change of rings · Lemma 0GMT
nodes.summary: Let R → A be a ring map. The functor D(R) → D(A), E ↦ E ⊗_R^L A of Lemma [Tag 06Y6] is left adjoint to the restriction functor D(A) → D(R).

nodes.title: Derived change of rings · Lemma 08YU
nodes.summary: Let A → B → C be ring maps. Let N^bullet be a complex of B-modules and K^bullet a complex of C-modules. The compositions of the functors D(A) xrightarrow- ⊗_A^L N^bullet D(B) xrightarrow- ⊗_B^L K^bullet D(C) is the functor - ⊗_A^L (N^bullet ⊗_B^L K^bullet) : D(A) → D(C). If M, N, K are modules over A, B, C, then we have (M ⊗_A^L N) ⊗_B^L K = M ⊗_A^L (N ⊗_B^L K) = (M ⊗_A^L C) ⊗_C^L (N ⊗_B^L K) in D(C). We also have a canonical isomorphism (M ⊗_A^L N) ⊗_B^L K → (M ⊗_A^L K)…

nodes.title: Tor independence · Definition 0660
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let A, B be R-algebras. We say A and B are Tor independent over R if Tor_p^R(A, B) = 0 for all p > 0.

nodes.title: Tor independence · Lemma 0661
nodes.summary: The comparison map ([Tag 065Z]) is an isomorphism if A' = A ⊗_R R' and A and R' are Tor independent over R.

nodes.title: Tor independence · Lemma 08HW
nodes.summary: Consider a commutative diagram of rings xymatrix A' & R' ar[r] ar[l] & B' A ar[u] & R ar[l] ar[u] ar[r] & B ar[u] Assume that R' is flat over R and A' is flat over A ⊗_R R' and B' is flat over R' ⊗_R B. Then Tor_i^R(A, B) ⊗_(A ⊗_R B) (A' ⊗_R' B') = Tor_i^R'(A', B')

nodes.title: Tor independence · Lemma 0FXF
nodes.summary: Let R → A and R → B be ring maps. Let R → R' be a ring map and set A' = A ⊗_R R' and B' = B ⊗_R R'. If A and B are tor independent over R and R → R' is flat, then A' and B' are tor independent over R'.

nodes.title: Tor independence · Lemma 0DJD
nodes.summary: Assumptions as in Lemma [Tag 08HW]. For M ∈ D(A) there are canonical isomorphisms H^i((M ⊗_A^L A') ⊗_R'^L B') = H^i(M ⊗_R^L B) ⊗_(A ⊗_R B) (A' ⊗_R' B') of A' ⊗_R' B'-modules.

nodes.title: Tor independence · Lemma 08HX
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let A, B be R-algebras. The following are equivalent • A and B are Tor independent over R, • for every pair of primes p ⊂ A and q ⊂ B lying over the same prime r ⊂ R the rings A_ p and B_ q are Tor independent over R_ r, and • For every prime s of A ⊗_R B the module Tor_i^R(A, B)_ s = Tor_i^R_ r(A_ p, B_ q)_ s (where p = A ∩ s, q = B ∩ s and r = R ∩ s) is zero.

nodes.title: Products and Tor · Lemma 068K
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let A, B, C be R-algebras and let B → C be an R-algebra map. Then the induced map Tor^R_star(B, A) → Tor^R_star(C, A) is an A-algebra homomorphism.

nodes.title: K\"unneth spectral sequence · Lemma 0H7W
nodes.summary: Under the assumptions above, if in addition • the filtration on K^bullet is finite and the filtration on L^bullet is finite, or • more generally the following are true • F^iK^bullet is acyclic for i gg 0, • F^iK^bullet → K^bullet is a quasi-isomorphism for i ll 0, • F^jL^bullet is acyclic for j gg 0, and • F^jL^bullet → L^bullet is a quasi-isomorphism for j ll 0. Then the spectral sequence is bounded, the associated filtration on each H^n(T^bullet) = H^n(K^bullet ⊗_R^L…

nodes.title: K\"unneth spectral sequence · Lemma 0H7X
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K^bullet be a filtered complex. There exists a map f : P^bullet → K^bullet of filtered complexes such that • each P^n, F^iP^n, gr^iP^n is a free R-module, • the complexes of R-modules P^bullet, F^iP^bullet, and gr^iP^bullet are K-flat, • f induces quasi-isomorphisms P^bullet → K^bullet, F^iP^bullet → F^iK^bullet, and gr^iP^bullet → gr^iK^bullet.

nodes.title: K\"unneth spectral sequence · Proposition 0H7Y
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K^bullet and L^bullet be filtered complexes of R-modules. Then there exists a filtered complex T^bullet representing K^bullet ⊗_R^L L^bullet in D(R) such that the associated spectral sequence has E_1-page E_1^p, q = bigoplus_i + j = p H^p + q(gr^iK^bullet ⊗_R^L gr^jL^bullet) If • F^iK^bullet is acyclic for i gg 0, • F^iK^bullet → K^bullet is a quasi-isomorphism for i ll 0, • F^jL^bullet is acyclic for j gg 0, and • F^jL^bullet → L^bullet is a…

nodes.title: K\"unneth Spectral Sequence · Lemma 0H7Z
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K and L be objects of D^b(R). There exists a bigraded bounded spectral sequence (E_r)_r ≥ 2 with E_2^p, q = bigoplus_i + j = q Tor^R_-p(H^i(K), H^j(L)) and d_r of bidegree (r, -r + 1) converging to H^p + q(K ⊗_R^L L).

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, I · Definition 064Q
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Denote D(R) its derived category. Let m ∈ Z. • An object K^bullet of D(R) is m-pseudo-coherent if there exists a bounded complex E^bullet of finite free R-modules and a morphism α : E^bullet → K^bullet such that H^i(α) is an isomorphism for i > m and H^m(α) is surjective. • An object K^bullet of D(R) is pseudo-coherent if it is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded above complex of finite free R-modules. • An R-module M is called m-pseudo-coherent if M[0] is an…

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, I · Lemma 064R
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring and m ∈ Z. Let (K^bullet, L^bullet, M^bullet, f, g, h) be a distinguished triangle in D(R). • If K^bullet is (m + 1)-pseudo-coherent and L^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent then M^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent. • If K^bullet, M^bullet are m-pseudo-coherent, then L^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent. • If L^bullet is (m + 1)-pseudo-coherent and M^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent, then K^bullet is (m + 1)-pseudo-coherent.

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, I · Lemma 064S
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K^bullet be a complex of R-modules. Let m ∈ Z. • If K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent and H^i(K^bullet) = 0 for i > m, then H^m(K^bullet) is a finite type R-module. • If K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent and H^i(K^bullet) = 0 for i > m + 1, then H^m + 1(K^bullet) is a finitely presented R-module.

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, I · Lemma 064T
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Then • M is 0-pseudo-coherent if and only if M is a finite R-module, • M is (-1)-pseudo-coherent if and only if M is a finitely presented R-module, • M is (-d)-pseudo-coherent if and only if there exists a resolution R^⊕ a_d → R^⊕ a_d - 1 → … → R^⊕ a_0 → M → 0 of length d, and • M is pseudo-coherent if and only if there exists an infinite resolution … → R^⊕ a_1 → R^⊕ a_0 → M → 0 by finite free R-modules.

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, I · Lemma 064U
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K^bullet be a complex of R-modules. The following are equivalent • K^bullet is pseudo-coherent, • K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent for every m ∈ Z, and • K^bullet is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded above complex of finite projective R-modules. If (1), (2), and (3) hold and H^i(K^bullet) = 0 for i > b, then we can find a quasi-isomorphism F^bullet → K^bullet with F^i finite free R-modules and F^i = 0 for i > b.

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, I · Lemma 064V
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let (K^bullet, L^bullet, M^bullet, f, g, h) be a distinguished triangle in D(R). If two out of three of K^bullet, L^bullet, M^bullet are pseudo-coherent then the third is also pseudo-coherent.

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, I · Lemma 064W
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K^bullet be a complex of R-modules. Let m ∈ Z. • If H^i(K^bullet) = 0 for all i ≥ m, then K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent. • If H^i(K^bullet) = 0 for i > m and H^m(K^bullet) is a finite R-module, then K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent. • If H^i(K^bullet) = 0 for i > m + 1, the module H^m + 1(K^bullet) is of finite presentation, and H^m(K^bullet) is of finite type, then K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent.

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, I · Lemma 064X
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let m ∈ Z. If K^bullet ⊕ L^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent (resp. pseudo-coherent) so are K^bullet and L^bullet.

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, I · Lemma 064Y
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let m ∈ Z. Let K^bullet be a bounded above complex of R-modules such that K^i is (m - i)-pseudo-coherent for all i. Then K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent. In particular, if K^bullet is a bounded above complex of pseudo-coherent R-modules, then K^bullet is pseudo-coherent.

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, I · Lemma 066B
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let m ∈ Z. Let K^bullet ∈ D^-(R) such that H^i(K^bullet) is (m - i)-pseudo-coherent (resp. pseudo-coherent) for all i. Then K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent (resp. pseudo-coherent).

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, I · Lemma 064Z
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Assume that B is pseudo-coherent as an A-module. Let K^bullet be a complex of B-modules. The following are equivalent • K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent as a complex of B-modules, and • K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent as a complex of A-modules. The same equivalence holds for pseudo-coherence.

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, I · Lemma 0650
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Let K^bullet be an m-pseudo-coherent (resp. pseudo-coherent) complex of A-modules. Then K^bullet ⊗_A^L B is an m-pseudo-coherent (resp. pseudo-coherent) complex of B-modules.

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, I · Lemma 066C
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a flat ring map. Let M be an m-pseudo-coherent (resp. pseudo-coherent) A-module. Then M ⊗_A B is an m-pseudo-coherent (resp. pseudo-coherent) B-module.

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, I · Lemma 066D
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let f_1, …, f_r ∈ R be elements which generate the unit ideal. Let m ∈ Z. Let K^bullet be a complex of R-modules. If for each i the complex K^bullet ⊗_R R_f_i is m-pseudo-coherent (resp. pseudo-coherent), then K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent (resp. pseudo-coherent).

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, I · Lemma 068R
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let m ∈ Z. Let K^bullet be a complex of R-modules. Let R → R' be a faithfully flat ring map. If the complex K^bullet ⊗_R R' is m-pseudo-coherent (resp. pseudo-coherent), then K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent (resp. pseudo-coherent).

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, I · Lemma 0DJE
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K, L be objects of D(R). • If K is n-pseudo-coherent and H^i(K) = 0 for i > a and L is m-pseudo-coherent and H^j(L) = 0 for j > b, then K ⊗_R^L L is t-pseudo-coherent with t = max(m + a, n + b). • If K and L are pseudo-coherent, then K ⊗_R^L L is pseudo-coherent.

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, I · Lemma 066E
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Then • A complex of R-modules K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent if and only if K^bullet ∈ D^-(R) and H^i(K^bullet) is a finite R-module for i ≥ m. • A complex of R-modules K^bullet is pseudo-coherent if and only if K^bullet ∈ D^-(R) and H^i(K^bullet) is a finite R-module for all i. • An R-module is pseudo-coherent if and only if it is finite.

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, I · Lemma 0EWZ
nodes.summary: Let R be a coherent ring (Algebra, Definition [Tag 05CV]). Let K ∈ D^-(R). The following are equivalent • K is m-pseudo-coherent, • H^m(K) is a finite R-module and H^i(K) is coherent for i > m, and • H^m(K) is a finite R-module and H^i(K) is finitely presented for i > m. Thus K is pseudo-coherent if and only if H^i(K) is a coherent module for all i.

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, II · Lemma 0G8W
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M = colim M_i be a filtered colimit of R-modules. Let K ∈ D(R) be m-pseudo-coherent. Then colim Ext^n_R(K, M_i) = Ext^n_R(K, M) for n < -m and colim Ext^-m_R(K, M_i) → Ext^-m_R(K, M) is injective.

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, II · Lemma 0G8X
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K ∈ D^-(R). Let m ∈ Z. Then K is m-pseudo-coherent if and only if for any filtered colimit M = colim M_i of R-modules we have colim Ext^n_R(K, M_i) = Ext^n_R(K, M) for n < -m and colim Ext^-m_R(K, M_i) → Ext^-m_R(K, M) is injective.

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, II · Lemma 087Q
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let L, M, N be R-modules. • If M is finitely presented and L is flat, then the canonical map Hom_R(M, N) ⊗_R L → Hom_R(M, N ⊗_R L) is an isomorphism. • If M is (-m)-pseudo-coherent and L is flat, then the canonical map Ext^i_R(M, N) ⊗_R L → Ext^i_R(M, N ⊗_R L) is an isomorphism for i < m.

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, II · Lemma 087R
nodes.summary: Let R → R' be a flat ring map. Let M, N be R-modules. • If M is a finitely presented R-module, then Hom_R(M, N) ⊗_R R' = Hom_R'(M ⊗_R R', N ⊗_R R'). • If M is (-m)-pseudo-coherent, then Ext^i_R(M, N) ⊗_R R' = Ext^i_R'(M ⊗_R R', N ⊗_R R') for i < m. In particular if R is Noetherian and M is a finite module this holds for all i.

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, II · Lemma 0CYB
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K ∈ D^-(R). The following are equivalent: • K is pseudo-coherent, • for every family (Q_α)_α ∈ A of R-modules, the canonical map α : K ⊗_R^L ( ∏_α Q_α ) → ∏_α (K ⊗_R^L Q_α) is an isomorphism in D(R), • for every R-module Q and every set A, the canonical map β : K ⊗_R^L Q^A → (K ⊗_R^L Q)^A is an isomorphism in D(R), and • for every set A, the canonical map γ : K ⊗_R^L R^A → K^A is an isomorphism in D(R). Given m ∈ Z the following are equivalent • [(a)]…

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, II · Lemma 0G8Y
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K ∈ D(R) be pseudo-coherent. Let i ∈ Z. There exists a finitely presented R-module M and a map K → M[-i] in D(R) which induces an injection H^i(K) → M.

nodes.title: Pseudo-coherent modules, II · Lemma 0A7D
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian ring. Let K ∈ D(A) be pseudo-coherent, i.e., K ∈ D^-(A) with finite cohomology modules. Let m be a maximal ideal of A. If H^i(K)/ m H^i(K) not = 0, then there exists a finite A-module E annihilated by a power of m and a map K → E[-i] which is nonzero on H^i(K).

nodes.title: Tor dimension · Definition 0652
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Denote D(R) its derived category. Let a, b ∈ Z. • An object K^bullet of D(R) has tor-amplitude in [a, b] if H^i(K^bullet ⊗_R^L M) = 0 for all R-modules M and all i not ∈ [a, b]. • An object K^bullet of D(R) has finite tor dimension if it has tor-amplitude in [a, b] for some a, b. • An R-module M has tor dimension ≤ d if M[0] as an object of D(R) has tor-amplitude in [-d, 0]. • An R-module M has finite tor dimension if M[0] as an object of D(R) has finite…

nodes.title: Tor dimension · Lemma 0653
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K^bullet be a bounded above complex of flat R-modules with tor-amplitude in [a, b]. Then Coker(d_K^a - 1) is a flat R-module.

nodes.title: Tor dimension · Lemma 0654
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K^bullet be an object of D(R). Let a, b ∈ Z. The following are equivalent • K^bullet has tor-amplitude in [a, b]. • K^bullet is quasi-isomorphic to a complex E^bullet of flat R-modules with E^i = 0 for i not ∈ [a, b].

nodes.title: Tor dimension · Lemma 0BYL
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let a ∈ Z and let K be an object of D(R). The following are equivalent • K has tor-amplitude in [a, ∞], and • K is quasi-isomorphic to a K-flat complex E^bullet whose terms are flat R-modules with E^i = 0 for i not ∈ [a, ∞].

nodes.title: Tor dimension · Lemma 0655
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let (K^bullet, L^bullet, M^bullet, f, g, h) be a distinguished triangle in D(R). Let a, b ∈ Z. • If K^bullet has tor-amplitude in [a + 1, b + 1] and L^bullet has tor-amplitude in [a, b] then M^bullet has tor-amplitude in [a, b]. • If K^bullet, M^bullet have tor-amplitude in [a, b], then L^bullet has tor-amplitude in [a, b]. • If L^bullet has tor-amplitude in [a + 1, b + 1] and M^bullet has tor-amplitude in [a, b], then K^bullet has tor-amplitude in [a +…

nodes.title: Tor dimension · Lemma 066F
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Let d ≥ 0. The following are equivalent • M has tor dimension ≤ d, and • there exists a resolution 0 → F_d → … → F_1 → F_0 → M → 0 with F_i a flat R-module. In particular an R-module has tor dimension 0 if and only if it is a flat R-module.

nodes.title: Tor dimension · Lemma 066G
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let a, b ∈ Z. If K^bullet ⊕ L^bullet has tor amplitude in [a, b] so do K^bullet and L^bullet.

nodes.title: Tor dimension · Lemma 066H
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K^bullet be a bounded complex of R-modules such that K^i has tor amplitude in [a - i, b - i] for all i. Then K^bullet has tor amplitude in [a, b]. In particular if K^bullet is a finite complex of R-modules of finite tor dimension, then K^bullet has finite tor dimension.

nodes.title: Tor dimension · Lemma 066I
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let a, b ∈ Z. Let K^bullet ∈ D^b(R) such that H^i(K^bullet) has tor amplitude in [a - i, b - i] for all i. Then K^bullet has tor amplitude in [a, b]. In particular if K^bullet ∈ D^b(R) and all its cohomology groups have finite tor dimension then K^bullet has finite tor dimension.

nodes.title: Tor dimension · Lemma 0B66
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Let K^bullet and L^bullet be complexes of B-modules. Let a, b, c, d ∈ Z. If • K^bullet as a complex of B-modules has tor amplitude in [a, b], • L^bullet as a complex of A-modules has tor amplitude in [c, d], then K^bullet ⊗^L_B L^bullet as a complex of A-modules has tor amplitude in [a + c, b + d].

nodes.title: Tor dimension · Lemma 066J
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Assume that B is flat as an A-module. Let K^bullet be a complex of B-modules. Let a, b ∈ Z. If K^bullet as a complex of B-modules has tor amplitude in [a, b], then K^bullet as a complex of A-modules has tor amplitude in [a, b].

nodes.title: Tor dimension · Lemma 066K
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Assume that B has tor dimension ≤ d as an A-module. Let K^bullet be a complex of B-modules. Let a, b ∈ Z. If K^bullet as a complex of B-modules has tor amplitude in [a, b], then K^bullet as a complex of A-modules has tor amplitude in [a - d, b].

nodes.title: Tor dimension · Lemma 066L
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Let a, b ∈ Z. Let K^bullet be a complex of A-modules with tor amplitude in [a, b]. Then K^bullet ⊗_A^L B as a complex of B-modules has tor amplitude in [a, b].

nodes.title: Tor dimension · Lemma 066M
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a flat ring map. Let d ≥ 0. Let M be an A-module of tor dimension ≤ d. Then M ⊗_A B is a B-module of tor dimension ≤ d.

nodes.title: Tor dimension · Lemma 0B67
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Let K^bullet be a complex of B-modules. Let a, b ∈ Z. The following are equivalent • K^bullet has tor amplitude in [a, b] as a complex of A-modules, • K^bullet_ q has tor amplitude in [a, b] as a complex of A_ p-modules for every prime q ⊂ B with p = A ∩ q, • K^bullet_ m has tor amplitude in [a, b] as a complex of A_ p-modules for every maximal ideal m ⊂ B with p = A ∩ m.

nodes.title: Tor dimension · Lemma 066N
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let f_1, …, f_r ∈ R be elements which generate the unit ideal. Let a, b ∈ Z. Let K^bullet be a complex of R-modules. If for each i the complex K^bullet ⊗_R R_f_i has tor amplitude in [a, b], then K^bullet has tor amplitude in [a, b].

nodes.title: Tor dimension · Lemma 068S
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let a, b ∈ Z. Let K^bullet be a complex of R-modules. Let R → R' be a faithfully flat ring map. If the complex K^bullet ⊗_R R' has tor amplitude in [a, b], then K^bullet has tor amplitude in [a, b].

nodes.title: Tor dimension · Lemma 0DJF
nodes.summary: Given ring maps R → A → B with A → B faithfully flat and K ∈ D(A) the tor amplitude of K over R is the same as the tor amplitude of K ⊗_A^L B over R.

nodes.title: Tor dimension · Lemma 066P
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring of finite global dimension d. Then • every module has tor dimension ≤ d, • a complex of R-modules K^bullet with H^i(K^bullet) not = 0 only if i ∈ [a, b] has tor amplitude in [a - d, b], and • a complex of R-modules K^bullet has finite tor dimension if and only if K^bullet ∈ D^b(R).

nodes.title: Tor dimension · Lemma 0H75
nodes.summary: Let R' → R be a surjective ring map whose kernel is a nilpotent ideal. Let K' ∈ D(R') and set K = K' ⊗_R'^L R. Let a, b ∈ Z. Then K has tor amplitude in [a, b] if and only if K' does.

nodes.title: Projective dimension · Definition 0A5N
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K be an object of D(R). We say K has finite projective dimension if K can be represented by a bounded complex of projective modules. We say K has projective-amplitude in [a, b] if K is quasi-isomorphic to a complex … → 0 → P^a → P^a + 1 → … → P^b - 1 → P^b → 0 → … where P^i is a projective R-module for all i ∈ Z.

nodes.title: Projective dimension · Lemma 0A5P
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K be an object of D(R). Let a, b ∈ Z. The following are equivalent • K has projective-amplitude in [a, b], • Ext^i_R(K, N) = 0 for all R-modules N and all i not ∈ [-b, -a], • H^n(K) = 0 for n > b and Ext^i_R(K, N) = 0 for all R-modules N and all i > -a, and • H^n(K) = 0 for n not ∈ [a - 1, b] and Ext^-a + 1_R(K, N) = 0 for all R-modules N.

nodes.title: Injective dimension · Definition 0A5S
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K be an object of D(R). We say K has finite injective dimension if K can be represented by a finite complex of injective R-modules. We say K has injective-amplitude in [a, b] if K is isomorphic to a complex … → 0 → I^a → I^a + 1 → … → I^b - 1 → I^b → 0 → … with I^i an injective R-module for all i ∈ Z.

nodes.title: Injective dimension · Lemma 0A5T
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K be an object of D(R). Let a, b ∈ Z. The following are equivalent • K has injective-amplitude in [a, b], • Ext^i_R(N, K) = 0 for all R-modules N and all i not ∈ [a, b], • Ext^i(R/I, K) = 0 for all ideals I ⊂ R and all i not ∈ [a, b].

nodes.title: Injective dimension · Lemma 0A5V
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K ∈ D(R). • If K is in D^b(R) and H^i(K) has finite injective dimension for all i, then K has finite injective dimension. • If K^bullet represents K, is a bounded complex of R-modules, and K^i has finite injective dimension for all i, then K has finite injective dimension.

nodes.title: Injective dimension · Lemma 0DW2
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical of R. Let K ∈ D^+(R) have finite cohomology modules. Then the following are equivalent • K has finite injective dimension, and • there exists a b such that Ext^i_R(R/J, K) = 0 for i > b and any ideal J ⊃ I.

nodes.title: Injective dimension · Lemma 0AVJ
nodes.summary: Let (R, m, kappa) be a local Noetherian ring. Let K ∈ D^+(R) have finite cohomology modules. Then the following are equivalent • K has finite injective dimension, and • Ext^i_R(kappa, K) = 0 for i gg 0.

nodes.title: Modules which are close to being projective · Lemma 0G90
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M, N be R-modules. • Given an R-module map φ : M → N the following are equivalent: (a) φ factors through a projective R-module, and (b) φ factors through a free R-module. • The set of φ : M → N satisfying the equivalent conditions of (1) is an R-submodule of Hom_R(M, N). • Given maps ψ : M' → M and xi : N → N', if φ : M → N satisfies the equivalent conditions of (1), then xi ∘ φ ∘ ψ : M' → N' does too.
nodes.section: Modules which are close to being projective

nodes.title: Modules which are close to being projective · Lemma 0G91
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let φ : M → N be an R-module map. If φ factors through a projective module and M is a finite R-module, then φ factors through a finite projective module.
nodes.section: Modules which are close to being projective

nodes.title: Modules which are close to being projective · Lemma 0G92
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let M be an R-module. The following conditions are equivalent • for every a ∈ I the map a : M → M factors through a projective R-module, • for every a ∈ I the map a : M → M factors through a free R-module, and • Ext^1_R(M, N) is annihilated by I for every R-module N.
nodes.section: Modules which are close to being projective

nodes.title: Modules which are close to being projective · Definition 0G93
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let M be an R-module. We say M is I-projective if the equivalent conditions of Lemma [Tag 0G92] hold.
nodes.section: Modules which are close to being projective

nodes.title: Modules which are close to being projective · Lemma 0G94
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let M be an R-module. If M is annihilated by I, then M is I-projective.
nodes.section: Modules which are close to being projective

nodes.title: Modules which are close to being projective · Lemma 0G95
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let 0 → K → P → M → 0 be a short exact sequence of R-modules. If M is I-projective and P is projective, then K is I-projective.
nodes.section: Modules which are close to being projective

nodes.title: Modules which are close to being projective · Lemma 0G96
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. If M is a finite, I-projective R-module, then M^vee = Hom_R(M, R) is I-projective.
nodes.section: Modules which are close to being projective

nodes.title: Hom complexes · Lemma 0A5Y
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Given complexes K^bullet, L^bullet, M^bullet of R-modules there is a canonical isomorphism Hom^bullet(K^bullet, Hom^bullet(L^bullet, M^bullet)) = Hom^bullet(Tot(K^bullet ⊗_R L^bullet), M^bullet) of complexes of R-modules.

nodes.title: Hom complexes · Lemma 0A8I
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Given complexes K^bullet, L^bullet, M^bullet of R-modules there is a canonical morphism Tot( Hom^bullet(L^bullet, M^bullet) ⊗_R Hom^bullet(K^bullet, L^bullet) ) → Hom^bullet(K^bullet, M^bullet) of complexes of R-modules.

nodes.title: Hom complexes · Lemma 0BYM
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Given complexes K^bullet, L^bullet, M^bullet of R-modules there is a canonical morphism Tot(K^bullet ⊗_R Hom^bullet(M^bullet, L^bullet)) → Hom^bullet(M^bullet, Tot(K^bullet ⊗_R L^bullet)) of complexes of R-modules functorial in all three complexes.

nodes.title: Hom complexes · Lemma 0A62
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Given complexes K^bullet, L^bullet of R-modules there is a canonical morphism K^bullet → Hom^bullet(L^bullet, Tot(K^bullet ⊗_R L^bullet)) of complexes of R-modules functorial in both complexes.

nodes.title: Hom complexes · Lemma 0A60
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Given complexes K^bullet, L^bullet, M^bullet of R-modules there is a canonical morphism Tot(Hom^bullet(L^bullet, M^bullet) ⊗_R K^bullet) → Hom^bullet(Hom^bullet(K^bullet, L^bullet), M^bullet) of complexes of R-modules functorial in all three complexes.

nodes.title: Sign rules · Lemma 0FNJ
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M be an R-module. Let N, eta, ε be a left dual of M in the monoidal category of R-modules, see Categories, Definition [Tag 0FFP]. Then • M and N are finite projective R-modules, • the map e : Hom_R(M, R) → N, λ ↦ (λ ⊗ 1)(eta) is an isomorphism, • we have ε(n, m) = e^-1(n)(m) for n ∈ N and m ∈ M.

nodes.title: Sign rules · Lemma 0FNK
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let M^bullet be a complex of R-modules. Let N^bullet, eta, ε be a left dual of M^bullet in the monoidal category of complexes of R-modules. Then • M^bullet and N^bullet are bounded, • M^n and N^n are finite projective R-modules, • writing ε = ∑ ε_n with ε_n : N^-n ⊗_R M^n → R and eta = ∑ eta_n with eta_n : R → M^n ⊗_R N^-n then (N^-n, eta_n, ε_n) is the left dual of M^n as in Lemma [Tag 0FNJ], • the differential d_N^n : N^n → N^n + 1 is equal to -(-1)^n…

nodes.title: Derived hom · Lemma 0A65
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K, L, M be objects of D(R). There is a canonical isomorphism RHom_R(K, RHom_R(L, M)) = RHom_R(K ⊗_R^L L, M) in D(R) functorial in K, L, M which recovers ([Tag 0A63]) by taking H^0.

nodes.title: Derived hom · Lemma 0A66
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let P^bullet be a bounded above complex of projective R-modules. Let L^bullet be a complex of R-modules. Then RHom_R(P^bullet, L^bullet) is represented by the complex Hom^bullet(P^bullet, L^bullet).

nodes.title: Derived hom · Lemma 0A67
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K, L, M be objects of D(R). There is a canonical morphism RHom_R(L, M) ⊗_R^L K → RHom_R(RHom_R(K, L), M) in D(R) functorial in K, L, M.

nodes.title: Derived hom · Lemma 0A8J
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Given K, L, M in D(R) there is a canonical morphism RHom_R(L, M) ⊗_R^L RHom_R(K, L) → RHom_R(K, M) in D(R) functorial in K, L, M.

nodes.title: Derived hom · Lemma 0BYN
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Given complexes K, L, M in D(R) there is a canonical morphism K ⊗_R^L RHom_R(M, L) → RHom_R(M, K ⊗_R^L L) in D(R) functorial in K, L, M.

nodes.title: Derived hom · Lemma 0A6B
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Given complexes K, L in D(R) there is a canonical morphism K → RHom_R(L, K ⊗_R^L L) in D(R) functorial in both K and L.

nodes.title: Perfect complexes · Definition 0657
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Denote D(R) the derived category of the abelian category of R-modules. • An object K of D(R) is perfect if it is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective R-modules. • An R-module M is perfect if M[0] is a perfect object in D(R).

nodes.title: Perfect complexes · Lemma 0658
nodes.summary: Let K^bullet be an object of D(R). The following are equivalent • K^bullet is perfect, and • K^bullet is pseudo-coherent and has finite tor dimension. If (1) and (2) hold and K^bullet has tor-amplitude in [a, b], then K^bullet is quasi-isomorphic to a complex E^bullet of finite projective R-modules with E^i = 0 for i not ∈ [a, b].

nodes.title: Perfect complexes · Lemma 066Q
nodes.summary: Let M be a module over a ring R. The following are equivalent • M is a perfect module, and • there exists a resolution 0 → F_d → … → F_1 → F_0 → M → 0 with each F_i a finite projective R-module.

nodes.title: Perfect complexes · Lemma 066R
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let (K^bullet, L^bullet, M^bullet, f, g, h) be a distinguished triangle in D(R). If two out of three of K^bullet, L^bullet, M^bullet are perfect then the third is also perfect.

nodes.title: Perfect complexes · Lemma 066S
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. If K^bullet ⊕ L^bullet is perfect, then so are K^bullet and L^bullet.

nodes.title: Perfect complexes · Lemma 066T
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K^bullet be a bounded complex of perfect R-modules. Then K^bullet is a perfect complex.

nodes.title: Perfect complexes · Lemma 066U
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. If K^bullet ∈ D^b(R) and all its cohomology modules are perfect, then K^bullet is perfect.

nodes.title: Perfect complexes · Lemma 066V
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Assume that B is perfect as an A-module. Let K^bullet be a perfect complex of B-modules. Then K^bullet is perfect as a complex of A-modules.

nodes.title: Perfect complexes · Lemma 066W
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Let K^bullet be a perfect complex of A-modules. Then K^bullet ⊗_A^L B is a perfect complex of B-modules.

nodes.title: Perfect complexes · Lemma 066X
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a flat ring map. Let M be a perfect A-module. Then M ⊗_A B is a perfect B-module.

nodes.title: Perfect complexes · Lemma 0GM0
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. If K and L are perfect objects of D(R), then K ⊗_R^L L is a perfect object too.

nodes.title: Perfect complexes · Lemma 066Y
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let f_1, …, f_r ∈ R be elements which generate the unit ideal. Let K^bullet be a complex of R-modules. If for each i the complex K^bullet ⊗_R R_f_i is perfect, then K^bullet is perfect.

nodes.title: Perfect complexes · Lemma 068T
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K^bullet be a complex of R-modules. Let R → R' be a faithfully flat ring map. If the complex K^bullet ⊗_R R' is perfect, then K^bullet is perfect.

nodes.title: Perfect complexes · Lemma 066Z
nodes.summary: Let R be a regular ring. Then • an R-module is perfect if and only if it is a finite R-module, and • a complex of R-modules K^bullet is perfect if and only if K^bullet ∈ D^b(R) and each H^i(K^bullet) is a finite R-module.

nodes.title: Perfect complexes · Lemma 07VI
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let K ∈ D(A) be perfect. Then K^vee = RHom_A(K, A) is a perfect complex and K ≅ (K^vee)^vee. There are functorial isomorphisms L ⊗_A^L K^vee = RHom_A(K, L) and H^0(L ⊗_A^L K^vee) = Ext_A^0(K, L) for L ∈ D(A).

nodes.title: Perfect complexes · Lemma 0BKB
nodes.summary: Trivial duality for systems of perfect objects. Let A be a ring. Let (K_n)_n ∈ N be a system of perfect objects of D(A). Let K = hocolim K_n be the derived colimit (Derived Categories, Definition [Tag 090Z]). Then for any object E of D(A) we have RHom_A(K, E) = Rlim E ⊗^L_A K_n^vee where (K_n^vee) is the inverse system of dual perfect complexes.

nodes.title: Perfect complexes · Lemma 0BC7
nodes.summary: Let R = colim_i ∈ I R_i be a filtered colimit of rings. • Given a perfect K in D(R) there exists an i ∈ I and a perfect K_i in D(R_i) such that K ≅ K_i ⊗_R_i^L R in D(R). • Given 0 ∈ I and K_0, L_0 ∈ D(R_0) with K_0 perfect, we have Hom_D(R)(K_0 ⊗_R_0^L R, L_0 ⊗_R_0^L R) = colim_i ≥ 0 Hom_D(R_i)(K_0 ⊗_R_0^L R_i, L_0 ⊗_R_0^L R_i) In other words, the triangulated category of perfect complexes over R is the colimit of the triangulated categories of perfect complexes over R_i.

nodes.title: Lifting complexes · Lemma 0BC9
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let P be a class of R-modules. Assume • each P ∈ P is a projective R-module, • if P_1 ∈ P and P_1 ⊕ P_2 ∈ P, then P_2 ∈ P, and • if f : P_1 → P_2, P_1, P_2 ∈ P is surjective modulo I, then f is surjective. Then given any bounded above acyclic complex E^bullet whose terms are of the form P/IP for P ∈ P there exists a bounded above acyclic complex P^bullet whose terms are in P lifting E^bullet.

nodes.title: Lifting complexes · Lemma 0BCA
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let P be a class of R-modules. Let K ∈ D(R) and let E^bullet be a complex of R/I-modules representing K ⊗_R^L R/I. Assume • each P ∈ P is a projective R-module, • P_1 ∈ P and P_1 ⊕ P_2 ∈ P if and only if P_1, P_2 ∈ P, • if f : P_1 → P_2, P_1, P_2 ∈ P is surjective modulo I, then f is surjective, • E^bullet is bounded above and E^i is of the form P/IP for P ∈ P, and • K can be represented by a bounded above complex whose terms are in…

nodes.title: Lifting complexes · Lemma 09AR
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let E^bullet be a complex of R/I-modules. Let K be an object of D(R). Assume that • E^bullet is a bounded above complex of projective R/I-modules, • K ⊗_R^L R/I is represented by E^bullet in D(R/I), and • I is a nilpotent ideal. Then there exists a bounded above complex P^bullet of projective R-modules representing K in D(R) such that P^bullet ⊗_R R/I is isomorphic to E^bullet.

nodes.title: Lifting complexes · Lemma 0H76
nodes.summary: Let R' → R be a surjective ring map whose kernel is a nilpotent ideal. Let K' ∈ D(R') and set K = K' ⊗_R'^L R. Then K is pseudo-coherent if and only if K' is pseudo-coherent.

nodes.title: Lifting complexes · Lemma 0BCB
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let E^bullet be a complex of R/I-modules. Let K be an object of D(R). Assume that • E^bullet is a bounded above complex of finite stably free R/I-modules, • K ⊗_R^L R/I is represented by E^bullet in D(R/I), • K^bullet is pseudo-coherent, and • every element of 1 + I is invertible. Then there exists a bounded above complex P^bullet of finite stably free R-modules representing K in D(R) such that P^bullet ⊗_R R/I is isomorphic to…

nodes.title: Lifting complexes · Lemma 0BCC
nodes.summary: Let (R, m, kappa) be a local ring. Let K ∈ D(R) be pseudo-coherent. Set d_i = dim_kappa H^i(K ⊗_R^L kappa). Then d_i < ∞ and for some b ∈ Z we have d_i = 0 for i > b. Then there exists a complex … → R^⊕ d_b - 2 → R^⊕ d_b - 1 → R^⊕ d_b → 0 → … representing K in D(R). Moreover, this complex is unique up to isomorphism(!).

nodes.title: Lifting complexes · Lemma 0BCD
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let p ⊂ R be a prime. Let K ∈ D(R) be perfect. Set d_i = dim_kappa( p) H^i(K ⊗_R^L kappa( p)). Then d_i < ∞ and only a finite number are nonzero. Then there exists an f ∈ R, f not ∈ p and a complex … → 0 → R_f^⊕ d_a → R_f^⊕ d_a + 1 → … → R_f^⊕ d_b - 1 → R_f^⊕ d_b → 0 → … representing K ⊗_R^L R_f in D(R_f).

nodes.title: Lifting complexes · Lemma 0F9V
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let p ⊂ R be a prime. Let M^bullet and N^bullet be bounded complexes of finite projective R-modules representing the same object of D(R). Then there exists an f ∈ R, f not ∈ p such that there is an isomorphism (!) of complexes M^bullet_f ⊕ P^bullet ≅ N^bullet_f ⊕ Q^bullet where P^bullet and Q^bullet are finite direct sums of trivial complexes, i.e., complexes of the form the form … → 0 → R_f xrightarrow1 R_f → 0 → … (placed in arbitrary degrees).

nodes.title: Lifting complexes · Lemma 0BCE
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let E^bullet be a complex of R/I-modules. Let K be an object of D(R). Assume that • E^bullet is a bounded above complex of finite projective R/I-modules, • K ⊗_R^L R/I is represented by E^bullet in D(R/I), • K is pseudo-coherent, and • (R, I) is a henselian pair. Then there exists a bounded above complex P^bullet of finite projective R-modules representing K in D(R) such that P^bullet ⊗_R R/I is isomorphic to E^bullet. Moreover, if…

nodes.title: Splitting complexes · Lemma 0BCG
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K and L be objects of D(R). Assume L has projective-amplitude in [a, b], for example if L is perfect of tor-amplitude in [a, b]. • If H^i(K) = 0 for i ≥ a, then Hom_D(R)(L, K) = 0. • If H^i(K) = 0 for i ≥ a + 1, then given any distinguished triangle K → M → L → K[1] there is an isomorphism M ≅ K ⊕ L in D(R) compatible with the maps in the distinguished triangle. • If H^i(K) = 0 for i ≥ a, then the isomorphism in (2) exists and is unique.

nodes.title: Splitting complexes · Lemma 0A1U
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let p ⊂ R be a prime ideal. Let K^bullet be a pseudo-coherent complex of R-modules. Assume that for some i ∈ Z the map H^i(K^bullet) ⊗_R kappa( p) → H^i(K^bullet ⊗_R^L kappa( p)) is surjective. Then there exists an f ∈ R, f not ∈ p such that τ_≥ i + 1(K^bullet ⊗_R R_f) is a perfect object of D(R_f) with tor amplitude in [i + 1, ∞] and a canonical isomorphism K^bullet ⊗_R R_f ≅ τ_≤ i(K^bullet ⊗_R R_f) ⊕ τ_≥ i + 1(K^bullet ⊗_R R_f) in D(R_f).

nodes.title: Splitting complexes · Lemma 0A1V
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let p ⊂ R be a prime ideal. Let K^bullet be a pseudo-coherent complex of R-modules. Assume that for some i ∈ Z the maps H^i(K^bullet) ⊗_R kappa( p) → H^i(K^bullet ⊗_R^L kappa( p)) and H^i - 1(K^bullet) ⊗_R kappa( p) → H^i - 1(K^bullet ⊗_R^L kappa( p)) are surjective. Then there exists an f ∈ R, f not ∈ p such that • τ_≥ i + 1(K^bullet ⊗_R R_f) is a perfect object of D(R_f) with tor amplitude in [i + 1, ∞], • H^i(K^bullet)_f is a finite free R_f-module,…

nodes.title: Splitting complexes · Lemma 068U
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let p ⊂ R be a prime ideal. Let i ∈ Z. Let K^bullet be a pseudo-coherent complex of R-modules such that H^i(K^bullet ⊗_R^L kappa( p)) = 0. Then there exists an f ∈ R, f not ∈ p and a canonical direct sum decomposition K^bullet ⊗_R R_f = τ_≥ i + 1(K^bullet ⊗_R R_f) ⊕ τ_≤ i - 1(K^bullet ⊗_R R_f) in D(R_f) with τ_≥ i + 1(K^bullet ⊗_R R_f) a perfect complex with tor-amplitude in [i + 1, ∞].

nodes.title: Splitting complexes · Lemma 0G97
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K ∈ D^-(R). Let a ∈ Z. Assume that for any injective R-module map M → M' the map Ext^-a_R(K, M) → Ext^-a_R(K, M') is injective. Then there is a unique direct sum decomposition K ≅ τ_≤ aK ⊕ τ_≥ a + 1K and τ_≥ a + 1K has projective-amplitude in [a + 1, b] for some b.

nodes.title: Splitting complexes · Lemma 0G98
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K ∈ D^-(R). Let a ∈ Z. Assume Ext^-a_R(K, M) = 0 for any R-module M. Then there is a unique direct sum decomposition K ≅ τ_≤ a - 1K ⊕ τ_≥ a + 1K and τ_≥ a + 1K has projective-amplitude in [a + 1, b] for some b.

nodes.title: Recognizing perfect complexes · Lemma 0BYP
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring and let p ⊂ R be a prime. Let K be pseudo-coherent and bounded below. Set d_i = dim_kappa( p) H^i(K ⊗_R^L kappa( p)). If there exists an a ∈ Z such that d_i = 0 for i < a, then there exists an f ∈ R, f not ∈ p and a complex … → 0 → R_f^⊕ d_a → R_f^⊕ d_a + 1 → … → R_f^⊕ d_b - 1 → R_f^⊕ d_b → 0 → … representing K ⊗_R^L R_f in D(R_f). In particular K ⊗_R^L R_f is perfect.

nodes.title: Recognizing perfect complexes · Lemma 068V
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let a, b ∈ Z. Let K^bullet be a pseudo-coherent complex of R-modules. The following are equivalent • K^bullet is perfect with tor amplitude in [a, b], • for every prime p we have H^i(K^bullet ⊗_R^L kappa( p)) = 0 for all i not ∈ [a, b], and • for every maximal ideal m we have H^i(K^bullet ⊗_R^L kappa( m)) = 0 for all i not ∈ [a, b].

nodes.title: Recognizing perfect complexes · Lemma 068W
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K^bullet be a pseudo-coherent complex of R-modules. Consider the following conditions • K^bullet is perfect, • for every prime ideal p the complex K^bullet ⊗_R R_ p is perfect, • for every maximal ideal m the complex K^bullet ⊗_R R_ m is perfect, • for every prime p we have H^i(K^bullet ⊗_R^L kappa( p)) = 0 for all i ll 0, • for every maximal ideal m we have H^i(K^bullet ⊗_R^L kappa( m)) = 0 for all i ll 0. We always have the implications (1) ⇒ (2) ⇔…

nodes.title: Recognizing perfect complexes · Lemma 0G9A
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K be a pseudo-coherent object of D(R). Let a, b ∈ Z. The following are equivalent • K has projective-amplitude in [a, b], • K is perfect of tor-amplitude in [a, b], • Ext^i_R(K, N) = 0 for all finitely presented R-modules N and all i not ∈ [-b, -a], • H^n(K) = 0 for n > b and Ext^i_R(K, N) = 0 for all finitely presented R-modules N and all i > -a, and • H^n(K) = 0 for n not ∈ [a - 1, b] and Ext^-a + 1_R(K, N) = 0 for all finitely presented R-modules N.

nodes.title: Recognizing perfect complexes · Lemma 068X
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Let a, b ∈ Z. Let d ≥ 0. Let K^bullet be a complex of B-modules. Assume • the ring map A → B is flat, • for every prime p ⊂ A the ring B ⊗_A kappa( p) has finite global dimension ≤ d, • K^bullet is pseudo-coherent as a complex of B-modules, and • K^bullet has tor amplitude in [a, b] as a complex of A-modules. Then K^bullet is perfect as a complex of B-modules with tor amplitude in [a - d, b].

nodes.title: Recognizing perfect complexes · Lemma 09PC
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a local ring homomorphism. Let a, b ∈ Z. Let d ≥ 0. Let K^bullet be a complex of B-modules. Assume • the ring map A → B is flat, • the ring B/ m_AB is regular of dimension d, • K^bullet is pseudo-coherent as a complex of B-modules, and • K^bullet has tor amplitude in [a, b] as a complex of A-modules, in fact it suffices if H^i(K^bullet ⊗_A^L kappa( m_A)) is nonzero only for i ∈ [a, b]. Then K^bullet is perfect as a complex of B-modules with tor amplitude in…

nodes.title: Characterizing perfect complexes · Lemma 0ATI
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. The full subcategory D_perf(R) ⊂ D(R) of perfect objects is the smallest strictly full, saturated, triangulated subcategory containing R = R[0]. In other words D_perf(R) = langle R rangle. In particular, R is a classical generator for D_perf(R).

nodes.title: Characterizing perfect complexes · Lemma 07LR
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let K ∈ D(R) be an object such that for every countable set of objects E_n ∈ D(R) the canonical map bigoplus Hom_D(R)(K, E_n) → Hom_D(R)(K, bigoplus E_n) is a bijection. Then, given any system L_n^bullet of complexes over N we have that colim Hom_D(R)(K, L^bullet_n) → Hom_D(R)(K, L^bullet) is a bijection, where L^bullet is the termwise colimit, i.e., L^m = colim L_n^m for all m ∈ Z.

nodes.title: Characterizing perfect complexes · Proposition 07LT
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. For an object K of D(R) the following are equivalent • K is perfect, and • K is a compact object of D(R).

nodes.title: Characterizing perfect complexes · Lemma 07LU
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I ⊂ R be an ideal. Let K be an object of D(R). Assume that • K ⊗_R^L R/I is perfect in D(R/I), and • I is a nilpotent ideal. Then K is perfect in D(R).

nodes.title: Characterizing perfect complexes · Lemma 09AS
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let I, J ⊂ R be ideals. Let K be an object of D(R). Assume that • K ⊗_R^L R/I is perfect in D(R/I), and • K ⊗_R^L R/J is perfect in D(R/J). Then K ⊗_R^L R/IJ is perfect in D(R/IJ).

nodes.title: Strong generators and regular rings · Lemma 0FXH
nodes.summary: [Kelly] Let R be a ring. Let n ≥ 1. Let K ∈ langle R rangle_n with notation as in Derived Categories, Section [Tag 09SI]. Consider maps K xrightarrowf_1 K_1 xrightarrowf_2 K_2 xrightarrowf_3 … xrightarrowf_n K_n in D(R). If H^i(f_j) = 0 for all i, j, then f_n ∘ … ∘ f_1 = 0.

nodes.title: Strong generators and regular rings · Lemma 0FXI
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. If R is a strong generator for D_perf(R), then R is regular of finite dimension.

nodes.title: Strong generators and regular rings · Lemma 0FXJ
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian regular ring of dimension d < ∞. Let K, L ∈ D^-(R). Assume there exists an k such that H^i(K) = 0 for i ≤ k and H^i(L) = 0 for i ≥ k - d + 1. Then Hom_D(R)(K, L) = 0.

nodes.title: Strong generators and regular rings · Lemma 0FXK
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian regular ring of dimension 1 ≤ d < ∞. Let K ∈ D(R) be perfect and let k ∈ Z such that H^i(K) = 0 for i = k - d + 2, …, k (empty condition if d = 1). Then K = τ_≤ k - d + 1K ⊕ τ_≥ k + 1K.

nodes.title: Strong generators and regular rings · Lemma 0FXL
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian regular ring of finite dimension. Then R is a strong generator for the full subcategory D_perf(R) ⊂ D(R) of perfect objects.

nodes.title: Strong generators and regular rings · Proposition 0FXM
nodes.summary: Let R be a Noetherian ring. The following are equivalent • R is regular of finite dimension, • D_perf(R) has a strong generator, and • R is a strong generator for D_perf(R).

nodes.title: Relatively finitely presented modules · Lemma 05GY
nodes.summary: Let R → A be a ring map of finite type. Let M be an A-module. The following are equivalent • for some presentation α : R[x_1, …, x_n] → A the module M is a finitely presented R[x_1, …, x_n]-module, • for all presentations α : R[x_1, …, x_n] → A the module M is a finitely presented R[x_1, …, x_n]-module, and • for any surjection A' → A where A' is a finitely presented R-algebra, the module M is finitely presented as A'-module. In this case M is a finitely presented A-module.

nodes.title: Relatively finitely presented modules · Definition 05GZ
nodes.summary: Let R → A be a finite type ring map. Let M be an A-module. We say M is an A-module finitely presented relative to R if the equivalent conditions of Lemma [Tag 05GY] hold.

nodes.title: Relatively finitely presented modules · Lemma 05H0
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let A → B be a finite map of finite type R-algebras. Let M be a B-module. Then M is an A-module finitely presented relative to R if and only if M is a B-module finitely presented relative to R.

nodes.title: Relatively finitely presented modules · Lemma 065A
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring, f ∈ R an element, R_f → A is a finite type ring map, g ∈ A, and M an A-module. If M of finite presentation relative to R_f, then M_g is an A_g-module of finite presentation relative to R.

nodes.title: Relatively finitely presented modules · Lemma 065B
nodes.summary: Let R → A be a finite type ring map. Let M be an A-module finitely presented relative to R. For any ring map R → R' the A ⊗_R R'-module M ⊗_A A' = M ⊗_R R' is finitely presented relative to R'.

nodes.title: Relatively finitely presented modules · Lemma 0670
nodes.summary: Let R → A be a finite type ring map. Let M be an A-module finitely presented relative to R. Let A → A' be a ring map of finite presentation. The A'-module M ⊗_A A' is finitely presented relative to R.

nodes.title: Relatively finitely presented modules · Lemma 065C
nodes.summary: Let R → A → B be finite type ring maps. Let M be a B-module. If M is finitely presented relative to A and A is of finite presentation over R, then M is finitely presented relative to R.

nodes.title: Relatively finitely presented modules · Lemma 065D
nodes.summary: Let R → A be a finite type ring map. Let M be an A-module. Let f_1, …, f_r ∈ A generate the unit ideal. The following are equivalent • each M_f_i is finitely presented relative to R, and • M is finitely presented relative to R.

nodes.title: Relatively finitely presented modules · Lemma 0671
nodes.summary: Let R → A be a finite type ring map. Let 0 → M' → M → M" → 0 be a short exact sequence of A-modules. • If M', M" are finitely presented relative to R, then so is M. • If M' is a finite type A-module and M is finitely presented relative to R, then M" is finitely presented relative to R.

nodes.title: Relatively finitely presented modules · Lemma 0672
nodes.summary: Let R → A be a finite type ring map. Let M, M' be A-modules. If M ⊕ M' is finitely presented relative to R, then so are M and M'.

nodes.title: Relatively pseudo-coherent modules · Lemma 065F
