nodes.title: Projective bundles · Definition 01OB
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let E be a quasi-coherent O_S-module is finite locally free. We do not do so in order to be consistent with [EGA].. We denote π : P(E) = underlineProj_S(Sym(E)) → S and we call it the projective bundle associated to E. The symbol O_P(E)(n) indicates the invertible O_P(E)-module of Lemma [Tag 01O4] and is called the nth twist of the structure sheaf.

nodes.title: Projective bundles · Lemma 01OD
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. The structure morphism P(E) → S of a projective bundle over S is separated.

nodes.title: Projective bundles · Lemma 01OE
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let n ≥ 0. Then P^n_S is a projective bundle over S.

nodes.title: Grassmannians · Lemma 089T
nodes.summary: Let 0 < k < n. The functor G(k, n) of ([Tag 089S]) is representable by a scheme.

nodes.title: Grassmannians · Definition 089U
nodes.summary: Let 0 < k < n. The scheme G(k, n) representing the functor G(k, n) is called Grassmannian over Z. Its base change G(k, n)_S to a scheme S is called Grassmannian over S. If R is a ring the base change to Spec(R) is denoted G(k, n)_R and called Grassmannian over R.

nodes.title: Grassmannians · Lemma 089V
nodes.summary: Let n ≥ 1. There is a canonical isomorphism G(n, n + 1) = P^n_Z.

nodes.title: Constructible sets · Lemma 054C
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. A subset E of X is locally constructible in X if and only if E ∩ U is constructible in U for every affine open U of X.

nodes.title: Constructible sets · Lemma 0AAW
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme and let E ⊂ X be a locally constructible subset. Let xi ∈ X be a generic point of an irreducible component of X. • If xi ∈ E, then an open neighbourhood of xi is contained in E. • If xi not ∈ E, then an open neighbourhood of xi is disjoint from E.

nodes.title: Constructible sets · Lemma 054D
nodes.summary: Let X be a quasi-separated scheme. The intersection of any two quasi-compact opens of X is a quasi-compact open of X. Every quasi-compact open of X is retrocompact in X.

nodes.title: Constructible sets · Lemma 094L
nodes.summary: Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Then the underlying topological space of X is a spectral space.

nodes.title: Constructible sets · Lemma 054E
nodes.summary: Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Any locally constructible subset of X is constructible.

nodes.title: Constructible sets · Lemma 07ZL
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. A subset E of X is retrocompact in X if and only if E ∩ U is quasi-compact for every affine open U of X.

nodes.title: Constructible sets · Lemma 0F2M
nodes.summary: A partition X = coprod_i ∈ I X_i of a scheme X with retrocompact parts is locally finite if and only if the parts are locally constructible.

nodes.title: Integral, irreducible, and reduced schemes · Definition 01OK
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. We say X is integral if it is nonempty and for every nonempty affine open Spec(R) = U ⊂ X the ring R is an integral domain.

nodes.title: Integral, irreducible, and reduced schemes · Lemma 01OL
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. The following are equivalent. • The scheme X is reduced, see Schemes, Definition [Tag 01J0]. • There exists an affine open covering X = ⋃ U_i such that each Γ(U_i, O_X) is reduced. • For every affine open U ⊂ X the ring O_X(U) is reduced. • For every open U ⊂ X the ring O_X(U) is reduced.

nodes.title: Integral, irreducible, and reduced schemes · Lemma 01OM
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. The following are equivalent. • The scheme X is irreducible. • There exists an affine open covering X = ⋃_i ∈ I U_i such that I is not empty, U_i is irreducible for all i ∈ I, and U_i ∩ U_j not = ∅ for all i, j ∈ I. • The scheme X is nonempty and every nonempty affine open U ⊂ X is irreducible.

nodes.title: Integral, irreducible, and reduced schemes · Lemma 01ON
nodes.summary: A scheme X is integral if and only if it is reduced and irreducible.

nodes.title: Types of schemes defined by properties of rings · Definition 01OP
nodes.summary: Let P be a property of rings. We say that P is local if the following hold: • For any ring R, and any f ∈ R we have P(R) ⇒ P(R_f). • For any ring R, and f_i ∈ R such that (f_1, …, f_n) = R then ∀ i, P(R_f_i) ⇒ P(R).
nodes.section: Types of schemes defined by properties of rings

nodes.title: Types of schemes defined by properties of rings · Definition 01OQ
nodes.summary: Let P be a property of rings. Let X be a scheme. We say X is locally P if for any x ∈ X there exists an affine open neighbourhood U of x in X such that O_X(U) has property P.
nodes.section: Types of schemes defined by properties of rings

nodes.title: Types of schemes defined by properties of rings · Lemma 01OR
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let P be a local property of rings. The following are equivalent: • The scheme X is locally P. • For every affine open U ⊂ X the property P(O_X(U)) holds. • There exists an affine open covering X = ⋃ U_i such that each O_X(U_i) satisfies P. • There exists an open covering X = ⋃ X_j such that each open subscheme X_j is locally P. Moreover, if X is locally P then every open subscheme is locally P.
nodes.section: Types of schemes defined by properties of rings

nodes.title: Types of schemes defined by properties of rings · Lemma 01OS
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Then X is reduced if and only if X is "locally reduced" in the sense of Definition [Tag 01OQ].
nodes.section: Types of schemes defined by properties of rings

nodes.title: Types of schemes defined by properties of rings · Lemma 01OT
nodes.summary: The following properties of a ring R are local. • (Cohen-Macaulay.) The ring R is Noetherian and CM, see Algebra, Definition [Tag 00NC]. • (Regular.) The ring R is Noetherian and regular, see Algebra, Definition [Tag 00OD]. • (Absolutely Noetherian.) The ring R is of finite type over Z. • Add more here as needed.
nodes.section: Types of schemes defined by properties of rings

nodes.title: Noetherian schemes · Definition 01OV
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. • We say X is locally Noetherian if every x ∈ X has an affine open neighbourhood Spec(R) = U ⊂ X such that the ring R is Noetherian. • We say X is Noetherian if X is locally Noetherian and quasi-compact.

nodes.title: Noetherian schemes · Lemma 01OW
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. The following are equivalent: • The scheme X is locally Noetherian. • For every affine open U ⊂ X the ring O_X(U) is Noetherian. • There exists an affine open covering X = ⋃ U_i such that each O_X(U_i) is Noetherian. • There exists an open covering X = ⋃ X_j such that each open subscheme X_j is locally Noetherian. Moreover, if X is locally Noetherian then every open subscheme is locally Noetherian.

nodes.title: Noetherian schemes · Lemma 01OX
nodes.summary: Any immersion Z → X with X locally Noetherian is quasi-compact.

nodes.title: Noetherian schemes · Lemma 01OY
nodes.summary: A locally Noetherian scheme is quasi-separated.

nodes.title: Noetherian schemes · Lemma 01OZ
nodes.summary: A (locally) Noetherian scheme has a (locally) Noetherian underlying topological space, see Topology, Definition [Tag 0051].

nodes.title: Noetherian schemes · Lemma 02IK
nodes.summary: Any locally closed subscheme of a (locally) Noetherian scheme is (locally) Noetherian.

nodes.title: Noetherian schemes · Lemma 0BA8
nodes.summary: A Noetherian scheme has a finite number of irreducible components.

nodes.title: Noetherian schemes · Lemma 01P0
nodes.summary: Any morphism of schemes f : X → Y with X Noetherian is quasi-compact.

nodes.title: Noetherian schemes · Lemma 02IL
nodes.summary: Any nonempty locally Noetherian scheme has a closed point. Any nonempty closed subset of a locally Noetherian scheme has a closed point. Equivalently, any point of a locally Noetherian scheme specializes to a closed point.

nodes.title: Noetherian schemes · Lemma 054F
nodes.summary: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let x' leadsto x be a specialization of points of X. Then • there exists a discrete valuation ring R and a morphism f : Spec(R) → X such that the generic point eta of Spec(R) maps to x' and the special point maps to x, and • provided x not = x' given a finitely generated field extension K/kappa(x'), we may arrange it so that the extension kappa(eta)/kappa(x') induced by f is isomorphic to the given one.

nodes.title: Noetherian schemes · Lemma 0CXG
nodes.summary: Let S be a Noetherian scheme. Let T ⊂ S be an infinite subset. Then there exists an infinite subset T' ⊂ T such that there are no nontrivial specializations among the points T'.

nodes.title: Noetherian schemes · Lemma 0G2R
nodes.summary: Let S be a Noetherian scheme. Let T ⊂ S be a subset. Let T_0 ⊂ T be the set of t ∈ T such that there is no nontrivial specialization t' leadsto t with t' ∈ T'. Then (a) there are no specializations among the points of T_0, (b) every point of T is a specialization of a point of T_0, and (c) the closures of T and T_0 are the same.

nodes.title: Noetherian schemes · Lemma 0G2F
nodes.summary: Let S be a Noetherian scheme. Let T ⊂ S be an infinite dense subset. Then there exist a countable subset E ⊂ T which is dense in S.

nodes.title: Jacobson schemes · Definition 01P2
nodes.summary: A scheme S is said to be Jacobson if its underlying topological space is Jacobson.

nodes.title: Jacobson schemes · Lemma 01P3
nodes.summary: An affine scheme Spec(R) is Jacobson if and only if the ring R is Jacobson.

nodes.title: Jacobson schemes · Lemma 01P4
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. The following are equivalent: • The scheme X is Jacobson. • The scheme X is "locally Jacobson" in the sense of Definition [Tag 01OQ]. • For every affine open U ⊂ X the ring O_X(U) is Jacobson. • There exists an affine open covering X = ⋃ U_i such that each O_X(U_i) is Jacobson. • There exists an open covering X = ⋃ X_j such that each open subscheme X_j is Jacobson. Moreover, if X is Jacobson then every open subscheme is Jacobson.

nodes.title: Jacobson schemes · Lemma 02IM
nodes.summary: Examples of Noetherian Jacobson schemes. • If (R, m) is a Noetherian local ring, then the punctured spectrum Spec(R) setminus ( m) is a Jacobson scheme. • If R is a Noetherian ring with Jacobson radical rad(R) then Spec(R) setminus V(rad(R)) is a Jacobson scheme. • If (R, I) is a Zariski pair (More on Algebra, Definition [Tag 0ELY]) with R Noetherian, then Spec(R) setminus V(I) is a Jacobson scheme.

nodes.title: Normal schemes · Definition 033I
nodes.summary: A scheme X is normal if and only if for all x ∈ X the local ring O_X, x is a normal domain.

nodes.title: Normal schemes · Lemma 033J
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. The following are equivalent: • The scheme X is normal. • For every affine open U ⊂ X the ring O_X(U) is normal. • There exists an affine open covering X = ⋃ U_i such that each O_X(U_i) is normal. • There exists an open covering X = ⋃ X_j such that each open subscheme X_j is normal. Moreover, if X is normal then every open subscheme is normal.

nodes.title: Normal schemes · Lemma 033K
nodes.summary: A normal scheme is reduced.

nodes.title: Normal schemes · Lemma 033L
nodes.summary: Let X be an integral scheme. Then X is normal if and only if for every nonempty affine open U ⊂ X the ring O_X(U) is a normal domain.

nodes.title: Normal schemes · Lemma 0357
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme such that any quasi-compact open has a finite number of irreducible components. The following are equivalent: • X is normal, and • X is a disjoint union of normal integral schemes.

nodes.title: Normal schemes · Lemma 033M
nodes.summary: Let X be a Noetherian scheme. The following are equivalent: • X is normal, and • X is a finite disjoint union of normal integral schemes.

nodes.title: Normal schemes · Lemma 033N
nodes.summary: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme. The following are equivalent: • X is normal, and • X is a disjoint union of integral normal schemes.

nodes.title: Normal schemes · Lemma 0358
nodes.summary: The ring of functions on a normal scheme is normal. Let X be an integral normal scheme. Then Γ(X, O_X) is a normal domain.

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay schemes · Definition 02IO
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. We say X is Cohen-Macaulay if for every x ∈ X there exists an affine open neighbourhood U ⊂ X of x such that the ring O_X(U) is Noetherian and Cohen-Macaulay.

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay schemes · Lemma 02IP
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. The following are equivalent: • X is Cohen-Macaulay, • X is locally Noetherian and all of its local rings are Cohen-Macaulay, and • X is locally Noetherian and for any closed point x ∈ X the local ring O_X, x is Cohen-Macaulay.

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay schemes · Lemma 02IQ
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. The following are equivalent: • The scheme X is Cohen-Macaulay. • For every affine open U ⊂ X the ring O_X(U) is Noetherian and Cohen-Macaulay. • There exists an affine open covering X = ⋃ U_i such that each O_X(U_i) is Noetherian and Cohen-Macaulay. • There exists an open covering X = ⋃ X_j such that each open subscheme X_j is Cohen-Macaulay. Moreover, if X is Cohen-Macaulay then every open subscheme is Cohen-Macaulay.

nodes.title: Regular schemes · Definition 02IS
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. We say X is regular, or nonsingular if for every x ∈ X there exists an affine open neighbourhood U ⊂ X of x such that the ring O_X(U) is Noetherian and regular.

nodes.title: Regular schemes · Lemma 02IT
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. The following are equivalent: • X is regular, • X is locally Noetherian and all of its local rings are regular, and • X is locally Noetherian and for any closed point x ∈ X the local ring O_X, x is regular.

nodes.title: Regular schemes · Lemma 02IU
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. The following are equivalent: • The scheme X is regular. • For every affine open U ⊂ X the ring O_X(U) is Noetherian and regular. • There exists an affine open covering X = ⋃ U_i such that each O_X(U_i) is Noetherian and regular. • There exists an open covering X = ⋃ X_j such that each open subscheme X_j is regular. Moreover, if X is regular then every open subscheme is regular.

nodes.title: Regular schemes · Lemma 0569
nodes.summary: A regular scheme is normal.

nodes.title: Dimension · Definition 04MT
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. • The dimension of X is just the dimension of X as a topological spaces, see Topology, Definition [Tag 0055]. • For x ∈ X we denote dim_x(X) the dimension of the underlying topological space of X at x as in Topology, Definition [Tag 0055]. We say dim_x(X) is the dimension of X at x.

nodes.title: Dimension · Lemma 04MU
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. The following are equal • The dimension of X. • The supremum of the dimensions of the local rings of X. • The supremum of dim_x(X) for x ∈ X.

nodes.title: Dimension · Lemma 02IZ
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let Y ⊂ X be an irreducible closed subset. Let xi ∈ Y be the generic point. Then codim(Y, X) = dim(O_X, xi) where the codimension is as defined in Topology, Definition [Tag 02I3].

nodes.title: Dimension · Lemma 0BA9
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let x ∈ X. Then x is a generic point of an irreducible component of X if and only if dim(O_X, x) = 0.

nodes.title: Dimension · Lemma 0AAX
nodes.summary: A locally Noetherian scheme of dimension 0 is a disjoint union of spectra of Artinian local rings.

nodes.title: Dimension · Lemma 0CKV
nodes.summary: Email from Ofer Gabber dated June 4, 2016 Let X be a scheme of dimension zero. The following are equivalent • X is quasi-separated, • X is separated, • X is Hausdorff, • every affine open is closed. In this case the connected components of X are points and every quasi-compact open of X is affine. In particular, if X is quasi-compact, then X is affine.

nodes.title: Dimension · Lemma 0H7C
nodes.summary: Let x be a point of a locally Noetherian scheme X. Then dim_x(X) = 0 if and only if x is an isolated point of X.

nodes.title: Catenary schemes · Definition 02IW
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. We say S is catenary if the underlying topological space of S is catenary.

nodes.title: Catenary schemes · Lemma 02IX
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. The following are equivalent • S is catenary, • there exists an open covering of S all of whose members are catenary schemes, • for every affine open Spec(R) = U ⊂ S the ring R is catenary, and • there exists an affine open covering S = ⋃ U_i such that each U_i is the spectrum of a catenary ring. Moreover, in this case any locally closed subscheme of S is catenary as well.

nodes.title: Catenary schemes · Lemma 02IY
nodes.summary: Let S be a locally Noetherian scheme. The following are equivalent: • S is catenary, and • locally in the Zariski topology there exists a dimension function on S (see Topology, Definition [Tag 02I9]).

nodes.title: Catenary schemes · Lemma 02J0
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. The following are equivalent • X is catenary, and • for any x ∈ X the local ring O_X, x is catenary.

nodes.title: Serre's conditions · Definition 033Q
nodes.summary: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let k ≥ 0. • We say X is regular in codimension k, or we say X has property (R_k) if for every x ∈ X we have dim(O_X, x) ≤ k ⇒ O_X, x is regular • We say X has property (S_k) if for every x ∈ X we have depth(O_X, x) ≥ min(k, dim(O_X, x)).

nodes.title: Serre's conditions · Lemma 0B3C
nodes.summary: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme. Then X is regular if and only if X has (R_k) for all k ≥ 0.

nodes.title: Serre's conditions · Lemma 0342
nodes.summary: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme. Then X is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if X has (S_k) for all k ≥ 0.

nodes.title: Serre's conditions · Lemma 0344
nodes.summary: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme. Then X is reduced if and only if X has properties (S_1) and (R_0).

nodes.title: Serre's conditions · Lemma 0345
nodes.summary: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme. Then X is normal if and only if X has properties (S_2) and (R_1).

nodes.title: Serre's conditions · Lemma 0BX2
nodes.summary: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme which is normal and has dimension ≤ 1. Then X is regular.

nodes.title: Serre's conditions · Lemma 0B3D
nodes.summary: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme which is normal and has dimension ≤ 2. Then X is Cohen-Macaulay.

nodes.title: Japanese and Nagata schemes · Definition 033S
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. • Assume X integral. We say X is Japanese if for every x ∈ X there exists an affine open neighbourhood x ∈ U ⊂ X such that the ring O_X(U) is Japanese (see Algebra, Definition [Tag 032F]). • We say X is universally Japanese if for every x ∈ X there exists an affine open neighbourhood x ∈ U ⊂ X such that the ring O_X(U) is universally Japanese (see Algebra, Definition [Tag 032R]). • We say X is Nagata if for every x ∈ X there exists an affine open…

nodes.title: Japanese and Nagata schemes · Lemma 033U
nodes.summary: A Nagata scheme is locally Noetherian.

nodes.title: Japanese and Nagata schemes · Lemma 033V
nodes.summary: Let X be an integral scheme. The following are equivalent: • The scheme X is Japanese. • For every affine open U ⊂ X the domain O_X(U) is Japanese. • There exists an affine open covering X = ⋃ U_i such that each O_X(U_i) is Japanese. • There exists an open covering X = ⋃ X_j such that each open subscheme X_j is Japanese. Moreover, if X is Japanese then every open subscheme is Japanese.

nodes.title: Japanese and Nagata schemes · Lemma 033W
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. The following are equivalent: • The scheme X is universally Japanese. • For every affine open U ⊂ X the ring O_X(U) is universally Japanese. • There exists an affine open covering X = ⋃ U_i such that each O_X(U_i) is universally Japanese. • There exists an open covering X = ⋃ X_j such that each open subscheme X_j is universally Japanese. Moreover, if X is universally Japanese then every open subscheme is universally Japanese.

nodes.title: Japanese and Nagata schemes · Lemma 033X
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. The following are equivalent: • The scheme X is Nagata. • For every affine open U ⊂ X the ring O_X(U) is Nagata. • There exists an affine open covering X = ⋃ U_i such that each O_X(U_i) is Nagata. • There exists an open covering X = ⋃ X_j such that each open subscheme X_j is Nagata. Moreover, if X is Nagata then every open subscheme is Nagata.

nodes.title: Japanese and Nagata schemes · Lemma 033Y
nodes.summary: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme. Then X is Nagata if and only if every integral closed subscheme Z ⊂ X is Japanese.

nodes.title: Japanese and Nagata schemes · Lemma 033Z
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. The following are equivalent: • X is Nagata, and • X is locally Noetherian and universally Japanese.

nodes.title: G-schemes · Definition 0HA3
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. We say X is a G-scheme if for every x ∈ X there exists an affine open neighbourhood x ∈ U ⊂ X such that the ring O_X(U) is a G-ring (see More on Algebra, Definition [Tag 07GH]).

nodes.title: G-schemes · Lemma 0HA4
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. The following are equivalent: • X is a G-scheme, • X is locally Noetherian and for all x ∈ X the ring map O_X, x → O_X, x^wedge is regular, and • X is locally Noetherian and for any closed point x ∈ X the ring map O_X, x → O_X, x^wedge is regular.

nodes.title: G-schemes · Lemma 0HA5
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. The following are equivalent: • The scheme X is a G-scheme. • For every affine open U ⊂ X the ring O_X(U) is a G-ring. • There exists an affine open covering X = ⋃ U_i such that each O_X(U_i) is a G-ring. • There exists an open covering X = ⋃ X_j such that each open subscheme X_j is a G-scheme. Moreover, if X is a G-scheme then every open subscheme is a G-scheme.

nodes.title: The singular locus · Definition 07R1
nodes.summary: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme. The regular locus Reg(X) of X is the set of x ∈ X such that O_X, x is a regular local ring. The singular locus Sing(X) is the complement X setminus Reg(X), i.e., the set of points x ∈ X such that O_X, x is not a regular local ring.

nodes.title: Local irreducibility · Definition 0BQ2
nodes.summary: [EGA4] Let X be a scheme. Let x ∈ X. We say X is unibranch at x if the local ring O_X, x is unibranch. We say X is geometrically unibranch at x if the local ring O_X, x is geometrically unibranch. We say X is unibranch if X is unibranch at all of its points. We say X is geometrically unibranch if X is geometrically unibranch at all of its points.

nodes.title: Local irreducibility · Lemma 0BQ3
nodes.summary: A normal scheme is geometrically unibranch.

nodes.title: Local irreducibility · Lemma 0BQ4
nodes.summary: Compare with [Etale-coverings] Let X be a Noetherian scheme. The following are equivalent • X is geometrically unibranch (Definition [Tag 0BQ2]), • for every point x ∈ X which is not the generic point of an irreducible component of X, the punctured spectrum of the strict henselization O_X, x^sh is connected.

nodes.title: Local irreducibility · Definition 0C38
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let x ∈ X. The number of branches of X at x is the number of branches of the local ring O_X, x as defined in More on Algebra, Definition [Tag 0C26]. The number of geometric branches of X at x is the number of geometric branches of the local ring O_X, x as defined in More on Algebra, Definition [Tag 0C26].

nodes.title: Local irreducibility · Lemma 0E20
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme and x ∈ X. Let X_i, i ∈ I be the irreducible components of X passing through x. Then the number of (geometric) branches of X at x is the sum over i ∈ I of the number of (geometric) branches of X_i at x.

nodes.title: Local irreducibility · Lemma 0C39
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let x ∈ X. • The number of branches of X at x is 1 if and only if X is unibranch at x. • The number of geometric branches of X at x is 1 if and only if X is geometrically unibranch at x.

nodes.title: Characterizing modules of finite type and finite presentation · Lemma 01PB
nodes.summary: Let X = Spec(R) be an affine scheme. The quasi-coherent sheaf of O_X-modules widetilde M is a finite type O_X-module if and only if M is a finite R-module.
nodes.section: Characterizing modules of finite type and finite presentation

nodes.title: Characterizing modules of finite type and finite presentation · Lemma 01PC
nodes.summary: Let X = Spec(R) be an affine scheme. The quasi-coherent sheaf of O_X-modules widetilde M is an O_X-module of finite presentation if and only if M is an R-module of finite presentation.
nodes.section: Characterizing modules of finite type and finite presentation

nodes.title: Sections over principal opens · Lemma 01P7
nodes.summary: Sections of quasi-coherent sheaves have only meromorphic singularities at infinity. Let X be a scheme. Let f ∈ Γ(X, O_X). Denote X_f ⊂ X the open where f is invertible, see Schemes, Lemma [Tag 01HZ]. If X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the canonical map Γ(X, O_X)_f → Γ(X_f, O_X) is an isomorphism. Moreover, if F is a quasi-coherent sheaf of O_X-modules the map Γ(X, F)_f → Γ(X_f, F) is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Sections over principal opens · Lemma 01PW
nodes.summary: [EGA1-second] Let X be a scheme. Let L be an invertible sheaf on X. Let s ∈ Γ(X, L). Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. • If X is quasi-compact, then ([Tag 0B5L]) is injective, and • if X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, then ([Tag 0B5L]) is an isomorphism. In particular, the canonical map Γ_*(X, L)_(s) → Γ(X_s, O_X), a/s^n ↦ a ⊗ s^-n is an isomorphism if X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

nodes.title: Sections over principal opens · Lemma 01XQ
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let L be an invertible O_X-module. Let s ∈ Γ(X, L) be a section. Let F, G be quasi-coherent O_X-modules. • If X is quasi-compact and F is of finite type, then ([Tag 0B5M]) is injective, and • if X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and F is of finite presentation, then ([Tag 0B5M]) is bijective.

nodes.title: Quasi-affine schemes · Definition 01P6
nodes.summary: A scheme X is called quasi-affine if it is quasi-compact and isomorphic to an open subscheme of an affine scheme.

nodes.title: Quasi-affine schemes · Lemma 0EHM
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring and let U ⊂ Spec(A) be a quasi-compact open subscheme. For F quasi-coherent on U the canonical map widetildeH^0(U, F)|_U → F is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Quasi-affine schemes · Lemma 01P8
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let f ∈ Γ(X, O_X). Assume X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and assume that X_f is affine. Then the canonical morphism j : X → Spec(Γ(X, O_X)) from Schemes, Lemma [Tag 01I1] induces an isomorphism of X_f = j^-1(D(f)) onto the standard affine open D(f) ⊂ Spec(Γ(X, O_X)).

nodes.title: Quasi-affine schemes · Lemma 01P9
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Then X is quasi-affine if and only if the canonical morphism X → Spec(Γ(X, O_X)) from Schemes, Lemma [Tag 01I1] is a quasi-compact open immersion.

nodes.title: Quasi-affine schemes · Lemma 0ARY
nodes.summary: Let U → V be an open immersion of quasi-affine schemes. Then xymatrix U ar[d] ar[rr]_-j & & Spec(Γ(U, O_U)) ar[d] U ar[r] & V ar[r]^-j' & Spec(Γ(V, O_V)) is cartesian.

nodes.title: Quasi-affine schemes · Lemma 0F82
nodes.summary: Let X be a quasi-affine scheme. There exists an integer n ≥ 0, an affine scheme T, and a morphism T → X such that for every morphism X' → X with X' affine the fibre product X' ×_X T is isomorphic to A^n_X' over X'.

nodes.title: Flat modules · Lemma 05P0
nodes.summary: Flatness is the same for modules and sheaves. Let X = Spec(R) be an affine scheme. Let F = widetildeM for some R-module M. The quasi-coherent sheaf F is a flat O_X-module if and only if M is a flat R-module.

nodes.title: Locally free modules · Lemma 05JM
nodes.summary: Let X = Spec(R) be an affine scheme. Let F = widetildeM for some R-module M. The quasi-coherent sheaf F is a (finite) locally free O_X-module of if and only if M is a (finite) locally free R-module.

nodes.title: Locally free modules · Lemma 05P2
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. The following are equivalent: • F is a flat O_X-module of finite presentation, • F is O_X-module of finite presentation and for all x ∈ X the stalk F_x is a free O_X, x-module, • F is a locally free, finite type O_X-module, • F is a finite locally free O_X-module, and • F is an O_X-module of finite type, for every x ∈ X the stalk F_x is a free O_X, x-module, and the function ρ_F : X → Z, x ↦ dim_kappa(x) F_x ⊗_O_X,…

nodes.title: Locally free modules · Lemma 0FWH
nodes.summary: Let X be a reduced scheme. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. Then the equivalent conditions of Lemma [Tag 05P2] are also equivalent to • [(6)] F is an O_X-module of finite type and the function ρ_F : X → Z, x ↦ dim_kappa(x) F_x ⊗_O_X, x kappa(x) is locally constant in the Zariski topology on X.

nodes.title: Locally projective modules · Definition 05JP
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. We say F is locally projective if for every affine open U ⊂ X the O_X(U)-module F(U) is projective.

nodes.title: Locally projective modules · Lemma 05JQ
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. The following are equivalent • F is locally projective, and • there exists an affine open covering X = ⋃ U_i such that the O_X(U_i)-module F(U_i) is projective for every i. In particular, if X = Spec(A) and F = widetildeM then F is locally projective if and only if M is a projective A-module.

nodes.title: Locally projective modules · Lemma 060M
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes. Let G be a quasi-coherent O_Y-module. If G is locally projective on Y, then f^*G is locally projective on X.

nodes.title: Extending quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 01PE
nodes.summary: Let j : U → X be a quasi-compact open immersion of schemes. • Any quasi-coherent sheaf on U extends to a quasi-coherent sheaf on X. • Let F be a quasi-coherent sheaf on X. Let G ⊂ F|_U be a quasi-coherent subsheaf. There exists a quasi-coherent subsheaf H of F such that H|_U = G as subsheaves of F|_U. • Let F be a quasi-coherent sheaf on X. Let G be a quasi-coherent sheaf on U. Let φ : G → F|_U be a morphism of O_U-modules. There exists a quasi-coherent sheaf H of…

nodes.title: Extending quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 01PF
nodes.summary: Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Let U ⊂ X be a quasi-compact open. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. Let G ⊂ F|_U be a quasi-coherent O_U-submodule which is of finite type. Then there exists a quasi-coherent submodule G' ⊂ F which is of finite type such that G'|_U = G.

nodes.title: Extending quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 01PG
nodes.summary: Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Any quasi-coherent sheaf of O_X-modules is the directed colimit of its quasi-coherent O_X-submodules which are of finite type.

nodes.title: Extending quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 01PI
nodes.summary: Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. Let U ⊂ X be a quasi-compact open. Let G be an O_U-module which is of finite presentation. Let φ : G → F|_U be a morphism of O_U-modules. Then there exists an O_X-module G' of finite presentation, and a morphism of O_X-modules φ' : G' → F such that G'|_U = G and such that φ'|_U = φ.

nodes.title: Extending quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 0G41
nodes.summary: Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Let U ⊂ X be a quasi-compact open. Let G be an O_U-module. • If G is quasi-coherent and of finite type, then there exists a quasi-coherent O_X-module G' of finite type such that G'|_U = G. • If G is of finite presentation, then there exists an O_X-module G' of finite presentation such that G'|_U = G.

nodes.title: Extending quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 01PJ
nodes.summary: Quasi-coherent modules on quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes are filtered colimits of finitely presented modules. Let X be a scheme. Assume X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. There exist • a filtered index category I (see Categories, Definition [Tag 002V]), • a diagram I → Mod(O_X) (see Categories, Section [Tag 002D]), i ↦ F_i, • morphisms of O_X-modules φ_i : F_i → F such that each F_i is of finite presentation and such…

nodes.title: Extending quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 01PK
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Assume X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. There exist • a directed set I (see Categories, Definition [Tag 00D3]), • a system (F_i, φ_ii') over I in Mod(O_X) (see Categories, Definition [Tag 0030]) • morphisms of O_X-modules φ_i : F_i → F such that each F_i is of finite presentation and such that the morphisms φ_i induce an isomorphism colim_i F_i = F.

nodes.title: Extending quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 086M
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Assume X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let F be a finite type quasi-coherent O_X-module. Then we can write F = colim F_i with F_i of finite presentation and all transition maps F_i → F_i' surjective.

nodes.title: Extending quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 080V
nodes.summary: Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Let F be a finite type quasi-coherent O_X-module. Let U ⊂ X be a quasi-compact open such that F|_U is of finite presentation. Then there exists a map of O_X-modules φ : G → F with (a) G of finite presentation, (b) φ is surjective, and (c) φ|_U is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Extending quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 05JS
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Assume X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let A be a quasi-coherent O_X-algebra. There exist • a directed set I (see Categories, Definition [Tag 00D3]), • a system (A_i, φ_ii') over I in the category of O_X-algebras, • morphisms of O_X-algebras φ_i : A_i → A such that each A_i is a quasi-coherent O_X-algebra of finite presentation and such that the morphisms φ_i induce an isomorphism colim_i A_i = A.

nodes.title: Extending quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 05JT
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Assume X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let A be a quasi-coherent O_X-algebra. Then A is the directed colimit of its finite type quasi-coherent O_X-subalgebras.

nodes.title: Extending quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 086N
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Assume X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let A be a finite quasi-coherent O_X-algebra. Then A = colim A_i is a directed colimit of finite and finitely presented quasi-coherent O_X-algebras such that all transition maps A_i' → A_i are surjective.

nodes.title: Extending quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 0817
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Assume X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let A be an integral quasi-coherent O_X-algebra. Then • A is the directed colimit of its finite quasi-coherent O_X-subalgebras, and • A is a direct colimit of finite and finitely presented quasi-coherent O_X-algebras.

nodes.title: Gabber's result · Definition 077L
nodes.summary: Let (X, O_X) be a ringed space. Let kappa be an infinite cardinal. We say a sheaf of O_X-modules F is kappa-generated if there exists an open covering X = ⋃ U_i such that F|_U_i is generated by a subset R_i ⊂ F(U_i) whose cardinality is at most kappa.

nodes.title: Gabber's result · Lemma 077M
nodes.summary: Let (X, O_X) be a ringed space. Let kappa be a cardinal. There exists a set T and a family (F_t)_t ∈ T of kappa-generated O_X-modules such that every kappa-generated O_X-module is isomorphic to one of the F_t.

nodes.title: Gabber's result · Lemma 077N
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. There exists a cardinal kappa such that every quasi-coherent module F is the directed colimit of its quasi-coherent kappa-generated submodules.

nodes.title: Gabber's result · Proposition 077P
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. • The category QCoh(O_X) is a Grothendieck abelian category. Consequently, QCoh(O_X) has enough injectives and all limits. • The inclusion functor QCoh(O_X) → Mod(O_X) has a right adjoint. Q : Mod(O_X) → QCoh(O_X) such that for every quasi-coherent sheaf F the adjunction mapping Q(F) → F is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Sections with support in a closed subset · Lemma 01PH
nodes.summary: Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Let U ⊂ X be an open subscheme. The following are equivalent: • U is retrocompact in X, • U is quasi-compact, • U is a finite union of affine opens, and • there exists a finite type quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals I ⊂ O_X such that X setminus U = V(I) (set theoretically).
nodes.section: Sections with support in a closed subset

nodes.title: Sections with support in a closed subset · Lemma 01PO
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let I ⊂ O_X be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. Consider the sheaf of O_X-modules F' which associates to every open U ⊂ X F'(U) = (s ∈ F(U) mid Is = 0) Assume I is of finite type. Then • F' is a quasi-coherent sheaf of O_X-modules, • on any affine open U ⊂ X we have F'(U) = (s ∈ F(U) mid I(U)s = 0), and • F'_x = (s ∈ F_x mid I_x s = 0).
nodes.section: Sections with support in a closed subset

nodes.title: Sections with support in a closed subset · Definition 01PP
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let I ⊂ O_X be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of finite type. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. The subsheaf F' ⊂ F defined in Lemma [Tag 01PO] above is called the subsheaf of sections annihilated by I.
nodes.section: Sections with support in a closed subset

nodes.title: Sections with support in a closed subset · Lemma 07ZN
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes. Let I ⊂ O_Y be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of finite type. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. Let F' ⊂ F be the subsheaf of sections annihilated by f^-1IO_X. Then f_*F' ⊂ f_*F is the subsheaf of sections annihilated by I.

nodes.title: Sections with support in a closed subset · Lemma 07ZP
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let Z ⊂ X be a closed subset. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. Consider the sheaf of O_X-modules F' which associates to every open U ⊂ X F'(U) = (s ∈ F(U) mid the support of s is contained in Z ∩ U) If X setminus Z is a retrocompact open of X, then • for an affine open U ⊂ X there exist a finitely generated ideal I ⊂ O_X(U) such that Z ∩ U = V(I), • for U and I as in (1) we have F'(U) = (x ∈ F(U) mid I^nx = 0 for some n), • F' is a quasi-coherent…
nodes.section: Sections with support in a closed subset

nodes.title: Sections with support in a closed subset · Definition 084L
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let T ⊂ X be a closed subset whose complement is retrocompact in X. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. The quasi-coherent subsheaf F' ⊂ F defined in Lemma [Tag 07ZP] is called the subsheaf of sections supported on T.
nodes.section: Sections with support in a closed subset

nodes.title: Sections with support in a closed subset · Lemma 07ZQ
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes. Let Z ⊂ Y be a closed subset such that Y setminus Z is retrocompact in Y. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. Let F' ⊂ F be the subsheaf of sections supported in f^-1Z. Then f_*F' ⊂ f_*F is the subsheaf of sections supported in Z.
nodes.section: Sections with support in a closed subset

nodes.title: Sections of quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 01PM
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let I ⊂ A be a finitely generated ideal. Let M be an A-module. Then there is a canonical map colim_n Hom_A(I^n, M) → Γ(Spec(A) setminus V(I), widetildeM). This map is always injective. If for all x ∈ M we have Ix = 0 ⇒ x = 0 then this map is an isomorphism. In general, set M_n = (x ∈ M mid I^nx = 0), then there is an isomorphism colim_n Hom_A(I^n, M/M_n) → Γ(Spec(A) setminus V(I), widetildeM).

nodes.title: Sections of quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 01PQ
nodes.summary: Let X be a quasi-compact scheme. Let I ⊂ O_X be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of finite type. Let Z ⊂ X be the closed subscheme defined by I and set U = X setminus Z. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. The canonical map colim_n Hom_O_X(I^n, F) → Γ(U, F) is injective. Assume further that X is quasi-separated. Let F_n ⊂ F be subsheaf of sections annihilated by I^n. The canonical map colim_n Hom_O_X(I^n, F/F_n) → Γ(U, F) is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Ample invertible sheaves · Definition 01PS
nodes.summary: [EGA] Let X be a scheme. Let L be an invertible O_X-module. We say L is ample if • X is quasi-compact, and • for every x ∈ X there exists an n ≥ 1 and s ∈ Γ(X, L^⊗ n) such that x ∈ X_s and X_s is affine.

nodes.title: Ample invertible sheaves · Lemma 01PT
nodes.summary: [EGA] Let X be a scheme. Let L be an invertible O_X-module. Let n ≥ 1. Then L is ample if and only if L^⊗ n is ample.

nodes.title: Ample invertible sheaves · Lemma 01PU
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let L be an ample invertible O_X-module. For any closed subscheme Z ⊂ X the restriction of L to Z is ample.

nodes.title: Ample invertible sheaves · Lemma 01PV
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let L be an invertible O_X-module. Let s ∈ Γ(X, L). For any affine U ⊂ X the intersection U ∩ X_s is affine.

nodes.title: Ample invertible sheaves · Lemma 0890
nodes.summary: [EGA] Let X be a scheme. Let L and M be invertible O_X-modules. If • L is ample, and • the open sets X_t where t ∈ Γ(X, M^⊗ m) for m > 0 cover X, then L ⊗ M is ample.

nodes.title: Ample invertible sheaves · Lemma 01PX
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let L be an invertible O_X-module. Assume the open sets X_s, where s ∈ Γ(X, L^⊗ n) and n ≥ 1, form a basis for the topology on X. Then among those opens, the open sets X_s which are affine form a basis for the topology on X.

nodes.title: Ample invertible sheaves · Lemma 01PY
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme and L be an invertible O_X-module. Assume for every point x of X there exists n ≥ 1 and s ∈ Γ(X, L^⊗ n) such that x ∈ X_s and X_s is affine. Then X is separated.

nodes.title: Ample invertible sheaves · Lemma 09MP
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. If there exists an ample invertible sheaf on X then X is separated.

nodes.title: Ample invertible sheaves · Lemma 01PZ
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let L be an invertible O_X-module. Set S = Γ_*(X, L) as a graded ring. If every point of X is contained in one of the open subschemes X_s, for some s ∈ S_+ homogeneous, then there is a canonical morphism of schemes f : X → Y = Proj(S), to the homogeneous spectrum of S (see Constructions, Section [Tag 01M3]). This morphism has the following properties • f^-1(D_+(s)) = X_s for any s ∈ S_+ homogeneous, • there are O_X-module maps f^*O_Y(n) → L^⊗ n…

nodes.title: Ample invertible sheaves · Lemma 01Q0
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let L be an invertible O_X-module. Set S = Γ_*(X, L). Assume (a) every point of X is contained in one of the open subschemes X_s, for some s ∈ S_+ homogeneous, and (b) X is quasi-compact. Then the canonical morphism of schemes f : X → Proj(S) of Lemma [Tag 01PZ] above is quasi-compact with dense image.

nodes.title: Ample invertible sheaves · Lemma 01Q1
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let L be an invertible O_X-module. Set S = Γ_*(X, L). Assume L is ample. Then the canonical morphism of schemes f : X → Proj(S) of Lemma [Tag 01PZ] is an open immersion with dense image.

nodes.title: Ample invertible sheaves · Lemma 01Q2
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let S be a graded ring. Assume X is quasi-compact, and assume there exists an open immersion j : X → Y = Proj(S). Then j^*O_Y(d) is an invertible ample sheaf for some d > 0.

nodes.title: Ample invertible sheaves · Proposition 01Q3
nodes.summary: Let X be a quasi-compact scheme. Let L be an invertible sheaf on X. Set S = Γ_*(X, L). The following are equivalent: • L is ample, • the open sets X_s, with s ∈ S_+ homogeneous, cover X and the associated morphism X → Proj(S) is an open immersion, • the open sets X_s, with s ∈ S_+ homogeneous, form a basis for the topology of X, • the open sets X_s, with s ∈ S_+ homogeneous, which are affine form a basis for the topology of X, • for every quasi-coherent sheaf F on X the…

nodes.title: Ample invertible sheaves · Lemma 0B3E
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let L be an ample invertible O_X-module. Let i : X' → X be a morphism of schemes. Assume at least one of the following conditions holds • i is a quasi-compact immersion, • X' is quasi-compact and i is an immersion, • i is quasi-compact and induces a homeomorphism between X' and i(X'), • X' is quasi-compact and i induces a homeomorphism between X' and i(X'). Then i^*L is ample on X'.

nodes.title: Ample invertible sheaves · Lemma 0DNK
nodes.summary: Let S be a quasi-separated scheme. Let X, Y be schemes over S. Let L be an ample invertible O_X-module and let N be an ample invertible O_Y-module. Then M = pr_1^*L ⊗_O_X ×_S Y pr_2^*N is an ample invertible sheaf on X ×_S Y.

nodes.title: Affine and quasi-affine schemes · Lemma 01QE
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Then X is quasi-affine if and only if O_X is ample.

nodes.title: Affine and quasi-affine schemes · Lemma 0BCK
nodes.summary: Let X be a quasi-affine scheme. For any quasi-compact immersion i : X' → X the scheme X' is quasi-affine.

nodes.title: Affine and quasi-affine schemes · Lemma 01QF
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Suppose that there exist finitely many elements f_1, …, f_n ∈ Γ(X, O_X) such that • each X_f_i is an affine open of X, and • the ideal generated by f_1, …, f_n in Γ(X, O_X) is equal to the unit ideal. Then X is affine.

nodes.title: Quasi-coherent sheaves and ample invertible sheaves · Lemma 01QI
nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 01QH]. The canonical morphism f : X → Y maps X into the open subscheme W = W_1 ⊂ Y where O_Y(1) is invertible and where all multiplication maps O_Y(n) ⊗_O_Y O_Y(m) → O_Y(n + m) are isomorphisms (see Constructions, Lemma [Tag 01MU]). Moreover, the maps f^*O_Y(n) → L^⊗ n are all isomorphisms.
nodes.section: Quasi-coherent sheaves and ample invertible sheaves

nodes.title: Quasi-coherent sheaves and ample invertible sheaves · Lemma 01QJ
nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 01QH]. Let F be a quasi-coherent sheaf on X. Set M = Γ_*(X, L, F) as a graded S-module. There are isomorphisms f^*widetildeM → F functorial in F such that M_0 → Γ(Proj(S), widetildeM) → Γ(X, F) is the identity map.
nodes.section: Quasi-coherent sheaves and ample invertible sheaves

nodes.title: Quasi-coherent sheaves and ample invertible sheaves · Lemma 0AG5
nodes.summary: Let S be a graded ring such that X = Proj(S) is quasi-compact. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. Set M = bigoplus_n ∈ Z Γ(X, F(n)) as a graded S-module, see Constructions, Section [Tag 01MM]. The map widetildeM → F of Constructions, Lemma [Tag 0B5I] is an isomorphism. If X is covered by standard opens D_+(f) where f has degree 1, then the induced maps M_n → Γ(X, F(n)) are the identity maps.
nodes.section: Quasi-coherent sheaves and ample invertible sheaves

nodes.title: Finding suitable affine opens · Lemma 01ZV
nodes.summary: Let X be a quasi-separated scheme. Let Z_1, …, Z_n be pairwise distinct irreducible components of X, see Topology, Section [Tag 004U]. Let eta_i ∈ Z_i be their generic points, see Schemes, Lemma [Tag 01IS]. There exist affine open neighbourhoods eta_i ∈ U_i such that U_i ∩ U_j = ∅ for all i not = j. In particular, U = U_1 ∪ … ∪ U_n is an affine open containing all of the points eta_1, …, eta_n.

nodes.title: Finding suitable affine opens · Lemma 03J1
nodes.summary: Let X be a quasi-compact scheme. There exists a dense open V ⊂ X which is separated.

nodes.title: Finding suitable affine opens · Lemma 01ZX
nodes.summary: Let X be a quasi-separated scheme. Let Z_1, …, Z_n be pairwise distinct irreducible components of X. Let eta_i ∈ Z_i be their generic points. Let x ∈ X be arbitrary. There exists an affine open U ⊂ X containing x and all the eta_i.

nodes.title: Finding suitable affine opens · Lemma 01ZY
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Assume either • The scheme X is quasi-affine. • The scheme X is isomorphic to a locally closed subscheme of an affine scheme. • There exists an ample invertible sheaf on X. • The scheme X is isomorphic to a locally closed subscheme of Proj(S) for some graded ring S. Then for any finite subset E ⊂ X there exists an affine open U ⊂ X with E ⊂ U.

nodes.title: Finding suitable affine opens · Lemma 09NV
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let L be an ample invertible sheaf on X. Let E ⊂ W ⊂ X with E finite and W open in X. Then there exists an n > 0 and a section s ∈ Γ(X, L^⊗ n) such that X_s is affine and E ⊂ X_s ⊂ W.

nodes.title: Finding suitable affine opens · Lemma 0F20
nodes.summary: Let X be a quasi-affine scheme. Let L be an invertible O_X-module. Let E ⊂ W ⊂ X with E finite and W open. Then there exists an s ∈ Γ(X, L) such that X_s is affine and E ⊂ X_s ⊂ W.

nodes.title: Finding suitable affine opens · Lemma 0BX3
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme and x ∈ X a point. There exists an affine open neighbourhood U ⊂ X of x such that the canonical map O_X(U) → O_X, x is injective in each of the following cases: • X is integral, • X is locally Noetherian, • X is reduced and has a finite number of irreducible components.

nodes.title: Finding suitable affine opens · Lemma 0H9B
nodes.summary: Let U, V be affine schemes and let W → U and W → V be open immersions. For any w ∈ W there exists an affine open neighbourhood W' ⊂ W of w such that W' maps to a standard open of both U and V.

nodes.title: Closed immersions · Lemma 01QO
nodes.summary: Let i : Z → X be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent: • The morphism i is a closed immersion. • For every affine open Spec(R) = U ⊂ X, there exists an ideal I ⊂ R such that i^-1(U) = Spec(R/I) as schemes over U = Spec(R). • There exists an affine open covering X = ⋃_j ∈ J U_j, U_j = Spec(R_j) and for every j ∈ J there exists an ideal I_j ⊂ R_j such that i^-1(U_j) = Spec(R_j/I_j) as schemes over U_j = Spec(R_j). • The morphism i induces a homeomorphism of Z…

nodes.title: Closed immersions · Lemma 01QP
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let i : Z → X and i' : Z' → X be closed immersions and consider the ideal sheaves I = Ker(i^sharp) and I' = Ker((i')^sharp) of O_X. • The morphism i : Z → X factors as Z → Z' → X for some a : Z → Z' if and only if I' ⊂ I. If this happens, then a is a closed immersion. • We have Z ≅ Z' over X if and only if I = I'.

nodes.title: Closed immersions · Lemma 01QQ
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let I ⊂ O_X be a sheaf of ideals. The following are equivalent: • I is locally generated by sections as a sheaf of O_X-modules, • I is quasi-coherent as a sheaf of O_X-modules, and • there exists a closed immersion i : Z → X of schemes whose corresponding sheaf of ideals Ker(i^sharp) is equal to I.

nodes.title: Closed immersions · Lemma 01QR
nodes.summary: The base change of a closed immersion is a closed immersion.

nodes.title: Closed immersions · Lemma 01QS
nodes.summary: A composition of closed immersions is a closed immersion.

nodes.title: Closed immersions · Lemma 01QT
nodes.summary: A closed immersion is quasi-compact.

nodes.title: Closed immersions · Lemma 01QU
nodes.summary: A closed immersion is separated.

nodes.title: Immersions · Lemma 07RK
nodes.summary: Let Z → Y → X be morphisms of schemes. • If Z → X is an immersion, then Z → Y is an immersion. • If Z → X is a quasi-compact immersion and Y → X is quasi-separated, then Z → Y is a quasi-compact immersion. • If Z → X is a closed immersion and Y → X is separated, then Z → Y is a closed immersion.

nodes.title: Immersions · Lemma 01QV
nodes.summary: Let h : Z → X be an immersion. If h is quasi-compact, then we can factor h = i ∘ j with j : Z → overlineZ an open immersion and i : overlineZ → X a closed immersion.

nodes.title: Immersions · Lemma 03DQ
nodes.summary: Let h : Z → X be an immersion. If Z is reduced, then we can factor h = i ∘ j with j : Z → overlineZ an open immersion and i : overlineZ → X a closed immersion.

nodes.title: Immersions · Lemma 0FCZ
nodes.summary: Let f : Y → X be a morphism of schemes. If for all y ∈ Y there is an open subscheme f(y) ∈ U ⊂ X such that f|_f^-1(U) : f^-1(U) → U is an immersion, then f is an immersion.

nodes.title: Closed immersions and quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 01QY
nodes.summary: Let i : Z → X be a closed immersion of schemes. Let I ⊂ O_X be the quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals cutting out Z. The functor i_* : QCoh(O_Z) → QCoh(O_X) is exact, fully faithful, with essential image those quasi-coherent O_X-modules G such that IG = 0.

nodes.title: Closed immersions and quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 01QZ
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. Let G ⊂ F be a O_X-submodule. There exists a unique quasi-coherent O_X-submodule G' ⊂ G with the following property: For every quasi-coherent O_X-module H the map Hom_O_X(H, G') → Hom_O_X(H, G) is bijective. In particular G' is the largest quasi-coherent O_X-submodule of F contained in G.

nodes.title: Closed immersions and quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 01R0
nodes.summary: Let i : Z → X be a closed immersion of schemes. There is a functor i^! : QCoh(O_X) → QCoh(O_Z) which is a right adjoint to i_*. (Compare Modules, Lemma [Tag 01AZ].)

nodes.title: Closed immersions and quasi-coherent sheaves · Definition 0C4H
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let Z, Y ⊂ X be closed subschemes corresponding to quasi-coherent ideal sheaves I, J ⊂ O_X. The scheme theoretic intersection of Z and Y is the closed subscheme of X cut out by I + J. The scheme theoretic union of Z and Y is the closed subscheme of X cut out by I ∩ J.

nodes.title: Closed immersions and quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 0C4I
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let Z, Y ⊂ X be closed subschemes. Let Z ∩ Y be the scheme theoretic intersection of Z and Y. Then Z ∩ Y → Z and Z ∩ Y → Y are closed immersions and xymatrix Z ∩ Y ar[r] ar[d] & Z ar[d] Y ar[r] & X is a cartesian diagram of schemes, i.e., Z ∩ Y = Z ×_X Y.

nodes.title: Closed immersions and quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 0C4J
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X, Y ⊂ S be closed subschemes. Let X ∪ Y be the scheme theoretic union of X and Y. Let X ∩ Y be the scheme theoretic intersection of X and Y. Then X → X ∪ Y and Y → X ∪ Y are closed immersions, there is a short exact sequence 0 → O_X ∪ Y → O_X × O_Y → O_X ∩ Y → 0 of O_S-modules, and the diagram xymatrix X ∩ Y ar[r] ar[d] & X ar[d] Y ar[r] & X ∪ Y is cocartesian in the category of schemes, i.e., X ∪ Y = X amalg_X ∩ Y Y.

nodes.title: Supports of modules · Lemma 056I
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let F be a quasi-coherent sheaf on X. Let Spec(A) = U ⊂ X be an affine open, and set M = Γ(U, F). Let x ∈ U, and let p ⊂ A be the corresponding prime. The following are equivalent • p is in the support of M, and • x is in the support of F.

nodes.title: Supports of modules · Lemma 05AC
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let F be a quasi-coherent sheaf on X. The support of F is closed under specialization.

nodes.title: Supports of modules · Lemma 056J
nodes.summary: Let F be a finite type quasi-coherent module on a scheme X. Then • The support of F is closed. • For x ∈ X we have x ∈ Supp(F) ⇔ F_x not = 0 ⇔ F_x ⊗_O_X, x kappa(x) not = 0. • For any morphism of schemes f : Y → X the pullback f^*F is of finite type as well and we have Supp(f^*F) = f^-1(Supp(F)).

nodes.title: Supports of modules · Lemma 05JU
nodes.summary: Let F be a finite type quasi-coherent module on a scheme X. There exists a smallest closed subscheme i : Z → X such that there exists a quasi-coherent O_Z-module G with i_*G ≅ F. Moreover: • If Spec(A) ⊂ X is any affine open, and F|_Spec(A) = widetildeM then Z ∩ Spec(A) = Spec(A/I) where I = Ann_A(M). • The quasi-coherent sheaf G is unique up to unique isomorphism. • The quasi-coherent sheaf G is of finite type. • The support of G and of F is Z.

nodes.title: Supports of modules · Definition 05JV
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module of finite type. The scheme theoretic support of F is the closed subscheme Z ⊂ X constructed in Lemma [Tag 05JU].

nodes.title: Scheme theoretic image · Lemma 01R6
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes. There exists a closed subscheme Z ⊂ Y such that f factors through Z and such that for any other closed subscheme Z' ⊂ Y such that f factors through Z' we have Z ⊂ Z'.

nodes.title: Scheme theoretic image · Definition 01R7
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes. The scheme theoretic image of f is the smallest closed subscheme Z ⊂ Y through which f factors, see Lemma [Tag 01R6] above.

nodes.title: Scheme theoretic image · Lemma 01R8
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes. Let Z ⊂ Y be the scheme theoretic image of f. If f is quasi-compact then • the sheaf of ideals I = Ker(O_Y → f_*O_X) is quasi-coherent, • the scheme theoretic image Z is the closed subscheme determined by I, • for any open U ⊂ Y the scheme theoretic image of f|_f^-1(U) : f^-1(U) → U is equal to Z ∩ U, and • the image f(X) ⊂ Z is a dense subset of Z, in other words the morphism X → Z is dominant (see Definition [Tag 01RJ]).

nodes.title: Scheme theoretic image · Lemma 02JQ
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a quasi-compact morphism. Let Z be the scheme theoretic image of f. Let z ∈ Z. There exists a valuation ring A with fraction field K and a commutative diagram xymatrix Spec(K) ar[rr] ar[d] & & X ar[d] ar[ld] Spec(A) ar[r] & Z ar[r] & Y such that the closed point of Spec(A) maps to z. In particular any point of Z is the specialization of a point of f(X).

nodes.title: Scheme theoretic image · Lemma 01R9
nodes.summary: Let xymatrix X_1 ar[d] ar[r]_f_1 & Y_1 ar[d] X_2 ar[r]^f_2 & Y_2 be a commutative diagram of schemes. Let Z_i ⊂ Y_i, i = 1, 2 be the scheme theoretic image of f_i. Then the morphism Y_1 → Y_2 induces a morphism Z_1 → Z_2 and a commutative diagram xymatrix X_1 ar[r] ar[d] & Z_1 ar[d] ar[r] & Y_1 ar[d] X_2 ar[r] & Z_2 ar[r] & Y_2

nodes.title: Scheme theoretic image · Lemma 056B
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes. If X is reduced, then the scheme theoretic image of f is the reduced induced scheme structure on overlinef(X).

nodes.title: Scheme theoretic image · Lemma 0CNG
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a separated morphism of schemes. Let V ⊂ Y be a retrocompact open. Let s : V → X be a morphism such that f ∘ s = id_V. Let Y' be the scheme theoretic image of s. Then Y' → Y is an isomorphism over V.

nodes.title: Scheme theoretic closure and density · Definition 01RB
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let U ⊂ X be an open subscheme. • The scheme theoretic image of the morphism U → X is called the scheme theoretic closure of U in X. • We say U is scheme theoretically dense in X if for every open V ⊂ X the scheme theoretic closure of U ∩ V in V is equal to V.

nodes.title: Scheme theoretic closure and density · Lemma 01RD
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let U ⊂ X be an open subscheme. If the inclusion morphism U → X is quasi-compact, then U is scheme theoretically dense in X if and only if the scheme theoretic closure of U in X is X.

nodes.title: Scheme theoretic closure and density · Lemma 01RE
nodes.summary: Let j : U → X be an open immersion of schemes. Then U is scheme theoretically dense in X if and only if O_X → j_*O_U is injective.

nodes.title: Scheme theoretic closure and density · Lemma 01RF
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. If U, V are scheme theoretically dense open subschemes of X, then so is U ∩ V.

nodes.title: Scheme theoretic closure and density · Lemma 01RG
nodes.summary: Let h : Z → X be an immersion. Assume either h is quasi-compact or Z is reduced. Let overlineZ ⊂ X be the scheme theoretic image of h. Then the morphism Z → overlineZ is an open immersion which identifies Z with a scheme theoretically dense open subscheme of overlineZ. Moreover, Z is topologically dense in overlineZ.

nodes.title: Scheme theoretic closure and density · Lemma 056D
nodes.summary: Let X be a reduced scheme and let U ⊂ X be an open subscheme. Then the following are equivalent • U is topologically dense in X, • the scheme theoretic closure of U in X is X, and • U is scheme theoretically dense in X.

nodes.title: Scheme theoretic closure and density · Lemma 056E
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme and let U ⊂ X be a reduced open subscheme. Then the following are equivalent • the scheme theoretic closure of U in X is X, and • U is scheme theoretically dense in X. If this holds then X is a reduced scheme.

nodes.title: Scheme theoretic closure and density · Lemma 01RH
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X, Y be schemes over S. Let f, g : X → Y be morphisms of schemes over S. Let U ⊂ X be an open subscheme such that f|_U = g|_U. If the scheme theoretic closure of U in X is X and Y → S is separated, then f = g.

nodes.title: Dominant morphisms · Definition 01RJ
nodes.summary: A morphism f : X → S of schemes is called dominant if the image of f is a dense subset of S.

nodes.title: Dominant morphisms · Lemma 01RK
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. If every generic point of every irreducible component of S is in the image of f, then f is dominant.

nodes.title: Dominant morphisms · Lemma 01RL
nodes.summary: Morphisms whose image contains the generic points are dominant Let f : X → S be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes. Then f is dominant if and only if for every irreducible component Z ⊂ S the generic point of Z is in the image of f.

nodes.title: Dominant morphisms · Lemma 0H3F
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a quasi-compact dominant morphism of schemes. Let g : S' → S be a morphism of schemes, and let f' : X' → S' be the base change of f by g. If generalizations lift along g, then f' is dominant.

nodes.title: Dominant morphisms · Lemma 0H8F
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a dominant morphism of schemes. Let g : S' → S be an open morphism of schemes, and let f' : X' → S' be the base change of f by g. Then f' is dominant.

nodes.title: Dominant morphisms · Lemma 02NE
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes. Let eta ∈ S be a generic point of an irreducible component of S. If eta not ∈ f(X) then there exists an open neighbourhood V ⊂ S of eta such that f^-1(V) = ∅.

nodes.title: Dominant morphisms · Lemma 01RM
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Suppose that X has finitely many irreducible components. Then f is dominant (if and) only if for every irreducible component Z ⊂ S the generic point of Z is in the image of f. If so, then S has finitely many irreducible components as well.

nodes.title: Dominant morphisms · Lemma 0CC1
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of integral schemes. The following are equivalent • f is dominant, • f maps the generic point of X to the generic point of Y, • for some nonempty affine opens U ⊂ X and V ⊂ Y with f(U) ⊂ V the ring map O_Y(V) → O_X(U) is injective, • for all nonempty affine opens U ⊂ X and V ⊂ Y with f(U) ⊂ V the ring map O_Y(V) → O_X(U) is injective, • for some x ∈ X with image y = f(x) ∈ Y the local ring map O_Y, y → O_X, x is injective, and • for all x ∈ X…

nodes.title: Surjective morphisms · Definition 01RZ
nodes.summary: A morphism of schemes is said to be surjective if it is surjective on underlying topological spaces.

nodes.title: Surjective morphisms · Lemma 01S0
nodes.summary: The composition of surjective morphisms is surjective.

nodes.title: Surjective morphisms · Lemma 0495
nodes.summary: Let X and Y be schemes over a base scheme S. Given points x ∈ X and y ∈ Y, there is a point of X ×_S Y mapping to x and y under the projections if and only if x and y lie above the same point of S.

nodes.title: Surjective morphisms · Lemma 01S1
nodes.summary: The base change of a surjective morphism is surjective.

nodes.title: Surjective morphisms · Lemma 04ZD
nodes.summary: Let xymatrix X ar[rr]_f ar[rd]_p & & Y ar[dl]^q & Z be a commutative diagram of morphisms of schemes. If f is surjective and p is quasi-compact, then q is quasi-compact.

nodes.title: Radicial and universally injective morphisms · Definition 01S3
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism. • We say that f is universally injective if and only if for any morphism of schemes S' → S the base change f' : X_S' → S' is injective (on underlying topological spaces). • We say f is radicial if f is injective as a map of topological spaces, and for every x ∈ X the field extension kappa(x)/kappa(f(x)) is purely inseparable.

nodes.title: Radicial and universally injective morphisms · Lemma 01S4
nodes.summary: [EGA1-second] Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent: • For every field K the induced map Mor(Spec(K), X) → Mor(Spec(K), S) is injective. • The morphism f is universally injective. • The morphism f is radicial. • The diagonal morphism Δ_X/S : X → X ×_S X is surjective.

nodes.title: Radicial and universally injective morphisms · Lemma 05VE
nodes.summary: A universally injective morphism is separated.

nodes.title: Radicial and universally injective morphisms · Lemma 0472
nodes.summary: A base change of a universally injective morphism is universally injective.

nodes.title: Radicial and universally injective morphisms · Lemma 02V1
nodes.summary: A composition of radicial morphisms is radicial, and so the same holds for the equivalent condition of being universally injective.

nodes.title: Affine morphisms · Definition 01S6
nodes.summary: A morphism of schemes f : X → S is called affine if the inverse image of every affine open of S is an affine open of X.

nodes.title: Affine morphisms · Lemma 01S7
nodes.summary: An affine morphism is separated and quasi-compact.

nodes.title: Affine morphisms · Lemma 01S8
nodes.summary: [EGA] Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent • The morphism f is affine. • There exists an affine open covering S = ⋃ W_j such that each f^-1(W_j) is affine. • There exists a quasi-coherent sheaf of O_S-algebras A and an isomorphism X ≅ underlineSpec_S(A) of schemes over S. See Constructions, Section [Tag 01LQ] for notation. Moreover, in this case X = underlineSpec_S(f_*O_X).

nodes.title: Affine morphisms · Lemma 01SA
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. There is an anti-equivalence of categories Schemes affine over S longleftrightarrow quasi-coherent sheaves of O_S-algebras which associates to f : X → S the sheaf f_*O_X. Moreover, this equivalence is compatible with arbitrary base change.

nodes.title: Affine morphisms · Lemma 0H88
nodes.summary: [EGA] Let S be a scheme and let A be a quasi-coherent O_S-algebra. An A-module is quasi-coherent as an O_S-module if and only if it is quasi-coherent as an A-module.

nodes.title: Affine morphisms · Lemma 01SB
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be an affine morphism of schemes. Let A = f_*O_X. The functor F ↦ f_*F induces an equivalence of categories ( category of quasi-coherent O_X-modules ) → ( category of quasi-coherent A-modules ) Moreover, an A-module is quasi-coherent as an O_S-module if and only if it is quasi-coherent as an A-module.

nodes.title: Affine morphisms · Lemma 01SC
nodes.summary: The composition of affine morphisms is affine.

nodes.title: Affine morphisms · Lemma 01SD
nodes.summary: The base change of an affine morphism is affine.

nodes.title: Affine morphisms · Lemma 01SE
nodes.summary: A closed immersion is affine.

nodes.title: Affine morphisms · Lemma 01SF
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let L be an invertible O_X-module. Let s ∈ Γ(X, L). The inclusion morphism j : X_s → X is affine.

nodes.title: Affine morphisms · Lemma 01SG
nodes.summary: Suppose g : X → Y is a morphism of schemes over S. • If X is affine over S and Δ : Y → Y ×_S Y is affine, then g is affine. • If X is affine over S and Y is separated over S, then g is affine. • A morphism from an affine scheme to a scheme with affine diagonal is affine. • A morphism from an affine scheme to a separated scheme is affine.

nodes.title: Affine morphisms · Lemma 01SH
nodes.summary: A morphism between affine schemes is affine.

nodes.title: Affine morphisms · Lemma 01SI
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let A be an Artinian ring. Any morphism Spec(A) → S is affine.

nodes.title: Affine morphisms · Lemma 0C3A
nodes.summary: Let j : Y → X be an immersion of schemes. Assume there exists an open U ⊂ X with complement Z = X setminus U such that • U → X is affine, • j^-1(U) → U is affine, and • j(Y) ∩ Z is closed. Then j is affine. In particular, if X is affine, so is Y.

nodes.title: Families of ample invertible modules · Definition 0FXR
nodes.summary: [SGA6] Let X be a scheme. Let (L_i)_i ∈ I be a family of invertible O_X-modules. We say (L_i)_i ∈ I is an ample family of invertible modules on X if • X is quasi-compact, and • for every x ∈ X there exists an i ∈ I, an n ≥ 1, and s ∈ Γ(X, L_i^⊗ n) such that x ∈ X_s and X_s is affine.

nodes.title: Families of ample invertible modules · Lemma 0FXS
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme such that for every point x ∈ X there exists an invertible O_X-module L and a global section s ∈ Γ(X, L) such that x ∈ X_s and X_s is affine. Then the diagonal of X is an affine morphism.

nodes.title: Quasi-affine morphisms · Definition 01SK
nodes.summary: A morphism of schemes f : X → S is called quasi-affine if the inverse image of every affine open of S is a quasi-affine scheme.

nodes.title: Quasi-affine morphisms · Lemma 01SL
nodes.summary: A quasi-affine morphism is separated and quasi-compact.

nodes.title: Quasi-affine morphisms · Lemma 01SM
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent • The morphism f is quasi-affine. • There exists an affine open covering S = ⋃ W_j such that each f^-1(W_j) is quasi-affine. • There exists a quasi-coherent sheaf of O_S-algebras A and a quasi-compact open immersion xymatrix X ar[rr] ar[rd] & & underlineSpec_S(A) ar[dl] & S & over S. • Same as in (3) but with A = f_*O_X and the horizontal arrow the canonical morphism of Constructions, Lemma [Tag 01LY].

nodes.title: Quasi-affine morphisms · Lemma 01SN
nodes.summary: The composition of quasi-affine morphisms is quasi-affine.

nodes.title: Quasi-affine morphisms · Lemma 01SO
nodes.summary: The base change of a quasi-affine morphism is quasi-affine.

nodes.title: Quasi-affine morphisms · Lemma 02JR
nodes.summary: A quasi-compact immersion is quasi-affine.

nodes.title: Quasi-affine morphisms · Lemma 01SP
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be an affine scheme. A morphism f : X → S is quasi-affine if and only if it is quasi-compact. In particular any morphism from an affine scheme to a quasi-separated scheme is quasi-affine.

nodes.title: Quasi-affine morphisms · Lemma 054G
nodes.summary: Suppose g : X → Y is a morphism of schemes over S. If X is quasi-affine over S and Y is quasi-separated over S, then g is quasi-affine. In particular, any morphism from a quasi-affine scheme to a quasi-separated scheme is quasi-affine.

nodes.title: Types of morphisms defined by properties of ring maps · Definition 01SR
nodes.summary: Let P be a property of ring maps. • We say that P is local if the following hold: • For any ring map R → A, and any f ∈ R we have P(R → A) ⇒ P(R_f → A_f). • For any rings R, A, any f ∈ R, a∈ A, and any ring map R_f → A we have P(R_f → A) ⇒ P(R → A_a). • For any ring map R → A, and a_i ∈ A such that (a_1, …, a_n) = A then ∀ i, P(R → A_a_i) ⇒ P(R → A). • We say that P is stable under base change if for any ring maps R → A, R → R' we have P(R → A) ⇒ P(R' → R' ⊗_R A). • We…
