nodes.title: Types of morphisms defined by properties of ring maps · Definition 01SS
nodes.summary: Let P be a property of ring maps. Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. We say f is locally of type P if for any x ∈ X there exists an affine open neighbourhood U of x in X which maps into an affine open V ⊂ S such that the induced ring map O_S(V) → O_X(U) has property P.
nodes.section: Types of morphisms defined by properties of ring maps

nodes.title: Types of morphisms defined by properties of ring maps · Lemma 01ST
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let P be a property of ring maps. Let U be an affine open of X, and V an affine open of S such that f(U) ⊂ V. If f is locally of type P and P is local, then P(O_S(V) → O_X(U)) holds.
nodes.section: Types of morphisms defined by properties of ring maps

nodes.title: Types of morphisms defined by properties of ring maps · Lemma 01SU
nodes.summary: Let P be a local property of ring maps. Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent • The morphism f is locally of type P. • For every affine opens U ⊂ X, V ⊂ S with f(U) ⊂ V we have P(O_S(V) → O_X(U)). • There exists an open covering S = ⋃_j ∈ J V_j and open coverings f^-1(V_j) = ⋃_i ∈ I_j U_i such that each of the morphisms U_i → V_j, j∈ J, i∈ I_j is locally of type P. • There exists an affine open covering S = ⋃_j ∈ J V_j and affine open…
nodes.section: Types of morphisms defined by properties of ring maps

nodes.title: Types of morphisms defined by properties of ring maps · Lemma 01SV
nodes.summary: Let P be a property of ring maps. Assume P is local and stable under composition. The composition of morphisms locally of type P is locally of type P.
nodes.section: Types of morphisms defined by properties of ring maps

nodes.title: Types of morphisms defined by properties of ring maps · Lemma 01SW
nodes.summary: Let P be a property of ring maps. Assume P is local and stable under base change. The base change of a morphism locally of type P is locally of type P.
nodes.section: Types of morphisms defined by properties of ring maps

nodes.title: Types of morphisms defined by properties of ring maps · Lemma 01SX
nodes.summary: The following properties of a ring map R → A are local. • (Isomorphism on local rings.) For every prime q of A lying over p ⊂ R the ring map R → A induces an isomorphism R_ p → A_ q. • (Open immersion.) For every prime q of A there exists an f ∈ R, φ(f) not ∈ q such that the ring map φ : R → A induces an isomorphism R_f → A_f. • (Reduced fibres.) For every prime p of R the fibre ring A ⊗_R kappa( p) is reduced. • (Fibres of dimension at most n.) For every prime p of R the…
nodes.section: Types of morphisms defined by properties of ring maps

nodes.title: Types of morphisms defined by properties of ring maps · Lemma 01SY
nodes.summary: The following properties of ring maps are stable under base change. • (Isomorphism on local rings.) For every prime q of A lying over p ⊂ R the ring map R → A induces an isomorphism R_ p → A_ q. • (Open immersion.) For every prime q of A there exists an f ∈ R, φ(f) not ∈ q such that the ring map φ : R → A induces an isomorphism R_f → A_f. • Add more here as needed.
nodes.section: Types of morphisms defined by properties of ring maps

nodes.title: Types of morphisms defined by properties of ring maps · Lemma 01SZ
nodes.summary: The following properties of ring maps are stable under composition. • (Isomorphism on local rings.) For every prime q of A lying over p ⊂ R the ring map R → A induces an isomorphism R_ p → A_ q. • (Open immersion.) For every prime q of A there exists an f ∈ R, φ(f) not ∈ q such that the ring map φ : R → A induces an isomorphism R_f → A_f. • (Locally Noetherian on the target.) The ring map R → A has the property that A is Noetherian. • Add more here as needed.
nodes.section: Types of morphisms defined by properties of ring maps

nodes.title: Morphisms of finite type · Definition 01T1
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. • We say that f is of finite type at x ∈ X if there exists an affine open neighbourhood Spec(A) = U ⊂ X of x and an affine open Spec(R) = V ⊂ S with f(U) ⊂ V such that the induced ring map R → A is of finite type. • We say that f is locally of finite type if it is of finite type at every point of X. • We say that f is of finite type if it is locally of finite type and quasi-compact.

nodes.title: Morphisms of finite type · Lemma 01T2
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent • The morphism f is locally of finite type. • For all affine opens U ⊂ X, V ⊂ S with f(U) ⊂ V the ring map O_S(V) → O_X(U) is of finite type. • There exist an open covering S = ⋃_j ∈ J V_j and open coverings f^-1(V_j) = ⋃_i ∈ I_j U_i such that each of the morphisms U_i → V_j, j∈ J, i∈ I_j is locally of finite type. • There exist an affine open covering S = ⋃_j ∈ J V_j and affine open coverings f^-1(V_j)…

nodes.title: Morphisms of finite type · Lemma 01T3
nodes.summary: The composition of two morphisms which are locally of finite type is locally of finite type. The same is true for morphisms of finite type.

nodes.title: Morphisms of finite type · Lemma 01T4
nodes.summary: The base change of a morphism which is locally of finite type is locally of finite type. The same is true for morphisms of finite type.

nodes.title: Morphisms of finite type · Lemma 01T5
nodes.summary: A closed immersion is of finite type. An immersion is locally of finite type.

nodes.title: Morphisms of finite type · Lemma 01T6
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism. If S is (locally) Noetherian and f (locally) of finite type then X is (locally) Noetherian.

nodes.title: Morphisms of finite type · Lemma 01T7
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be locally of finite type with S locally Noetherian. Then f is quasi-separated.

nodes.title: Morphisms of finite type · Lemma 01T8
nodes.summary: Let X → Y be a morphism of schemes over a base scheme S. If X is locally of finite type over S, then X → Y is locally of finite type.

nodes.title: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes · Lemma 01TA
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let k be a field. Let f : Spec(k) → S be a morphism. The following are equivalent: • The morphism f is of finite type. • The morphism f is locally of finite type. • There exists an affine open U = Spec(R) of S such that f corresponds to a finite ring map R → k. • There exists an affine open U = Spec(R) of S such that the image of f consists of a closed point u in U and the field extension k/kappa(u) is finite.
nodes.section: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes

nodes.title: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes · Lemma 02HV
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let A be an Artinian local ring with residue field kappa. Let f : Spec(A) → S be a morphism of schemes. Then f is of finite type if and only if the composition Spec(kappa) → Spec(A) → S is of finite type.
nodes.section: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes

nodes.title: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes · Definition 02J1
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let us say that a point s of S is a finite type point if the canonical morphism Spec(kappa(s)) → S is of finite type. We denote S_ft-pts the set of finite type points of S.
nodes.section: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes

nodes.title: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes · Lemma 02J2
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. We have S_ft-pts = ⋃_U ⊂ S open U_0 where U_0 is the set of closed points of U. Here we may let U range over all opens or over all affine opens of S.
nodes.section: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes

nodes.title: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes · Lemma 02J3
nodes.summary: Let f : T → S be a morphism of schemes. If f is locally of finite type, then f(T_ft-pts) ⊂ S_ft-pts.
nodes.section: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes

nodes.title: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes · Lemma 06EB
nodes.summary: Let f : T → S be a morphism of schemes. If f is locally of finite type and surjective, then f(T_ft-pts) = S_ft-pts.
nodes.section: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes

nodes.title: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes · Lemma 02J4
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. For any locally closed subset T ⊂ S we have T not = ∅ ⇒ T ∩ S_ft-pts not = ∅. In particular, for any closed subset T ⊂ S we see that T ∩ S_ft-pts is dense in T.
nodes.section: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes

nodes.title: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes · Lemma 01TB
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. The following are equivalent: • the scheme S is Jacobson, • S_ft-pts is the set of closed points of S, • for all T → S locally of finite type closed points map to closed points, and • for all T → S locally of finite type closed points t ∈ T map to closed points s ∈ S with kappa(s) ⊂ kappa(t) finite.
nodes.section: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes

nodes.title: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes · Lemma 02J5
nodes.summary: Let S be a Jacobson scheme. Any scheme locally of finite type over S is Jacobson.
nodes.section: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes

nodes.title: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes · Lemma 02J6
nodes.summary: The following types of schemes are Jacobson. • Any scheme locally of finite type over a field. • Any scheme locally of finite type over Z. • Any scheme locally of finite type over a 1-dimensional Noetherian domain with infinitely many primes. • A scheme of the form Spec(R) setminus ( m) where (R, m) is a Noetherian local ring. Also any scheme locally of finite type over it.
nodes.section: Points of finite type and Jacobson schemes

nodes.title: Universally catenary schemes · Definition 02J8
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Assume S is locally Noetherian. We say S is universally catenary if for every morphism X → S locally of finite type the scheme X is catenary.

nodes.title: Universally catenary schemes · Lemma 02J9
nodes.summary: Let S be a locally Noetherian scheme. The following are equivalent • S is universally catenary, • there exists an open covering of S all of whose members are universally catenary schemes, • for every affine open Spec(R) = U ⊂ S the ring R is universally catenary, and • there exists an affine open covering S = ⋃ U_i such that each U_i is the spectrum of a universally catenary ring. Moreover, in this case any scheme locally of finite type over S is universally catenary as well.

nodes.title: Universally catenary schemes · Lemma 02JA
nodes.summary: Let S be a locally Noetherian scheme. The following are equivalent: • S is universally catenary, and • all local rings O_S, s of S are universally catenary.

nodes.title: Universally catenary schemes · Lemma 0G42
nodes.summary: Let S be a locally Noetherian scheme. Then S is universally catenary if and only if the irreducible components of S are universally catenary.

nodes.title: Universally catenary schemes · Lemma 02JB
nodes.summary: The following types of schemes are universally catenary. • Any scheme locally of finite type over a field. • Any scheme locally of finite type over a Cohen-Macaulay scheme. • Any scheme locally of finite type over Z. • Any scheme locally of finite type over a 1-dimensional Noetherian domain. • And so on.

nodes.title: Nagata schemes, reprise · Lemma 035A
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism. If S is Nagata and f locally of finite type then X is Nagata. If S is universally Japanese and f locally of finite type then X is universally Japanese.

nodes.title: Nagata schemes, reprise · Lemma 035B
nodes.summary: The following types of schemes are Nagata. • Any scheme locally of finite type over a field. • Any scheme locally of finite type over a Noetherian complete local ring. • Any scheme locally of finite type over Z. • Any scheme locally of finite type over a Dedekind ring of characteristic zero. • And so on.

nodes.title: The singular locus, reprise · Definition 07R3
nodes.summary: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme. We say X is J-2 if for every morphism Y → X which is locally of finite type the regular locus Reg(Y) is open in Y.

nodes.title: The singular locus, reprise · Lemma 07R4
nodes.summary: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme. The following are equivalent • X is J-2, • there exists an open covering of X all of whose members are J-2 schemes, • for every affine open Spec(R) = U ⊂ X the ring R is J-2, and • there exists an affine open covering S = ⋃ U_i such that each O(U_i) is J-2 for all i. Moreover, in this case any scheme locally of finite type over X is J-2 as well.

nodes.title: The singular locus, reprise · Lemma 07R5
nodes.summary: The following types of schemes are J-2. • Any scheme locally of finite type over a field. • Any scheme locally of finite type over a Noetherian complete local ring. • Any scheme locally of finite type over Z. • Any scheme locally of finite type over a Noetherian local ring of dimension 1. • Any scheme locally of finite type over a Nagata ring of dimension 1. • Any scheme locally of finite type over a Dedekind ring of characteristic zero. • And so on.

nodes.title: Excellent schemes · Definition 0HA7
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. • We say X is quasi-excellent if for every x ∈ X there exists an affine open neighbourhood x ∈ U ⊂ X such that the ring O_X(U) is quasi-excellent (see More on Algebra, Definition [Tag 07QT]). • We say X is excellent if for every x ∈ X there exists an affine open neighbourhood x ∈ U ⊂ X such that the ring O_X(U) is excellent (see More on Algebra, Definition [Tag 07QT]).

nodes.title: Excellent schemes · Lemma 0HA8
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. The following are equivalent • X is quasi-excellent, and • X is a G-scheme and J-2.

nodes.title: Excellent schemes · Lemma 0HA9
nodes.summary: A quasi-excellent scheme is Nagata.

nodes.title: Excellent schemes · Lemma 0HAA
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. The following are equivalent • X is excellent, and • X is quasi-excellent and universally catenary.

nodes.title: Excellent schemes · Lemma 0HAB
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. The following are equivalent: • The scheme X is (quasi-)excellent. • For every affine open U ⊂ X the ring O_X(U) is (quasi-)excellent. • There exists an affine open covering X = ⋃ U_i such that each O_X(U_i) is (quasi-)excellent. • There exists an open covering X = ⋃ X_j such that each open subscheme X_j is (quasi-)excellent. Moreover, if X is (quasi-)excellent then every open subscheme is (quasi-)excellent.

nodes.title: Excellent schemes · Lemma 0HAC
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism. If S is (quasi-)excellent and f locally of finite type then X is (quasi-)excellent.

nodes.title: Excellent schemes · Lemma 0HAD
nodes.summary: The following types of schemes are excellent. • Any scheme locally of finite type over a field. • Any scheme locally of finite type over a Noetherian complete local ring. • Any scheme locally of finite type over Z. • Any scheme locally of finite type over a Dedekind ring of characteristic zero.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite morphisms · Definition 01TD
nodes.summary: [EGA] Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. • We say that f is quasi-finite at a point x ∈ X if there exist an affine neighbourhood Spec(A) = U ⊂ X of x and an affine open Spec(R) = V ⊂ S such that f(U) ⊂ V, the ring map R → A is of finite type, and R → A is quasi-finite at the prime of A corresponding to x (see above). • We say f is locally quasi-finite if f is quasi-finite at every point x of X. • We say that f is quasi-finite if f is of finite type and every point x…

nodes.title: Quasi-finite morphisms · Lemma 01TE
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let x ∈ X be a point. Set s = f(x). If kappa(x)/kappa(s) is an algebraic field extension, then • x is a closed point of its fibre, and • if in addition s is a closed point of S, then x is a closed point of X.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite morphisms · Lemma 01TF
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let x ∈ X be a point. Set s = f(x). Assume f is locally of finite type. Then x is a closed point of its fibre if and only if kappa(x)/kappa(s) is a finite field extension.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite morphisms · Lemma 053M
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes which is locally of finite type. Let g : S' → S be any morphism. Denote f' : X' → S' the base change. If x' ∈ X' maps to a point x ∈ X which is closed in X_f(x) then x' is closed in X'_f'(x').

nodes.title: Quasi-finite morphisms · Lemma 01TG
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let x ∈ X be a point. Set s = f(x). If f is quasi-finite at x, then the residue field extension kappa(x)/kappa(s) is finite.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite morphisms · Lemma 01TH
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let x ∈ X be a point. Set s = f(x). Let X_s be the fibre of f at s. Assume f is locally of finite type. The following are equivalent: • The morphism f is quasi-finite at x. • The point x is isolated in X_s. • The point x is closed in X_s and there is no point x' ∈ X_s, x' not = x which specializes to x. • For any pair of affine opens Spec(A) = U ⊂ X, Spec(R) = V ⊂ S with f(U) ⊂ V and x ∈ U corresponding to q ⊂ A the ring map R → A…

nodes.title: Quasi-finite morphisms · Lemma 02NG
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let s ∈ S. Assume that • f is locally of finite type, and • f^-1((s)) is a finite set. Then X_s is a finite discrete topological space, and f is quasi-finite at each point of X lying over s.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite morphisms · Lemma 06RT
nodes.summary: Finite type morphisms with discrete fibers are quasi-finite. Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Assume f is locally of finite type. Then the following are equivalent • f is locally quasi-finite, • for every s ∈ S the fibre X_s is a discrete topological space, and • for every morphism Spec(k) → S where k is a field the base change X_k has an underlying discrete topological space.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite morphisms · Lemma 01TJ
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Then f is quasi-finite if and only if f is locally quasi-finite and quasi-compact.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite morphisms · Lemma 02NH
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent: • f is quasi-finite, and • f is locally of finite type, quasi-compact, and has finite fibres.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite morphisms · Lemma 01TK
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent • The morphism f is locally quasi-finite. • For every pair of affine opens U ⊂ X, V ⊂ S with f(U) ⊂ V the ring map O_S(V) → O_X(U) is quasi-finite. • There exists an open covering S = ⋃_j ∈ J V_j and open coverings f^-1(V_j) = ⋃_i ∈ I_j U_i such that each of the morphisms U_i → V_j, j∈ J, i∈ I_j is locally quasi-finite. • There exists an affine open covering S = ⋃_j ∈ J V_j and affine open coverings…

nodes.title: Quasi-finite morphisms · Lemma 01TL
nodes.summary: The composition of two morphisms which are locally quasi-finite is locally quasi-finite. The same is true for quasi-finite morphisms.

nodes.summary: (Locally) quasi-finite morphisms are stable under base change. Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let g : S' → S be a morphism of schemes. Denote f' : X' → S' the base change of f by g and denote g' : X' → X the projection. Assume X is locally of finite type over S. • Let U ⊂ X (resp. U' ⊂ X') be the set of points where f (resp. f') is quasi-finite. Then U' = U ×_S S' = (g')^-1(U). • The base change of a locally quasi-finite morphism is locally quasi-finite. • The…

nodes.title: Quasi-finite morphisms · Lemma 0AAY
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes of finite type. Let s ∈ S. There are at most finitely many points of X lying over s at which f is quasi-finite.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite morphisms · Lemma 0CT8
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes. If f is locally of finite type and a monomorphism, then f is separated and locally quasi-finite.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite morphisms · Lemma 01TN
nodes.summary: Any immersion is locally quasi-finite.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite morphisms · Lemma 03WR
nodes.summary: Let X → Y be a morphism of schemes over a base scheme S. Let x ∈ X. If X → S is quasi-finite at x, then X → Y is quasi-finite at x. If X is locally quasi-finite over S, then X → Y is locally quasi-finite.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite morphisms · Lemma 0GWS
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y and g : Y → S be morphisms of schemes. If f is surjective, g ∘ f locally quasi-finite, and g locally of finite type, then g : Y → S is locally quasi-finite.

nodes.title: Morphisms of finite presentation · Definition 01TP
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. • We say that f is of finite presentation at x ∈ X if there exists an affine open neighbourhood Spec(A) = U ⊂ X of x and affine open Spec(R) = V ⊂ S with f(U) ⊂ V such that the induced ring map R → A is of finite presentation. • We say that f is locally of finite presentation if it is of finite presentation at every point of X. • We say that f is of finite presentation if it is locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and…

The following are equivalent • The morphism f is locally of finite presentation. • For every affine opens U ⊂ X, V ⊂ S with f(U) ⊂ V the ring map O_S(V) → O_X(U) is of finite presentation. • There exist an open covering S = ⋃_j ∈ J V_j and open coverings f^-1(V_j) = ⋃_i ∈ I_j U_i such that each of the morphisms U_i → V_j, j∈ J, i∈ I_j is locally of finite presentation. • There exist an affine open covering S = ⋃_j ∈ J V_j and affine…

nodes.title: Morphisms of finite presentation · Lemma 01TR
nodes.summary: The composition of two morphisms which are locally of finite presentation is locally of finite presentation. The same is true for morphisms of finite presentation.

nodes.title: Morphisms of finite presentation · Lemma 01TS
nodes.summary: The base change of a morphism which is locally of finite presentation is locally of finite presentation. The same is true for morphisms of finite presentation.

nodes.title: Morphisms of finite presentation · Lemma 01TT
nodes.summary: Any open immersion is locally of finite presentation.

nodes.title: Morphisms of finite presentation · Lemma 01TU
nodes.summary: Any open immersion is of finite presentation if and only if it is quasi-compact.

nodes.title: Morphisms of finite presentation · Lemma 01TV
nodes.summary: Closed immersions of finite presentation correspond to quasi-coherent sheaves of ideals of finite type. A closed immersion i : Z → X is of finite presentation if and only if the associated quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals I = Ker(O_X → i_*O_Z) is of finite type (as an O_X-module).

nodes.title: Morphisms of finite presentation · Lemma 01TW
nodes.summary: A morphism which is locally of finite presentation is locally of finite type. A morphism of finite presentation is of finite type.

nodes.title: Morphisms of finite presentation · Lemma 01TX
nodes.summary: Over a locally Noetherian base, finite type is finite presentation. Let f : X → S be a morphism. • If S is locally Noetherian and f locally of finite type then f is locally of finite presentation. • If S is locally Noetherian and f of finite type then f is of finite presentation.

nodes.title: Morphisms of finite presentation · Lemma 01TY
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. If X is of finite presentation over S, then X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

nodes.title: Morphisms of finite presentation · Lemma 02FV
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes over S. • If X is locally of finite presentation over S and Y is locally of finite type over S, then f is locally of finite presentation. • If X is of finite presentation over S and Y is quasi-separated and locally of finite type over S, then f is of finite presentation.

nodes.title: Morphisms of finite presentation · Lemma 0818
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes with diagonal Δ : X → X ×_Y X. If f is locally of finite type then Δ is locally of finite presentation. If f is quasi-separated and locally of finite type, then Δ is of finite presentation.

nodes.title: Constructible sets · Lemma 054I
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes. Let E ⊂ Y be a subset. If E is (locally) constructible in Y, then f^-1(E) is (locally) constructible in X.

nodes.title: Constructible sets · Lemma 054J
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes. Assume • f is quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation, and • Y is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then the image of every constructible subset of X is constructible in Y.

nodes.title: Chevalley's Theorem · Theorem 054K
nodes.summary: [EGA] Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes. Assume f is quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation. Then the image of every locally constructible subset is locally constructible.

nodes.title: Constructible sets · Lemma 05LW
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let x ∈ X. Let E ⊂ X be a locally constructible subset. If (x' mid x' leadsto x) ⊂ E, then E contains an open neighbourhood of x.

nodes.title: Open morphisms · Definition 01U0
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism. • We say f is open if the map on underlying topological spaces is open. • We say f is universally open if for any morphism of schemes S' → S the base change f' : X_S' → S' is open.

nodes.title: Open morphisms · Lemma 01U1
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism. • If f is locally of finite presentation and generalizations lift along f, then f is open. • If f is locally of finite presentation and generalizations lift along every base change of f, then f is universally open.

nodes.title: Open morphisms · Lemma 02V2
nodes.summary: A composition of (universally) open morphisms is (universally) open.

nodes.title: Open morphisms · Lemma 0383
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let X be a scheme over k. The structure morphism X → Spec(k) is universally open.

nodes.title: Open morphisms · Lemma 040F
nodes.summary: Follows from the implication (a) ⇒ (b) in [EGA] Let φ : X → Y be a morphism of schemes. If φ is open, then φ is generizing (i.e., generalizations lift along φ). If φ is universally open, then φ is universally generizing.

nodes.title: Open morphisms · Lemma 04ZE
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes. Let g : Y' → Y be open and surjective such that the base change f' : X' → Y' is quasi-compact. Then f is quasi-compact.

nodes.title: Submersive morphisms · Definition 040H
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes. • We say f is submersive if the continuous map of underlying topological spaces is submersive, see Topology, Definition [Tag 0406]. • We say f is universally submersive if for every morphism of schemes Y' → Y the base change Y' ×_Y X → Y' is submersive.

nodes.title: Submersive morphisms · Lemma 0CES
nodes.summary: The base change of a universally submersive morphism of schemes by any morphism of schemes is universally submersive.

nodes.title: Submersive morphisms · Lemma 0CET
nodes.summary: The composition of a pair of (universally) submersive morphisms of schemes is (universally) submersive.

nodes.title: Flat morphisms · Definition 01U3
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let F be a quasi-coherent sheaf of O_X-modules. • We say f is flat at a point x ∈ X if the local ring O_X, x is flat over the local ring O_S, f(x). • We say that F is flat over S at a point x ∈ X if the stalk F_x is a flat O_S, f(x)-module. • We say f is flat if f is flat at every point of X. • We say that F is flat over S if F is flat over S at every point x of X.

nodes.title: Flat morphisms · Lemma 01U4
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let F be a quasi-coherent sheaf of O_X-modules. The following are equivalent • The sheaf F is flat over S. • For every affine opens U ⊂ X, V ⊂ S with f(U) ⊂ V the O_S(V)-module F(U) is flat. • There exists an open covering S = ⋃_j ∈ J V_j and open coverings f^-1(V_j) = ⋃_i ∈ I_j U_i such that each of the modules F|_U_i is flat over V_j, for all j∈ J, i∈ I_j. • There exists an affine open covering S = ⋃_j ∈ J V_j and affine open…

nodes.title: Flat morphisms · Lemma 01U5
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent • The morphism f is flat. • For every affine opens U ⊂ X, V ⊂ S with f(U) ⊂ V the ring map O_S(V) → O_X(U) is flat. • There exists an open covering S = ⋃_j ∈ J V_j and open coverings f^-1(V_j) = ⋃_i ∈ I_j U_i such that each of the morphisms U_i → V_j, j∈ J, i∈ I_j is flat. • There exists an affine open covering S = ⋃_j ∈ J V_j and affine open coverings f^-1(V_j) = ⋃_i ∈ I_j U_i such that O_S(V_j) →…

nodes.title: Flat morphisms · Lemma 0FLM
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be an affine morphism of schemes over a base scheme S. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. Then F is flat over S if and only if f_*F is flat over S.

nodes.title: Flat morphisms · Lemma 01U6
nodes.summary: Let X → Y → Z be morphisms of schemes. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. Let x ∈ X with image y in Y. If F is flat over Y at x, and Y is flat over Z at y, then F is flat over Z at x.

nodes.title: Flat morphisms · Lemma 01U7
nodes.summary: The composition of flat morphisms is flat.

nodes.title: Flat morphisms · Lemma 01U8
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let F be a quasi-coherent sheaf of O_X-modules. Let g : S' → S be a morphism of schemes. Denote g' : X' = X_S' → X the projection. Let x' ∈ X' be a point with image x = g'(x') ∈ X. If F is flat over S at x, then (g')^*F is flat over S' at x'. In particular, if F is flat over S, then (g')^*F is flat over S'.

nodes.title: Flat morphisms · Lemma 01U9
nodes.summary: The base change of a flat morphism is flat.

nodes.title: Flat morphisms · Lemma 03HV
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a flat morphism of schemes. Then generalizations lift along f, see Topology, Definition [Tag 0063].

nodes.title: Flat morphisms · Lemma 01UA
nodes.summary: A flat morphism locally of finite presentation is universally open.

nodes.title: Flat morphisms · Lemma 0CVT
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. Assume f locally finite presentation, F of finite type, X = Supp(F), and F flat over Y. Then f is universally open.

nodes.title: Flat morphisms · Lemma 02JY
nodes.summary: [SGA1] and [EGA] Let f : X → Y be a quasi-compact, surjective, flat morphism. A subset T ⊂ Y is open (resp. closed) if and only f^-1(T) is open (resp. closed). In other words, f is a submersive morphism.

nodes.title: Flat morphisms · Lemma 02JZ
nodes.summary: Let h : X → Y be a morphism of schemes over S. Let G be a quasi-coherent sheaf on Y. Let x ∈ X with y = h(x) ∈ Y. If h is flat at x, then G flat over S at y ⇔ h^*G flat over S at x. In particular: If h is surjective and flat, then G is flat over S, if and only if h^*G is flat over S. If h is surjective and flat, and X is flat over S, then Y is flat over S.

nodes.title: Flat morphisms · Lemma 07T9
nodes.summary: Let f : Y → X be a morphism of schemes. Let F be a finite type quasi-coherent O_X-module with scheme theoretic support Z ⊂ X. If f is flat, then f^-1(Z) is the scheme theoretic support of f^*F.

nodes.title: Flat morphisms · Lemma 081H
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a flat morphism of schemes. Let V ⊂ Y be a retrocompact open which is scheme theoretically dense. Then f^-1V is scheme theoretically dense in X.

nodes.title: Flat morphisms · Lemma 081I
nodes.summary: Taking scheme theoretic images commutes with flat base change in the quasi-compact case Let f : X → Y be a flat morphism of schemes. Let g : V → Y be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes. Let Z ⊂ Y be the scheme theoretic image of g and let Z' ⊂ X be the scheme theoretic image of the base change V ×_Y X → X. Then Z' = f^-1Z.

nodes.title: Flat closed immersions · Lemma 04PW
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. The rule which associates to a closed subscheme of X its underlying closed subset defines a bijection ( closed subschemes Z ⊂ X such that Z → X is flat ) ↔ ( closed subsets Z ⊂ X closed under generalizations ) If Z ⊂ X is such a closed subscheme, every morphism of schemes g : Y → X with g(Y) ⊂ Z set theoretically factors (scheme theoretically) through Z.

nodes.title: Flat closed immersions · Lemma 0819
nodes.summary: A flat closed immersion of finite presentation is the open immersion of an open and closed subscheme.

nodes.title: Flat closed immersions · Definition 04PX
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let T ⊂ X be a connected component. The canonical scheme structure on T is the unique scheme structure on T such that the closed immersion T → X is flat, see Lemma [Tag 04PW].

nodes.title: Flat closed immersions · Lemma 053N
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. The following are equivalent • every finite flat quasi-coherent O_X-module is finite locally free, and • every closed subset Z ⊂ X which is closed under generalizations is open.

nodes.title: Generic flatness · Proposition 052A
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let F be a quasi-coherent sheaf of O_X-modules. Assume • S is integral, • f is of finite type, and • F is a finite type O_X-module. Then there exists an open dense subscheme U ⊂ S such that X_U → U is flat and of finite presentation and such that F|_X_U is flat over U and of finite presentation over O_X_U.

nodes.title: Generic flatness, reduced case · Proposition 052B
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let F be a quasi-coherent sheaf of O_X-modules. Assume • S is reduced, • f is of finite type, and • F is a finite type O_X-module. Then there exists an open dense subscheme U ⊂ S such that X_U → U is flat and of finite presentation and such that F|_X_U is flat over U and of finite presentation over O_X_U.

nodes.title: Morphisms and dimensions of fibres · Lemma 02FX
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let x ∈ X and set s = f(x). Assume f is locally of finite type. Then dim_x(X_s) = dim(O_X_s, x) + trdeg_kappa(s)(kappa(x)).

nodes.title: Morphisms and dimensions of fibres · Lemma 02JS
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y and g : Y → S be morphisms of schemes. Let x ∈ X and set y = f(x), s = g(y). Assume f and g locally of finite type. Then dim_x(X_s) ≤ dim_x(X_y) + dim_y(Y_s). Moreover, equality holds if O_X_s, x is flat over O_Y_s, y, which holds for example if O_X, x is flat over O_Y, y.

nodes.title: Morphisms and dimensions of fibres · Lemma 02FY
nodes.summary: Let xymatrix X' ar[r]_g' ar[d]_f' & X ar[d]^f S' ar[r]^g & S be a fibre product diagram of schemes. Assume f locally of finite type. Suppose that x' ∈ X', x = g'(x'), s' = f'(x') and s = g(s') = f(x). Then • dim_x(X_s) = dim_x'(X'_s'), • if F is the fibre of the morphism X'_s' → X_s over x, then dim(O_F, x') = dim(O_X'_s', x') - dim(O_X_s, x) = trdeg_kappa(s)(kappa(x)) - trdeg_kappa(s')(kappa(x')) In particular dim(O_X'_s', x') ≥ dim(O_X_s, x) and trdeg_kappa(s)(kappa(x))…

nodes.title: Morphisms and dimensions of fibres · Lemma 02FZ
nodes.summary: [EGA] Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let n ≥ 0. Assume f is locally of finite type. The set U_n = (x ∈ X mid dim_x X_f(x) ≤ n) is open in X.

nodes.title: Morphisms and dimensions of fibres · Lemma 0A3V
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of finite type with Y quasi-compact. Then the dimension of the fibres of f is bounded.

nodes.title: Morphisms and dimensions of fibres · Lemma 02G0
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let n ≥ 0. Assume f is locally of finite presentation. The open U_n = (x ∈ X mid dim_x X_f(x) ≤ n) of Lemma [Tag 02FZ] is retrocompact in X. (See Topology, Definition [Tag 005A].)

nodes.title: Morphisms and dimensions of fibres · Lemma 06RU
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let x leadsto x' be a nontrivial specialization of points in X lying over the same point s ∈ S. Assume f is locally of finite type. Then • dim_x(X_s) ≤ dim_x'(X_s), • dim(O_X_s, x) < dim(O_X_s, x'), and • trdeg_kappa(s)(kappa(x)) > trdeg_kappa(s)(kappa(x')).

nodes.title: Morphisms of given relative dimension · Definition 02NJ
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Assume f is locally of finite type. • We say f is of relative dimension ≤ d at x if dim_x(X_f(x)) ≤ d. • We say f is of relative dimension ≤ d if dim_x(X_f(x)) ≤ d for all x ∈ X. • We say f is of relative dimension d if all nonempty fibres X_s are equidimensional of dimension d.

nodes.title: Morphisms of given relative dimension · Lemma 02NK
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes which is locally of finite type. If f has relative dimension d, then so does any base change of f. Same for relative dimension ≤ d.

nodes.title: Morphisms of given relative dimension · Lemma 02NL
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y, g : Y → Z be locally of finite type. If f has relative dimension ≤ d and g has relative dimension ≤ e then g ∘ f has relative dimension ≤ d + e. If • f has relative dimension d, • g has relative dimension e, and • f is flat, then g ∘ f has relative dimension d + e.

nodes.title: Morphisms of given relative dimension · Lemma 02NM
nodes.summary: Cohen-Macaulay morphisms decompose into clopens of pure relative dimension Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Assume that • f is flat, • f is locally of finite presentation, and • for all s ∈ S the fibre X_s is Cohen-Macaulay (Properties, Definition [Tag 02IO]) Then there exist open and closed subschemes X_d ⊂ X such that X = coprod_d ≥ 0 X_d and f|_X_d : X_d → S has relative dimension d.

nodes.title: Morphisms of given relative dimension · Lemma 0397
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Assume f is locally of finite type. Let x ∈ X with s = f(x). Then f is quasi-finite at x if and only if dim_x(X_s) = 0. In particular, f is locally quasi-finite if and only if f has relative dimension 0.

nodes.title: Morphisms of given relative dimension · Lemma 0AFE
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of locally Noetherian schemes which is flat, locally of finite type and of relative dimension d. For every point x in X with image y in Y we have dim_x(X) = dim_y(Y) + d.

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Definition 01UC
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. • We say that f is syntomic at x ∈ X if there exists an affine open neighbourhood Spec(A) = U ⊂ X of x and affine open Spec(R) = V ⊂ S with f(U) ⊂ V such that the induced ring map R → A is syntomic. • We say that f is syntomic if it is syntomic at every point of X. • If S = Spec(k) and f is syntomic, then we say that X is a local complete intersection over k. • A morphism of affine schemes f : X → S is called standard syntomic if…

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Lemma 01UD
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent • The morphism f is syntomic. • For every affine opens U ⊂ X, V ⊂ S with f(U) ⊂ V the ring map O_S(V) → O_X(U) is syntomic. • There exists an open covering S = ⋃_j ∈ J V_j and open coverings f^-1(V_j) = ⋃_i ∈ I_j U_i such that each of the morphisms U_i → V_j, j∈ J, i∈ I_j is syntomic. • There exists an affine open covering S = ⋃_j ∈ J V_j and affine open coverings f^-1(V_j) = ⋃_i ∈ I_j U_i such that the…

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Lemma 01UH
nodes.summary: The composition of two morphisms which are syntomic is syntomic.

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Lemma 01UI
nodes.summary: The base change of a morphism which is syntomic is syntomic.

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Lemma 01UJ
nodes.summary: Any open immersion is syntomic.

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Lemma 01UK
nodes.summary: A syntomic morphism is locally of finite presentation.

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Lemma 01UL
nodes.summary: A syntomic morphism is flat.

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Lemma 056F
nodes.summary: A syntomic morphism is universally open.

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Lemma 01UG
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let X be a scheme locally of finite type over k. The following are equivalent: • X is a local complete intersection over k, • for every x ∈ X there exists an affine open U = Spec(R) ⊂ X neighbourhood of x such that R ≅ k[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c) is a global complete intersection over k, and • for every x ∈ X the local ring O_X, x is a complete intersection over k.

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Lemma 01UE
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let x ∈ X be a point with image s = f(x). Let V ⊂ S be an affine open neighbourhood of s. The following are equivalent • The morphism f is syntomic at x. • There exist an affine open U ⊂ X with x ∈ U and f(U) ⊂ V such that f|_U : U → V is standard syntomic. • The morphism f is of finite presentation at x, the local ring map O_S, s → O_X, x is flat and O_X, x/ m_s O_X, x is a complete intersection over kappa(s) (see Algebra,…

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Lemma 01UF
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. If f is flat, locally of finite presentation, and all fibres X_s are local complete intersections, then f is syntomic.

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Lemma 02V3
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Assume f locally of finite type. Formation of the set T = (x ∈ X mid O_X_f(x), x is a complete intersection over kappa(f(x))) commutes with arbitrary base change: For any morphism g : S' → S, consider the base change f' : X' → S' of f and the projection g' : X' → X. Then the corresponding set T' for the morphism f' is equal to T' = (g')^-1(T). In particular, if f is assumed flat, and locally of finite presentation then the same…

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Lemma 02K0
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Let R → A = R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c) be a relative global complete intersection. Set S = Spec(R) and X = Spec(A). Consider the morphism f : X → S associated to the ring map R → A. The function x ↦ dim_x(X_f(x)) is constant with value n - c.

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Lemma 02K1
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a syntomic morphism. The function x ↦ dim_x(X_f(x)) is locally constant on X.

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Definition 02K2
nodes.summary: Let d ≥ 0 be an integer. We say a morphism of schemes f : X → S is syntomic of relative dimension d if f is syntomic and the function dim_x(X_f(x)) = d for all x ∈ X.

nodes.title: Syntomic morphisms · Lemma 02K3
nodes.summary: Let xymatrix X ar[rr]_f ar[rd]_p & & Y ar[dl]^q & S be a commutative diagram of morphisms of schemes. Assume that • f is surjective and syntomic, • p is syntomic, and • q is locally of finite presentation. Then q is syntomic.

nodes.title: Conormal sheaf of an immersion · Definition 01R2
nodes.summary: Let i : Z → X be an immersion. The conormal sheaf C_Z/X of Z in X or the conormal sheaf of i is the quasi-coherent O_Z-module I/I^2 described above.

nodes.title: Conormal sheaf of an immersion · Lemma 01R3
nodes.summary: Let i : Z → X be an immersion. The conormal sheaf of i has the following properties: • Let U ⊂ X be any open subscheme such that i factors as Z xrightarrowi' U → X where i' is a closed immersion. Let I = Ker((i')^sharp) ⊂ O_U. Then C_Z/X = (i')^*I and i'_*C_Z/X = I/I^2 • For any affine open Spec(R) = U ⊂ X such that Z ∩ U = Spec(R/I) there is a canonical isomorphism Γ(Z ∩ U, C_Z/X) = I/I^2.

nodes.title: Conormal sheaf of an immersion · Lemma 01R4
nodes.summary: Let xymatrix Z ar[r]_i ar[d]_f & X ar[d]^g Z' ar[r]^i' & X' be a commutative diagram in the category of schemes. Assume i, i' immersions. There is a canonical map of O_Z-modules f^*C_Z'/X' → C_Z/X characterized by the following property: For every pair of affine opens (Spec(R) = U ⊂ X, Spec(R') = U' ⊂ X') with g(U) ⊂ U' such that Z ∩ U = Spec(R/I) and Z' ∩ U' = Spec(R'/I') the induced map Γ(Z' ∩ U', C_Z'/X') = I'/I'^2 → I/I^2 = Γ(Z ∩ U, C_Z/X) is the one induced by the…

nodes.title: Conormal sheaf of an immersion · Lemma 0473
nodes.summary: Let xymatrix Z ar[r]_i ar[d]_f & X ar[d]^g Z' ar[r]^i' & X' be a fibre product diagram in the category of schemes with i, i' immersions. Then the canonical map f^*C_Z'/X' → C_Z/X of Lemma [Tag 01R4] is surjective. If g is flat, then it is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Conormal sheaf of an immersion · Lemma 062S
nodes.summary: Let Z → Y → X be immersions of schemes. Then there is a canonical exact sequence i^*C_Y/X → C_Z/X → C_Z/Y → 0 where the maps come from Lemma [Tag 01R4] and i : Z → Y is the first morphism.

nodes.title: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism · Definition 01UQ
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. The sheaf of differentials Ω_X/S of X over S is the sheaf of differentials of f viewed as a morphism of ringed spaces (Modules, Definition [Tag 08RT]) equipped with its universal S-derivation d_X/S : O_X → Ω_X/S.
nodes.section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism

nodes.title: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism · Lemma 01UR
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. The map Hom_O_X(Ω_X/S, F) → Der_S(O_X, F), α ↦ α ∘ d_X/S is an isomorphism of functors Mod(O_X) → Sets.
nodes.section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism

nodes.title: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism · Lemma 01US
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let U ⊂ X, V ⊂ S be open subschemes such that f(U) ⊂ V. Then there is a unique isomorphism Ω_X/S|_U = Ω_U/V of O_U-modules such that d_X/S|_U = d_U/V.
nodes.section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism

nodes.title: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism · Lemma 01UO
nodes.summary: Let R → A be a ring map. Let F be a sheaf of O_X-modules on X = Spec(A). Set S = Spec(R). The rule which associates to an S-derivation on F its action on global sections defines a bijection between the set of S-derivations of F and the set of R-derivations on M = Γ(X, F).
nodes.section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism

nodes.title: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism · Lemma 01UT
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. For any pair of affine opens Spec(A) = U ⊂ X, Spec(R) = V ⊂ S with f(U) ⊂ V there is a unique isomorphism Γ(U, Ω_X/S) = Ω_A/R. compatible with d_X/S and d : A → Ω_A/R.
nodes.section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism

nodes.title: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism · Lemma 08S2
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. There is a canonical isomorphism between Ω_X/S and the conormal sheaf of the diagonal morphism Δ_X/S : X → X ×_S X.
nodes.section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism

nodes.title: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism · Lemma 01UV
nodes.summary: Let xymatrix X' ar[d] ar[r]_f & X ar[d] S' ar[r] & S be a commutative diagram of schemes. The canonical map O_X → f_*O_X' composed with the map f_*d_X'/S' : f_*O_X' → f_*Ω_X'/S' is a S-derivation. Hence we obtain a canonical map of O_X-modules Ω_X/S → f_*Ω_X'/S', and by adjointness of f_* and f^* a canonical O_X'-module homomorphism c_f : f^*Ω_X/S → Ω_X'/S'. It is uniquely characterized by the property that f^*d_X/S(h) maps to d_X'/S'(f^* h) for any local section h of O_X.
nodes.section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism

nodes.title: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism · Lemma 01UX
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y, g : Y → S be morphisms of schemes. Then there is a canonical exact sequence f^*Ω_Y/S → Ω_X/S → Ω_X/Y → 0 where the maps come from applications of Lemma [Tag 01UV].
nodes.section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism

nodes.title: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism · Lemma 01V0
nodes.summary: Let X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let g : S' → S be a morphism of schemes. Let X' = X_S' be the base change of X. Denote g' : X' → X the projection. Then the map (g')^*Ω_X/S → Ω_X'/S' of Lemma [Tag 01UV] is an isomorphism.
nodes.section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism

nodes.title: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism · Lemma 01V1
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S and g : Y → S be morphisms of schemes with the same target. Let p : X ×_S Y → X and q : X ×_S Y → Y be the projection morphisms. The maps from Lemma [Tag 01UV] p^*Ω_X/S ⊕ q^*Ω_Y/S → Ω_X ×_S Y/S give an isomorphism.
nodes.section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism

nodes.title: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism · Lemma 01V2
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. If f is locally of finite type, then Ω_X/S is a finite type O_X-module.
nodes.section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism

nodes.title: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism · Lemma 01V3
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. If f is locally of finite presentation, then Ω_X/S is an O_X-module of finite presentation.
nodes.section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism

nodes.title: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism · Lemma 01UY
nodes.summary: If X → S is an immersion, or more generally a monomorphism, then Ω_X/S is zero.
nodes.section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism

nodes.title: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism · Lemma 01UZ
nodes.summary: Let i : Z → X be an immersion of schemes over S. There is a canonical exact sequence C_Z/X → i^*Ω_X/S → Ω_Z/S → 0 where the first arrow is induced by d_X/S and the second arrow comes from Lemma [Tag 01UV].
nodes.section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism

nodes.title: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism · Lemma 0474
nodes.summary: Let i : Z → X be an immersion of schemes over S, and assume i (locally) has a left inverse. Then the canonical sequence 0 → C_Z/X → i^*Ω_X/S → Ω_Z/S → 0 of Lemma [Tag 01UZ] is (locally) split exact. In particular, if s : S → X is a section of the structure morphism X → S then the map C_S/X → s^*Ω_X/S induced by d_X/S is an isomorphism.
nodes.section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism

nodes.title: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism · Lemma 067L
nodes.summary: Let xymatrix Z ar[r]_i ar[rd]_j & X ar[d] & Y be a commutative diagram of schemes where i and j are immersions. Then there is a canonical exact sequence C_Z/Y → C_Z/X → i^*Ω_X/Y → 0 where the first arrow comes from Lemma [Tag 01R4] and the second from Lemma [Tag 01UZ].
nodes.section: Sheaf of differentials of a morphism

nodes.title: Finite order differential operators · Lemma 0G44
nodes.summary: Let R → A be a ring map. Denote f : X → S the corresponding morphism of affine schemes. Let F and G be O_X-modules. If F is quasi-coherent then the map Diff^k_X/S(F, G) → Diff^k_A/R(Γ(X, F), Γ(X, G)) sending a differential operator to its action on global sections is bijective.

nodes.title: Finite order differential operators · Lemma 0G45
nodes.summary: Let a : X → S and b : Y → S be morphisms of schemes. Let F and F' be quasi-coherent O_X-modules. Let D : F → F' be a differential operator of order k on X/S. Let G be a quasi-coherent O_Y-module. Then there is a unique differential operator D' : pr_1^*F ⊗_O_X ×_S Y pr_2^*G → pr_1^*F' ⊗_O_X ×_S Y pr_2^*G of order k on X ×_S Y / Y such that D'(s ⊗ t) = D(s) ⊗ t for local sections s of F and t of G.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms · Definition 01V5
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. • We say that f is smooth at x ∈ X if there exist an affine open neighbourhood Spec(A) = U ⊂ X of x and affine open Spec(R) = V ⊂ S with f(U) ⊂ V such that the induced ring map R → A is smooth. • We say that f is smooth if it is smooth at every point of X. • A morphism of affine schemes f : X → S is called standard smooth if there exists a standard smooth ring map R → R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c) (see Algebra, Definition [Tag 00T6])…

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms · Lemma 01V6
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent • The morphism f is smooth. • For every affine opens U ⊂ X, V ⊂ S with f(U) ⊂ V the ring map O_S(V) → O_X(U) is smooth. • There exists an open covering S = ⋃_j ∈ J V_j and open coverings f^-1(V_j) = ⋃_i ∈ I_j U_i such that each of the morphisms U_i → V_j, j∈ J, i∈ I_j is smooth. • There exists an affine open covering S = ⋃_j ∈ J V_j and affine open coverings f^-1(V_j) = ⋃_i ∈ I_j U_i such that the ring…

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms · Lemma 01V8
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. If f is flat, locally of finite presentation, and all fibres X_s are smooth, then f is smooth.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms · Lemma 01VA
nodes.summary: The composition of two morphisms which are smooth is smooth.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms · Lemma 01VB
nodes.summary: The base change of a morphism which is smooth is smooth.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms · Lemma 01VC
nodes.summary: Any open immersion is smooth.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms · Lemma 01VD
nodes.summary: A smooth morphism is syntomic.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms · Lemma 01VE
nodes.summary: A smooth morphism is locally of finite presentation.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms · Lemma 01VF
nodes.summary: A smooth morphism is flat.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms · Lemma 056G
nodes.summary: A smooth morphism is universally open.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms · Lemma 01V7
nodes.summary: Smooth morphisms are locally standard smooth. Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let x ∈ X be a point. Let V ⊂ S be an affine open neighbourhood of f(x). The following are equivalent • The morphism f is smooth at x. • There exists an affine open U ⊂ X, with x ∈ U and f(U) ⊂ V such that the induced morphism f|_U : U → V is standard smooth.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms · Lemma 02G1
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Assume f is smooth. Then the module of differentials Ω_X/S of X over S is finite locally free and rank_x(Ω_X/S) = dim_x(X_f(x)) for every x ∈ X.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms · Definition 02G2
nodes.summary: Let d ≥ 0 be an integer. We say a morphism of schemes f : X → S is smooth of relative dimension d if f is smooth and Ω_X/S is finite locally free of constant rank d.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms · Lemma 01V9
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let x ∈ X. Set s = f(x). Assume f is locally of finite presentation. The following are equivalent: • The morphism f is smooth at x. • The local ring map O_S, s → O_X, x is flat and X_s → Spec(kappa(s)) is smooth at x. • The local ring map O_S, s → O_X, x is flat and the O_X, x-module Ω_X/S, x can be generated by at most dim_x(X_f(x)) elements. • The local ring map O_S, s → O_X, x is flat and the kappa(x)-vector space Ω_X_s/s, x…

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms · Lemma 02V4
nodes.summary: Let xymatrix X' ar[r]_g' ar[d]_f' & X ar[d]^f S' ar[r]^g & S be a cartesian diagram of schemes. Let W ⊂ X, resp. W' ⊂ X' be the open subscheme of points where f, resp. f' is smooth. Then W' = (g')^-1(W) if • f is flat and locally of finite presentation, or • f is locally of finite presentation and g is flat.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms · Lemma 02K4
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y, g : Y → S be morphisms of schemes. Assume f is smooth. Then 0 → f^*Ω_Y/S → Ω_X/S → Ω_X/Y → 0 (see Lemma [Tag 01UX]) is short exact.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms · Lemma 06AA
nodes.summary: Let i : Z → X be an immersion of schemes over S. Assume that Z is smooth over S. Then the canonical exact sequence 0 → C_Z/X → i^*Ω_X/S → Ω_Z/S → 0 of Lemma [Tag 01UZ] is short exact.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms · Lemma 06AB
nodes.summary: Let xymatrix Z ar[r]_i ar[rd]_j & X ar[d] & Y be a commutative diagram of schemes where i and j are immersions and X → Y is smooth. Then the canonical exact sequence 0 → C_Z/Y → C_Z/X → i^*Ω_X/Y → 0 of Lemma [Tag 067L] is exact.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms · Lemma 02K5
nodes.summary: Let xymatrix X ar[rr]_f ar[rd]_p & & Y ar[dl]^q & S be a commutative diagram of morphisms of schemes. Assume that • f is surjective, and smooth, • p is smooth, and • q is locally of finite presentation. Then q is smooth.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms · Lemma 05D9
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let σ : S → X be a section of f. Let s ∈ S be a point such that f is smooth at x = σ(s). Then there exist affine open neighbourhoods Spec(A) = U ⊂ S of s and Spec(B) = V ⊂ X of x such that • f(V) ⊂ U and σ(U) ⊂ V, • with I = Ker(σ^\# : B → A) the module I/I^2 is a free A-module, and • B^wedge ≅ A[[x_1, …, x_d]] as A-algebras where B^wedge denotes the completion of B with respect to I.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms · Lemma 0AFF
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a smooth morphism of locally Noetherian schemes. For every point x in X with image y in Y, dim_x(X) = dim_y(Y) + dim_x(X_y), where X_y denotes the fiber over y.

nodes.title: Unramified morphisms · Definition 02G4
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. • We say that f is unramified at x ∈ X if there exists an affine open neighbourhood Spec(A) = U ⊂ X of x and affine open Spec(R) = V ⊂ S with f(U) ⊂ V such that the induced ring map R → A is unramified. • We say that f is G-unramified at x ∈ X if there exists an affine open neighbourhood Spec(A) = U ⊂ X of x and affine open Spec(R) = V ⊂ S with f(U) ⊂ V such that the induced ring map R → A is G-unramified. • We say that f is…

nodes.title: Unramified morphisms · Lemma 02G5
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Then • f is unramified if and only if f is locally of finite type and Ω_X/S = 0, and • f is G-unramified if and only if f is locally of finite presentation and Ω_X/S = 0.

nodes.title: Unramified morphisms · Lemma 02G6
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent • The morphism f is unramified (resp. G-unramified). • For every affine open U ⊂ X, V ⊂ S with f(U) ⊂ V the ring map O_S(V) → O_X(U) is unramified (resp. G-unramified). • There exists an open covering S = ⋃_j ∈ J V_j and open coverings f^-1(V_j) = ⋃_i ∈ I_j U_i such that each of the morphisms U_i → V_j, j∈ J, i∈ I_j is unramified (resp. G-unramified). • There exists an affine open covering S = ⋃_j ∈ J…

nodes.title: Unramified morphisms · Lemma 02G9
nodes.summary: The composition of two morphisms which are unramified is unramified. The same holds for G-unramified morphisms.

nodes.title: Unramified morphisms · Lemma 02GA
nodes.summary: The base change of a morphism which is unramified is unramified. The same holds for G-unramified morphisms.

nodes.title: Unramified morphisms · Lemma 04EV
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Assume S is locally Noetherian. Then f is unramified if and only if f is G-unramified.

nodes.title: Unramified morphisms · Lemma 02GB
nodes.summary: Any open immersion is G-unramified.

nodes.title: Unramified morphisms · Lemma 02GC
nodes.summary: A closed immersion i : Z → X is unramified. It is G-unramified if and only if the associated quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals I = Ker(O_X → i_*O_Z) is of finite type (as an O_X-module).

nodes.title: Unramified morphisms · Lemma 02GD
nodes.summary: An unramified morphism is locally of finite type. A G-unramified morphism is locally of finite presentation.

nodes.title: Unramified morphisms · Lemma 02V5
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. If f is unramified at x then f is quasi-finite at x. In particular, an unramified morphism is locally quasi-finite.

nodes.title: Unramified morphisms · Lemma 02G7
nodes.summary: Fibres of unramified morphisms. • Let X be a scheme over a field k. The structure morphism X → Spec(k) is unramified if and only if X is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field extensions of k. • If f : X → S is an unramified morphism then for every s ∈ S the fibre X_s is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field extensions of kappa(s).

nodes.title: Unramified morphisms · Lemma 02G8
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. • If f is unramified then for any x ∈ X the field extension kappa(x)/kappa(f(x)) is finite separable. • If f is locally of finite type, and for every s ∈ S the fibre X_s is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field extensions of kappa(s) then f is unramified. • If f is locally of finite presentation, and for every s ∈ S the fibre X_s is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field extensions of kappa(s) then f…

nodes.title: Unramified morphisms · Lemma 02GE
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism. • If f is unramified, then the diagonal morphism Δ : X → X ×_S X is an open immersion. • If f is locally of finite type and Δ is an open immersion, then f is unramified. • If f is locally of finite presentation and Δ is an open immersion, then f is G-unramified.

nodes.title: Unramified morphisms · Lemma 02GF
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let x ∈ X. Set s = f(x). Assume f is locally of finite type (resp. locally of finite presentation). The following are equivalent: • The morphism f is unramified (resp. G-unramified) at x. • The fibre X_s is unramified over kappa(s) at x. • The O_X, x-module Ω_X/S, x is zero. • The O_X_s, x-module Ω_X_s/s, x is zero. • The kappa(x)-vector space Ω_X_s/s, x ⊗_O_X_s, x kappa(x) = Ω_X/S, x ⊗_O_X, x kappa(x) is zero. • We have m_sO_X, x =…

nodes.title: Unramified morphisms · Lemma 0475
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Assume f locally of finite type. Formation of the open set T & = (x ∈ X mid X_f(x) is unramified over kappa(f(x)) at x) & = (x ∈ X mid X is unramified over S at x) commutes with arbitrary base change: For any morphism g : S' → S, consider the base change f' : X' → S' of f and the projection g' : X' → X. Then the corresponding set T' for the morphism f' is equal to T' = (g')^-1(T). If f is assumed locally of finite presentation then…

nodes.title: Unramified morphisms · Lemma 02GG
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes over S. • If X is unramified over S, then f is unramified. • If X is G-unramified over S and Y is locally of finite type over S, then f is G-unramified.

nodes.title: Unramified morphisms · Lemma 04HB
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X, Y be schemes over S. Let f, g : X → Y be morphisms over S. Let x ∈ X. Assume that • the structure morphism Y → S is unramified, • f(x) = g(x) in Y, say y = f(x) = g(x), and • the induced maps f^sharp, g^sharp : kappa(y) → kappa(x) are equal. Then there exists an open neighbourhood of x in X on which f and g are equal.

nodes.title: Étale morphisms · Definition 02GI
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. • We say that f is étale at x ∈ X if there exists an affine open neighbourhood Spec(A) = U ⊂ X of x and affine open Spec(R) = V ⊂ S with f(U) ⊂ V such that the induced ring map R → A is étale. • We say that f is étale if it is étale at every point of X. • A morphism of affine schemes f : X → S is called standard étale if X → S is isomorphic to Spec(R[x]_h/(g)) → Spec(R) where R → R[x]_h/(g) is a standard étale ring map, see Algebra,…

nodes.title: Étale morphisms · Lemma 02GJ
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent • The morphism f is étale. • For every affine opens U ⊂ X, V ⊂ S with f(U) ⊂ V the ring map O_S(V) → O_X(U) is étale. • There exists an open covering S = ⋃_j ∈ J V_j and open coverings f^-1(V_j) = ⋃_i ∈ I_j U_i such that each of the morphisms U_i → V_j, j∈ J, i∈ I_j is étale. • There exists an affine open covering S = ⋃_j ∈ J V_j and affine open coverings f^-1(V_j) = ⋃_i ∈ I_j U_i such that the ring map…

nodes.title: Étale morphisms · Lemma 02GN
nodes.summary: The composition of two morphisms which are étale is étale.

nodes.title: Étale morphisms · Lemma 02GO
nodes.summary: The base change of a morphism which is étale is étale.

nodes.title: Étale morphisms · Lemma 02GK
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let x ∈ X. Then f is étale at x if and only if f is smooth and unramified at x.

nodes.title: Étale morphisms · Lemma 03WS
nodes.summary: An étale morphism is locally quasi-finite.

nodes.title: Étale morphisms · Lemma 02GL
nodes.summary: Description of the étale schemes over fields and fibres of étale morphisms. Fibres of étale morphisms. • Let X be a scheme over a field k. The structure morphism X → Spec(k) is étale if and only if X is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field extensions of k. • If f : X → S is an étale morphism, then for every s ∈ S the fibre X_s is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field extensions of kappa(s).

nodes.title: Étale morphisms · Lemma 02GM
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. If f is flat, locally of finite presentation, and for every s ∈ S the fibre X_s is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field extensions of kappa(s), then f is étale.

nodes.title: Étale morphisms · Lemma 02GP
nodes.summary: Any open immersion is étale.

nodes.title: Étale morphisms · Lemma 02GQ
nodes.summary: An étale morphism is syntomic.

nodes.title: Étale morphisms · Lemma 02GR
nodes.summary: An étale morphism is locally of finite presentation.

nodes.title: Étale morphisms · Lemma 02GS
nodes.summary: An étale morphism is flat.

nodes.title: Étale morphisms · Lemma 03WT
nodes.summary: An étale morphism is open.

nodes.title: Étale morphisms · Lemma 02GT
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let x ∈ X be a point. Let V ⊂ S be an affine open neighbourhood of f(x). The following are equivalent • The morphism f is étale at x. • There exist an affine open U ⊂ X with x ∈ U and f(U) ⊂ V such that the induced morphism f|_U : U → V is standard étale (see Definition [Tag 02GI]).

nodes.title: Étale morphisms · Lemma 02GU
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let x ∈ X. Set s = f(x). Assume f is locally of finite presentation. The following are equivalent: • The morphism f is étale at x. • The local ring map O_S, s → O_X, x is flat and X_s → Spec(kappa(s)) is étale at x. • The local ring map O_S, s → O_X, x is flat and X_s → Spec(kappa(s)) is unramified at x. • The local ring map O_S, s → O_X, x is flat and the O_X, x-module Ω_X/S, x is zero. • The local ring map O_S, s → O_X, x is flat…

nodes.title: Étale morphisms · Lemma 02GV
nodes.summary: A morphism is étale at a point if and only if it is flat and G-unramified at that point. A morphism is étale if and only if it is flat and G-unramified.

nodes.title: Étale morphisms · Lemma 0476
nodes.summary: Let xymatrix X' ar[r]_g' ar[d]_f' & X ar[d]^f S' ar[r]^g & S be a cartesian diagram of schemes. Let W ⊂ X, resp. W' ⊂ X' be the open subscheme of points where f, resp. f' is étale. Then W' = (g')^-1(W) if • f is flat and locally of finite presentation, or • f is locally of finite presentation and g is flat.

nodes.title: Étale morphisms · Lemma 0HB1
nodes.summary: See for example [GWII]. Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes over S. If X is étale over S and Y is unramified over S, then f is étale.

nodes.title: Étale morphisms · Lemma 02GW
nodes.summary: Cancellation law for étale morphisms Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes over S. If X and Y are étale over S, then f is étale.

nodes.title: Étale morphisms · Lemma 02K6
nodes.summary: Let xymatrix X ar[rr]_f ar[rd]_p & & Y ar[dl]^q & S be a commutative diagram of morphisms of schemes. Assume that • f is surjective, and étale, • p is étale, and • q is locally of finite presentation. Then q is étale.

nodes.title: Étale morphisms · Lemma 054L
nodes.summary: Smooth schemes are étale-locally like affine spaces. Let φ : X → Y be a morphism of schemes. Let x ∈ X. Let V ⊂ Y be an affine open neighbourhood of φ(x). If φ is smooth at x, then there exists an integer d ≥ 0 and an affine open U ⊂ X with x ∈ U and φ(U) ⊂ V such that there exists a commutative diagram xymatrix X ar[d] & U ar[l] ar[d] ar[r]_-π & A^d_V ar[ld] Y & V ar[l] where π is étale.

nodes.title: Relatively ample sheaves · Definition 01VH
nodes.summary: [EGA] Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let L be an invertible O_X-module. We say L is relatively ample, or f-relatively ample, or ample on X/S, or f-ample if f : X → S is quasi-compact, and if for every affine open V ⊂ S the restriction of L to the open subscheme f^-1(V) of X is ample.

nodes.title: Relatively ample sheaves · Lemma 02NN
nodes.summary: Let X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let L be an invertible O_X-module. Let n ≥ 1. Then L is f-ample if and only if L^⊗ n is f-ample.

nodes.title: Relatively ample sheaves · Lemma 01VI
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. If there exists an f-ample invertible sheaf, then f is separated.

nodes.title: Relatively ample sheaves · Lemma 01VJ
nodes.summary: [EGA] Let f : X → S be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes. Let L be an invertible sheaf on X. The following are equivalent: • The invertible sheaf L is f-ample. • There exists an open covering S = ⋃ V_i such that each L|_f^-1(V_i) is ample relative to f^-1(V_i) → V_i. • There exists an affine open covering S = ⋃ V_i such that each L|_f^-1(V_i) is ample. • There exists a quasi-coherent graded O_S-algebra A and a map of graded O_X-algebras ψ : f^*A → bigoplus_d ≥ 0 L^⊗ d…

nodes.title: Relatively ample sheaves · Lemma 01VK
nodes.summary: [EGA] Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let L be an invertible O_X-module. Assume S affine. Then L is f-relatively ample if and only if L is ample on X.

nodes.title: Relatively ample sheaves · Lemma 0891
nodes.summary: [EGA] Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Then f is quasi-affine if and only if O_X is f-relatively ample.

nodes.title: Relatively ample sheaves · Lemma 0892
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes, M an invertible O_Y-module, and L an invertible O_X-module. • If L is f-ample and M is ample, then L ⊗ f^*M^⊗ a is ample for a gg 0. • If M is ample and f quasi-affine, then f^*M is ample.

nodes.title: Relatively ample sheaves · Lemma 0C4K
nodes.summary: Let g : Y → S and f : X → Y be morphisms of schemes. Let M be an invertible O_Y-module. Let L be an invertible O_X-module. If S is quasi-compact, M is g-ample, and L is f-ample, then L ⊗ f^*M^⊗ a is g ∘ f-ample for a gg 0.

nodes.title: Relatively ample sheaves · Lemma 0893
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let L be an invertible O_X-module. Let S' → S be a morphism of schemes. Let f' : X' → S' be the base change of f and denote L' the pullback of L to X'. If L is f-ample, then L' is f'-ample.

nodes.title: Relatively ample sheaves · Lemma 0C4L
nodes.summary: Let g : Y → S and f : X → Y be morphisms of schemes. Let L be an invertible O_X-module. If L is g ∘ f-ample and f is quasi-compact then L is f-ample.

nodes.title: Very ample sheaves · Definition 01VM
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let L be an invertible O_X-module. We say L is relatively very ample or more precisely f-relatively very ample, or very ample on X/S, or f-very ample if there exist a quasi-coherent O_S-module E and an immersion i : X → P(E) over S such that L ≅ i^*O_P(E)(1).

nodes.title: Very ample sheaves · Lemma 01VN
nodes.summary: [EGA] Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let L be an invertible O_X-module. If f is quasi-compact and L is a relatively very ample invertible sheaf, then L is a relatively ample invertible sheaf.

nodes.title: Very ample sheaves · Lemma 01VQ
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let L be an invertible sheaf on X. If L is relatively very ample on X/S then f is separated.

nodes.title: Very ample sheaves · Lemma 01VR
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let L be an invertible sheaf on X. Assume f is quasi-compact. The following are equivalent • L is relatively very ample on X/S, • there exists an open covering S = ⋃ V_j such that L|_f^-1(V_j) is relatively very ample on f^-1(V_j)/V_j for all j, • there exists a quasi-coherent sheaf of graded O_S-algebras A generated in degree 1 over O_S and a map of graded O_X-algebras ψ : f^*A → bigoplus_n ≥ 0 L^⊗ n such that f^*A_1 → L is…

nodes.title: Very ample sheaves · Lemma 0B3F
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let L be an invertible O_X-module. Let S' → S be a morphism of schemes. Let f' : X' → S' be the base change of f and denote L' the pullback of L to X'. If L is f-very ample, then L' is f'-very ample.

nodes.title: Ample and very ample sheaves relative to finite type morphisms · Lemma 02NP
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let L be an invertible sheaf on X. Assume that • the invertible sheaf L is very ample on X/S, • the morphism X → S is of finite type, and • S is affine. Then there exist an n ≥ 0 and an immersion i : X → P^n_S over S such that L ≅ i^*O_P^n_S(1).
nodes.section: Ample and very ample sheaves relative to finite type morphisms

nodes.title: Ample and very ample sheaves relative to finite type morphisms · Lemma 04II
nodes.summary: Let π : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Assume that X is quasi-affine and that π is locally of finite type. Then there exist n ≥ 0 and an immersion i : X → A^n_S over S.
nodes.section: Ample and very ample sheaves relative to finite type morphisms

nodes.title: Ample and very ample sheaves relative to finite type morphisms · Lemma 01VS
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let L be an invertible sheaf on X. Assume that • the invertible sheaf L is ample on X, and • the morphism X → S is locally of finite type. Then there exists a d_0 ≥ 1 such that for every d ≥ d_0 there exist an n ≥ 0 and an immersion i : X → P^n_S over S such that L^⊗ d ≅ i^*O_P^n_S(1).
nodes.section: Ample and very ample sheaves relative to finite type morphisms

nodes.title: Ample and very ample sheaves relative to finite type morphisms · Lemma 01VT
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let L be an invertible O_X-module. Assume S affine and f of finite type. The following are equivalent • L is ample on X, • L is f-ample, • L^⊗ d is f-very ample for some d ≥ 1, • L^⊗ d is f-very ample for all d gg 1, • for some d ≥ 1 there exist n ≥ 1 and an immersion i : X → P^n_S such that L^⊗ d ≅ i^*O_P^n_S(1), and • for all d gg 1 there exist n ≥ 1 and an immersion i : X → P^n_S such that L^⊗ d ≅ i^*O_P^n_S(1).
nodes.section: Ample and very ample sheaves relative to finite type morphisms

nodes.title: Ample and very ample sheaves relative to finite type morphisms · Lemma 01VU
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let L be an invertible O_X-module. Assume S quasi-compact and f of finite type. The following are equivalent • L is f-ample, • L^⊗ d is f-very ample for some d ≥ 1, • L^⊗ d is f-very ample for all d gg 1.
nodes.section: Ample and very ample sheaves relative to finite type morphisms

nodes.title: Ample and very ample sheaves relative to finite type morphisms · Lemma 02NQ
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let L be an invertible sheaf on X. Assume f is of finite type. The following are equivalent: • L is f-relatively very ample, and • there exist an open covering S = ⋃ V_j, for each j an integer n_j, and immersions i_j : X_j = f^-1(V_j) = V_j ×_S X → P^n_j_V_j over V_j such that L|_X_j ≅ i_j^*O_P^n_j_V_j(1).
nodes.section: Ample and very ample sheaves relative to finite type morphisms

nodes.title: Ample and very ample sheaves relative to finite type morphisms · Lemma 02NR
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let L be an invertible sheaf on X. Assume f is of finite type. The following are equivalent: • L is f-relatively ample, and • there exist an open covering S = ⋃ V_j, for each j an integers d_j ≥ 1, n_j ≥ 0, and immersions i_j : X_j = f^-1(V_j) = V_j ×_S X → P^n_j_V_j over V_j such that L^⊗ d_j|_X_j ≅ i_j^*O_P^n_j_V_j(1).
nodes.section: Ample and very ample sheaves relative to finite type morphisms

nodes.title: Ample and very ample sheaves relative to finite type morphisms · Lemma 0FVC
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let N, L be invertible O_X-modules. Assume S is quasi-compact, f is of finite type, and L is f-ample. Then N ⊗_O_X L^⊗ d is f-very ample for all d gg 1.
nodes.section: Ample and very ample sheaves relative to finite type morphisms

nodes.title: Quasi-projective morphisms · Definition 01VW
nodes.summary: [EGA] and [H] Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. • We say f is quasi-projective if f is of finite type and there exists an f-relatively ample invertible O_X-module. • We say f is H-quasi-projective if there exists a quasi-compact immersion X → P^n_S over S for some n. • We say f is locally quasi-projective if there exists an open covering S = ⋃ V_j such that each f^-1(V_j) → V_j is quasi-projective.

nodes.title: Quasi-projective morphisms · Lemma 0B3G
nodes.summary: A base change of a quasi-projective morphism is quasi-projective.

nodes.title: Quasi-projective morphisms · Lemma 0C4M
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y and g : Y → S be morphisms of schemes. If S is quasi-compact and f and g are quasi-projective, then g ∘ f is quasi-projective.

nodes.title: Quasi-projective morphisms · Lemma 01VX
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. If f is quasi-projective, or H-quasi-projective or locally quasi-projective, then f is separated of finite type.

nodes.title: Quasi-projective morphisms · Lemma 01VY
nodes.summary: A H-quasi-projective morphism is quasi-projective.

nodes.title: Quasi-projective morphisms · Lemma 01VZ
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent: • The morphism f is locally quasi-projective. • There exists an open covering S = ⋃ V_j such that each f^-1(V_j) → V_j is H-quasi-projective.

nodes.title: Quasi-projective morphisms · Lemma 0B3H
nodes.summary: [EGA] A quasi-affine morphism of finite type is quasi-projective.

nodes.title: Quasi-projective morphisms · Lemma 0C4N
nodes.summary: Let g : Y → S and f : X → Y be morphisms of schemes. If g ∘ f is quasi-projective and f is quasi-compact, then f is quasi-projective.

nodes.title: Proper morphisms · Definition 01W1
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. We say f is proper if f is separated, finite type, and universally closed.

nodes.title: Proper morphisms · Lemma 02K7
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent: • The morphism f is universally closed. • There exists an open covering S = ⋃ V_j such that f^-1(V_j) → V_j is universally closed for all indices j.

nodes.title: Proper morphisms · Lemma 01W2
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent: • The morphism f is proper. • There exists an open covering S = ⋃ V_j such that f^-1(V_j) → V_j is proper for all indices j.

nodes.title: Proper morphisms · Lemma 01W3
nodes.summary: The composition of proper morphisms is proper. The same is true for universally closed morphisms.

nodes.title: Proper morphisms · Lemma 01W4
nodes.summary: The base change of a proper morphism is proper. The same is true for universally closed morphisms.

nodes.title: Proper morphisms · Lemma 01W5
nodes.summary: A closed immersion is proper, hence a fortiori universally closed.

nodes.title: Proper morphisms · Lemma 01W6
nodes.summary: Suppose given a commutative diagram of schemes xymatrix X ar[rr] ar[rd] & & Y ar[ld] & S & with Y separated over S. • If X → S is universally closed, then the morphism X → Y is universally closed. • If X is proper over S, then the morphism X → Y is proper. In particular, in both cases the image of X in Y is closed.

nodes.title: Proper morphisms · Lemma 04XU
nodes.summary: Due to Bjorn Poonen. A universally closed morphism of schemes is quasi-compact.

nodes.title: Proper morphisms · Lemma 03GN
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes over S. If X is universally closed over S and f is surjective then Y is universally closed over S. In particular, if also Y is separated and locally of finite type over S, then Y is proper over S.

nodes.title: Proper morphisms · Lemma 0AH6
nodes.summary: Suppose given a commutative diagram of schemes xymatrix X ar[rr]_h ar[rd]_f & & Y ar[ld]^g & S Assume • X → S is a universally closed (for example proper) morphism, and • Y → S is separated and locally of finite type. Then the scheme theoretic image Z ⊂ Y of h is proper over S and X → Z is surjective.
