nodes.title: The fppf topology · Definition 021S
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let Sch_fppf be a big fppf site containing S. • The big fppf site of S, denoted (Sch/S)_fppf, is the site Sch_fppf/S introduced in Sites, Section [Tag 00XZ]. • The big affine fppf site of S, denoted (Aff/S)_fppf, is the full subcategory of (Sch/S)_fppf whose objects are affine U/S. A covering of (Aff/S)_fppf is any covering (U_i → U) of (Sch/S)_fppf which is a standard fppf covering.

nodes.title: The fppf topology · Lemma 021T
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let Sch_fppf be a big fppf site containing S. Then (Aff/S)_fppf is a site.

nodes.title: The fppf topology · Lemma 021U
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let Sch_fppf be a big fppf site containing S. The underlying categories of the sites Sch_fppf, (Sch/S)_fppf, and (Aff/S)_fppf have fibre products. In each case the obvious functor into the category Sch of all schemes commutes with taking fibre products. The category (Sch/S)_fppf has a final object, namely S/S.

nodes.title: The fppf topology · Lemma 021V
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let Sch_fppf be a big fppf site containing S. The functor (Aff/S)_fppf → (Sch/S)_fppf is cocontinuous and induces an equivalence of topoi from Sh((Aff/S)_fppf) to Sh((Sch/S)_fppf).

nodes.title: The fppf topology · Lemma 021W
nodes.summary: Let Sch_fppf be a big fppf site. Let f : T → S be a morphism in Sch_fppf. The functor u : (Sch/T)_fppf → (Sch/S)_fppf, V/T ↦ V/S is cocontinuous, and has a continuous right adjoint v : (Sch/S)_fppf → (Sch/T)_fppf, (U → S) ↦ (U ×_S T → T). They induce the same morphism of topoi f_big : Sh((Sch/T)_fppf) → Sh((Sch/S)_fppf) We have f_big^-1(G)(U/T) = G(U/S). We have f_big, *(F)(U/S) = F(U ×_S T/T). Also, f_big^-1 has a left adjoint f_big! which commutes with fibre products…

nodes.title: The fppf topology · Lemma 021X
nodes.summary: Given schemes X, Y, Z in (Sch/S)_fppf and morphisms f : X → Y, g : Y → Z we have g_big ∘ f_big = (g ∘ f)_big.

nodes.title: The ph topology · Definition 0DBD
nodes.summary: Let T be an affine scheme. A standard ph covering is a family (f_j : U_j → T)_j = 1, …, m constructed from a proper surjective morphism f : U → T and an affine open covering U = ⋃_j = 1, …, m U_j by setting f_j = f|_U_j.

nodes.title: The ph topology · Lemma 0DBE
nodes.summary: Let (f_j : U_j → T)_j = 1, …, m be a standard ph covering. Let T' → T be a morphism of affine schemes. Then (U_j ×_T T' → T')_j = 1, …, m is a standard ph covering.

nodes.title: The ph topology · Lemma 0DBF
nodes.summary: Let T be an affine scheme. Each of the following types of families of maps with target T has a refinement by a standard ph covering: • any Zariski open covering of T, • (W_ji → T)_j = 1, …, m, i = 1, … n_j where (W_ji → U_j)_i = 1, …, n_j and (U_j → T)_j = 1, …, m are standard ph coverings.

nodes.title: The ph topology · Definition 0DBG
nodes.summary: Let T be a scheme. A ph covering of T is a family of morphisms (f_i : T_i → T)_i ∈ I of schemes such that f_i is locally of finite type and such that for every affine open U ⊂ T there exists a standard ph covering (U_j → U)_j = 1, …, m refining the family (T_i ×_T U → U)_i ∈ I.

nodes.title: The ph topology · Lemma 0DBH
nodes.summary: A Zariski covering is a ph covering.

nodes.title: The ph topology · Lemma 0DES
nodes.summary: Let f : Y → X be a surjective proper morphism of schemes. Then (Y → X) is a ph covering.

nodes.title: The ph topology · Lemma 0ET9
nodes.summary: Let T be a scheme. Let (f_i : T_i → T)_i ∈ I be a family of morphisms such that f_i is locally of finite type for all i. The following are equivalent • (T_i → T)_i ∈ I is a ph covering, • there is a ph covering which refines (T_i → T)_i ∈ I, and • (coprod_i ∈ I T_i → T) is a ph covering.

nodes.title: The ph topology · Lemma 0DBI
nodes.summary: Let T be a scheme. • If T' → T is an isomorphism then (T' → T) is a ph covering of T. • If (T_i → T)_i∈ I is a ph covering and for each i we have a ph covering (T_ij → T_i)_j∈ J_i, then (T_ij → T)_i ∈ I, j∈ J_i is a ph covering. • If (T_i → T)_i∈ I is a ph covering and T' → T is a morphism of schemes then (T' ×_T T_i → T')_i∈ I is a ph covering.

nodes.title: The ph topology · Definition 0DBJ
nodes.summary: A big ph site is any site Sch_ph as in Sites, Definition [Tag 00VH] constructed as follows: • Choose any set of schemes S_0, and any set of ph coverings Cov_0 among these schemes. • As underlying category take any category Sch_α constructed as in Sets, Lemma [Tag 000J] starting with the set S_0. • Choose any set of coverings as in Sets, Lemma [Tag 000X] starting with the category Sch_α and the class of ph coverings, and the set Cov_0 chosen above.

nodes.title: The ph topology · Lemma 0DBK
nodes.summary: Let Sch_ph be a big ph site as in Definition [Tag 0DBJ]. Let T ∈ Ob(Sch_ph). Let (T_i → T)_i ∈ I be an arbitrary ph covering of T. • There exists a covering (U_j → T)_j ∈ J of T in the site Sch_ph which refines (T_i → T)_i ∈ I. • If (T_i → T)_i ∈ I is a standard ph covering, then it is tautologically equivalent to a covering of Sch_ph. • If (T_i → T)_i ∈ I is a Zariski covering, then it is tautologically equivalent to a covering of Sch_ph.

nodes.title: The ph topology · Definition 0DBL
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let Sch_ph be a big ph site containing S. • The big ph site of S, denoted (Sch/S)_ph, is the site Sch_ph/S introduced in Sites, Section [Tag 00XZ]. • The big affine ph site of S, denoted (Aff/S)_ph, is the full subcategory of (Sch/S)_ph whose objects are affine U/S. A covering of (Aff/S)_ph is any finite covering (U_i → U) of (Sch/S)_ph with U_i and U affine.

nodes.title: The ph topology · Lemma 0DBM
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let Sch_ph be a big ph site containing S. Then (Aff/S)_ph is a site.

nodes.title: The ph topology · Lemma 0DBN
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let Sch_ph be a big ph site containing S. The underlying categories of the sites Sch_ph, (Sch/S)_ph, and (Aff/S)_ph have fibre products. In each case the obvious functor into the category Sch of all schemes commutes with taking fibre products. The category (Sch/S)_ph has a final object, namely S/S.

nodes.title: The ph topology · Lemma 0DBP
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let Sch_ph be a big ph site containing S. The functor (Aff/S)_ph → (Sch/S)_ph is cocontinuous and induces an equivalence of topoi from Sh((Aff/S)_ph) to Sh((Sch/S)_ph).

nodes.title: The ph topology · Lemma 0DBQ
nodes.summary: Let F be a presheaf on (Sch/S)_ph. Then F is a sheaf if and only if • F satisfies the sheaf condition for Zariski coverings, and • if f : V → U is proper surjective, then F(U) maps bijectively to the equalizer of the two maps F(V) → F(V ×_U V). Moreover, in the presence of (1) property (2) is equivalent to property • [(2')] the sheaf property for (V → U) as in (2) with U affine.

nodes.title: The ph topology · Lemma 0DBR
nodes.summary: Let Sch_ph be a big ph site. Let f : T → S be a morphism in Sch_ph. The functor u : (Sch/T)_ph → (Sch/S)_ph, V/T ↦ V/S is cocontinuous, and has a continuous right adjoint v : (Sch/S)_ph → (Sch/T)_ph, (U → S) ↦ (U ×_S T → T). They induce the same morphism of topoi f_big : Sh((Sch/T)_ph) → Sh((Sch/S)_ph) We have f_big^-1(G)(U/T) = G(U/S). We have f_big, *(F)(U/S) = F(U ×_S T/T). Also, f_big^-1 has a left adjoint f_big! which commutes with fibre products and equalizers.

nodes.title: The ph topology · Lemma 0DBS
nodes.summary: Given schemes X, Y, Y in (Sch/S)_ph and morphisms f : X → Y, g : Y → Z we have g_big ∘ f_big = (g ∘ f)_big.

nodes.title: The fpqc topology · Definition 022B
nodes.summary: Let T be a scheme. An fpqc covering of T is a family of morphisms (f_i : T_i → T)_i ∈ I of schemes such that each f_i is flat and such that for every affine open U ⊂ T there exists n ≥ 0, a map a : (1, …, n) → I and affine opens V_j ⊂ T_a(j), j = 1, …, n with ⋃_j = 1^n f_a(j)(V_j) = U.

nodes.title: The fpqc topology · Lemma 03L7
nodes.summary: Let T be a scheme. Let (f_i : T_i → T)_i ∈ I be a family of morphisms of schemes with target T. The following are equivalent • (f_i : T_i → T)_i ∈ I is an fpqc covering, • each f_i is flat and for every affine open U ⊂ T there exist quasi-compact opens U_i ⊂ T_i which are almost all empty, such that U = ⋃ f_i(U_i), • each f_i is flat and there exists an affine open covering T = ⋃_α ∈ A U_α and for each α ∈ A there exist i_α, 1, …, i_α, n(α) ∈ I and quasi-compact opens…

nodes.title: The fpqc topology · Lemma 040I
nodes.summary: Let T be a scheme. Let (f_i : T_i → T)_i ∈ I be a family of morphisms of schemes with target T. The following are equivalent • (f_i : T_i → T)_i ∈ I is an fpqc covering, and • setting T' = coprod_i ∈ I T_i, and f = coprod_i ∈ I f_i the family (f : T' → T) is an fpqc covering.

nodes.title: The fpqc topology · Lemma 03L8
nodes.summary: Let T be a scheme. Let (f_i : T_i → T)_i ∈ I be a family of morphisms of schemes with target T. Assume that • each f_i is flat, and • the family (f_i : T_i → T)_i ∈ I can be refined by an fpqc covering of T. Then (f_i : T_i → T)_i ∈ I is an fpqc covering of T.

nodes.title: The fpqc topology · Lemma 03L9
nodes.summary: Let T be a scheme. Let (f_i : T_i → T)_i ∈ I be a family of morphisms of schemes with target T. Assume that • each f_i is flat, and • there exists an fpqc covering (g_j : S_j → T)_j ∈ J such that each (S_j ×_T T_i → S_j)_i ∈ I is an fpqc covering. Then (f_i : T_i → T)_i ∈ I is an fpqc covering of T.

nodes.title: The fpqc topology · Lemma 022C
nodes.summary: Any fppf covering is an fpqc covering, and a fortiori, any syntomic, smooth, étale or Zariski covering is an fpqc covering.

nodes.title: The fpqc topology · Lemma 022D
nodes.summary: Let T be a scheme. • If T' → T is an isomorphism then (T' → T) is an fpqc covering of T. • If (T_i → T)_i∈ I is an fpqc covering and for each i we have an fpqc covering (T_ij → T_i)_j∈ J_i, then (T_ij → T)_i ∈ I, j∈ J_i is an fpqc covering. • If (T_i → T)_i∈ I is an fpqc covering and T' → T is a morphism of schemes then (T' ×_T T_i → T')_i∈ I is an fpqc covering.

nodes.title: The fpqc topology · Lemma 022E
nodes.summary: Let T be an affine scheme. Let (T_i → T)_i ∈ I be an fpqc covering of T. Then there exists an fpqc covering (U_j → T)_j = 1, …, n which is a refinement of (T_i → T)_i ∈ I such that each U_j is an affine scheme. Moreover, we may choose each U_j to be open affine in one of the T_i.

nodes.title: The fpqc topology · Definition 022F
nodes.summary: Let T be an affine scheme. A standard fpqc covering of T is a family (f_j : U_j → T)_j = 1, …, n with each U_j is affine, flat over T and T = ⋃ f_j(U_j).

nodes.title: The fpqc topology · Lemma 03LA
nodes.summary: Let T be an affine scheme. • If T' → T is an isomorphism then (T' → T) is a standard fpqc covering of T. • If (T_i → T)_i∈ I is a standard fpqc covering and for each i we have a standard fpqc covering (T_ij → T_i)_j∈ J_i, then (T_ij → T)_i ∈ I, j∈ J_i is a standard fpqc covering. • If (T_i → T)_i∈ I is a standard fpqc covering and T' → T is a morphism of affine schemes then (T' ×_T T_i → T')_i∈ I is a standard fpqc covering.

nodes.title: The fpqc topology · Lemma 03LB
nodes.summary: Let T be a scheme. Let (f_i : T_i → T)_i ∈ I be a family of morphisms of schemes with target T. Assume that • each f_i is flat, and • every affine scheme Z and morphism h : Z → T there exists a standard fpqc covering (Z_j → Z)_j = 1, …, n which refines the family (T_i ×_T Z → Z)_i ∈ I. Then (f_i : T_i → T)_i ∈ I is an fpqc covering of T.

nodes.title: The fpqc topology · Definition 022G
nodes.summary: Let F be a contravariant functor on the category of schemes with values in sets. • Let (U_i → T)_i ∈ I be a family of morphisms of schemes with fixed target. We say that F satisfies the sheaf property for the given family if for any collection of elements xi_i ∈ F(U_i) such that xi_i|_U_i ×_T U_j = xi_j|_U_i ×_T U_j there exists a unique element xi ∈ F(T) such that xi_i = xi|_U_i in F(U_i). • We say that F satisfies the sheaf property for the fpqc topology if it satisfies…

nodes.title: The fpqc topology · Lemma 022H
nodes.summary: Let F be a contravariant functor on the category of schemes with values in sets. Then F satisfies the sheaf property for the fpqc topology if and only if it satisfies • the sheaf property for every Zariski covering, and • the sheaf property for any standard fpqc covering. Moreover, in the presence of (1) property (2) is equivalent to property • [(2')] the sheaf property for (V → U) with V, U affine and V → U faithfully flat.

nodes.title: The fpqc topology · Lemma 0BBK
nodes.summary: Let R be a nonzero ring. There does not exist a set A of fpqc-coverings of Spec(R) such that every fpqc-covering can be refined by an element of A.

nodes.title: The V topology · Definition 0ETB
nodes.summary: Let T be an affine scheme. A standard V covering is a finite family (T_j → T)_j = 1, …, m with T_j affine such that for every morphism g : Spec(V) → T where V is a valuation ring, there is an extension V ⊂ W of valuation rings (More on Algebra, Definition [Tag 0ASG]), an index 1 ≤ j ≤ m, and a commutative diagram xymatrix Spec(W) ar[r] ar[d] & T_j ar[d] Spec(V) ar[r]^g & T

nodes.title: The V topology · Lemma 0ETC
nodes.summary: A standard fpqc covering is a standard V covering.

nodes.title: The V topology · Lemma 0ETD
nodes.summary: A standard ph covering is a standard V covering.

nodes.title: The V topology · Lemma 0ETE
nodes.summary: Let (T_j → T)_j = 1, …, m be a standard V covering. Let T' → T be a morphism of affine schemes. Then (T_j ×_T T' → T')_j = 1, …, m is a standard V covering.

nodes.title: The V topology · Lemma 0ETF
nodes.summary: Let T be an affine scheme. Let (T_j → T)_j = 1, …, m be a standard V covering. Let (T_ji → T_j)_i = 1, … n_j be a standard V covering. Then (T_ji → T)_i, j is a standard V covering.

nodes.title: The V topology · Lemma 0ETG
nodes.summary: Let T be an affine scheme. Let (T_j → T)_j = 1, …, m be a family of morphisms with T_j affine for all j. The following are equivalent • (T_j → T)_j = 1, …, m is a standard V covering, • there is a standard V covering which refines (T_j → T)_j = 1, …, m, and • (coprod_j = 1, …, m T_j → T) is a standard V covering.

nodes.title: The V topology · Definition 0ETH
nodes.summary: Let T be a scheme. A V covering of T is a family of morphisms (T_i → T)_i ∈ I of schemes such that for every affine open U ⊂ T there exists a standard V covering (U_j → U)_j = 1, …, m refining the family (T_i ×_T U → U)_i ∈ I.

nodes.title: The V topology · Lemma 0ETI
nodes.summary: Let T be a scheme. Let (f_i : T_i → T)_i ∈ I be a family of morphisms. The following are equivalent • (T_i → T)_i ∈ I is a V covering, • there is a V covering which refines (T_i → T)_i ∈ I, and • (coprod_i ∈ I T_i → T) is a V covering.

nodes.title: The V topology · Lemma 0ETJ
nodes.summary: Let T be a scheme. • If T' → T is an isomorphism then (T' → T) is a V covering of T. • If (T_i → T)_i∈ I is a V covering and for each i we have a V covering (T_ij → T_i)_j∈ J_i, then (T_ij → T)_i ∈ I, j∈ J_i is a V covering. • If (T_i → T)_i∈ I is a V covering and T' → T is a morphism of schemes then (T' ×_T T_i → T')_i∈ I is a V covering.

nodes.title: The V topology · Lemma 0ETK
nodes.summary: Any fpqc covering is a V covering. A fortiori, any fppf, syntomic, smooth, étale or Zariski covering is a V covering. Also, a ph covering is a V covering.

nodes.title: The V topology · Definition 0ETL
nodes.summary: Let F be a contravariant functor on the category of schemes with values in sets. We say that F satisfies the sheaf property for the V topology if it satisfies the sheaf property for any V covering (see Definition [Tag 022G]).

nodes.title: The V topology · Lemma 0ETM
nodes.summary: Let F be a contravariant functor on the category of schemes with values in sets. Then F satisfies the sheaf property for the V topology if and only if it satisfies • the sheaf property for every Zariski covering, and • the sheaf property for any standard V covering. Moreover, in the presence of (1) property (2) is equivalent to property • [(2')] the sheaf property for a standard V covering of the form (V → U), i.e., consisting of a single arrow.

nodes.title: The V topology · Lemma 0ETN
nodes.summary: Let X → Y be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes. The following are equivalent • (X → Y) is a V covering, • for any valuation ring V and morphism g : Spec(V) → Y there exists an extension of valuation rings V ⊂ W and a commutative diagram xymatrix Spec(W) ar[r] ar[d] & X ar[d] Spec(V) ar[r] & Y • for any morphism Z → Y and specialization z' leadsto z of points in Z, there is a specialization w' leadsto w of points in Z ×_Y X mapping to z' leadsto z.

nodes.title: The V topology · Lemma 0ETP
nodes.summary: Let (f_i : X_i → X)_i ∈ I be a V covering. Then coprod_i ∈ I f_i : coprod_i ∈ I X_i → X is a universally submersive morphism of schemes (Morphisms, Definition [Tag 040H]).

nodes.title: Change of big sites · Lemma 022J
nodes.summary: Any set of big Zariski sites is contained in a common big Zariski site. The same is true, mutatis mutandis, for big fppf and big étale sites.

nodes.title: Change of big sites · Lemma 022K
nodes.summary: Let τ ∈ (Zariski, etale, smooth, syntomic, fppf). Suppose given big sites Sch_τ and Sch'_τ. Assume that Sch_τ is contained in Sch'_τ. The inclusion functor Sch_τ → Sch'_τ satisfies the assumptions of Sites, Lemma [Tag 00XU]. There are morphisms of topoi g : Sh(Sch_τ) & → & Sh(Sch'_τ) f : Sh(Sch'_τ) & → & Sh(Sch_τ) such that f ∘ g ≅ id. For any object S of Sch_τ the inclusion functor (Sch/S)_τ → (Sch'/S)_τ satisfies the assumptions of Sites, Lemma [Tag 00XU] also. Hence…

nodes.title: Extending functors · Lemma 0EUW
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let C be a full subcategory of the category Sch/S of all schemes over S. Assume • if X → S is an object of C and U ⊂ X is an affine open, then U → S is isomorphic to an object of C, • if V is an affine scheme lying over an affine open U ⊂ S such that V → U is of finite presentation, then V → S is isomorphic to an object of C. Let F : C^opp → Sets be a functor. Assume • [(a)] for any Zariski covering (f_i : X_i → X)_i ∈ I with X, X_i objects of C we have…

nodes.title: Extending functors · Lemma 049N
nodes.summary: Let τ ∈ (Zariski, etale, smooth, syntomic, fppf). Let T be an affine scheme which is written as a limit T = lim_i ∈ I T_i of a directed inverse system of affine schemes. • Let V = (V_j → T)_j = 1, …, m be a standard τ-covering of T, see Definitions [Tag 020R], [Tag 0219], [Tag 0223], [Tag 0229], and [Tag 021Q]. Then there exists an index i and a standard τ-covering V_i = (V_i, j → T_i)_j = 1, …, m whose base change T ×_T_i V_i to T is isomorphic to V. • Let V_i, V'_i be a…

nodes.title: Extending functors · Lemma 0GDW
nodes.summary: Let S, C, F satisfy conditions (1), (2), (a), and (b) of Lemma [Tag 0EUW] and denote F' : (Sch/S)^opp → Sets the unique extension constructed in the lemma. Let τ ∈ (Zariski, etale, smooth, syntomic, fppf). Assume • [(c)] for any standard τ-covering (V_i → V)_i = 1, …, n of affines in Sch/S such that V → S factors through an affine open U ⊂ S and V → U is of finite presentation, the sheaf condition hold for F and (V_i → V)_i = 1, …, n by (2).. Then F' satisfies the sheaf…

nodes.title: Extending functors · Lemma 0EUX
nodes.summary: Let τ ∈ (Zariski, etale, smooth, syntomic, fppf). Let S be a scheme contained in a big site Sch_τ. Let F : (Sch/S)_τ^opp → Sets be a τ-sheaf satisfying property (b) of Lemma [Tag 0EUW] with C = (Sch/S)_τ. Then the extension F' of F to the category of all schemes over S satisfies the sheaf condition for all τ-coverings.

nodes.title: Descent data for quasi-coherent sheaves · Definition 023B
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let (f_i : S_i → S)_i ∈ I be a family of morphisms with target S. • A descent datum (F_i, φ_ij) for quasi-coherent sheaves with respect to the given family is given by a quasi-coherent sheaf F_i on S_i for each i ∈ I, an isomorphism of quasi-coherent O_S_i ×_S S_j-modules φ_ij : pr_0^*F_i → pr_1^*F_j for each pair (i, j) ∈ I^2 such that for every triple of indices (i, j, k) ∈ I^3 the diagram xymatrix pr_0^*F_i ar[rd]_pr_01^*φ_ij ar[rr]_pr_02^*φ_ik & &…

nodes.title: Descent data for quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 023C
nodes.summary: Let U = (U_i → U)_i ∈ I and V = (V_j → V)_j ∈ J be families of morphisms of schemes with fixed target. Let (g, α : I → J, (g_i)) : U → V be a morphism of families of maps with fixed target, see Sites, Definition [Tag 00VT]. Let (F_j, φ_jj') be a descent datum for quasi-coherent sheaves with respect to the family (V_j → V)_j ∈ J. Then • The system (g_i^*F_α(i), (g_i × g_i')^*φ_α(i)α(i')) is a descent datum with respect to the family (U_i → U)_i ∈ I. • This construction is…

nodes.title: Descent data for quasi-coherent sheaves · Definition 023D
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let (S_i → S)_i ∈ I be a family of morphisms with target S. • Let F be a quasi-coherent O_S-module. We call the unique descent on F datum with respect to the covering (S → S) the trivial descent datum. • The pullback of the trivial descent datum to (S_i → S) is called the canonical descent datum. Notation: (F|_S_i, can). • A descent datum (F_i, φ_ij) for quasi-coherent sheaves with respect to the given covering is said to be effective if there exists a…

nodes.title: Descent data for quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 023E
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let S = ⋃ U_i be an open covering. Any descent datum on quasi-coherent sheaves for the family U = (U_i → S) is effective. Moreover, the functor from the category of quasi-coherent O_S-modules to the category of descent data with respect to U is fully faithful.

nodes.title: Descent for modules · Definition 023G
nodes.summary: Let R → A be a ring map. • A descent datum (N, φ) for modules with respect to R → A is given by an A-module N and an isomorphism of A ⊗_R A-modules φ : N ⊗_R A → A ⊗_R N such that the cocycle condition holds: the diagram of A ⊗_R A ⊗_R A-module maps xymatrix N ⊗_R A ⊗_R A ar[rr]_φ_02 ar[rd]_φ_01 & & A ⊗_R A ⊗_R N & A ⊗_R N ⊗_R A ar[ru]_φ_12 & commutes (see below for notation). • A morphism (N, φ) → (N', φ') of descent data is a morphism of A-modules ψ : N → N' such that…

nodes.title: Descent for modules · Lemma 023H
nodes.summary: Let R → A be a ring map. Given a descent datum (N, φ) we can associate to it a cosimplicial (A/R)_bullet-module N_bullet by the rules N_n = N_n, n and given β : [n] → [m] setting we define N_bullet(β) = (φ^m_β(n)m) ∘ N_β, n : N_n, n → N_m, m. This procedure is functorial in the descent datum.

nodes.title: Descent for modules · Lemma 023I
nodes.summary: Let R → A be a ring map. Let M be an R-module. The cosimplicial (A/R)_bullet-module associated to the canonical descent datum is isomorphic to the cosimplicial module (A/R)_bullet ⊗_R M.

nodes.title: Descent for modules · Definition 023J
nodes.summary: Let R → A be a ring map. We say a descent datum (N, φ) is effective if there exists an R-module M and an isomorphism of descent data from (M ⊗_R A, can) to (N, φ).

nodes.title: Descent for modules · Lemma 023L
nodes.summary: Suppose that R → A has a section. Then for any R-module M the extended cochain complex ([Tag 023K]) is exact.

nodes.title: Descent for modules · Lemma 023M
nodes.summary: Suppose that R → A is faithfully flat, see Algebra, Definition [Tag 00HB]. Then for any R-module M the extended cochain complex ([Tag 023K]) is exact.

nodes.title: Descent for modules · Lemma 039W
nodes.summary: Let R → A be a faithfully flat ring map. Let (N, φ) be a descent datum. Then (N, φ) is effective if and only if the canonical map A ⊗_R H^0(s(N_bullet)) → N is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Descent for modules · Lemma 039X
nodes.summary: Let R → A be a faithfully flat ring map, and let R → R' be faithfully flat. Set A' = R' ⊗_R A. If all descent data for R' → A' are effective, then so are all descent data for R → A.

nodes.title: Descent for modules · Proposition 023N
nodes.summary: Effective descent for modules along faithfully flat ring maps. Let R → A be a faithfully flat ring map. Then • any descent datum on modules with respect to R → A is effective, • the functor M ↦ (A ⊗_R M, can) from R-modules to the category of descent data is an equivalence, and • the inverse functor is given by (N, φ) ↦ H^0(s(N_bullet)).

nodes.title: Descent for universally injective morphisms · Definition 08WH
nodes.summary: A split equalizer is a diagram ([Tag 08WG]) with g_1 ∘ f = g_2 ∘ f for which there exist auxiliary morphisms h : B → A and i : C → B such that h ∘ f = 1_A, f ∘ h = i ∘ g_1, i ∘ g_2 = 1_B.

nodes.title: Descent for universally injective morphisms · Definition 08WL
nodes.summary: A ring map f: R → S is universally injective if it is universally injective as a morphism in Mod_R.

nodes.title: Descent for universally injective morphisms · Lemma 08WP
nodes.summary: Any faithfully flat ring map is universally injective.

nodes.title: Descent for universally injective morphisms · Definition 08WQ
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. Define the contravariant functor C : Mod_R → Mod_R by setting C(M) = Hom_Ab(M, Q/Z), with the R-action on C(M) given by rf(s) = f(rs).

nodes.title: Descent for universally injective morphisms · Lemma 08WR
nodes.summary: For a ring R, the functor C : Mod_R → Mod_R is exact and reflects injections and surjections.

nodes.title: Descent for universally injective morphisms · Lemma 08WU
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. A morphism f: M → N in Mod_R is universally injective if and only if C(f): C(N) → C(M) is a split surjection.

nodes.title: Descent for universally injective morphisms · Definition 08WY
nodes.summary: The functor f^*: Mod_R → DD_S/R is called base extension along f. We say that f is a descent morphism for modules if f^* is fully faithful. We say that f is an effective descent morphism for modules if f^* is an equivalence of categories.

nodes.summary: For (M,theta) ∈ DD_S/R, the diagram xymatrix@C=8pc M ar[r]^theta ∘ (1_M ⊗ δ_0^1) & M ⊗_S, δ_1^1 S_2 ar@<1ex>[r]^(theta ⊗ δ_2^2) ∘ (1_M ⊗ δ^2_0) ar@<-1ex>[r]_1_M ⊗ S_2 ⊗ δ^2_1 & M ⊗_S, δ_12^1 S_3 is a split equalizer.

nodes.title: Descent for universally injective morphisms · Definition 08X5

nodes.summary: If f is universally injective, then the diagram xymatrix@C=8pc f_*(M, theta) ⊗_R S ar[r]^theta ∘ (1_M ⊗ δ_0^1) & M ⊗_S, δ_1^1 S_2 ar@<1ex>[r]^(theta ⊗ δ_2^2) ∘ (1_M ⊗ δ^2_0) ar@<-1ex>[r]_1_M ⊗ S_2 ⊗ δ^2_1 & M ⊗_S, δ_12^1 S_3 obtained by tensoring ([Tag 08X6]) over R with S is an equalizer.

nodes.title: Descent for universally injective morphisms · Theorem 08XA
nodes.summary: The following conditions are equivalent. • [(a)] The morphism f is a descent morphism for modules. • [(b)] The morphism f is an effective descent morphism for modules. • [(c)] The morphism f is universally injective.

nodes.title: Descent for universally injective morphisms · Lemma 08XC
nodes.summary: If M ∈ Mod_R is flat, then C(M) is an injective R-module.

nodes.title: Descent for universally injective morphisms · Theorem 08XD
nodes.summary: If M ⊗_R S has one of the following properties as an S-module • [(a)] finitely generated; • [(b)] finitely presented; • [(c)] flat; • [(d)] faithfully flat; • [(e)] finite projective; then so does M as an R-module (and conversely).

nodes.title: Descent for universally injective morphisms · Theorem 08XE
nodes.summary: If A ⊗_R S has one of the following properties as an S-algebra • [(a)] of finite type; • [(b)] of finite presentation; • [(c)] formally unramified; • [(d)] unramified; • [(e)] étale; then so does A as an R-algebra (and of course conversely).

nodes.title: Fpqc descent of quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 023S
nodes.summary: Let S be an affine scheme. Let U = (f_i : U_i → S)_i = 1, …, n be a standard fpqc covering of S, see Topologies, Definition [Tag 022F]. Any descent datum on quasi-coherent sheaves for U = (U_i → S) is effective. Moreover, the functor from the category of quasi-coherent O_S-modules to the category of descent data with respect to U is fully faithful.

nodes.title: Fpqc descent of quasi-coherent sheaves · Proposition 023T
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let U = (φ_i : U_i → S) be an fpqc covering, see Topologies, Definition [Tag 022B]. Any descent datum on quasi-coherent sheaves for U = (U_i → S) is effective. Moreover, the functor from the category of quasi-coherent O_S-modules to the category of descent data with respect to U is fully faithful.

nodes.title: Galois descent for quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 0CDR
nodes.summary: Let k'/k be a (finite) Galois extension with Galois group G. Let X be a scheme over k. The category of quasi-coherent O_X-modules is equivalent to the category of systems (F, (φ_σ)_σ ∈ G) where • F is a quasi-coherent module on X_k', • φ_σ : F → f_σ^*F is an isomorphism of modules, • φ_στ = f_σ^*φ_τ ∘ φ_σ for all σ, τ ∈ G. Here f_σ = id_X × Spec(σ) : X_k' → X_k'.

nodes.title: Galois descent for quasi-coherent sheaves · Lemma 0D1V
nodes.summary: Let X → Y, G, and f_σ : X → X be as above. The category of quasi-coherent O_Y-modules is equivalent to the category of systems (F, (φ_σ)_σ ∈ G) where • F is a quasi-coherent O_X-module, • φ_σ : F → f_σ^*F is an isomorphism of modules, • φ_στ = f_σ^*φ_τ ∘ φ_σ for all σ, τ ∈ G.

nodes.title: Descent of finiteness properties of modules · Lemma 05AZ
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. Let (f_i : X_i → X)_i ∈ I be an fpqc covering such that each f_i^*F is a finite type O_X_i-module. Then F is a finite type O_X-module.

nodes.title: Descent of finiteness properties of modules · Lemma 05B0

nodes.title: Descent of finiteness properties of modules · Lemma 082U

nodes.title: Descent of finiteness properties of modules · Lemma 05B2

nodes.title: Germs of schemes · Definition 04QR
nodes.summary: Germs of schemes. • A pair (X, x) consisting of a scheme X and a point x ∈ X is called the germ of X at x. • A morphism of germs f : (X, x) → (S, s) is an equivalence class of morphisms of schemes f : U → S with f(x) = s where U ⊂ X is an open neighbourhood of x. Two such f, f' are said to be equivalent if and only if f and f' agree in some open neighbourhood of x. • We define the composition of morphisms of germs by composing representatives (this is well defined).

nodes.title: Germs of schemes · Definition 04QS
