Assume • the morphisms f_i'i : X_i' → X_i are affine, • the morphisms g_i'i : Y_i' → Y_i are affine, • the morphisms X_i → Y_i are closed immersions. Then lim X_i → lim Y_i is a closed immersion.

nodes.title: Limits of algebraic spaces · Lemma 0CUI
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let I be a directed set. Let (X_i, f_i'i) be an inverse systems over I of algebraic spaces over S. If X_i is reduced for all i, then X is reduced.

nodes.title: Limits of algebraic spaces · Lemma 0CP4
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X → Y be a morphism of algebraic spaces over S. The equivalent conditions (1) and (2) of Proposition [Tag 04AK] are also equivalent to • [(3)] for every directed limit T = lim T_i of quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic spaces T_i over S with affine transition morphisms the diagram of sets xymatrix colim_i Mor(T_i, X) ar[r] ar[d] & Mor(T, X) ar[d] colim_i Mor(T_i, Y) ar[r] & Mor(T, Y) is a fibre product diagram.

nodes.title: Descending properties · Lemma 0CUJ
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X = lim_i ∈ I X_i be the limit of a directed inverse system of algebraic spaces over S with affine transition morphisms (Lemma [Tag 07SF]). If each X_i is decent (for example quasi-separated or locally separated) then |X| = lim_i |X_i| as sets.

nodes.title: Descending properties · Lemma 086V
nodes.summary: With same notation and assumptions as in Lemma [Tag 0CUJ] we have |X| = lim_i |X_i| as topological spaces.

nodes.title: Descending properties · Lemma 086W
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X = lim_i ∈ I X_i be the limit of a directed inverse system of algebraic spaces over S with affine transition morphisms (Lemma [Tag 07SF]). If each X_i is quasi-compact and nonempty, then |X| is nonempty.

nodes.title: Descending properties · Lemma 0CUK
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X = lim_i ∈ I X_i be the limit of a directed inverse system of algebraic spaces over S with affine transition morphisms (Lemma [Tag 07SF]). Let x ∈ |X| with images x_i ∈ |X_i|. If each X_i is decent, then overline(x) = lim_i overline(x_i) as sets and as algebraic spaces if endowed with reduced induced scheme structure.

nodes.title: Descending properties · Lemma 07SI
nodes.summary: Notation and assumptions as in Situation [Tag 084R]. Suppose that F_0 is a quasi-coherent sheaf on X_0. Set F_i = f_0i^*F_0 for i ≥ 0 and set F = f_0^*F_0. Then Γ(X, F) = colim_i ≥ 0 Γ(X_i, F_i)

nodes.title: Descending properties · Lemma 0827
nodes.summary: Notation and assumptions as in Situation [Tag 084R]. For any quasi-compact open subspace U ⊂ X there exists an i and a quasi-compact open U_i ⊂ X_i whose inverse image in X is U.

nodes.title: Descending properties · Lemma 084S
nodes.summary: Notation and assumptions as in Situation [Tag 084R]. Let f_0 : Y_0 → Z_0 be a morphism of algebraic spaces over X_0. Assume (a) Y_0 → X_0 and Z_0 → X_0 are representable, (b) Y_0, Z_0 quasi-compact and quasi-separated, (c) f_0 locally of finite presentation, and (d) Y_0 ×_X_0 X → Z_0 ×_X_0 X an isomorphism. Then there exists an i ≥ 0 such that Y_0 ×_X_0 X_i → Z_0 ×_X_0 X_i is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Descending properties · Lemma 084T
nodes.summary: Notation and assumptions as in Situation [Tag 084R]. If X is separated, then X_i is separated for some i ∈ I.

nodes.title: Descending properties · Lemma 07SQ
nodes.summary: Notation and assumptions as in Situation [Tag 084R]. If X is affine, then there exists an i such that X_i is affine.

nodes.title: Descending properties · Lemma 07SR
nodes.summary: Notation and assumptions as in Situation [Tag 084R]. If X is a scheme, then there exists an i such that X_i is a scheme.

nodes.title: Descending properties · Lemma 0828
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let B be an algebraic space over S. Let X = lim X_i be a directed limit of algebraic spaces over B with affine transition morphisms. Let Y → X be a morphism of algebraic spaces over B. • If Y → X is a closed immersion, X_i quasi-compact, and Y → B locally of finite type, then Y → X_i is a closed immersion for i large enough. • If Y → X is an immersion, X_i quasi-separated, Y → B locally of finite type, and Y quasi-compact, then Y → X_i is an immersion…

nodes.title: Descending properties · Lemma 086X
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let Y be an algebraic space over S. Let X = lim X_i be a directed limit of algebraic spaces over Y with affine transition morphisms. Assume • Y is quasi-separated, • X_i is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, • the morphism X → Y is separated. Then X_i → Y is separated for all i large enough.

nodes.title: Descending properties · Lemma 0A0R
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let Y be an algebraic space over S. Let X = lim X_i be a directed limit of algebraic spaces over Y with affine transition morphisms. Assume • Y quasi-compact and quasi-separated, • X_i quasi-compact and quasi-separated, • X → Y affine. Then X_i → Y is affine for i large enough.

nodes.title: Descending properties · Lemma 0A0S
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let Y be an algebraic space over S. Let X = lim X_i be a directed limit of algebraic spaces over Y with affine transition morphisms. Assume • Y quasi-compact and quasi-separated, • X_i quasi-compact and quasi-separated, • the transition morphisms X_i' → X_i are finite, • X_i → Y locally of finite type • X → Y integral. Then X_i → Y is finite for i large enough.

nodes.title: Descending properties · Lemma 0A0T
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let Y be an algebraic space over S. Let X = lim X_i be a directed limit of algebraic spaces over Y with affine transition morphisms. Assume • Y quasi-compact and quasi-separated, • X_i quasi-compact and quasi-separated, • the transition morphisms X_i' → X_i are closed immersions, • X_i → Y locally of finite type • X → Y is a closed immersion. Then X_i → Y is a closed immersion for i large enough.

nodes.title: Descending properties of morphisms · Lemma 07SL
nodes.summary: With notation and assumptions as in Situation [Tag 084W]. If • f is étale, • f_0 is locally of finite presentation, then f_i is étale for some i ≥ 0.

nodes.title: Descending properties of morphisms · Lemma 0CN2
nodes.summary: With notation and assumptions as in Situation [Tag 084W]. If • f is smooth, • f_0 is locally of finite presentation, then f_i is smooth for some i ≥ 0.

nodes.title: Descending properties of morphisms · Lemma 07SN
nodes.summary: With notation and assumptions as in Situation [Tag 084W]. If • f is surjective, • f_0 is locally of finite presentation, then f_i is surjective for some i ≥ 0.

nodes.title: Descending properties of morphisms · Lemma 084X
nodes.summary: Notation and assumptions as in Situation [Tag 084W]. If • f is universally injective, • f_0 is locally of finite type, then f_i is universally injective for some i ≥ 0.

nodes.title: Descending properties of morphisms · Lemma 084Y
nodes.summary: Notation and assumptions as in Situation [Tag 084W]. If f is affine, then f_i is affine for some i ≥ 0.

nodes.title: Descending properties of morphisms · Lemma 084Z
nodes.summary: Notation and assumptions as in Situation [Tag 084W]. If • f is finite, • f_0 is locally of finite type, then f_i is finite for some i ≥ 0.

nodes.title: Descending properties of morphisms · Lemma 0850
nodes.summary: Notation and assumptions as in Situation [Tag 084W]. If • f is a closed immersion, • f_0 is locally of finite type, then f_i is a closed immersion for some i ≥ 0.

nodes.title: Descending properties of morphisms · Lemma 0851
nodes.summary: Notation and assumptions as in Situation [Tag 084W]. If f is separated, then f_i is separated for some i ≥ 0.

nodes.title: Descending properties of morphisms · Lemma 0852
nodes.summary: Notation and assumptions as in Situation [Tag 084W]. If • f is an isomorphism, • f_0 is locally of finite presentation, then f_i is an isomorphism for some i ≥ 0.

nodes.title: Descending properties of morphisms · Lemma 07SM
nodes.summary: Notation and assumptions as in Situation [Tag 084W]. If • f is a monomorphism, • f_0 is locally of finite type, then f_i is a monomorphism for some i ≥ 0.

nodes.title: Descending properties of morphisms · Lemma 08K0
nodes.summary: Notation and assumptions as in Situation [Tag 084W]. Let F_0 be a quasi-coherent O_X_0-module and denote F_i the pullback to X_i and F the pullback to X. If • F is flat over Y, • F_0 is of finite presentation, and • f_0 is locally of finite presentation, then F_i is flat over Y_i for some i ≥ 0. In particular, if f_0 is locally of finite presentation and f is flat, then f_i is flat for some i ≥ 0.

nodes.title: Descending properties of morphisms · Lemma 08K1
nodes.summary: Assumptions and notation as in Situation [Tag 084W]. If • f is proper, and • f_0 is locally of finite type, then there exists an i such that f_i is proper.

nodes.title: Descending properties of morphisms · Lemma 0D4K
nodes.summary: Assumptions and notation as in Situation [Tag 084W]. Let d ≥ 0. If • f has relative dimension ≤ d (Morphisms of Spaces, Definition [Tag 06LR]), and • f_0 is locally of finite type, then there exists an i such that f_i has relative dimension ≤ d.

nodes.title: Descending relative objects · Lemma 07SK
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let I be a directed set. Let (X_i, f_ii') be an inverse system over I of algebraic spaces over S. Assume • the morphisms f_ii' : X_i → X_i' are affine, • the spaces X_i are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let X = lim_i X_i. Then the category of algebraic spaces of finite presentation over X is the colimit over I of the categories of algebraic spaces of finite presentation over X_i.

nodes.title: Descending relative objects · Lemma 07V7
nodes.summary: With notation and assumptions as in Lemma [Tag 07SK]. The category of O_X-modules of finite presentation is the colimit over I of the categories O_X_i-modules of finite presentation.

nodes.title: Descending relative objects · Lemma 0D2X
nodes.summary: With notation and assumptions as in Lemma [Tag 07SK]. Then • any finite locally free O_X-module is the pullback of a finite locally free O_X_i-module for some i, • any invertible O_X-module is the pullback of an invertible O_X_i-module for some i.

nodes.title: Absolute Noetherian approximation · Proposition 07SU
nodes.summary: Our proof follows closely the proof given in [CLO]. Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over Spec(Z). There exist a directed set I and an inverse system of algebraic spaces (X_i, f_ii') over I such that • the transition morphisms f_ii' are affine • each X_i is quasi-separated and of finite type over Z, and • X = lim X_i.

nodes.title: Applications · Lemma 07V9
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over S. Every quasi-coherent O_X-module is a filtered colimit of finitely presented O_X-modules.

nodes.title: Applications · Lemma 0829
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over S. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. Then F is the directed colimit of its finite type quasi-coherent submodules.

nodes.title: Applications · Lemma 086Y
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over S. Let F be a finite type quasi-coherent O_X-module. Then we can write F = lim F_i where each F_i is an O_X-module of finite presentation and all transition maps F_i → F_i' surjective.

nodes.title: Applications · Lemma 082A
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over S. Let A be a quasi-coherent O_X-algebra. Then A is a directed colimit of finitely presented quasi-coherent O_X-algebras.

nodes.title: Applications · Lemma 082B
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over S. Let A be a quasi-coherent O_X-algebra. Then A is the directed colimit of its finite type quasi-coherent O_X-subalgebras.

nodes.title: Applications · Lemma 086Z
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over S. Let A be a finite quasi-coherent O_X-algebra. Then A = colim A_i is a directed colimit of finite and finitely presented quasi-coherent O_X-algebras with surjective transition maps.

nodes.title: Applications · Lemma 082C
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over S. Let A be an integral quasi-coherent O_X-algebra. Then • A is the directed colimit of its finite quasi-coherent O_X-subalgebras, and • A is a directed colimit of finite and finitely presented O_X-algebras.

nodes.title: Applications · Lemma 0853
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over S. Let U ⊂ X be a quasi-compact open. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. Let G ⊂ F|_U be a quasi-coherent O_U-submodule which is of finite type. Then there exists a quasi-coherent submodule G' ⊂ F which is of finite type such that G'|_U = G.

nodes.title: Relative approximation · Lemma 0GS3
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic spaces over Z. Then there exists a direct set I and an inverse system (f_i : X_i → Y_i) of morphisms algebraic spaces over I, such that the transition morphisms X_i → X_i' and Y_i → Y_i' are affine, such that X_i and Y_i are quasi-separated and of finite type over Z, and such that (X → Y) = lim (X_i → Y_i).

nodes.title: Relative approximation · Lemma 09NS
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a morphism of algebraic spaces over S. Assume that • X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and • Y is quasi-separated. Then X = lim X_i is a limit of a directed inverse system of algebraic spaces X_i of finite presentation over Y with affine transition morphisms over Y.

nodes.title: Finite type closed in finite presentation · Lemma 0870
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be an affine morphism of algebraic spaces over S. If Y quasi-compact and quasi-separated, then X is a directed limit X = lim X_i with each X_i affine and of finite presentation over Y.
nodes.section: Finite type closed in finite presentation

nodes.title: Finite type closed in finite presentation · Lemma 09YA
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be an integral morphism of algebraic spaces over S. Assume Y quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then X can be written as a directed limit X = lim X_i where X_i are finite and of finite presentation over Y.
nodes.section: Finite type closed in finite presentation

nodes.title: Finite type closed in finite presentation · Lemma 07VR
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a finite morphism of algebraic spaces over S. Assume Y quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then X can be written as a directed limit X = lim X_i where the transition maps are closed immersions and the objects X_i are finite and of finite presentation over Y.
nodes.section: Finite type closed in finite presentation

nodes.title: Finite type closed in finite presentation · Lemma 0A0U
nodes.summary: Closed immersions of qcqs algebraic spaces can be approximated by finitely presented closed immersions. Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a closed immersion of algebraic spaces over S. Assume Y quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then X can be written as a directed limit X = lim X_i where the transition maps are closed immersions and the morphisms X_i → Y are closed immersions of finite presentation.
nodes.section: Finite type closed in finite presentation

nodes.title: Finite type closed in finite presentation · Lemma 0871
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a morphism of algebraic spaces over S. Assume • f is locally of finite type and quasi-affine, and • Y is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then there exists a morphism of finite presentation f' : X' → Y and a closed immersion X → X' over Y.
nodes.section: Finite type closed in finite presentation

nodes.title: Finite type closed in finite presentation · Lemma 0872
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a morphism of algebraic spaces over S. Assume: • f is of locally of finite type. • X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and • Y is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then there exists a morphism of finite presentation f' : X' → Y and a closed immersion X → X' of algebraic spaces over Y.
nodes.section: Finite type closed in finite presentation

nodes.title: Finite type closed in finite presentation · Proposition 0873
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. f : X → Y be a morphism of algebraic spaces over S. Assume • f is of finite type and separated, and • Y is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then there exists a separated morphism of finite presentation f' : X' → Y and a closed immersion X → X' over Y.

nodes.title: Approximating proper morphisms · Lemma 0A0W
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a proper morphism of algebraic spaces over S with Y quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then X = lim X_i is a directed limit of algebraic spaces X_i proper and of finite presentation over Y and with transition morphisms and morphisms X → X_i closed immersions.

nodes.title: Approximating proper morphisms · Lemma 0A0X
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a proper morphism of algebraic spaces over Z with Y quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then there exists a directed set I, an inverse system (f_i : X_i → Y_i) of morphisms of algebraic spaces over I, such that the transition morphisms X_i → X_i' and Y_i → Y_i' are affine, such that f_i is proper and of finite presentation, such that Y_i is of finite presentation over Z, and such that (X → Y) = lim (X_i → Y_i).

nodes.title: Approximating proper morphisms · Lemma 08K2
nodes.summary: Assumptions and notation as in Situation [Tag 084W]. Let F_0 be a quasi-coherent O_X_0-module. Denote F and F_i the pullbacks of F_0 to X and X_i. Assume • f_0 is locally of finite type, • F_0 is of finite type, • the scheme theoretic support of F is proper over Y. Then the scheme theoretic support of F_i is proper over Y_i for some i.

nodes.title: Embedding into affine space · Lemma 088L
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : U → X be a morphism of algebraic spaces over S. Assume U is an affine scheme, f is locally of finite type, and X quasi-separated and locally separated. Then there exists an immersion U → A^n_X over X.

nodes.title: Embedding into affine space · Lemma 088N
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : Y → X be a morphism of algebraic spaces over S. Assume X Noetherian and f of finite presentation. Then there exists a dense open V ⊂ Y and an immersion V → A^n_X.

nodes.title: Sections with support in a closed subset · Lemma 0855
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space. Let U ⊂ X be an open subspace. The following are equivalent: • U → X is quasi-compact, • U is quasi-compact, and • there exists a finite type quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals I ⊂ O_X such that |X| setminus |U| = |V(I)|.

nodes.title: Sections with support in a closed subset · Lemma 0856
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be an algebraic space over S. Let I ⊂ O_X be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. Consider the sheaf of O_X-modules F' which associates to every object U of X_etale the module F'(U) = (s ∈ F(U) mid Is = 0) Assume I is of finite type. Then • F' is a quasi-coherent sheaf of O_X-modules, • for affine U in X_etale we have F'(U) = (s ∈ F(U) mid I(U)s = 0), and • F'_x = (s ∈ F_x mid I_x s = 0).

nodes.title: Sections with support in a closed subset · Definition 0857
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be an algebraic space over S. Let I ⊂ O_X be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of finite type. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. The subsheaf F' ⊂ F defined in Lemma [Tag 0856] above is called the subsheaf of sections annihilated by I.

nodes.title: Sections with support in a closed subset · Lemma 0858
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces over S. Let I ⊂ O_Y be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of finite type. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. Let F' ⊂ F be the subsheaf of sections annihilated by f^-1IO_X. Then f_*F' ⊂ f_*F is the subsheaf of sections annihilated by I.

nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be an algebraic space over S. Let T ⊂ |X| be a closed subset and let U ⊂ X be the open subspace such that T amalg |U| = |X|. nodes.title: Sections with support in a closed subset · Definition 085A
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be an algebraic space over S. Let T ⊂ |X| be a closed subset whose complement corresponds to an open subspace U ⊂ X with quasi-compact inclusion morphism U → X. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. The quasi-coherent subsheaf F' ⊂ F defined in Lemma [Tag 0859] above is called the subsheaf of sections supported on T.

nodes.title: Sections with support in a closed subset · Lemma 085B
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces over S. Let T ⊂ |Y| be a closed subset. Assume |Y| setminus T corresponds to an open subspace V ⊂ Y such that V → Y is quasi-compact. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. Let F' ⊂ F be the subsheaf of sections supported on |f|^-1T. Then f_*F' ⊂ f_*F is the subsheaf of sections supported on T.

nodes.title: Characterizing affine spaces · Lemma 07VS
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a morphism of algebraic spaces over S. Assume that f is surjective and finite, and assume that X is affine. Then Y is affine.

nodes.title: Characterizing affine spaces · Proposition 07VT
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a morphism of algebraic spaces over S. Assume that X is affine and f is surjective and universally closed. Then Y is affine.

nodes.title: Characterizing affine spaces · Lemma 07VU
nodes.summary: [CLO] Let S be a scheme. Let X be an algebraic space over S. If X_red is a scheme, then X is a scheme.

nodes.title: Characterizing affine spaces · Lemma 07VV
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a morphism of algebraic spaces over S. Assume f is integral and induces a bijection |X| → |Y|. Then X is a scheme if and only if Y is a scheme.

nodes.title: Characterizing affine spaces · Lemma 08B2
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → B and B' → B be morphisms of algebraic spaces over S. Assume • B' → B is a closed immersion, • |B'| → |B| is bijective, • X ×_B B' → B' is a closed immersion, and • X → B is of finite type or B' → B is of finite presentation. Then f : X → B is a closed immersion.

nodes.title: Finite cover by a scheme · Proposition 09YC
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over S. • There exists a surjective finite morphism Y → X of finite presentation where Y is a scheme, • given a surjective étale morphism U → X we may choose Y → X such that for every y ∈ Y there is an open neighbourhood V ⊂ Y such that V → X factors through U.

nodes.title: Finite cover by a scheme · Lemma 0GUM
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be an integral morphism of algebraic spaces over S. Assume Y quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let V ⊂ Y be a quasi-compact open subspace such that f^-1(V) → V is finite and of finite presentation. Then X can be written as a directed limit X = lim X_i where f_i : X_i → Y are finite and of finite presentation such that f^-1(V) → f_i^-1(V) is an isomorphism for all i.

nodes.title: Finite cover by a scheme · Lemma 0GUN
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over S such that |X| has finitely many irreducible components. • There exists a surjective finite morphism f : Y → X of finite presentation where Y is a scheme such that f is finite étale over a quasi-compact dense open U ⊂ X, • given a surjective étale morphism V → X we may choose Y → X such that for every y ∈ Y there is an open neighbourhood W ⊂ Y such that W → X factors through V.

nodes.title: Finite cover by a scheme · Lemma 0GUP
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over S. There exists a t ≥ 0 and closed subspaces X ⊃ Z_0 ⊃ Z_1 ⊃ … ⊃ Z_t = ∅ such that Z_i → X is of finite presentation, Z_0 ⊂ X is a thickening, and for each i = 0, … t - 1 there exists a scheme Y_i, a surjective, finite, and finitely presented morphism Y_i → Z_i which is finite étale over Z_i setminus Z_i + 1.

nodes.title: Obtaining schemes · Lemma 0B7Y
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over S. If X is not a scheme, then there exists a closed subspace Z ⊂ X such that Z is not a scheme, but every proper closed subspace Z' ⊂ Z is a scheme.

nodes.title: Obtaining schemes · Lemma 0B7Z
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over S. Assume that every proper closed subspace Z ⊂ X is a scheme, but X is not a scheme. Then X is reduced and irreducible.

nodes.title: Obtaining schemes · Lemma 0B80
nodes.summary: Let f: X → S be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism from an algebraic space to a scheme S. If for every x ∈ |X| with image s = f(x) ∈ S the algebraic space X ×_S Spec(O_S,s) is a scheme, then X is a scheme.

nodes.title: Obtaining schemes · Lemma 0B81
nodes.summary: Let φ : X → Spec(A) be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism from an algebraic space to an affine scheme. If X is not a scheme, then there exists an ideal I ⊂ A such that the base change X_A/I is not a scheme, but for every I ⊂ I', I not = I' the base change X_A/I' is a scheme.

nodes.title: Glueing in closed fibres · Lemma 0E8Z
nodes.summary: Let S = U ∪ W be an open covering of a scheme. Then the functor FP_S → FP_U ×_FP_U ∩ W FP_W given by base change is an equivalence where FP_T is the category of algebraic spaces of finite presentation over the scheme T.

nodes.title: Glueing in closed fibres · Lemma 0E90
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let s ∈ S be a closed point such that U = S setminus (s) → S is quasi-compact. With V = Spec(O_S, s) setminus (s) there is an equivalence of categories FP_S → FP_U ×_FP_V FP_Spec(O_S, s) where FP_T is the category of algebraic spaces of finite presentation over T.

nodes.title: Glueing in closed fibres · Lemma 0E91
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let U ⊂ S be a retrocompact open. Let s ∈ S be a point in the complement of U. With V = Spec(O_S, s) ∩ U there is an equivalence of categories colim_s ∈ U' ⊃ U open FP_U' → FP_U ×_FP_V FP_Spec(O_S, s) where FP_T is the category of algebraic spaces of finite presentation over T.

nodes.title: Glueing in closed fibres · Lemma 0E92
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let s_1, …, s_n ∈ S be pairwise distinct closed points such that U = S setminus (s_1, …, s_n) → S is quasi-compact. With S_i = Spec(O_S, s_i) and U_i = S_i setminus (s_i) there is an equivalence of categories FP_S → FP_U ×_(FP_U_1 × … × FP_U_n) (FP_S_1 × … × FP_S_n) where FP_T is the category of algebraic spaces of finite presentation over T.

nodes.title: Application to modifications · Lemma 0BGY
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Consider a separated étale morphism f : V → W of algebraic spaces over S. Assume there exists a closed subspace T ⊂ W such that f^-1T → T is an isomorphism. Then, with W^0 = W setminus T and V^0 = f^-1W^0 the base change functor ( g : X → W morphism of algebraic spaces g^-1(W^0) → W^0 is an isomorphism ) → ( h : Y → V morphism of algebraic spaces h^-1(V^0) → V^0 is an isomorphism ) is an equivalence of categories.

nodes.summary: Notation and assumptions as in Lemma [Tag 0BGY]. Let g : X → W correspond to h : Y → V via the equivalence. Then g is quasi-compact, quasi-separated, separated, locally of finite presentation, of finite presentation, locally of finite type, of finite type, proper, integral, finite, and add more here if and only if h is so.

nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a decent algebraic space over S. Let x ∈ |X| be a closed point such that U = X setminus (x) → X is quasi-compact. With V = Spec(O_X, x^h) setminus ( m_x^h) the base change functor ( f : Y → X of finite presentation f^-1(U) → U is an isomorphism ) → ( g : Y → Spec(O_X, x^h) of finite presentation g^-1(V) → V is an isomorphism ) is an equivalence of categories.

nodes.title: Universally closed morphisms · Lemma 0CM9
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces over S. The following are equivalent • f is universally closed, • for every morphism Z → Y which is locally of finite presentation the map |X ×_Y Z| → |Z| is closed, and • there exists a scheme V and a surjective étale morphism V → Y such that |A^n × (X ×_Y V)| → |A^n × V| is closed for all n ≥ 0.

nodes.title: Universally closed morphisms · Lemma 0CMA
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a morphism of algebraic spaces over S. Assume f separated and of finite type. The following are equivalent • The morphism f is proper. • For any morphism Y → Z which is locally of finite presentation the map |X ×_Y Z| → |Z| is closed, and • there exists a scheme V and a surjective étale morphism V → Y such that |A^n × (X ×_Y V)| → |A^n × V| is closed for all n ≥ 0.

nodes.title: Descending finite type spaces · Lemma 0CP7
nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 0CP6]. Let X → B be a quasi-separated and finite type morphism of algebraic spaces. Then there exists an i ∈ I and a diagram vcenter xymatrix X ar[r] ar[d] & W ar[d] B ar[r] & B_i such that W → B_i is of finite type and such that the induced morphism X → B ×_B_i W is a closed immersion.

nodes.title: Descending finite type spaces · Lemma 0CP9
nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 0CP6]. Let X → B be a quasi-separated and finite type morphism of algebraic spaces. Given i ∈ I and a diagram vcenter xymatrix X ar[r] ar[d] & W ar[d] B ar[r] & B_i as in ([Tag 0CP8]) for i' ≥ i let X_i' be the scheme theoretic image of X → B_i' ×_B_i W. Then X = lim_i' ≥ i X_i'.

nodes.summary: In Situation [Tag 0CP6]. Let f : X → Y be a morphism of algebraic spaces quasi-separated and of finite type over B. nodes.title: Associated and weakly associated points · Lemma 0CTY

nodes.title: Associated and weakly associated points · Lemma 0CUL
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be an algebraic space over S. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. Let x ∈ |X|. If • x ∈ Supp(F) • x is a codimension 0 point of X (Properties of Spaces, Definition [Tag 04NA]). Then x ∈ WeakAss(F). If F is a finite type O_X-module with scheme theoretic support Z (Morphisms of Spaces, Definition [Tag 07U1]) and x is a codimension 0 point of Z, then x ∈ WeakAss(F).

nodes.title: Associated and weakly associated points · Lemma 0CUM
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be an algebraic space over S. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. Let x ∈ |X|. If • X is decent (for example quasi-separated or locally separated), • x ∈ Supp(F) • x is not a specialization of another point in Supp(F). Then x ∈ WeakAss(F).

nodes.title: Associated and weakly associated points · Lemma 0CUN
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a locally Noetherian algebraic space over S. Let F be a coherent O_X-module. Then Ass(F) ∩ W is finite for every quasi-compact open W ⊂ |X|.

nodes.title: Associated and weakly associated points · Lemma 0CUP
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be an algebraic space over S. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. If U → X is an étale morphism such that WeakAss(F) ⊂ Im(|U| → |X|), then Γ(X, F) → Γ(U, F) is injective.

nodes.title: Associated and weakly associated points · Lemma 0CUQ
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces over S. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. Let y ∈ |Y| be a point which is not in the image of |f|. Then y is not weakly associated to f_*F.

nodes.title: Associated and weakly associated points · Lemma 0CUR
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be an algebraic space over S. Let φ : F → G be a map of quasi-coherent O_X-modules. Assume that for every x ∈ |X| at least one of the following happens • F_overlinex → G_overlinex is injective, or • x not ∈ WeakAss(F). Then φ is injective.

nodes.title: Associated and weakly associated points · Lemma 0EN1
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a reduced algebraic space over S. Then the weakly associated point of X are exactly the codimension 0 points of X.

nodes.title: Morphisms and weakly associated points · Lemma 0CU2

nodes.title: Morphisms and weakly associated points · Lemma 0CU8

nodes.title: Morphisms and weakly associated points · Lemma 0CU9

nodes.title: Morphisms and weakly associated points · Lemma 0CUS
nodes.summary: Let K/k be a field extension. Let X be an algebraic space over k. Let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module. Let y ∈ X_K with image x ∈ X. If y is a weakly associated point of the pullback F_K, then x is a weakly associated point of F.
