nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian ring and let I be an ideal. Let B be an object of ([Tag 0AL4]). If B is rig-étale over (A, I), then B is rig-smooth over (A, I).

nodes.title: Rig-étale algebras · Lemma 0ALQ
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian ring and let I be an ideal. Let B be a finite type A-algebra. • If Spec(B) → Spec(A) is étale over Spec(A) setminus V(I), then B^wedge satisfies the equivalent conditions of Lemma [Tag 0AJU]. • If B^wedge satisfies the equivalent conditions of Lemma [Tag 0AJU], then there exists g ∈ 1 + IB such that Spec(B_g) is étale over Spec(A) setminus V(I).

nodes.summary: Let (A_1, I_1) → (A_2, I_2) be as in Remark [Tag 0AL5] with A_1 and A_2 Noetherian. Let B_1 be in ([Tag 0AL4]) for (A_1, I_1). Let B_2 be the base change of B_1. nodes.title: Rig-étale algebras · Lemma 0GB2
nodes.summary: Let A_1 → A_2 be a map of Noetherian rings. Let I_i ⊂ A_i be an ideal such that V(I_1A_2) = V(I_2). Let B_1 be in ([Tag 0AL4]) for (A_1, I_1). Let B_2 be the base change of B_1 as in Remark [Tag 0AL5]. If B_1 is rig-étale over (A_1, I_1), then B_2 is rig-étale over (A_2, I_2).

nodes.summary: The rig-étale case of [Elkik] Let A be a Noetherian ring and I = (a) a principal ideal. Let B be an object of ([Tag 0AL4]) which is rig-étale over (A, I). Then there exists a finite type A-algebra C and an isomorphism B ≅ C^wedge.

nodes.title: Flat morphisms · Lemma 0GCG

nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian adic topological ring. Let q ⊂ A be a prime ideal. We say q is rig-closed if the equivalent conditions of Lemma [Tag 0GG8] are satisfied.

nodes.title: Rig-closed points · Lemma 0GGH

nodes.title: Rig-closed points · Lemma 0GGI

nodes.title: Rig-closed points · Lemma 0GGJ
nodes.summary: Let A be an adic Noetherian topological ring. Let p ⊂ A be a rig-closed prime. For any n ≥ 1 the ring map A/ p → A(x_1, …, x_n) ⊗_A A/ p = A/ p(x_1, …, x_n) is regular. In particular, the algebra A(x_1, …, x_n) ⊗_A kappa( p) is geometrically regular over kappa( p).

nodes.title: Rig-flat homomorphisms · Lemma 0GGL
nodes.summary: Let φ : A → B be a morphism in WAdm^adic* (Formal Spaces, Section [Tag 0ANA]). Assume φ is adic. The following are equivalent: • B_f is flat over A for all topologically nilpotent f ∈ A, • B_g is flat over A for all topologically nilpotent g ∈ B, • B_ q is flat over A for all primes q ⊂ B which do not contain an ideal of definition, • B_ q is flat over A for every rig-closed prime q ⊂ B, and • add more here.

nodes.title: Rig-flat homomorphisms · Definition 0GGM
nodes.summary: Let φ : A → B be a continuous ring homomorphism between adic Noetherian topological rings, i.e., φ is an arrow of WAdm^Noeth. We say φ is naively rig-flat if φ is adic, topologically of finite type, and satisfies the equivalent conditions of Lemma [Tag 0GGL].

nodes.title: Rig-flat homomorphisms · Definition 0GGP
nodes.summary: Let φ : A → B be a continuous ring homomorphism between adic Noetherian topological rings, i.e., φ is an arrow of WAdm^Noeth. We say φ is rig-flat if φ is adic, topologically of finite type, and for all f ∈ A the induced map A_(f) → B_(f) is naively rig-flat (Definition [Tag 0GGM]).

nodes.title: Rig-flat homomorphisms · Lemma 0GGQ
nodes.summary: Let φ : A → B be an arrow of WAdm^Noeth. If A/I is Jacobson for some (equivalently any) ideal of definition I ⊂ A and φ is naively rig-flat, then φ is rig-flat.

nodes.title: Rig-flat homomorphisms · Lemma 0GGR
nodes.summary: Let φ : A → B and A → C be arrows of WAdm^Noeth. Assume φ is rig-flat and A → C adic and topologically of finite type. Then C → B widehat⊗_A C is rig-flat.

nodes.title: Rig-flat homomorphisms · Lemma 0GGS

nodes.title: Rig-flat homomorphisms · Lemma 0GGT
nodes.summary: Consider a commutative diagram xymatrix B ar[r] & B' A ar[r] ar[u]^φ & A' ar[u]_φ' in WAdm^Noeth with all arrows adic and topologically of finite type. Assume A → A' flat and B → B' faithfully flat. If φ' is rig-flat, then φ is rig-flat.

nodes.title: Rig-flat morphisms · Lemma 0GH0

The following are equivalent: • [(a)] A → B satisfies the equivalent conditions of Lemma [Tag 0GBW] and there exists an ideal of definition I ⊂ B such that B is rig-smooth over (A, I), and • [(b)] A → B satisfies the equivalent conditions of Lemma [Tag 0GBW] and for all ideals of definition I ⊂ A the algebra B is rig-smooth over (A, I).

nodes.title: Rig-smooth homomorphisms · Definition 0GCJ
nodes.summary: Let φ : A → B be a continuous ring homomorphism between adic Noetherian topological rings, i.e., φ is an arrow of WAdm^Noeth. We say φ is rig-smooth if the equivalent conditions of Lemma [Tag 0GCI] hold.

nodes.title: Rig-smooth homomorphisms · Lemma 0GCK

nodes.title: Rig-smooth homomorphisms · Lemma 0GCM

nodes.title: Rig-smooth homomorphisms · Lemma 0GH1
nodes.summary: Let φ : A → B be an arrow of WAdm^Noeth. If φ is rig-smooth, then φ is rig-flat, and for any presentation B = A(x_1, …, x_n)/J and prime J ⊂ q ⊂ A(x_1, …, x_n) not containing an ideal of definition the ideal J_ q ⊂ A(x_1, …, x_n)_ q is generated by a regular sequence.

nodes.title: Rig-smooth morphisms · Lemma 0GCR

nodes.title: Rig-smooth morphisms · Lemma 0GCS

nodes.title: Rig-smooth morphisms · Lemma 0GH3

nodes.title: Rig-étale homomorphisms · Definition 0GCV

nodes.title: Rig-étale homomorphisms · Lemma 0AQL
nodes.summary: The property P(φ)="φ is rig-étale" on arrows of WAdm^Noeth is a local property as defined in Formal Spaces, Remark [Tag 0ANI].

nodes.title: Rig-étale homomorphisms · Lemma 0GCW
nodes.summary: Consider the properties P(φ)="φ is rig-étale" and Q(φ)="φ is adic" on arrows of WAdm^Noeth. Then P is stable under base change by Q as defined in Formal Spaces, Remark [Tag 0GBG].

nodes.title: Rig-étale homomorphisms · Lemma 0GCX
nodes.summary: The property P(φ)="φ is rig-étale" on arrows of WAdm^Noeth is stable under composition as defined in Formal Spaces, Remark [Tag 0GBK].

nodes.title: Rig-étale morphisms · Definition 0AQM

nodes.title: Rig-étale morphisms · Lemma 0GCZ
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a morphism of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces over S. The following are equivalent • f is rig-étale, • for every commutative diagram xymatrix U ar[d] ar[r] & V ar[d] X ar[r] & Y with U and V affine formal algebraic spaces, U → X and V → Y representable by algebraic spaces and étale, the morphism U → V corresponds to a rig-étale map in WAdm^Noeth, • there exists a covering (Y_j → Y) as in Formal Spaces, Definition [Tag 0AIM]…

nodes.summary: A rig-étale morphism of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces is locally of finite type.

nodes.title: Rig-étale morphisms · Lemma 0GD0
nodes.summary: A rig-étale morphism of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces is rig-smooth.

nodes.title: Rig-étale morphisms · Lemma 0GD1
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y and g : Z → Y be morphisms of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces over S. If f is rig-étale and g is adic, then the base change X ×_Y Z → Z is rig-étale.

nodes.title: Rig-étale morphisms · Lemma 0GD2
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y and g : Y → Z be morphisms of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces over S. If f and g are rig-étale, then so is g ∘ f.

nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y and g : Y → Z be a morphism of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces over S. If g ∘ f and g are rig-étale, then so is f.

nodes.summary: Rig-surjectivity of locally finite type morphisms is preserved under composition Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y and g : Y → Z be morphisms of formal algebraic spaces over S. Assume X, Y, Z are locally Noetherian and f and g locally of finite type. Then if f and g are rig-surjective, so is g ∘ f.

nodes.title: Rig-surjective morphisms · Lemma 0AQS

nodes.title: Rig-surjective morphisms · Lemma 0GH5

nodes.title: Rig-surjective morphisms · Lemma 0AQT
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y and g : Y → Z be morphisms of formal algebraic spaces over S. Assume X, Y, Z locally Noetherian and f and g locally of finite type. If g ∘ f : X → Z is rig-surjective, so is g : Y → Z.

nodes.title: Rig-surjective morphisms · Lemma 0AQU
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a morphism of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces which is representable by algebraic spaces, étale, and surjective. Then f is rig-surjective.

nodes.title: Rig-surjective morphisms · Lemma 0AQV
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a morphism of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces which is locally of finite type. Let (g_i : Y_i → Y) be a family of morphisms of formal algebraic spaces which are representable by algebraic spaces and étale such that coprod g_i is surjective. Then f is rig-surjective if and only if each f_i : X ×_Y Y_i → Y_i is rig-surjective.

nodes.title: Rig-surjective morphisms · Lemma 0AQX
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal I. Let B be an I-adically complete A-algebra. If A/I^n → B/I^nB is of finite type and flat for all n and faithfully flat for n = 1, then Spf(B) → Spf(A) is rig-surjective.

nodes.title: Rig-surjective morphisms · Lemma 0AQY
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal I. Let B be an I-adically complete A-algebra. Assume that • the I-torsion in A is 0, • A/I^n → B/I^nB is flat and of finite type for all n. Then Spf(B) → Spf(A) is rig-surjective if and only if A/I → B/IB is faithfully flat.

nodes.title: Rig-surjective morphisms · Lemma 0AR0
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a morphism of formal algebraic spaces. Assume X and Y are locally Noetherian, f locally of finite type, and f a monomorphism. Then f is rig surjective if and only if every adic morphism Spf(R) → Y where R is a complete discrete valuation ring factors through X.

nodes.title: Rig-surjective morphisms · Lemma 0GD5
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a morphism of formal algebraic spaces. Assume that X and Y are locally Noetherian and f is a closed immersion. The following are equivalent • f is rig-surjective, and • for every affine formal algebraic space V and every morphism V → Y which is representable by algebraic spaces and étale the morphism X ×_Y V → V corresponds to a surjective morphism B → A in WAdm^Noeth whose kernel J has the following property: IJ^n = 0 for some ideal of…

nodes.title: Rig-surjective morphisms · Lemma 0GD6
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a morphism of formal algebraic spaces. Assume that X and Y are locally Noetherian and f is a closed immersion. The following are equivalent • f is rig-smooth and rig-surjective, • f is rig-étale and rig-surjective, and • for every affine formal algebraic space V and every morphism V → Y which is representable by algebraic spaces and étale the morphism X ×_Y V → V corresponds to a surjective morphism B → A in WAdm^Noeth whose kernel J…

nodes.title: Rig-surjective morphisms · Lemma 0GH6
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y and g : Y → Z be morphisms of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces over S. Assume • g is locally of finite type, • f is rig-smooth (resp. rig-étale) and rig-surjective, • g ∘ f is rig-smooth (resp. rig-étale) then g is rig-smooth (resp. rig-étale).

nodes.title: Formal algebraic spaces over cdvrs · Lemma 0GD8
nodes.summary: Let X be a locally Noetherian formal algebraic space over a complete discrete valuation ring A. Then there exists a closed immersion X' → X of formal algebraic spaces such that X' is flat over A and such that any morphism Y → X of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces with Y flat over A factors through X'.

nodes.title: Formal algebraic spaces over cdvrs · Lemma 0GD9
nodes.summary: Let X be a locally Noetherian formal algebraic space which is locally of finite type over a complete discrete valuation ring A. Let X' ⊂ X be as in Lemma [Tag 0GD8]. If X → X ×_Spf(A) X is rig-étale and rig-surjective, then X' = Spf(A) or X' = ∅.

nodes.title: Formal algebraic spaces over cdvrs · Lemma 0GDA
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a morphism of formal algebraic spaces. Assume • X and Y are locally Noetherian, • f locally of finite type, • Δ_f : X → X ×_Y X is rig-étale and rig-surjective. Then f is rig surjective if and only if every adic morphism Spf(R) → Y where R is a complete discrete valuation ring lifts to a morphism Spf(R) → X.

nodes.title: The completion functor · Lemma 0AQ9
nodes.summary: In the situation above. If f is locally of finite type, then f_/T is locally of finite type.

nodes.title: The completion functor · Lemma 0GI0
nodes.summary: In the situation above. If f is étale, then f_/T is étale.

nodes.title: The completion functor · Lemma 0GDC
nodes.summary: In the situation above. If f is a closed immersion, then f_/T is a closed immersion.

nodes.title: The completion functor · Lemma 0GDD
nodes.summary: In the situation above. If f is proper, then f_/T is proper.

nodes.title: The completion functor · Lemma 0GDE
nodes.summary: In the situation above. If f is quasi-compact, then f_/T is quasi-compact.

nodes.title: The completion functor · Lemma 0GDG
nodes.summary: In the situation above. If f is (quasi-)separated, then f_/T is too.

nodes.title: The completion functor · Lemma 0GDH
nodes.summary: In the situation above. If X is locally Noetherian, f is locally of finite type, and U' → U is smooth, then f_/T is rig-smooth.

nodes.title: The completion functor · Lemma 0AR2
nodes.summary: In the situation above. If X is locally Noetherian, f is locally of finite type, and U' → U is étale, then f_/T is rig-étale.

nodes.title: The completion functor · Lemma 0AQW
nodes.summary: In the situation above. If X is locally Noetherian, f is proper, and U' → U is surjective, then f_/T is rig-surjective.

nodes.title: The completion functor · Lemma 0GDI
nodes.summary: In the situation above. If X is locally Noetherian, f is separated and locally of finite type, and U' → U is a monomorphism, then Δ_f_/T is rig-surjective.

nodes.title: Formal modifications · Definition 0GDK
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a morphism of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces over S. We say f is a formal modification if • f is a proper morphism (Formal Spaces, Definition [Tag 0AM6]), • f is rig-étale, • f is rig-surjective, • Δ_f : X → X ×_Y X is rig-surjective.

nodes.title: Formal modifications · Lemma 0GDM
nodes.summary: Let S, f : X' → X, T ⊂ |X|, U ⊂ X, T' ⊂ |X'|, and U' ⊂ X' be as in Section [Tag 0GDB]. If X is locally Noetherian, f is proper, and U' → U is an isomorphism, then f_/T : X'_/T' → X_/T is a formal modification.

nodes.title: Formal modifications · Lemma 0GDN
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a morphism of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces over S which is a formal modification. Then for any adic morphism Y' → Y of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces, the base change f' : X ×_Y Y' → Y' is a formal modification.

nodes.title: Completions and morphisms, I · Lemma 0AR4
nodes.summary: Let T ⊂ X be a closed subset of a Noetherian affine scheme X. Let W be a Noetherian affine formal algebraic space. Let g : W → X_/T be a rig-étale morphism. Then there exists an affine scheme X' and a finite type morphism f : X' → X étale over X setminus T such that there is an isomorphism X'_/f^-1T ≅ W compatible with f_/T and g. Moreover, if W → X_/T is étale, then X' → X is étale.

nodes.title: Completions and morphisms, I · Lemma 0AR3
nodes.summary: Assume we have • Noetherian affine schemes X, X', and Y, • a closed subset T ⊂ |X|, • a morphism f : X' → X locally of finite type and étale over X setminus T, • a morphism h : Y → X, • a morphism α : Y_/T → X'_/T over X_/T (see proof for notation). Then there exists an étale morphism b : Y' → Y of affine schemes which induces an isomorphism b_/T : Y'_/T → Y_/T and a morphism a : Y' → X' over X such that α = a_/T ∘ b_/T^-1.

nodes.title: Completions and morphisms, I · Lemma 0AR6
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y and g : Z → Y be morphisms of algebraic spaces. Let T ⊂ |X| be closed. Assume that • X is locally Noetherian, • g is a monomorphism and locally of finite type, • f|_X setminus T : X setminus T → Y factors through g, and • f_/T : X_/T → Y factors through g, then f factors through g.

nodes.title: Completions and morphisms, I · Lemma 0GI1
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X, W be algebraic spaces over S with X locally Noetherian. Let T ⊂ |X| be a closed subset. Let a, b : X → W be morphisms of algebraic spaces over S such that a|_X setminus T = b|_X setminus T and such that a_/T = b_/T as morphisms X_/T → W. Then a = b.

nodes.title: Completions and morphisms, I · Lemma 0AR7
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X, Y be locally Noetherian algebraic spaces over S. Let T ⊂ |X| and T' ⊂ |Y| be closed subsets. Let a, b : X → Y be morphisms of algebraic spaces over S such that a|_X setminus T = b|_X setminus T, such that |a|(T) ⊂ T' and |b|(T) ⊂ T', and such that a_/T = b_/T as morphisms X_/T → Y_/T'. Then a = b.

nodes.title: Completions and morphisms, I · Lemma 0AR8
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a locally Noetherian algebraic space over S. Let T ⊂ |X| be a closed subset. Let s, t : R → U be two morphisms of algebraic spaces over X. Assume • R, U are locally of finite type over X, • the base change of s and t to X setminus T is an étale equivalence relation, and • the formal completion (t_/T, s_/T) : R_/T → U_/T ×_X_/T U_/T is an equivalence relation too (see proof for notation). Then (t, s) : R → U ×_X U is an étale equivalence relation.

nodes.title: Completions and morphisms, I · Lemma 0AR9
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a locally Noetherian algebraic space over S and let T ⊂ |X| be a closed subset. Let f : X' → X be a morphism of algebraic spaces which is locally of finite type and étale outside of T. There exists a factorization X' → X" → X of f with the following properties: X" → X is locally of finite type, X" → X is an isomorphism over X setminus T, and X'_/T → X"_/T is an isomorphism (see proof for notation).

nodes.title: Rig glueing of morphisms · Proposition 0GI3
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a locally Noetherian algebraic space over S. Let T ⊂ |X| be a closed subset with complementary open subspace U ⊂ X. Let f : X' → X be a proper morphism of algebraic spaces such that f^-1(U) → U is an isomorphism. For any algebraic space W over S the map Mor_S(X, W) → Mor_S(X', W) ×_Mor_S(X'_/T, W) Mor_S(X_/T, W) is bijective.

nodes.title: Algebraization of rig-étale morphisms · Lemma 0GDQ
nodes.summary: In the situation above, let X_1 → X be a morphism of algebraic spaces with X_1 locally Noetherian. Denote T_1 ⊂ |X_1| the inverse image of T and U_1 ⊂ X_1 the inverse image of U. We denote • C_X, T the category whose objects are morphisms of algebraic spaces f : X' → X which are locally of finite type and such that U' = f^-1U → U is an isomorphism, • C_X_1, T_1 the category whose objects are morphisms of algebraic spaces f_1 : X_1' → X_1 which are locally of finite type…

nodes.title: Algebraization of rig-étale morphisms · Lemma 0GDR
nodes.summary: In the situation above. Let f : X' → X be a morphism of algebraic spaces which is locally of finite type and an isomorphism over U. Let g : Y → X be a morphism with Y locally Noetherian. Then completion defines a bijection Mor_X(Y, X') → Mor_X_/T(Y_/T, X'_/T) In particular, the functor ([Tag 0AR5]) is fully faithful.

nodes.title: Algebraization of rig-étale morphisms · Lemma 0ARA
nodes.summary: In the situation above. Assume X is affine. Then the functor ([Tag 0AR5]) is an equivalence.

nodes.title: Algebraization of rig-étale morphisms · Theorem 0ARB
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a locally Noetherian algebraic space over S. Let T ⊂ |X| be a closed subset. Let U ⊂ X be the open subspace with |U| = |X| setminus T. The completion functor ([Tag 0AR5]) ( morphisms of algebraic spaces f : X' → X which are locally of finite type and such that f^-1U → U is an isomorphism ) → ( morphisms g : W → X_/T of formal algebraic spaces with W locally Noetherian and g rig-étale ) sending f : X' → X to f_/T : X'_/T' → X_/T is an equivalence.

nodes.title: Completions and morphisms, II · Lemma 0ARU
nodes.summary: With assumptions and notation as in Theorem [Tag 0ARB] let f : X' → X correspond to g : W → X_/T. Then f is quasi-compact if and only if g is quasi-compact.

nodes.title: Completions and morphisms, II · Lemma 0ARV
nodes.summary: With assumptions and notation as in Theorem [Tag 0ARB] let f : X' → X correspond to g : W → X_/T. Then f is quasi-separated if and only if g is so.

nodes.title: Completions and morphisms, II · Lemma 0ARW
nodes.summary: With assumptions and notation as in Theorem [Tag 0ARB] let f : X' → X correspond to g : W → X_/T. Then f is separated ⇔ g is separated and Δ_g : W → W ×_X_/T W is rig-surjective.

nodes.title: Completions and morphisms, II · Lemma 0ARX
nodes.summary: With assumptions and notation as in Theorem [Tag 0ARB] let f : X' → X correspond to g : W → X_/T. Then f is proper if and only if g is a formal modification (Definition [Tag 0GDK]).

nodes.title: Completions and morphisms, II · Lemma 0GI4
nodes.summary: With assumptions and notation as in Theorem [Tag 0ARB] let f : X' → X correspond to g : W → X_/T. Then f is étale if and only if g is étale.

nodes.title: Artin's theorem on dilatations · Theorem 0GDU
nodes.summary: [ArtinII] Let S be a scheme. Let X be a locally Noetherian algebraic space over S. Let T ⊂ |X| be a closed subset. Let X = X_/T be the formal completion of X along T. Let f : X' → X be a formal modification (Definition [Tag 0GDK]). Then there exists a unique proper morphism f : X' → X which is an isomorphism over the complement of T in X whose completion f_/T recovers f.

nodes.title: Artin's theorem on dilatations · Lemma 0GDV
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X' → X be a formal modification (Definition [Tag 0GDK]) of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces over S. Given • any adic Noetherian topological ring A, • any adic morphism Spf(A) → X there exists a proper morphism X → Spec(A) of algebraic spaces and an isomorphism Spf(A) ×_ X X' → X_/Z over Spf(A) of the base change of X with the formal completion of X along the "closed fibre" Z = X ×_Spec(A) Spf(A)_red of X over A.

nodes.title: Application to modifications · Lemma 0AE5
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring homomorphism of Noetherian rings inducing an isomorphism on I-adic completions for some ideal I ⊂ A (for example if B is the I-adic completion of A). Then base change defines an equivalence of categories between the category ([Tag 0AS2]) for (A, I) with the category ([Tag 0AS2]) for (B, IB).

nodes.title: Application to modifications · Lemma 0BH5
nodes.summary: Notation and assumptions as in Lemma [Tag 0AE5]. Let f : X' → Spec(A) correspond to g : Y' → Spec(B) via the equivalence. Then f is quasi-compact, quasi-separated, separated, proper, finite, and add more here if and only if g is so.

nodes.title: Application to modifications · Lemma 0AF7
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a local map of local Noetherian rings such that • A → B is flat, • m_B = m_A B, and • kappa( m_A) = kappa( m_B) Then the base change functor from the category ([Tag 0AS2]) for (A, m_A) to the category ([Tag 0AS2]) for (B, m_B) is an equivalence.

nodes.title: Application to modifications · Lemma 0AE6
nodes.summary: Let (A, m, kappa) be a Noetherian local ring. Let f : X → S be an object of ([Tag 0AS2]) such that f is proper. Then there exists a U-admissible blowup S' → S which dominates X.

nodes.title: Modifications · Lemma 0AE3
nodes.summary: Let (A, m, kappa) be a 2-dimensional Noetherian local domain such that U = Spec(A) setminus ( m) is a normal scheme. Then any modification f : X → Spec(A) is a morphism as in ([Tag 0AE2]).

nodes.title: Modifications · Lemma 0AGM
nodes.summary: Let (A, m, kappa) be a Noetherian local ring. Let g : X → Y be a morphism in the category ([Tag 0AE2]). If the induced morphism X_kappa → Y_kappa of special fibres is a closed immersion, then g is a closed immersion.

nodes.title: Modifications · Lemma 0AYJ
nodes.summary: Let (A, m, kappa) be a Noetherian local domain of dimension ≥ 1. Let f : X → Spec(A) be a morphism of algebraic spaces. Assume at least one of the following conditions is satisfied • f is a modification (Spaces over Fields, Definition [Tag 0AD8]), • f is an alteration (Spaces over Fields, Definition [Tag 0ADA]), • f is locally of finite type, quasi-separated, X is integral, and there is exactly one point of |X| mapping to the generic point of Spec(A), • f is locally of…

nodes.title: Modifications · Lemma 0AGN
nodes.summary: If (A, m, kappa) is a complete Noetherian local domain of dimension 2, then every modification of Spec(A) is projective over A.

nodes.title: Strategy · Lemma 0BHB
nodes.summary: The functor F ([Tag 0BHA]) is an equivalence.

nodes.title: Strategy · Lemma 0BHC
nodes.summary: Let X, x_i, U_i → X, u_i be as in ([Tag 0BHA]). If f : Y → X corresponds to g_i : Y_i → U_i under F, then f is quasi-compact, quasi-separated, separated, locally of finite presentation, of finite presentation, locally of finite type, of finite type, proper, integral, finite, if and only if g_i is so for i = 1, …, n.

nodes.title: Strategy · Lemma 0BHD
nodes.summary: Let X, x_i, U_i → X, u_i be as in ([Tag 0BHA]). If f : Y → X corresponds to g_i : Y_i → U_i under F, then Y_x_i ≅ (Y_i)_u_i as algebraic spaces.

nodes.title: Dominating by quadratic transformations · Definition 0BHE
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a decent algebraic space over S. Let x ∈ |X| be a closed point. By Decent Spaces, Lemma [Tag 0AHB] we can represent x by a closed immersion i : Spec(k) → X. The blowing up X' → X of X at x means the blowing up of X in the closed subspace Z = i(Spec(k)) ⊂ X.

nodes.title: Dominating by quadratic transformations · Lemma 0BHF
nodes.summary: Let X, x_i, U_i → X, u_i be as in ([Tag 0BHA]) and assume f : Y → X corresponds to g_i : Y_i → U_i under F. Then there exists a factorization Y = Z_m → Z_m - 1 → … → Z_1 → Z_0 = X of f where Z_j + 1 → Z_j is the blowing up of Z_j at a closed point z_j lying over (x_1, …, x_n) if and only if for each i there exists a factorization Y_i = Z_i, m_i → Z_i, m_i - 1 → … → Z_i, 1 → Z_i, 0 = U_i of g_i where Z_i, j + 1 → Z_i, j is the blowing up of Z_i, j at a closed point z_i, j…

nodes.title: Dominating by quadratic transformations · Lemma 0BHG
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a Noetherian algebraic space over S. Let T ⊂ |X| be a finite set of closed points x such that (1) X is regular at x and (2) the local ring of X at x has dimension 2. Let I ⊂ O_X be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals such that O_X/I is supported on T. Then there exists a sequence X_m → X_m - 1 → … → X_1 → X_0 = X where X_j + 1 → X_j is the blowing up of X_j at a closed point x_j lying above a point of T such that IO_X_n is an invertible ideal sheaf.

nodes.title: Dominating by quadratic transformations · Lemma 0BHH
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a Noetherian algebraic space over S. Let T ⊂ |X| be a finite set of closed points x such that (1) X is regular at x and (2) the local ring of X at x has dimension 2. Let f : Y → X be a proper morphism of algebraic spaces which is an isomorphism over U = X setminus T. Then there exists a sequence X_n → X_n - 1 → … → X_1 → X_0 = X where X_i + 1 → X_i is the blowing up of X_i at a closed point x_i lying above a point of T and a factorization X_n →…

nodes.title: Dominating by normalized blowups · Definition 0BHJ
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a decent algebraic space over S satisfying the equivalent conditions of Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma [Tag 0BB1]. Let x ∈ |X| be a closed point. The normalized blowup of X at x is the composition X" → X' → X where X' → X is the blowup of X at x (Definition [Tag 0BHE]) and X" → X' is the normalization of X'.

nodes.title: Dominating by normalized blowups · Lemma 0BHK
nodes.summary: In Definition [Tag 0BHJ] if X is Nagata, then the normalized blowing up of X at x is a normal Nagata algebraic space proper over X.

nodes.title: Dominating by normalized blowups · Lemma 0BHL
nodes.summary: Let X, x_i, U_i → X, u_i be as in ([Tag 0BHA]) and assume f : Y → X corresponds to g_i : Y_i → U_i under F. Assume X satisfies the equivalent conditions of Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma [Tag 0BB1]. Then there exists a factorization Y = Z_m → Z_m - 1 → … → Z_1 → Z_0 = X of f where Z_j + 1 → Z_j is the normalized blowing up of Z_j at a closed point z_j lying over (x_1, …, x_n) if and only if for each i there exists a factorization Y_i = Z_i, m_i → Z_i, m_i - 1 → … → Z_i, 1 →…

nodes.title: Dominating by normalized blowups · Lemma 0BHM
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let X be a Noetherian Nagata algebraic space over S with dim(X) = 2. Let f : Y → X be a proper birational morphism. Then there exists a commutative diagram xymatrix X_n ar[r] ar[d] & X_n - 1 ar[r] & … ar[r] & X_1 ar[r] & X_0 ar[d] Y ar[rrrr] & & & & X where X_0 → X is the normalization and where X_i + 1 → X_i is the normalized blowing up of X_i at a closed point.

nodes.title: Base change to the completion · Lemma 0BHP
nodes.summary: Let (A, m, kappa) be a local ring with finitely generated maximal ideal m. Let X be a decent algebraic space over A. Let Y = X ×_Spec(A) Spec(A^wedge) where A^wedge is the m-adic completion of A. For a point q ∈ |Y| with image p ∈ |X| lying over the closed point of Spec(A) the map O_X, p^h → O_Y, q^h of henselian local rings induces an isomorphism on completions.

nodes.title: Base change to the completion · Lemma 0BHQ
nodes.summary: Let (A, m, kappa) be a Noetherian local ring. Let X → Spec(A) be a morphism which is locally of finite type with X a decent algebraic space. Set Y = X ×_Spec(A) Spec(A^wedge). Let y ∈ |Y| with image x ∈ |X|. Then • if O_Y, y^h is regular, then O_X, x^h is regular, • if y is in the closed fibre, then O_Y, y^h is regular ⇔ O_X, x^h is regular, and • If X is proper over A, then X is regular if and only if Y is regular.

nodes.title: Base change to the completion · Lemma 0BHR
nodes.summary: Let (A, m) be a local Noetherian ring. Let X be an algebraic space over A. Assume • A is analytically unramified (Algebra, Definition [Tag 032X]), • X is locally of finite type over A, • X → Spec(A) is étale at every point of codimension 0 in X. Then the normalization of X is finite over X.

nodes.title: Implied properties · Lemma 0BHT
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let Y be a Noetherian integral algebraic space over S. Assume there exists an alteration f : X → Y with X regular. Then the normalization Y^ν → Y is finite and Y has a dense open which is regular.

nodes.title: Implied properties · Lemma 0BHU
nodes.summary: Let (A, m, kappa) be a local Noetherian domain. Assume there exists an alteration f : X → Spec(A) with X regular. Then • there exists a nonzero f ∈ A such that A_f is regular, • the integral closure B of A in its fraction field is finite over A, • the m-adic completion of B is a normal ring, i.e., the completions of B at its maximal ideals are normal domains, and • the generic formal fibre of A is regular.

nodes.title: Resolution · Definition 0BHW
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let Y be a Noetherian integral algebraic space over S. A resolution of singularities of X is a modification f : X → Y such that X is regular.

nodes.title: Resolution · Definition 0BHX
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let Y be a 2-dimensional Noetherian integral algebraic space over S. We say Y has a resolution of singularities by normalized blowups if there exists a sequence Y_n → X_n - 1 → … → Y_1 → Y_0 → Y where • Y_i is proper over Y for i = 0, …, n, • Y_0 → Y is the normalization, • Y_i → Y_i - 1 is a normalized blowup for i = 1, …, n, and • Y_n is regular.

nodes.title: Resolution · Theorem 0BHY
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let Y be a two dimensional integral Noetherian algebraic space over S. The following are equivalent • there exists an alteration X → Y with X regular, • there exists a resolution of singularities of Y, • Y has a resolution of singularities by normalized blowups, • the normalization Y^ν → Y is finite, Y^ν has finitely many singular points y_1, …, y_m ∈ |Y|, and for each i the completion of the henselian local ring O_Y^ν, y_i^h is normal.

nodes.title: The base category · Definition 06GC
nodes.summary: Let Lambda be a Noetherian ring and let Lambda → k be a finite ring map where k is a field. We define C_Lambda to be the category with • objects are pairs (A, φ) where A is an Artinian local Lambda-algebra and where φ : A/ m_A → k is a Lambda-algebra isomorphism, and • morphisms f : (B, ψ) → (A, φ) are local Lambda-algebra homomorphisms such that φ ∘ (f bmod m) = ψ. We say we are in the classical case if Lambda is a Noetherian complete local ring and k is its residue field.

nodes.title: The base category · Definition 06GD
nodes.summary: Let f: B → A be a ring map in C_Lambda. We say f is a small extension if it is surjective and Ker(f) is a nonzero principal ideal which is annihilated by m_B.

nodes.title: The base category · Lemma 06GE
nodes.summary: Let f: B → A be a surjective ring map in C_Lambda. Then f can be factored as a composition of small extensions.

nodes.title: The base category · Lemma 06GG
nodes.summary: Let A be a local Lambda-algebra with residue field k. Let M be an A-module. Then [k : k'] length_A(M) = length_Lambda(M). In the classical case we have length_A(M) = length_Lambda(M).

nodes.title: The base category · Lemma 06S3
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map in C_Lambda. The following are equivalent • f is surjective, • m_A/ m_A^2 → m_B/ m_B^2 is surjective, and • m_A/( m_Lambda A + m_A^2) → m_B/( m_Lambda B + m_B^2) is surjective.

nodes.title: The base category · Definition 06GY
nodes.summary: Let R → S be a local homomorphism of local rings. The relative cotangent space_Lambda over Lambda should not be defined simply as the k-linear dual of the relative cotangent space. In fact, the correct definition of the relative cotangent space is Ω_S/R ⊗_S S/ m_S. of R over S is the S/ m_S-vector space m_S/( m_R S + m_S^2).

nodes.title: The base category · Lemma 06GH
nodes.summary: Let f_1 : A_1 → A and f_2 : A_2 → A be ring maps in C_Lambda. Then: • If f_1 or f_2 is surjective, then A_1 ×_A A_2 is in C_Lambda. • If f_2 is a small extension, then so is A_1 ×_A A_2 → A_1. • If the field extension k/k' is separable, then A_1 ×_A A_2 is in C_Lambda.

nodes.title: The base category · Definition 06GF
nodes.summary: Let f: B → A be a ring map in C_Lambda. We say f is an essential surjection if it has the following properties: • f is surjective. • If g: C → B is a ring map in C_Lambda such that f ∘ g is surjective, then g is surjective.

nodes.title: The base category · Lemma 06S5
nodes.summary: Let f: B → A be a ring map in C_Lambda. The following are equivalent • f is an essential surjection, • the map B/ m_B^2 → A/ m_A^2 is an essential surjection, and • the map B/( m_Lambda B + m_B^2) → A/( m_Lambda A + m_A^2) is an essential surjection.

nodes.title: The base category · Lemma 06S9
nodes.summary: There is a canonical map m_Lambda/ m_Lambda^2 → H_1(L_k/Lambda). If k' ⊂ k is separable (for example if the characteristic of k is zero), then this map induces an isomorphism m_Lambda/ m_Lambda^2 ⊗_k' k = H_1(L_k/Lambda). nodes.title: Categories cofibered in groupoids · Definition 06GJ

A morphism of predeformation categories is a morphism of categories cofibered in groupoids over C_Lambda.

nodes.summary: Let F, G: C_Lambda → Sets be deformation functors. Let φ : F → G be a smooth morphism which induces an isomorphism dφ : TF → TG of tangent spaces. Then φ is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Schlessinger's theorem on prorepresentable functors · Theorem 06JM
nodes.summary: Let F: C_Lambda → Sets be a functor. Then F is prorepresentable if and only if (a) F is a deformation functor, (b) dim_k TF is finite, and (c) γ : Der_Lambda(k, k) → TF is injective.

nodes.title: Infinitesimal automorphisms · Definition 06JP
nodes.summary: Let F be a category cofibered in groupoids over C_Lambda. Let x' → x be a morphism in F lying over A' → A. The kernel Inf(x'/x) = Ker(Aut_A'(x') → Aut_A(x)) is the group of infinitesimal automorphisms of x' over x.

nodes.title: Infinitesimal automorphisms · Definition 06JQ
nodes.summary: Let F be a category cofibered in groupoids over C_Lambda. Let x_0 ∈ Ob(F(k)). Assume a choice of pushforward x_0 → x_0' of x_0 along the map k → k[ε], a ↦ a has been made. Then there is a unique map x'_0 → x_0 such that x_0 → x_0' → x_0 is the identity on x_0. Then Inf_x_0( F) = Inf(x'_0/x_0) is the group of infinitesimal automorphisms of x_0

nodes.title: Infinitesimal automorphisms · Definition 06JT
nodes.summary: Let p : F → C be a category cofibered in groupoids over an arbitrary base category C. Assume a choice of pushforwards has been made. Let x ∈ Ob(F) and let U = p(x). Let U/C denote the category of objects under U. The automorphism functor of x is the functor mathitAut(x) : U/C → Sets sending an object f : U → V to Aut_V(f_*x) and sending a morphism xymatrix V' ar[rr] & & V & U ar[ul]^f' ar[ur]_f & to the homomorphism Aut_V'(f'_*x) → Aut_V(f_*x) coming from the unique…

nodes.title: Infinitesimal automorphisms · Lemma 06JU
nodes.summary: Let F be a category cofibered in groupoids over C_Lambda satisfying (RS). Let x ∈ Ob(F(A)). Then mathitAut(x): C_A → Sets satisfies (RS).

nodes.title: Infinitesimal automorphisms · Lemma 06JV
nodes.summary: Let F be a category cofibered in groupoids over C_Lambda satisfying (RS). Let x ∈ Ob(F(A)). Let x_0 be a pushforward of x to F(k). • T_id_x_0 mathitAut(x) has a natural k-vector space structure such that addition agrees with composition in T_id_x_0 mathitAut(x). In particular, composition in T_id_x_0 mathitAut(x) is commutative. • There is a canonical isomorphism T_id_x_0 mathitAut(x) → T_id_x_0 mathitAut(x_0) of k-vector spaces.

nodes.title: Infinitesimal automorphisms · Lemma 06JX
nodes.summary: Let F be a category cofibered in groupoids over C_Lambda satisfying (RS). Let x_0 ∈ Ob(F(k)). Then Inf_x_0(F) is equal as a set to T_id_x_0 mathitAut(x_0), and so has a natural k-vector space structure such that addition agrees with composition of automorphisms.

nodes.title: Infinitesimal automorphisms · Lemma 07W6
nodes.summary: Let φ : F → G be a morphism of categories cofibred in groupoids over C_Lambda satisfying (RS). Let x_0 ∈ Ob(F(k)). Then φ induces a k-linear map Inf_x_0(F) → Inf_φ(x_0)(G).

nodes.title: Infinitesimal automorphisms · Lemma 06JY
nodes.summary: Let F be a category cofibered in groupoids over C_Lambda satisfying (RS). Let x' → x be a morphism lying over a surjective ring map A' → A with kernel I annihilated by m_A'. Let x_0 be a pushforward of x to F(k). Then Inf(x'/x) has a free and transitive action by T_id_x_0 mathitAut(x') ⊗_k I = Inf_x_0(F) ⊗_k I.

nodes.title: Infinitesimal automorphisms · Lemma 06JZ
nodes.summary: Let F be a category cofibered in groupoids over C_Lambda satisfying (RS). Let x' → x be a morphism in F lying over a surjective ring map. Let x_0 be a pushforward of x to F(k). If Inf_x_0(F) = 0 then Inf(x'/x) = 0.

nodes.title: Infinitesimal automorphisms · Lemma 06K0
nodes.summary: Let F be a category cofibered in groupoids over C_Lambda satisfying (RS). Let x_0 ∈ Ob(F(k)). Then Inf_x_0(F) = 0 if and only if the natural morphism F_x_0 → overlineF_x_0 of categories cofibered in groupoids is an equivalence.

nodes.title: Applications · Lemma 0DYN
nodes.summary: Let H_1 → G, H_2 → G, and G → F be maps of categories cofibred in groupoids over C_Lambda. Assume • F and G are deformation categories, • TG → TF is injective, and • Inf(G) → Inf(F) is surjective. Then H_1 ×_G H_2 → H_1 ×_F H_2 is smooth.

nodes.title: Applications · Lemma 0DYP
nodes.summary: Let f : F → G be a map of deformation categories. Let x_0 ∈ Ob(F(k)) with image y_0 ∈ Ob(G(k)). If • the map TF → TG is surjective, and • for every small extension A' → A in C_Lambda and x ∈ F(A) with image y ∈ G(A) if there is a lift of y to A', then there is a lift of x to A', then F → G is smooth (and vice versa).

nodes.title: Applications · Lemma 0E3R
nodes.summary: Let F → G → H be maps of categories cofibred in groupoids over C_Lambda. If • F, G are deformation categories • the map TF → TG is surjective, and • F → H is smooth. Then F → G is smooth.

nodes.title: Groupoids in functors on the base category · Lemma 06KG
nodes.summary: Let (U, R, s, t, c) be a groupoid in functors on C_Lambda. • (U, R, s, t, c) is prorepresentable if and only if its completion is representable as a groupoid in functors on widehatC_Lambda. • (U, R, s, t, c) is prorepresentable if and only if U and R are prorepresentable.

nodes.title: Smooth groupoids in functors on the base category · Definition 06KI
nodes.summary: Let (U, R, s, t, c) be a groupoid in functors on C_Lambda. We say (U, R, s, t, c) is smooth if s, t: R → U are smooth.

Let (U, R, s, t, c) be the groupoid in functors on C constructed from f : U → F in Lemma [Tag 06KY]. Then: • If (U, R, s, t, c) is the groupoid in functors on C_Lambda constructed from f : U → F in Lemma [Tag 06KY], then (U, R, s, t, c) is smooth. • If f : U(k) → F(k) is essentially surjective, then the morphism [f] : [U/R] → F of Lemma [Tag 06KZ] is an equivalence.

nodes.title: Presentations of deformation categories · Lemma 06L6
nodes.summary: Let F be a deformation category. Let U : C_Lambda → Sets be a deformation functor. Let f: U → F be a morphism of categories cofibered in groupoids. nodes.title: Presentations of deformation categories · Lemma 06L7
nodes.summary: Let F be a deformation category. Let U : C_Lambda → Sets be a prorepresentable functor. Let f : U → F be a morphism of categories cofibered in groupoids. Let (U, R, s, t, c) be the groupoid in functors on C_Lambda constructed from f : U → F in Lemma [Tag 06KY]. If dim_k Inf(F) < ∞, then (U, R, s, t, c) is prorepresentable.

nodes.title: Presentations of deformation categories · Theorem 06L8
nodes.summary: Let F be a category cofibered in groupoids over C_Lambda. Then F admits a presentation by a smooth prorepresentable groupoid in functors on C_Lambda if and only if the following conditions hold: • F is a deformation category. • dim_k TF is finite. • dim_k Inf(F) is finite.

nodes.title: Remarks regarding minimality · Definition 06KM
nodes.summary: Let (U, R, s, t, c) be a smooth prorepresentable groupoid in functors on C_Lambda. • We say (U, R, s, t, c) is normalized if the groupoid (U(k[ε]), R(k[ε]), s, t, c) is totally disconnected, i.e., there are no morphisms between distinct objects. • We say (U, R, s, t, c) is minimal if the U → [U/R] is given by a minimal versal formal object of [U/R].

nodes.title: Remarks regarding minimality · Lemma 06KN
nodes.summary: Let (U, R, s, t, c) be a smooth prorepresentable groupoid in functors on C_Lambda. • (U, R, s, t, c) is normalized if and only if the morphism U → [U/R] induces an isomorphism on tangent spaces, and • (U, R, s, t, c) is minimal if and only if the kernel of TU → T[U/R] is contained in the image of Der_Lambda(k, k) → TU.

nodes.title: Remarks regarding minimality · Lemma 06KP
nodes.summary: Let U: C_Lambda → Sets be a prorepresentable functor. Let φ : U → U be a morphism such that dφ : TU → TU is an isomorphism. Then φ is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Remarks regarding minimality · Lemma 06KQ
nodes.summary: Let (U, R, s, t, c) be a minimal smooth prorepresentable groupoid in functors on C_Lambda. If φ : [U/R] → [U/R] is an equivalence of categories cofibered in groupoids, then φ is an isomorphism.

Let n ∈ Z. • If H^i(α) is an isomorphism for i ≥ n, then H^i(α ⊗_O^L id_F) is an isomorphism for i ≥ n. • If H^i(α) is an isomorphism for i > n and surjective for i = n, then H^i(α ⊗_O^L id_F) is an isomorphism for i > n and surjective for i = n.
nodes.section: Deformations of complexes on ringed topoi

nodes.title: Deformations of complexes on ringed topoi · Lemma 0DIW
nodes.summary: Let C be a site. Let O → O_0 be a surjection of sheaves of rings whose kernel is an ideal sheaf I of square zero. For every object K_0 in D^-(O_0) the following are equivalent • the class ω(K_0) ∈ Ext^2_O_0(K_0, K_0 ⊗_O_0 I) constructed in Lemma [Tag 0DIU] is zero, • there exists K ∈ D^-(O) with K ⊗_O^L O_0 = K_0 in D(O_0).
nodes.section: Deformations of complexes on ringed topoi

nodes.title: Deformations of complexes on ringed topoi · Lemma 0DIX
nodes.summary: Let C be a site. Let O → O_0 be a surjection of sheaves of rings. Assume given the following data • a complex of O-modules F^bullet, • a complex K_0^bullet of O_0-modules, • a quasi-isomorphism K_0^bullet → F^bullet ⊗_O O_0, Then there exist a quasi-isomorphism G^bullet → F^bullet such that the map of complexes G^bullet ⊗_O O_0 → F^bullet ⊗_O O_0 factors through K_0^bullet in the homotopy category of complexes of O_0-modules.
nodes.section: Deformations of complexes on ringed topoi

nodes.title: Deformations of complexes on ringed topoi · Lemma 0DIY
nodes.summary: Let C be a site. Let O → O_0 be a surjection of sheaves of rings whose kernel is an ideal sheaf I of square zero. Let K, L ∈ D^-(O). Set K_0 = K ⊗_O^L O_0 and L_0 = L ⊗_O^L O_0 in D^-(O_0). Given α_0 : K_0 → L_0 in D(O_0) there is a canonical element o(α_0) ∈ Ext^1_O_0(K_0, L_0 ⊗_O_0^L I) whose vanishing is necessary and sufficient for the existence of a map α : K → L in D(O) with α_0 = α ⊗_O^L id.
nodes.section: Deformations of complexes on ringed topoi

nodes.title: Deformations of complexes on ringed topoi · Lemma 0DIZ
nodes.summary: Let C be a site. Let O → O_0 be a surjection of sheaves of rings whose kernel is an ideal sheaf I of square zero. Let K_0 ∈ D^-(O). A lift of K_0 is a pair (K, α_0) consisting of an object K in D^-(O) and an isomorphism α_0 : K ⊗_O^L O_0 → K_0 in D(O_0). • Given a lift (K, α) the group of automorphism of the pair is canonically the cokernel of a map Ext^-1_O_0(K_0, K_0) → Hom_O_0(K_0, K_0 ⊗_O_0^L I) • If there is a lift, then the set of isomorphism classes of lifts is…
nodes.section: Deformations of complexes on ringed topoi

nodes.title: The cotangent complex of a ring map · Definition 08PM
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. The standard resolution of B over A is the augmentation ε : P_bullet → B with terms P_0 = A[B], P_1 = A[A[B]], … and maps as constructed in Simplicial, Example [Tag 09CB].
nodes.section: The cotangent complex of a ring map

nodes.title: The cotangent complex of a ring map · Definition 08PN
nodes.summary: The cotangent complex L_B/A of a ring map A → B is the complex of B-modules associated to the simplicial B-module Ω_P_bullet/A ⊗_P_bullet, ε B where ε : P_bullet → B is the standard resolution of B over A.
nodes.section: The cotangent complex of a ring map

nodes.title: The cotangent complex of a ring map · Lemma 08S9
nodes.summary: Let A_i → B_i be a system of ring maps over a directed index set I. Then colim L_B_i/A_i = L_colim B_i/colim A_i.
nodes.section: The cotangent complex of a ring map

nodes.title: Simplicial resolutions and derived lower shriek · Lemma 08PS
nodes.summary: With notation as above let P_bullet be a simplicial A-algebra endowed with an augmentation ε : P_bullet → B. Assume each P_n is a polynomial algebra over A and ε is a trivial Kan fibration on underlying simplicial sets. Then Lπ_!(F) = F(P_bullet, ε) in D(Ab), resp. D(B) functorially in F in Ab(C), resp. Mod(underlineB).
nodes.section: Simplicial resolutions and derived lower shriek

nodes.title: Simplicial resolutions and derived lower shriek · Lemma 08PT
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Let ε : P_bullet → B be the standard resolution of B over A. Let π be as in ([Tag 08PR]). Then Lπ_!(F) = F(P_bullet, ε) in D(Ab), resp. D(B) functorially in F in Ab(C), resp. Mod(underlineB).
nodes.section: Simplicial resolutions and derived lower shriek

nodes.title: Simplicial resolutions and derived lower shriek · Lemma 08PU
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Let π and i be as in ([Tag 08PR]). There is a canonical isomorphism L_B/A = Lπ_!(Li^*Ω_O/A) = Lπ_!(i^*Ω_O/A) = Lπ_!(Ω_O/A ⊗_O underlineB) in D(B).
nodes.section: Simplicial resolutions and derived lower shriek

nodes.title: Simplicial resolutions and derived lower shriek · Lemma 08QE
nodes.summary: If A → B is a ring map, then Lπ_!(π^-1M) = M with π as in ([Tag 08PR]).
nodes.section: Simplicial resolutions and derived lower shriek

nodes.title: Simplicial resolutions and derived lower shriek · Lemma 08QF
nodes.summary: If A → B is a ring map, then H^0(L_B/A) = Ω_B/A.
nodes.section: Simplicial resolutions and derived lower shriek

nodes.title: Simplicial resolutions and derived lower shriek · Lemma 08QG
nodes.summary: If B is a polynomial algebra over the ring A, then with π as in ([Tag 08PR]) we have that π_! is exact and π_!F = F(B → B).
nodes.section: Simplicial resolutions and derived lower shriek

nodes.title: Simplicial resolutions and derived lower shriek · Lemma 08QH
nodes.summary: If B is a polynomial algebra over the ring A, then L_B/A is quasi-isomorphic to Ω_B/A[0].
nodes.section: Simplicial resolutions and derived lower shriek

nodes.title: Constructing a resolution · Lemma 08PW
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian ring. Let A → B be a finite type ring map. Let A be the category of A-algebra maps C → B. Let n ≥ 0 and let P_bullet be a simplicial object of A such that • P_bullet → B is a trivial Kan fibration of simplicial sets, • P_k is finite type over A for k ≤ n, • P_bullet = cosk_n sk_n P_bullet as simplicial objects of A. Then P_n + 1 is a finite type A-algebra.

nodes.title: Constructing a resolution · Proposition 08PX
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian ring. Let A → B be a finite type ring map. There exists a simplicial A-algebra P_bullet with an augmentation ε : P_bullet → B such that each P_n is a polynomial algebra of finite type over A and such that ε is a trivial Kan fibration of simplicial sets.

nodes.title: Constructing a resolution · Lemma 08PY
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian ring. Let A → B be a finite type ring map. Let π, underlineB be as in ([Tag 08PR]). If F is an underlineB-module such that F(P, α) is a finite B-module for all α : P = A[x_1, …, x_n] → B, then the cohomology modules of Lπ_!(F) are finite B-modules.

nodes.title: Constructing a resolution · Lemma 08PZ
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian ring. Let A → B be a finite type ring map. Then H^n(L_B/A) is a finite B-module for all n ∈ Z.

nodes.title: Constructing a resolution · Lemma 08QJ
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Let π, O, underlineB be as in ([Tag 08PR]). For any O-module F we have Lπ_!(F) = Lπ_!(Li^*F) = Lπ_!(F ⊗_O^L underlineB) in D(Ab).

nodes.title: Constructing a resolution · Lemma 08QK
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Let π, O, underlineB be as in ([Tag 08PR]). We have Lπ_!(O) = Lπ_!(underlineB) = B and L_B/A = Lπ_!(Ω_O/A ⊗_O underlineB) = Lπ_!(Ω_O/A) in D(Ab).

nodes.title: Constructing a resolution · Lemma 08SA
nodes.summary: Let A → B → C be ring maps. If B is a polynomial algebra over A, then there is a distinguished triangle L_B/A ⊗_B^L C → L_C/A → L_C/B → L_B/A ⊗_B^L C[1] in D(C).

nodes.title: Functoriality · Lemma 08QP
nodes.summary: Assume ([Tag 08QM]) induces a quasi-isomorphism B ⊗_A^L A' = B'. Then, with notation as in ([Tag 08QN]) and F' ∈ Ab(C'), we have Lπ_!(g^-1F') = Lπ'_!(F').

nodes.title: Functoriality · Lemma 08QQ
nodes.summary: If ([Tag 08QM]) induces a quasi-isomorphism B ⊗_A^L A' = B', then the functoriality map induces an isomorphism L_B/A ⊗_B^L B' → L_B'/A'

nodes.title: Functoriality · Lemma 08SC
nodes.summary: Let A → B and A → C be ring maps. Then the map L_B × C/A → L_B/A ⊕ L_C/A is an isomorphism in D(B × C).

nodes.title: The fundamental triangle · Lemma 08QU
nodes.summary: With notation as in ([Tag 08QT]) set Ω_1 = Ω_O/A ⊗_O underlineB on C_B/A Ω_2 = Ω_O/A ⊗_O underlineC on C_C/A Ω_3 = Ω_O/B ⊗_O underlineC on C_C/B Then we have a canonical short exact sequence of sheaves of underlineC-modules 0 → g_1^-1Ω_1 ⊗_underlineB underlineC → g_2^-1Ω_2 → g_3^-1Ω_3 → 0 on C_C/B/A.

nodes.title: The fundamental triangle · Lemma 08QV
nodes.summary: With notation as in ([Tag 08QT]) suppose that C is a polynomial algebra over B. Then Lπ_!(g_3^-1F) = Lπ_3, !F = π_3, !F for any abelian sheaf F on C_C/B

nodes.title: The fundamental triangle · Lemma 08QW
nodes.summary: With notation as in ([Tag 08QT]) we have Lg_i, ! ∘ g_i^-1 = id for i = 1, 2, 3 and hence also Lπ_! ∘ g_i^-1 = Lπ_i, ! for i = 1, 2, 3.

nodes.title: The fundamental triangle · Proposition 08QX
nodes.summary: Let A → B → C be ring maps. There is a canonical distinguished triangle L_B/A ⊗_B^L C → L_C/A → L_C/B → L_B/A ⊗_B^L C[1] in D(C).

nodes.title: Localization and étale ring maps · Lemma 08QZ
nodes.summary: Let A → A' → B be ring maps such that B = B ⊗_A^L A'. Then L_B/A = L_B/A' in D(B).

nodes.title: Localization and étale ring maps · Lemma 08R0
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map such that B = B ⊗_A^L B. Then L_B/A = 0 in D(B).

nodes.title: Localization and étale ring maps · Lemma 08R1
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map such that Tor^A_i(B, B) = 0 for i > 0 and such that L_B/B ⊗_A B = 0. Then L_B/A = 0 in D(B).

nodes.title: Localization and étale ring maps · Lemma 08R2
nodes.summary: The cotangent complex L_B/A is zero in each of the following cases: • A → B and B ⊗_A B → B are flat, i.e., A → B is weakly étale (More on Algebra, Definition [Tag 092B]), • A → B is a flat epimorphism of rings, • B = S^-1A for some multiplicative subset S ⊂ A, • A → B is unramified and flat, • A → B is étale, • A → B is a filtered colimit of ring maps for which the cotangent complex vanishes, • B is a henselization of a local ring of A, • B is a strict henselization of a…

nodes.title: Localization and étale ring maps · Lemma 08R3
nodes.summary: Let A → B → C be ring maps such that L_C/B = 0. Then L_C/A = L_B/A ⊗_B^L C.

nodes.title: Localization and étale ring maps · Lemma 08SF
nodes.summary: Let A → B be ring maps and S ⊂ A, T ⊂ B multiplicative subsets such that S maps into T. Then L_T^-1B/S^-1A = L_B/A ⊗_B T^-1B in D(T^-1B).

nodes.title: Localization and étale ring maps · Lemma 08UN
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a local ring homomorphism of local rings. Let A^h → B^h, resp. A^sh → B^sh be the induced maps of henselizations, resp. strict henselizations. Then L_B^h/A^h = L_B^h/A = L_B/A ⊗_B^L B^h resp. L_B^sh/A^sh = L_B^sh/A = L_B/A ⊗_B^L B^sh in D(B^h), resp. D(B^sh).

nodes.title: Smooth ring maps · Lemma 08R5
nodes.summary: If A → B is a smooth ring map, then L_B/A = Ω_B/A[0].

nodes.title: Positive characteristic · Lemma 0G5Y
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map with p = 0 in A. Let P_bullet be the standard resolution of B over A. The map P_bullet → P_bullet induced by the diagram xymatrix B ar[r]_F_B & B A ar[u] ar[r]^F_A & A ar[u] discussed in Section [Tag 08QL] is homotopic to the Frobenius endomorphism P_bullet → P_bullet given by Frobenius on each P_n.

nodes.title: Positive characteristic · Lemma 0G5Z
nodes.summary: Let p be a prime number. Let A → B be a ring homomorphism and assume that p = 0 in A. The map L_B/A → L_B/A of Section [Tag 08QL] induced by the Frobenius maps F_A and F_B is homotopic to zero.

nodes.title: Positive characteristic · Lemma 0G60
nodes.summary: Let p be a prime number. Let A → B be a ring homomorphism and assume that p = 0 in A. If A and B are perfect, then L_B/A is zero in D(B).

nodes.title: Comparison with the naive cotangent complex · Lemma 08RA
nodes.summary: The cohomology of the cotangent complex of a surjective ring map is trivial in degree zero; it is the kernel modulo its square in degree -1. Let A → B be a surjective ring map with kernel I. Then H^0(L_B/A) = 0 and H^-1(L_B/A) = I/I^2. This isomorphism comes from the map ([Tag 08R9]) for the object (A → B) of C_B/A.
nodes.section: Comparison with the naive cotangent complex

nodes.title: Comparison with the naive cotangent complex · Lemma 08RB
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Then τ_≥ -1L_B/A is canonically quasi-isomorphic to the naive cotangent complex.
nodes.section: Comparison with the naive cotangent complex

nodes.title: A spectral sequence of Quillen · Lemma 08RD
nodes.summary: Notation and assumptions as in Cohomology on Sites, Example [Tag 08PF]. Assume C has a cosimplicial object as in Cohomology on Sites, Lemma [Tag 08Q9]. Let F be a flat underlineB-module such that H_0(C, F) = 0. Then H_l(C, Sym_underlineB^k(F)) = 0 for l < k.

nodes.title: A spectral sequence of Quillen · Lemma 08RE
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let P = A[E] be a polynomial ring. Set I = (e; e ∈ E) ⊂ P. The maps Tor_i^P(A, I^n + 1) → Tor_i^P(A, I^n) are zero for all i and n.

nodes.title: Quillen spectral sequence · Theorem 08RF
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a surjective ring map. Consider the sheaf Ω = Ω_O/A ⊗_O underlineB of underlineB-modules on C_B/A, see Section [Tag 08PQ]. Then there is a spectral sequence with E_1-page E_1^p, q = H_- p - q(C_B/A, Sym^p_underlineB(Ω)) ⇒ Tor^A_- p - q(B, B) with d_r of bidegree (r, -r + 1). Moreover, H_i(C_B/A, Sym^k_underlineB(Ω)) = 0 for i < k.

nodes.title: Comparison with Lichtenbaum-Schlessinger · Definition 09CE
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Let M be a (B, B)-bimodule over A. An A-biderivation is an A-linear map λ : B → M such that λ(xy) = xλ(y) + λ(x)y.

nodes.title: Comparison with Lichtenbaum-Schlessinger · Lemma 09CF
nodes.summary: Let P = A[S] be a polynomial ring over A. Let M be a (P, P)-bimodule over A. Given m_s ∈ M for s ∈ S, there exists a unique A-biderivation λ : P → M mapping s to m_s for s ∈ S.

nodes.title: Comparison with Lichtenbaum-Schlessinger · Lemma 09CG
nodes.summary: In the situation above denote L the complex ([Tag 09CD]). There is a canonical map L_B/A → L in D(B) which induces an isomorphism τ_≥ -2L_B/A → L in D(B).

nodes.title: The cotangent complex of a local complete intersection · Lemma 08SI
nodes.summary: Let A = Z[x_1, …, x_n] → B = Z be the ring map which sends x_i to 0 for i = 1, …, n. Let I = (x_1, …, x_n) ⊂ A. Then L_B/A is quasi-isomorphic to I/I^2[1].
nodes.section: The cotangent complex of a local complete intersection

nodes.title: The cotangent complex of a local complete intersection · Lemma 08SJ
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a surjective ring map whose kernel I is generated by a Koszul-regular sequence (for example a regular sequence). Then L_B/A is quasi-isomorphic to I/I^2[1].
nodes.section: The cotangent complex of a local complete intersection

nodes.title: The cotangent complex of a local complete intersection · Lemma 08SK
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a surjective ring map whose kernel I is Koszul. Then L_B/A is quasi-isomorphic to I/I^2[1].
nodes.section: The cotangent complex of a local complete intersection

nodes.title: The cotangent complex of a local complete intersection · Proposition 08SL
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a local complete intersection map. Then L_B/A is a perfect complex with tor amplitude in [-1, 0].
nodes.section: The cotangent complex of a local complete intersection

nodes.title: Tensor products and the cotangent complex · Lemma 09DA
nodes.summary: If A and B are Tor independent R-algebras, then the object E in ([Tag 09D9]) is zero. In this case we have L_A ⊗_R B/R = L_A/R ⊗_A^L (A ⊗_R B) ⊕ L_B/R ⊗_B^L (A ⊗_R B) which is represented by the complex L_A/R ⊗_R B ⊕ L_B/R ⊗_R A of A ⊗_R B-modules.
nodes.section: Tensor products and the cotangent complex

nodes.title: Tensor products and the cotangent complex · Lemma 09DB
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring and let A, B be R-algebras. The object E in ([Tag 09D9]) satisfies H^i(E) = ( 0 & if & i ≥ -1 Tor_1^R(A, B) & if & i = -2 .
nodes.section: Tensor products and the cotangent complex

nodes.title: Deformations of ring maps and the cotangent complex · Lemma 08SP
nodes.summary: In the situation above we have • There is a canonical element xi ∈ Ext^2_B(L_B/A, N) whose vanishing is a sufficient and necessary condition for the existence of a solution to ([Tag 08SN]). • If there exists a solution, then the set of isomorphism classes of solutions is principal homogeneous under Ext^1_B(L_B/A, N). • Given a solution B', the set of automorphisms of B' fitting into ([Tag 08SN]) is canonically isomorphic to Ext^0_B(L_B/A, N).
nodes.section: Deformations of ring maps and the cotangent complex

nodes.title: The Atiyah class of a module · Definition 09DE
nodes.summary: Let A → B be a ring map. Let M be a B-module. The map M → L_B/A ⊗_B^L M[1] in ([Tag 09DD]) is called the Atiyah class of M.
nodes.section: The Atiyah class of a module

nodes.title: The cotangent complex · Definition 08SR
nodes.summary: Let C be a site. Let A → B be a homomorphism of sheaves of rings on C. The standard resolution of B over A is the augmentation ε : P_bullet → B with terms P_0 = A[B], P_1 = A[A[B]], … and maps as constructed above.

nodes.title: The cotangent complex · Definition 08SS
nodes.summary: Let C be a site. Let A → B be a homomorphism of sheaves of rings on C. The cotangent complex L_B/A is the complex of B-modules associated to the simplicial module Ω_P_bullet/A ⊗_P_bullet, ε B where ε : P_bullet → B is the standard resolution of B over A. We usually think of L_B/A as an object of D(B).

nodes.title: The cotangent complex · Lemma 08SV
nodes.summary: Let f : Sh(D) → Sh(C) be a morphism of topoi. Let A → B be a homomorphism of sheaves of rings on C. Then f^-1L_B/A = L_f^-1B/f^-1A.

nodes.title: The cotangent complex · Lemma 08SW
nodes.summary: Let C be a site. Let A → B be a homomorphism of sheaves of rings on C. Then H^i(L_B/A) is the sheaf associated to the presheaf U ↦ H^i(L_B(U)/A(U)).

nodes.title: The cotangent complex · Lemma 08UR
nodes.summary: Let C be a site. Let A → B be a homomorphism of sheaves of rings on C. Then H^0(L_B/A) = Ω_B/A.

nodes.title: The cotangent complex · Lemma 08SY
nodes.summary: Let C be a site. Let A → B and A → B' be homomorphisms of sheaves of rings on C. Then L_B × B'/A → L_B/A ⊕ L_B'/A is an isomorphism in D(B × B').

nodes.title: The cotangent complex · Lemma 08SZ
nodes.summary: Let D be a site. Let A → B → C be homomorphisms of sheaves of rings on D. There is a canonical distinguished triangle L_B/A ⊗_B^L C → L_C/A → L_C/B → L_B/A ⊗_B^L C[1] in D(C).

nodes.title: The cotangent complex · Lemma 08T0
nodes.summary: Let C be a site. Let A → B be a homomorphism of sheaves of rings on C. If p is a point of C, then (L_B/A)_p = L_B_p/A_p.

nodes.title: The cotangent complex · Lemma 08US
nodes.summary: Let C be a site. Let A → B be a homomorphism of sheaves of rings on C. There is a canonical map L_B/A → NL_B/A which identifies the naive cotangent complex with the truncation τ_≥ -1L_B/A.

nodes.title: The Atiyah class of a sheaf of modules · Definition 09DI
nodes.summary: Let C be a site. Let A → B be a homomorphism of sheaves of rings. Let F be a sheaf of B-modules. The map F → L_B/A ⊗_B^L F[1] in ([Tag 09DH]) is called the Atiyah class of F.
nodes.section: The Atiyah class of a sheaf of modules

nodes.title: The cotangent complex of a morphism of ringed spaces · Definition 08UU
nodes.summary: Let f : (X, O_X) → (S, O_S) be a morphism of ringed spaces. The cotangent complex L_f of f is L_f = L_O_X/f^-1O_S. We will also use the notation L_f = L_X/S = L_O_X/O_S.
nodes.section: The cotangent complex of a morphism of ringed spaces

nodes.title: The cotangent complex of a morphism of ringed spaces · Lemma 08UV
nodes.summary: Let f : (X, O_X) → (S, O_S) be a morphism of ringed spaces. Then H^0(L_X/S) = Ω_X/S.
nodes.section: The cotangent complex of a morphism of ringed spaces

nodes.title: The cotangent complex of a morphism of ringed spaces · Lemma 08T4
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y and g : Y → Z be morphisms of ringed spaces. Then there is a canonical distinguished triangle Lf^* L_Y/Z → L_X/Z → L_X/Y → Lf^*L_Y/Z[1] in D(O_X).
nodes.section: The cotangent complex of a morphism of ringed spaces

nodes.title: The cotangent complex of a morphism of ringed spaces · Lemma 08UW
nodes.summary: Let f : (X, O_X) → (Y, O_Y) be a morphism of ringed spaces. There is a canonical map L_X/Y → NL_X/Y which identifies the naive cotangent complex with the truncation τ_≥ -1L_X/Y.
nodes.section: The cotangent complex of a morphism of ringed spaces

nodes.title: Deformations of ringed spaces and the cotangent complex · Lemma 08UZ
nodes.summary: In the situation above we have • There is a canonical element xi ∈ Ext^2_O_X(L_X/S, G) whose vanishing is a sufficient and necessary condition for the existence of a solution to ([Tag 08UY]). • If there exists a solution, then the set of isomorphism classes of solutions is principal homogeneous under Ext^1_O_X(L_X/S, G). • Given a solution X', the set of automorphisms of X' fitting into ([Tag 08UY]) is canonically isomorphic to Ext^0_O_X(L_X/S, G).
nodes.section: Deformations of ringed spaces and the cotangent complex

nodes.title: The cotangent complex of a morphism of ringed topoi · Definition 08SU
nodes.summary: Let (f, f^sharp) : (Sh(C), O_C) → (Sh(D), O_D) be a morphism of ringed topoi. The cotangent complex L_f of f is L_f = L_O_C/f^-1O_D. We sometimes write L_f = L_O_C/O_D.
nodes.section: The cotangent complex of a morphism of ringed topoi

nodes.title: The cotangent complex of a morphism of ringed topoi · Lemma 08V0
nodes.summary: Let f : (Sh(C), O) → (Sh(B), O_B) be a morphism of ringed topoi. Then H^0(L_f) = Ω_f.
nodes.section: The cotangent complex of a morphism of ringed topoi

nodes.title: The cotangent complex of a morphism of ringed topoi · Lemma 08V1
nodes.summary: Let f : (Sh(C_1), O_1) → (Sh(C_2), O_2) and g : (Sh(C_2), O_2) → (Sh(C_3), O_3) be morphisms of ringed topoi. Then there is a canonical distinguished triangle Lf^* L_g → L_g ∘ f → L_f → Lf^*L_g[1] in D(O_1).
nodes.section: The cotangent complex of a morphism of ringed topoi

nodes.title: The cotangent complex of a morphism of ringed topoi · Lemma 08V2
nodes.summary: Let f : (Sh(C), O) → (Sh(B), O_B) be a morphism of ringed topoi. There is a canonical map L_f → NL_f which identifies the naive cotangent complex with the truncation τ_≥ -1L_f.
nodes.section: The cotangent complex of a morphism of ringed topoi

nodes.title: Deformations of ringed topoi and the cotangent complex · Lemma 08V5
nodes.summary: In the situation above we have • There is a canonical element xi ∈ Ext^2_O(L_f, G) whose vanishing is a sufficient and necessary condition for the existence of a solution to ([Tag 08V4]). • If there exists a solution, then the set of isomorphism classes of solutions is principal homogeneous under Ext^1_O(L_f, G). • Given a solution X', the set of automorphisms of X' fitting into ([Tag 08V4]) is canonically isomorphic to Ext^0_O(L_f, G).
nodes.section: Deformations of ringed topoi and the cotangent complex

nodes.title: The cotangent complex of a morphism of schemes · Definition 08T2
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes. The cotangent complex L_X/Y of X over Y is the cotangent complex of f as a morphism of ringed spaces (Definition [Tag 08UU]).

nodes.title: The cotangent complex of a morphism of schemes · Lemma 08T3
nodes.summary: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of schemes. Let U = Spec(B) ⊂ X and V = Spec(A) ⊂ Y be affine opens such that f(U) ⊂ V. There is a canonical map widetildeL_B/A → L_X/Y|_U of complexes which is an isomorphism in D(O_U). This map is compatible with restricting to smaller affine opens of X and Y.

nodes.title: The cotangent complex of a morphism of schemes · Lemma 08V6
nodes.summary: Let Lambda be a ring. Let X be a scheme over Lambda. Then L_X/Spec(Lambda) = L_O_X/underlineLambda where underlineLambda is the constant sheaf with value Lambda on X.

nodes.section: The cotangent complex of a scheme over a ring

nodes.title: The cotangent complex of a morphism of algebraic spaces · Definition 08VD
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a morphism of algebraic spaces over S. The cotangent complex L_X/Y of X over Y is the cotangent complex of the morphism of ringed topoi f_small between the small étale sites of X and Y (see Properties of Spaces, Lemma [Tag 03G8] and Definition [Tag 08SU]).

nodes.section: The cotangent complex of a morphism of algebraic spaces

nodes.title: The cotangent complex of a morphism of algebraic spaces · Lemma 08VF
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let f : X → Y be a morphism of algebraic spaces over S. Assume X and Y representable by schemes X_0 and Y_0. Then there is a canonical identification L_X/Y = ε^*L_X_0/Y_0 in D(O_X) where ε is as in Derived Categories of Spaces, Section [Tag 071P] and L_X_0/Y_0 is as in Definition [Tag 08T2].

nodes.title: The cotangent complex of a morphism of algebraic spaces · Lemma 08VG
