nodes.summary: There exists a flat group scheme of finite type over the affine line which is not separated.

nodes.title: A non-separated flat group scheme · Lemma 08IX
nodes.summary: There exists a flat group scheme of finite type over the infinite dimensional affine space which is not quasi-separated.

nodes.title: A non-flat group scheme with flat identity component · Lemma 06RK
nodes.summary: There exists a group scheme G over a base S whose identity component is flat over S but which is not flat over S.
nodes.section: A non-flat group scheme with flat identity component

nodes.title: A non-separated group algebraic space over a field · Lemma 06EA
nodes.summary: There exists a group algebraic space of finite type over a field which is not separated (and not even quasi-separated or locally separated).
nodes.section: A non-separated group algebraic space over a field

nodes.title: Specializations between points in fibre étale morphism · Lemma 06UK
nodes.summary: There exists an étale morphism of algebraic spaces f : X → Y and a nontrivial specialization of points x leadsto x' in |X| with f(x) = f(x') in |Y|.
nodes.section: Specializations between points in fibre étale morphism

nodes.title: A torsor which is not an fppf torsor · Lemma 077B
nodes.summary: Let S be a scheme. Let G be a group scheme over S. The stack G-Principal classifying principal homogeneous G-spaces (see Examples of Stacks, Subsection [Tag 04UN]) and the stack G-Torsors classifying fppf G-torsors (see Examples of Stacks, Subsection [Tag 04UR]) are not equivalent in general.
nodes.section: A torsor which is not an fppf torsor

nodes.title: Stack with quasi-compact flat covering which is not algebraic · Lemma 04AH
nodes.summary: Let k be a field. Let G be an affine group scheme over k. If the stack [Spec(k)/G] has a smooth covering by a scheme, then G is of finite type over k.
nodes.section: Stack with quasi-compact flat covering which is not algebraic

nodes.title: Limit preserving on objects, not limit preserving · Lemma 07Z1
nodes.summary: Let S be a nonempty scheme. There exists a stack in groupoids p : X → (Sch/S)_fppf such that p is limit preserving on objects, but X is not limit preserving.
nodes.section: Limit preserving on objects, not limit preserving

nodes.title: Sheaf with quasi-compact flat covering which is not algebraic · Lemma 078F
nodes.summary: There exists a functor F : Sch^opp → Sets which satisfies the sheaf condition for the fpqc topology, has representable diagonal Δ : F → F × F, and such that there exists a surjective, flat, universally open, quasi-compact morphism U → F where U is a scheme, but such that F is not an algebraic space.
nodes.section: Sheaf with quasi-compact flat covering which is not algebraic

nodes.title: The étale topology vs Zariski and finite étale Covers · Lemma 0HAR
nodes.summary: The étale cover U → X cannot be refined by any finite composition of open immersions and finite étale morphisms.
nodes.section: The étale topology vs Zariski and finite étale Covers

nodes.title: Sheaves and specializations · Lemma 05LE
nodes.summary: There exists a sheaf of abelian groups G on Sch_etale with the following properties • G(X) = 0 whenever dim(X) < n, • G(X) is not zero if dim(X) ≥ n, and • if X ⊂ X' is a thickening, then G(X) = G(X').

nodes.title: Sheaves and constructible functions · Lemma 05LH
nodes.summary: There exists a sheaf of abelian groups G on Sch_etale with the following properties • G(Spec(k)) = 0 whenever k is a field, • G is limit preserving, • if X ⊂ X' is a thickening, then G(X) = G(X'), and • G is not zero.

nodes.title: The lisse-étale site is not functorial · Lemma 07BG
nodes.summary: The lisse-étale site is not functorial, even for morphisms of schemes.
nodes.section: The lisse-étale site is not functorial

nodes.title: Sheaves on the category of Noetherian schemes · Lemma 0GE9
nodes.summary: With S = Spec(F_p) the inclusion functor (Noetherian/S)_fppf → (Sch/S)_fppf does not define a morphism of sites.
nodes.section: Sheaves on the category of Noetherian schemes

nodes.title: Derived pushforward of quasi-coherent modules · Lemma 08IY
nodes.summary: Let X be an algebraic stack. Let K be an object of D(O_X) whose cohomology sheaves are locally quasi-coherent (Sheaves on Stacks, Definition [Tag 06WJ]) and satisfy the flat base change property (Cohomology of Stacks, Definition [Tag 0762]). Then there exists a distinguished triangle K → ∏_n ≥ 0 τ_≥ -n K → ∏_n ≥ 0 τ_≥ -n K → K[1] in D(O_X). In other words, K is the derived limit of its canonical truncations.

nodes.title: Derived pushforward of quasi-coherent modules · Lemma 08IZ
nodes.summary: Let X be an algebraic stack. If F_n is a collection of locally quasi-coherent sheaves with the flat base change property on X, then ⊕_n F_n[n] → ∏_n F_n[n] is an isomorphism in D(O_X).

nodes.title: Derived pushforward of quasi-coherent modules · Lemma 07DD
nodes.summary: A quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism f : X → Y of algebraic stacks need not induce a functor Rf_* : D_QCoh(O_X) → D_QCoh(O_Y).

nodes.title: A big abelian category · Lemma 07JT
nodes.summary: There exists a "big" abelian category A whose Ext-groups are proper classes.

nodes.title: Weakly associated points and scheme theoretic density · Lemma 084K
nodes.summary: There exists a reduced scheme X and a schematically dense open U ⊂ X such that some weakly associated point x ∈ X is not in U.
nodes.section: Weakly associated points and scheme theoretic density

nodes.title: Example of non-additivity of traces · Lemma 087L
nodes.summary: There exists a ring R, a distinguished triangle (K, L, M, α, β, γ) in the homotopy category K(R), and an endomorphism (a, b, c) of this distinguished triangle, such that K, L, M are perfect complexes and Tr_K(a) + Tr_M(c) not = Tr_L(b).

nodes.title: Nonfinite cohomology of the structure sheaf of a projective scheme · Lemma 0HAT
nodes.summary: Non-finite H^0. • There exists a ring R and a projective scheme X over R such that H^0(X, O_X) is not a finite R-module. • There exists a ring R and a finite type quasi-coherent module F on P^1_R such that H^0(P^1_R, F) is not a finite R-module.
nodes.section: Nonfinite cohomology of the structure sheaf of a projective scheme

nodes.title: Being projective is not local on the base · Lemma 08J1
nodes.summary: The properties • [] P(f) ="f is projective", and • [] P(f) ="f is quasi-projective" are not Zariski local on the base. A fortiori, they are not fpqc local on the base.
nodes.section: Being projective is not local on the base

nodes.title: Non-effective descent data for projective schemes · Lemma 08KF
nodes.summary: There is an etale covering X→ S of schemes and a descent datum (V/X,φ) relative to X→ S such that V→ X is projective, but the descent datum is not effective in the category of schemes.
nodes.section: Non-effective descent data for projective schemes

nodes.title: A family of curves whose total space is not a scheme · Lemma 0D5E
nodes.summary: There exists a field k and a family of curves X → A^1_k such that X is not a scheme.
nodes.section: A family of curves whose total space is not a scheme

nodes.title: Derived base change · Lemma 08J3
nodes.summary: Let R → R' and R → A be ring maps. In general there does not exist a functor T : D(A) → D(A ⊗_R R') of triangulated categories such that an A-module M gives an object T(M) of D(A ⊗_R R') which maps to M ⊗_R^L R' under the map D(A ⊗_R R') → D(R').

nodes.title: An interesting compact object · Lemma 09R5
nodes.summary: There exists a differential graded algebra (A, d) and a compact object E of D(A, d) such that E cannot be represented by a finite and graded projective differential graded A-module.

nodes.title: The stack of proper algebraic spaces is not algebraic · Lemma 0D1R
nodes.summary: The stack in groupoids p'_fp, flat, proper : Spacesstack'_fp, flat, proper → Sch_fppf whose category of sections over a scheme S is the category of flat, proper, finitely presented algebraic spaces over S (see Quot, Section [Tag 0D1D]) is not an algebraic stack.
nodes.section: The stack of proper algebraic spaces is not algebraic

nodes.title: An example of a non-algebraic Hom-stack · Lemma 0AF9
nodes.summary: Let W be a two dimensional regular integral Noetherian scheme with function field K. Let G → W be an abelian scheme. Then the map H^1_fppf(W, G) → H^1_fppf(Spec(K), G) is injective.
nodes.section: An example of a non-algebraic Hom-stack

nodes.title: An example of a non-algebraic Hom-stack · Lemma 0AFA
nodes.summary: Let G be a smooth commutative group algebraic space over a field K. Then H^1_fppf(Spec(K), G) is torsion.
nodes.section: An example of a non-algebraic Hom-stack

nodes.title: An example of a non-algebraic Hom-stack · Lemma 0AFB
nodes.summary: The canonical map X(S) → lim X(S_n) is not essentially surjective.
nodes.section: An example of a non-algebraic Hom-stack

nodes.title: An example of a non-algebraic Hom-stack · Proposition 0AFC
nodes.summary: The stack X = underlineMor_S(X, [S/A]) is not algebraic.
nodes.section: An example of a non-algebraic Hom-stack

nodes.title: An algebraic stack not satisfying strong formal effectiveness · Lemma 0CXX
nodes.summary: Let k be an algebraically closed field which is not the closure of a finite field. Let A be an abelian variety over k. Let X = [Spec(k)/A]. There exists an inverse system of k-algebras R_n with surjective transition maps whose kernels are locally nilpotent and a system (xi_n) of X lying over the system (Spec(R_n)) such that this system is not effective in the sense of Artin's Axioms, Remark [Tag 0CXT].
nodes.section: An algebraic stack not satisfying strong formal effectiveness

nodes.title: A counter example to Grothendieck's existence theorem · Lemma 0ARF
nodes.summary: Counter examples to algebraization of coherent sheaves. • Grothendieck's existence theorem as stated in Cohomology of Schemes, Theorem [Tag 088E] is false if we drop the assumption that X → Spec(A) is separated. • The stack of coherent sheaves Cohstack_X/B of Quot, Theorems [Tag 09DS] and [Tag 08WC] is in general not algebraic if we drop the assumption that X → S is separated • The functor Quotfunctor_F/X/B of Quot, Proposition [Tag 09TU] is not an algebraic space in…
nodes.section: A counter example to Grothendieck's existence theorem

nodes.title: Affine formal algebraic spaces · Lemma 0CBC
nodes.summary: There exists an affine formal algebraic space which is not McQuillan.

nodes.title: Affine formal algebraic spaces · Lemma 0CBD
nodes.summary: There exists an affine formal algebraic space X whose regular functions do not separate points, in the following sense: If we write X = colim X_λ as in Formal Spaces, Definition [Tag 0AI7] then lim Γ(X_λ, O_X_λ) is a field, but X_red has infinitely many points.

nodes.title: Affine formal algebraic spaces · Lemma 0CBE
nodes.summary: There exists a representable morphism f : X → Y of affine formal algebraic spaces with Y McQuillan, but X not McQuillan.

nodes.title: Flat maps are not directed limits of finitely presented flat maps · Lemma 0ATF
nodes.summary: There exists a commutative ring A and a flat A-algebra B which cannot be written as a filtered colimit of finitely presented flat A-algebras. In fact, we may either choose A to be a finite type F_p-algebra or a 1-dimensional Noetherian local ring with residue field of characteristic 0.
nodes.section: Flat maps are not directed limits of finitely presented flat maps

nodes.title: The category of modules modulo torsion modules · Proposition 0EA5
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let S be a multiplicative subset of A. Let Mod_A denote the category of A-modules and T its Serre subcategory of modules for which any element is annihilated by some element of S. Then there is a canonical equivalence Mod_A/T → Mod_S^-1A.
nodes.section: The category of modules modulo torsion modules

nodes.title: The category of modules modulo torsion modules · Proposition 0B0K
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let Q(A) denote its total quotient ring (as in Algebra, Example [Tag 02C5]). Let Mod_A denote the category of A-modules and T its Serre subcategory of torsion modules. Let Mod_Q(A) denote the category of Q(A)-modules. Then there is a canonical equivalence Mod_A/T → Mod_Q(A).
nodes.section: The category of modules modulo torsion modules

nodes.title: The category of modules modulo torsion modules · Proposition 0B0L
nodes.summary: Let A be a Noetherian integral domain. Let K denote its field of fractions. Let Mod_A^fg denote the category of finitely generated A-modules and T^fg its Serre subcategory of finitely generated torsion modules. Then Mod_A^fg/T^fg is canonically equivalent to the category of finite dimensional K-vector spaces.
nodes.section: The category of modules modulo torsion modules

nodes.title: The category of modules modulo torsion modules · Proposition 0B0M
nodes.summary: The quotient of the category of abelian groups modulo its Serre subcategory of torsion groups is the category of Q-vector spaces.
nodes.section: The category of modules modulo torsion modules

nodes.title: Different colimit topologies · Lemma 0B2Z
nodes.summary: There exists a system G_1 → G_2 → G_3 → … of (abelian) topological groups such that colim G_n taken in the category of topological spaces is different from colim G_n taken in the category of topological groups.

nodes.title: Universally submersive but not V covering · Lemma 0EU9
nodes.summary: There exists a morphism X → Y of affine schemes which is universally submersive such that (X → Y) is not a V covering.
nodes.section: Universally submersive but not V covering

nodes.title: The spectrum of the integers is not quasi-compact · Lemma 0EUF
nodes.summary: There exists a ring A and an infinite family of flat ring maps (A → A_i)_i ∈ I such that for every A-module M M = Equalizer( xymatrix ∏_i ∈ I M ⊗_A A_i ar@<1ex>[r] ar@<-1ex>[r] & ∏_i, j ∈ I M ⊗_A A_i ⊗_A A_j ) but there is no finite subfamily where the same thing is true.
nodes.section: The spectrum of the integers is not quasi-compact

nodes.title: The spectrum of the integers is not quasi-compact · Lemma 0EUG
nodes.summary: The scheme Spec(Z) is not quasi-compact in the canonical topology on the category of schemes.
nodes.section: The spectrum of the integers is not quasi-compact

nodes.title: Colimits · Definition 078I
nodes.summary: A directed set is a nonempty set I endowed with a preorder ≤ such that given any pair i, j ∈ I there exists a k ∈ I such that i ≤ k and j ≤ k. A system of rings over I is given by a ring A_i for each i ∈ I and a map of rings φ_ij : A_i → A_j whenever i ≤ j such that the composition A_i → A_j → A_k is equal to A_i → A_k whenever i ≤ j ≤ k.

nodes.title: Colimits · Definition 078K
nodes.summary: The ring A constructed in Exercise [Tag 078J] is called the colimit of the system. Notation colim A_i.

nodes.title: Colimits · Definition 0278
nodes.summary: A module M over R is said to be of finite presentation over R if it is isomorphic to the cokernel of a map of finite free modules R^⊕ n → R^⊕ m.

nodes.title: The Spectrum of a ring · Definition 027B
nodes.summary: A topological space X is called quasi-compact if for any open covering X = ⋃_i∈ I U_i there is a finite subset (i_1, …, i_n)⊂ I such that X = U_i_1∪… U_i_n.

nodes.title: The Spectrum of a ring · Definition 027C
nodes.summary: A topological space X is said to verify the separation axiom T_0 if for any pair of points x, y∈ X, xnot = y there is an open subset of X containing one but not the other. We say that X is Hausdorff if for any pair x, y∈ X, xnot = y there are disjoint open subsets U, V such that x∈ U and y∈ V.

nodes.title: The Spectrum of a ring · Definition 027D
nodes.summary: A topological space X is called irreducible if X is not empty and if X = Z_1∪ Z_2 with Z_1, Z_2⊂ X closed, then either Z_1 = X or Z_2 = X. A subset T⊂ X of a topological space is called irreducible if it is an irreducible topological space with the topology induced from X. This definition implies T is irreducible if and only if the closure bar T of T in X is irreducible.

nodes.title: The Spectrum of a ring · Definition 027E
nodes.summary: A point x of an irreducible topological space X is called a generic point of X if X is equal to the closure of the subset (x).

nodes.title: The Spectrum of a ring · Definition 027F
nodes.summary: A topological space X is called Noetherian if any decreasing sequence Z_1⊃ Z_2 ⊃ Z_3⊃ … of closed subsets of X stabilizes. (It is called Artinian if any increasing sequence of closed subsets stabilizes.)

nodes.title: The Spectrum of a ring · Definition 027G
nodes.summary: A maximal irreducible subset T⊂ X is called an irreducible component of the space X. Such an irreducible component of X is automatically a closed subset of X.

nodes.title: The Spectrum of a ring · Definition 027H
nodes.summary: A point x∈ X is called closed if overline(x) = ( x). Let x, y be points of X. We say that x is a specialization of y, or that y is a generalization of x if x∈ overline(y).

nodes.title: The Spectrum of a ring · Definition 027I
nodes.summary: A topological space X is called connected if it is nonempty and not the union of two nonempty disjoint open subsets. A connected component of X is a maximal connected subset. Any point of X is contained in a connected component of X and any connected component of X is closed in X. (But in general a connected component need not be open in X.)

nodes.title: Length · Definition 076E
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Let M be an A-module. The length of M as an R-module is length_A(M) = sup ( n mid ∃ 0 = M_0 ⊂ M_1 ⊂ … ⊂ M_n = M, M_i not = M_i + 1 ). In other words, the supremum of the lengths of chains of submodules.

nodes.title: Catenary rings · Definition 027O
nodes.summary: A Noetherian ring A is said to be catenary if for any triple of prime ideals p_1 ⊂ p_2 ⊂ p_3 we have ht( p_3 / p_1) = ht( p_3/ p_2) + ht( p_2/ p_1). Here ht( p/ q) means the height of p/ q in the ring A/ q. In a formula ht( p/ q) = dim(A_ p/ qA_ p) = dim((A/ q)_ p) = dim((A/ q)_ p/ q) A topological space X is catenary, if given T ⊂ T' ⊂ X with T and T' closed and irreducible, then there exists a maximal chain of irreducible closed subsets T = T_0 ⊂ T_1 ⊂ … ⊂ T_n = T' and…

nodes.title: Finite locally free modules · Definition 027R
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. Recall that a finite locally free A-module M is a module such that for every p ∈ Spec(A) there exists an f∈ A, f not ∈ p such that M_f is a finite free A_f-module. We say M is an invertible module if M is finite locally free of rank 1, i.e., for every p ∈ Spec(A) there exists an f∈ A, f not ∈ p such that M_f ≅ A_f as an A_f-module.

nodes.title: Finite locally free modules · Definition 078Q
nodes.summary: Let A be a ring. The class group of A, sometimes called the Picard group of A is the set Pic(A) of isomorphism classes of invertible A-modules endowed with a group operation defined by tensor product (see Exercise [Tag 078P]).

nodes.title: Going up and going down · Definition 027U
nodes.summary: Let φ : A → B be a homomorphism of rings. We say that the going-up theorem holds for φ if the following condition is satisfied: • [(GU)] for any p, p' ∈ Spec(A) such that p ⊂ p', and for any P ∈ Spec(B) lying over p, there exists P'∈ Spec(B) lying over p' such that P ⊂ P'. Similarly, we say that the going-down theorem holds for φ if the following condition is satisfied: • [(GD)] for any p, p' ∈ Spec(A) such that p ⊂ p', and for any P' ∈ Spec(B) lying over p', there exists…

nodes.title: Hilbert functions · Definition 027X
nodes.summary: A numerical polynomial is a polynomial f(x) ∈ Q[x] such that f(n) ∈ Z for every integer n.

nodes.title: Hilbert functions · Definition 027Y
nodes.summary: A graded module M over a ring A is an A-module M endowed with a direct sum decomposition bigoplus_n ∈ Z M_n into A-submodules. We will say that M is locally finite if all of the M_n are finite A-modules. Suppose that A is a Noetherian ring and that φ is a Euler-Poincaré function on finite A-modules. This means that for every finitely generated A-module M we are given an integer φ(M) ∈ Z and for every short exact sequence 0 → M' → M → M" → 0 we have φ(M) = φ(M') + φ(M").…

nodes.title: Hilbert functions · Definition 027Z
nodes.summary: A graded A-algebra is a graded A-module B = bigoplus_n ≥ 0 B_n together with an A-bilinear map B × B → B, (b, b') ↦ bb' that turns B into an A-algebra so that B_n · B_m ⊂ B_n + m. Finally, a graded module M over a graded A-algebra B is given by a graded A-module M together with a (compatible) B-module structure such that B_n · M_d ⊂ M_n + d. Now you can define homomorphisms of graded modules/rings, graded submodules, graded ideals, exact sequences of graded modules, etc, etc.

nodes.title: Proj of a ring · Definition 0281
nodes.summary: Let R be a graded ring. A homogeneous ideal is simply an ideal I ⊂ R which is also a graded submodule of R. Equivalently, it is an ideal generated by homogeneous elements. Equivalently, if f ∈ I and f = f_0 + f_1 + … + f_n is the decomposition of f into homogeneous pieces in R then f_i ∈ I for each i.

nodes.title: Proj of a ring · Definition 0282
nodes.summary: We define the homogeneous spectrum Proj(R) of the graded ring R to be the set of homogeneous, prime ideals p of R such that R_+ not ⊂ p. Note that Proj(R) is a subset of Spec(R) and hence has a natural induced topology.

nodes.title: Proj of a ring · Definition 0283
nodes.summary: Let R = ⊕_d ≥ 0 R_d be a graded ring, let f∈ R_d and assume that d ≥ 1. We define R_(f) to be the subring of R_f consisting of elements of the form r/f^n with r homogeneous and deg(r) = nd. Furthermore, we define D_+(f) = ( p ∈ Proj(R) | f not∈ p ). Finally, for a homogeneous ideal I ⊂ R we define V_+(I) = V(I) ∩ Proj(R).

nodes.title: Cohen-Macaulay rings of dimension 1 · Definition 0285
nodes.summary: A Noetherian local ring A is said to be Cohen-Macaulay of dimension d if it has dimension d and there exists a system of parameters x_1, …, x_d for A such that x_i is a nonzerodivisor in A/(x_1, …, x_i-1) for i = 1, …, d.

nodes.title: Filtered derived category · Definition 028A
nodes.summary: Let A be an abelian category. Let I be a filtered object of A. Assume the filtration on I is finite. We say I is filtered injective if each gr^p(I) is an injective object of A.

nodes.title: Filtered derived category · Definition 028B
nodes.summary: Let A be an abelian category. We denote Fil^f(A) the full subcategory of Fil(A) whose objects consist of those A ∈ Ob(Fil(A)) whose filtration is finite.

nodes.title: Filtered derived category · Definition 028D
nodes.summary: Let A be an abelian category. Let α : K^bullet → L^bullet be a morphism of complexes of Fil(A). We say that α is a filtered quasi-isomorphism if for each p ∈ Z the morphism gr^p(K^bullet) → gr^p(L^bullet) is a quasi-isomorphism.

nodes.title: Filtered derived category · Definition 028E
nodes.summary: Let A be an abelian category. Let K^bullet be a complex of Fil^f(A). We say that K^bullet is filtered acyclic if for each p ∈ Z the complex gr^p(K^bullet) is acyclic.

nodes.title: Schemes · Definition 028Y
nodes.summary: A scheme X is called integral if X is nonempty and for every nonempty affine open U ⊂ X the ring Γ(U, O_X) = O_X(U) is a domain.

nodes.title: Tangent Spaces · Definition 029D
nodes.summary: For any ring R we denote R[ε] the ring of dual numbers. As an R-module it is free with basis 1, ε. The ring structure comes from setting ε^2 = 0.

nodes.title: Tangent Spaces · Definition 029F
nodes.summary: Let f : X → S be a morphism of schemes. Let x ∈ X. We dub the set of dotted arrows of Exercise [Tag 029E] the tangent space of X over S and we denote it T_X/S, x. An element of this space is called a tangent vector of X/S at x.

nodes.title: Quasi-coherent Sheaves · Definition 029O
nodes.summary: Let X be a scheme. A sheaf F of O_X-modules is quasi-coherent if for every affine open Spec(R) = U ⊂ X the restriction F|_U is of the form widetilde M for some R-module M.

nodes.title: Quasi-coherent Sheaves · Definition 029P
nodes.summary: Let X be a topological space. Let x, x' ∈ X. We say x is a specialization of x' if and only if x ∈ overline(x').

nodes.title: Quasi-coherent Sheaves · Definition 029S
nodes.summary: A scheme X is called locally Noetherian if and only if for every point x ∈ X there exists an affine open Spec(R) = U ⊂ X such that R is Noetherian. A scheme is Noetherian if it is locally Noetherian and quasi-compact.

nodes.title: Quasi-coherent Sheaves · Definition 029T
nodes.summary: Let X be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let F be a quasi-coherent sheaf of O_X-modules. We say F is coherent if for every point x ∈ X there exists an affine open Spec(R) = U ⊂ X such that F|_U is isomorphic to widetilde M for some finite R-module M.

nodes.title: Invertible sheaves · Definition 02AD
nodes.summary: Let X be a locally ringed space. An invertible O_X-module on X is a sheaf of O_X-modules L such that every point has an open neighbourhood U ⊂ X such that L|_U is isomorphic to O_U as O_U-module. We say that L is trivial if it is isomorphic to O_X as a O_X-module.

nodes.title: Invertible sheaves · Definition 02AG
nodes.summary: Let R be a ring. An invertible module M is an R-module M such that widetilde M is an invertible sheaf on the spectrum of R. We say M is trivial if M ≅ R as an R-module.

nodes.title: Invertible sheaves · Definition 02AM
nodes.summary: Let X be a locally ringed space. The Picard group of X is the set Pic(X) of isomorphism classes of invertible O_X-modules with addition given by tensor product. See Modules, Definition [Tag 01CX]. For a ring R we set Pic(R) = Pic(Spec(R)).

nodes.title: v Cech Cohomology · Definition 02AP
nodes.summary: (Definition of delta.) Suppose that 0 → F_1 → F_2 → F_3 → 0 is a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on any topological space X. The boundary map δ : H^0(X, F_3) → check H^1(X, F_1) is defined as follows. Take an element τ ∈ H^0(X, F_3). Choose an open covering U : X = ⋃_i∈ I U_i such that for each i there exists a section tilde τ_i ∈ F_2 lifting the restriction of τ to U_i. Then consider the assignment (i_0, i_1) ↦ tilde τ_i_0|_U_i_0i_1 - tilde τ_i_1|_U_i_0i_1. This…

nodes.title: Divisors · Definition 02AR
nodes.summary: Throughout, let S be any scheme and let X be a Noetherian, integral scheme. • A Weil divisor on X is a formal linear combination Sigma n_i[Z_i] of prime divisors Z_i with integer coefficients. • A prime divisor is a closed subscheme Z ⊂ X, which is integral with generic point xi ∈ Z such that O_X, xi has dimension 1. We will use the notation O_X, Z = O_X, xi when xi ∈ Z ⊂ X is as above. Note that O_X, Z ⊂ K(X) is a subring of the function field of X. • The Weil divisor…
